column12: Means "games, celebration" in Mongolian. This is the name of a traditional festival held throughout Mongolia during midsummer, involving competitions of wrestling, horse racing, and archery. It is also called эрийн гурван наадам (eriin gurvan naadam) meaning "the three games of men".
Derived from the Arabic ناد (nād) meaning "call" and Ali 1, one of The 99 Names of Allah. Naad-e-Ali is a praise suggested by the angel Jibril to Prophet Muhammad in order to conquer a town.
From the Hawaiian nā meaning "quieted, pacified" or "the (plural)" and 'ai meaning "ruler".
Means "gull hatchling" in Greenlandic, deriving from naaja meaning "gull; seagull" and raq meaning "cub; hatchling; baby animal".

The Hebrew meaning of the boy's name Naaman is "pleasant; pleasantness" or even "beautiful; agreeable; delightful."  Biblically, Naaman was a Syrian, the commander-in-chief of the armies of Benhadad (Syria). In the time of Joram, king of Israel. He was afflicted with leprosy; and when the little Hebrew slave-girl that waited on his wife told her of a prophet in Samaria who could cure her master, he obtained a letter from Benhadad and proceeded with it to Joram.  The king of Israel suspected in this some evil design against him, and rent his clothes. Elisha the prophet hearing of this, sent for Naaman, and the strange interview which took place is recorded in 2 Kings 5. The narrative contains all that is known of the Syrian commander. He was cured of his leprosy by dipping himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the word of Elisha. His cure is alluded to by our Lord (Luke 4:27).
Possibly a variant transliteration of Namuunaa.
From Hebrew נַעֲרָה (na'ará) meaning "girl" or "maiden". Naarah was of the tribe of Judah and as the second wife of Ashhur she gave birth to Ahuzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari.
Variant transcription of Naarai.This transcription is used in The Complete Jewish Bible, Hebrew Names Version, Orthodox Jewish Bible, and Revised Standard Version.

This name comes from the root נער (na'ar), which has three meanings. The meaning that is most likely is "youth" or "child", but it can also mean "to growl" and "to shake loose". The second part of the name, י (yod), is also of uncertain meaning. It can make the word an adjective, become possesive, or may be referring to Yahweh. The most accepted meaning for this name is "child of Yah" or "child of the Lord".In the Bible, Naarai is one of David's warriors and the son of Ezbai. He is only mentioned once in the Bible, in 1 Chronicles 11:37.

Derived from נַעַר (na’ar) meaning “teen, boy, youth” in Hebrew. Naaran (also Na'aran) (Hebrew: נערן) was an ancient Jewish village dating to the 5th and 6th century CE. Remains of the village have been excavated north-west of Jericho. Naaran is archeologically notable for the mosaic floor of a synagogue, featuring a large zodiac design, which was discovered at the site.

Naardiid is a Somali name with the following characteristics:Meaning: Naardiid generally means "eternal" or "everlasting."Origin: It is derived from the Somali language, where names often reflect timeless qualities or enduring attributes. The name Naardiid conveys a sense of permanence and enduring presence.
Variant transcription of Naarai.This transcription is used in the Lexham English Bible and God's Word Translation of the Bible.
Short form of Athanaas, Donaas and Ignaas.A notable bearer of this name is the South African rugby player Naas Botha (b. 1958).
A benevolent Navajo deity whose name comes from naʼashjéʼii meaning "spider" and asdzáán meaning "woman".
Variant of Nahshon used in the King James Version of the Old Testament.
Comes from the arabic verb "nasara" which means to help or support. Saladin Al-Nasir Salah ad-Din Yusuf contributed to making this name more popular.

Of Australian Aboriginal origin (Pintupi, to be precise), the meaning of this name is not yet known to me at the moment. A known bearer of this name is Naata Nungurrayi (b. circa 1932), an Australian Aboriginal painter.
a Dutch diminutive form of Anna or Johanna
Could be a variant of Navia
Means "in the center of the universe" in Ojibwe.

column3: 菜彩, 愛綺, 七彩, 奈郁, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens" combined with 彩 (aya) meaning "colour". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Medieval diminutive of Abel. It used to be a medieval custom to drop syllables before a first name therefore “mine Abel” led to “Nab”.
Means "news, tidings, announcement" in Arabic. This is the name of the 78th chapter (surah an-Naba) of the Quran.Also compare the related masculine name Nabi 2.
Means "new light" from Sanskrit नव (nava) meaning "new, fresh" and दीप (dīpa) meaning "lamp, light".

column3: 娜白, 娜百, 娜柏, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Combination of the names Na and Bai.
Means "fool; senseless; failure". This was the name of a rich Calebite who was the first husband of Abigail.

column3: 菜花(Japanese Kanji)|なばな(Japanese Hiragana)|ナバナ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 菜花 (nabana) meaning "rape blossom", which combines the kanji 菜 (na, sai) meaning "vegetables, greens" with 花 (hana, bana, ka) meaning "flower". Other kanji combinations are possible.

A warrior rescued by Gawain. Nabaor had lived in the realm of Illyricum until the barbarian King Milocrates kidnapped him. When a young Gawain and a Roman fleet landed on Milocrates’ island, Nabaor helped them to defeat the king and to take over the island.
Of uncertain origin and meaning. Current theories include a derivation from the place name Navarre and a derivation from Basque nabar "multicolored".

Means "she of the pasture", from the Hurrian element naw ("pasture"). Nabarbi was a major Hittite goddess associated with ritual purification, and with farming. She was also possibly worshipped as part of a dyad with the goddess Šauška.
From Persian نبات (nabāt) meaning "rock candy, rock sugar".

column3: ナビ(Japanese Katakana)|なべ(Japanese Hiragana)|鍋(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 鍋 (nabe) meaning "pot".Onna Nabe was a female Ryukyuan poet of the 1700s who improvised a poem when she received King Shokei at Manzakage. She was the first-recognized female poet in Okinawa.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نبيه (see Nabih).
Alternate transcription of Arabic نبيهة (see Nabiha).
Alternate transcription of Arabic نبيلة (see Nabila), as well as the usual Urdu transcription.

Meaning uncertain, possibly inspired by Cerberus. This is the name of a three-headed demon who appears in several works on demonology, including the 17th-century grimoire The Lesser Key of Solomon (author unknown), the Pseudomonarchia Daemonum (1563) by Dutch physician Johann Weyer and the Dictionnaire Infernal (1818) by French occultist Jacques Collin de Plancy.
Indian masculine name derived from the Gujarati word નભ (nabh) meaning "sky".
Nabha is an Indian name meaning "the heart center" in Sanskrit.

column3: 나비(Korean Hangul)|نبي(Arabic)|نبی(Urdu, Persian)|নবী(Bengali)|奈美, 奈弥, 凪火, 菜彌, 奈琵, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ナビ(Japanese Katakana)|なべ(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: Means "butterfly" in Korean. Nabi is also used in Korean an endearment for a cat, like "kitty".
Alternate transcription of Arabic نبيه (see Nabih).
Indonesian and Malay form of Nabila.

In Perlesvaus, a malevolent lord.He killed King Marin the Jealous and tried to deprive Meliot, Marin’s son, of his lands. He also stole the holy Circle of Gold, which belonged to Perceval. Gawain reclaimed the Circle and killed Nabigan in combat.Nabigan’s brother, Anurez, later caused trouble for Gawain and Arthur.
Means "keen, astute, clever, bright" in Arabic, from the root نبه (nabbaha) meaning "to alarm, to alert, to inform".
Alternate transcription of Arabic نبيهة (see Nabiha), as well as a Malay variant.
Combination of the name Nabi 2 and the Persian word جان (jân) meaning "soul, life".
from the Japanese word nabiku, which means "to bend, yield, or sway to.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نبيلة (see Nabila), as well as the Malay and Indonesian form.
Indonesian and Malay form of Nabila.
Indonesian and Malay variant of Nabila.
Means "new, fresh," derived from Bengali নতুন (notun), which means “new, recent, modern”.
Possibly a variant of Navin, meaning "new". The oldest recorded birth by the Social Security Administration for the name Nabina is Sunday, March 29th, 1908.
The name of the last king of an independent Sparta, who reigned from 207 BC until his assassination in 192 BC.
From Bit prefixed with the first-person singular plain pronoun 나 (na).
From Bom prefixed with the first-person singular plain pronoun 나 (na).

He was “a great mighty giant”, lord of the Isle of Servage.One of several giants killed by Tristan. Nabon ruled Glait or Mormonda Castle on the Island of Servage, and he hated all of Arthur’s knights. He had killed several of them, including Mennon the Small, a cousin of Sir Lamorat.As the result of a shipwreck, Lamorat washed upon Nabon’s island just before a tournament which Nabon had declared in honor of his newly-knighted son, Nathan. In jousting, Nabon had a trick of killing his opponent’s horse. Determined to slay Nabon, Lamorat entered the tournament, but, although he fared best of the visiting knights, Nabon nearly killed him.Tristan, who had also come to the tournament, stepped in just in time, and killed both Nabon and his son. Tristan awarded Nabon’s island to the noble Sir Seguarades.
Means "may Nabu be exalted" or "Nabu is praised" in Akkadian. Nabonidus (c.615 BC - after 522 BC) was the last native king of the Neo-Babylonian Empire and ancient Mesopotamia.
Meaning unknown, possibly based on Nabu or Noboru. The name of a character from "The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time". Nabooru is a Gerudo warrior.
In the Hebrew Bible, Naboth was a Jezreelite who was executed by Jezebel so her husband Ahab could have his vineyard.
Greek form of Nabu (see Nebo), as it first appeared in the Septuagint.
Italian rare form for Nebuchadnezzar.It appears in Dante Alighieri's Commedia, Paradiso, IV Canto.
Italian, Portuguese and Spanish form of Nebuchadnezzar.
From Assyrian 𒁹𒀭𒀝𒊺𒍦𒀀𒉌 (Nabu-šezibanni), meaning "o Nabu, save me". This was what the Assyrians named Psamtik I as.
Means "Nabu, make the name prosper" in Akkadian.

The prefix of this name, "Na-" is a traditional Ugandan honorary that means "Mother of", which implies someone (usually a woman) who is deserving of or connected to a person with high respect; the suffix is derived from the Swahili word "bwana"; which can be used in reference to a master, boss, sir, or an important leader. When combined, this name roughly translates to "Mother of a leader".
From Nəcəf, the name of a city in Iraq.
From Catalan nàcara, a variant of nacra meaning "pen shell".
Meaning unknown. It has particular usage in Venezuela.
Possibly an invented name blending the popular phonetic prefix na and the name Ricardo.
Means "he lies looking sideways", derived from Nahuatl nacazitta "to look at someone with fondness, to cast a sidelong glance" and the suffix -toc "to be lying down".
Alternate transcription of Arabic ناصف (see Nasif) chiefly used in Tunisia.
Diminutive of Ignác, not used as a given name in its own right.
Maghrebi transcription of Nasir al-Din (chiefly Algerian).
Alternate transcription of Arabic ناصر (see Nasir) chiefly used in North Africa.
Possibly derived from the Hebrew name Nathan.
Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐชานนท์ (see Natchanon).
Of uncertain origin, uses the popular feminine suffix -ine.

column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens" or 樹 (na) meaning "tree, plant" or 奈 (na), a phonetic character or 那 (na) meaning "what" combined with 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" or 知 (chi) meaning "wisdom, knowledge, intellect" or 散 (chi) meaning "scatter". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.
Diminutive of Nacho; in other words, a double diminutive of Ignacio.
Greek Ναχμανίδης (Nakhmanídēs) "son of Nachman". It was borne by a famous Sephardic Rabbi in the 13th century.

The word "American" spelled backwards, used as a feminine given name.
Of obscure origins; perhaps from a surname.

Diminutive of Ignacio. In Mexican Spanish, this coincides with an ethnic slur for a man of indigenous descent who is deemed to be low-class or uncultured, derived from a short form of totonaco "Totonac (an indigenous group)".
Spanish and Italian form of Nahor.

Means "walker, traveller", from Nahuatl nahui "four" and icxitl "foot". This was also the name of a brother of the Aztec god of travellers, Yacatecuhtli, and sometimes used as an epithet of Quetzalcoatl.
Short form of names beginning with Naczę, such as Naczęsław, Naczęmir.
Diminutive of names beginning with Naczę, such as Naczęsław, Naczęmir.
Derived from the Slavic elements načęti "to begin" and mirŭ "peace".
Derived from the Slavic elements načęti "to begin" and radŭ "happy, willing".
Derived from the Slavic elements načęti "to begin" and slava "glory".
Derived from the Slavic elements načęti "to begin" and vojĭ "warrior".
Derived from the Slavic elements načęti "to begin" and ujĭ "maternal uncle".
Diminutive of names beginning with Naczę, such as Naczęsław, Naczęmir.
Diminutive of names beginning with Naczę, such as Naczęsław, Naczęmir.

MEANING : a river (if thought of as a male), thunderer (as cloud), roarer, neigher(as a horse), bellowerUsage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhalese, Hindi, Sikh, Buddhist, Kannada, Marathi, Gujarati, Assamese, Bengali, Malayalam, Fijian
Venetian cognate of Natale. The name coincides with the Venetian word for Christmas.
Latin natalis "natal, of birth" + Old High German berg "mountain, hill".
Latin natalis "natal, of birth" + Old High German beraht, Old Saxon berht "bright" from Proto-Germanic berhtaz.

column12: From Japanese 雪崩 or 崩 (nadare) meaning "snowslide, avalanche".
Provençal and Gascon cognate of Nadal.
Meaning uncertain, possibly derived from the Akkadian element nadānu ("gift, tribute, payment").
Legendary figure reported to be Pictish
A short form and nickname for Nadja or Nadine.The German presenter and singer Nadja abd el Farrag goes with the stage name Naddel.
Derived from the Old Norse name elements naddr "stud, nail, small man" and oddr "point of a sword". Naddoðr was a Norwegian-born Faroese viking who discovered Iceland in the 9th century.
From Old Norse naddr "stud, nail", indicating a little person.

Name of Sanskrit origin, meaning Lord or God of the rivers. It originates from the Sanskrit word for ocean, "nadīśa" नदीश.
Provençal and Haitian form of Nadezhda (via Nadège).
Variant of Nadège predominantly found in French-speaking African countries.
Derived from Czech naděje "hope", this name is a cognate of Naděžda.
From japanese 撫 (nade) meaning "stroke" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child".

column3: 撫子(Japanese Kanji)|なでし子(Kanji/Hiragana)|なでしこ(Japanese Hiragana)|ナデシコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 撫子 (nadeshiko), generally referring to any flower belonging to the Dianthus genus but can also refer to a lovable, caressable child. It is derived from 撫で (nade), the continuative form of classical verb 撫づ (nadzu) meaning "to stroke, caress," combined with a continuative suffix shi and 子 (ko) meaning "child."Fictional examples include Nadeshiko Kinomoto (木之本 撫子) from 'Cardcaptor Sakura' and Nadeshiko Fujisaki (藤咲 なでしこ) from 'Shugo Chara!'.This name is rarely used.
Diminutive of Bernadetta as well as Italian form and German variant of Nadette.

An evil knight from Benoic (Benwick) who served King Claudas against Arthur.
Probably derived from Arabic نَظِيف (naẓīf) meaning "clean".

To be "pure", and "clean." Can be literal or figurative, taken as "pure of heart", or "clean minded".Possible relation to the arabic name Nazif.A more common spelling is Nadifa. The masculine form is most typically Nadif.
Georgian diminutive of Nadezhda and its derivatives Nadia 1 and Nado.
Means "compete, contend, fight, defend" in Arabic, from the root ناضل (nāḍala) meaning "to defend, to struggle".
Alternate transcription of Arabic ناضلة (see Nadila), as well as an Indonesian variant.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نديمة (see Nadima), as well as an Indonesian and Malay variant.
Derived from Croatian nada meaning ''hope'' and mir meaning ''peace''.
Derived from Uzbek nadim meaning "companion" and oy meaning "moon".
Hungarian borrowing of Nadine, reflecting the French pronunciation.
Slovene, Provençal and Gascon form of Nadine.
Diminutive of Nadin, used as a given name in its own right.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نادرة (see Nadira), as well as a Malay and Indonesian variant.

Combination of Nadir with the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".In Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan, this name is less common than the local forms of the name, which are Nadyrbek and Nodirbek respectively.
Derived from Serbian and Croatian nada "hope" combined with slava "glory".
Alternate transcription of Nadyusha, diminutive of Nadezhda.
Alternate transcription of Nadyushka, diminutive of Nadezhda, variant of Nadyusha/Nadiusha.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نادية (see Nadiyya).
Older spelling of Najamuddin influenced by Dutch orthography.

German form of Nadezhda. Also compare Nadeschda.

From Persian نازلی (nazli) meaning "delicate, beautiful, coy" and Bashkir һылыу (hïlïw) meaning "beautiful".
A knight defeated, with his cousin Daton, by Claris and Laris after he besieged Queen Blanche.
Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐธิดา (see Natthida).
Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐธิดา (see Natthida).

Variant of Na'ura, the Comanche name given to American woman Cynthia Ann Parker, who was kidnapped at the age of 9 or 10 in May 1836 by a Comanche war band, who massacred her family's settlement. She was adopted by the Comanche and lived with them for 24 years. She married a Comanche chieftain, Peta Nocona, and had three children with him, including the last free Comanche chief Quanah Parker.

According to some sources, a King of Syria during the Arthurian period. One of the allies of Emperor Thereus of Rome. Nadus joined Thereus in a war against Arthur, and he was slain in battle against Claris and Laris.
Feminine Indian name meaning "one covered with reeds".
Possibly derived from Zapotec nadxiie lii "I love you" (compare Nayeli).
Kyrgyz form of Nadirbek. A known bearer of this name is the Kyrgyz freestyle wrestler Ulan Nadyrbek Uulu (b. 1981).
Variant of Nadiyya or a short form of Nadežda.

Indonesian and Malay variant of Nazif.
Indonesian and Malay variant of Nazifa.
Indonesian and Malay variant of Nazira.

column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens", 津 (dzu) meaning "harbor" or 摘 (dzu) meaning "to pluck, to pick" combined with 名 (na) meaning "name" or 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Means "blonde hairs" in Tahitian. Contracted form of Tahitian nā ehu fānau maeha'a tapu nui meaning "most sacred blonde newborn twins".
Means "to rise, to go up, to climb" in Toba Batak.
From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens", 絵 (e) meaning "picture, painting, drawing, sketch" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Naëma Lösche (Maiden name: von Kahlden) - German writer, born Sept 27, 1854
A German and Nordic variant of Naomi 1. This name was used in the German translation of The Bible.

Created by George R.R. Martin for the character Naerys Targaryen, a historical figure, it is presumably of Valyrian origin but is most likely inspired by the Welsh elaboration of ner "lord, chief" thus changing the meaning to "lady, noblewoman."
Derived from the Germanic name elements nes "ness, spit of land" and bjǫrn "bear".
Old Swedish from of Næskunungr used up until the late medieval period.

Originally a byname meaning "king over a small area", from Old Norse nės "ness, promontory, spit of land" and konungr "king". The name appears on at least one runestone (as niskunukʀ) and was later used sparingly (as Næskonung) up until the late middle ages.
From Sino-Korean 娜 "elegant, graceful, delicate" and 恩 "kindness, mercy, charity".

Naeun(나은) means "better" in Korean. Also, from combination of 娜(na) meaning "elegant, graceful, delicate" or 奈(na) meaning "apple tree" with 恩(eun) "kindness, mercy, charity" or 殷(eun) meaning "abundant, flourishing". Other hanja combinations are possible.
Naeva Okasian of New Thinking Magazine is one bearer of this name.
Derived from nafas meaning "breath, breathing", also in culture meaning a breath which has healing powers, and oy meaning "moon".
Alternate transcription of Arabic نافذ (see Nafiz).
From Arabic نَافِع (nāfiʕ) meaning "useful, beneficial, wholesome".

Alternate transcription of Arabic نفيسة (see Nafisa), chiefly used in Northern Africa and other French-influenced regions of the continent.

Means "piercing, penetrating, effective" in Arabic, a derivative of نفذ (nafadha) meaning "to pierce, to penetrate, to pass through". As a Bengali name it is occasionally feminine, while it is solely masculine elsewhere.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نافذة (see Nafiza), as well as the usual Malay and Indonesian form.
Name meaning “longing” or “I miss you” in Amharic. It is used as a word as well as a name, and usually associated with deep feelings of connection to home or family.
Old Swedish and Old Danish form of Nafni.
Old Norse name and byname, from Old Norse nafni meaning "namesake" or from Old Norse nafn meaning "name".
Means "soul" in Arabic. It has common usage in Egypt and Iran.

Commonly used in Bangladesh and Indonesia, it means "myself" or "my soul" in Arabic. In Arabic it is not used as a name. In Swahili Nafsi is loosely translated to English as the soul, or sometimes it could mean conscience.
An antagonist from Rudyard Kipling's book, Rikki-Tikki-Tavi. Coincides with the English word "nag" meaning "to irritate".

column3: 長治, 長陽, 長春, 長晴, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 長 (naga) meaning "chief, head, leader, long" combined with 治 (haru) meaning "govern, regulate, administer". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Name that was given during the Hēan Period, to a Nobleman and Waka Poet, "藤原 長家" FUJIWARANONAGAIE. The Kanji Character "長" meaning "Long" with the Kanji Character "家" meaning "House".
An antagonist from the book "Rikki-Tikki-Tavi" (1978) by Rudyard Kipling. A Nagaina is also a type of spider.

column3: ながきよ(Japanese Hiragana)|永清, 長淳, 長清(Japanese Kanji)
column12: The name originates from Ogasawara Nagakiyo, the founder of the Ogasawara clan, who was a samurai warlord during the Heian period.
From Japanese 良 (naga) meaning "good" and 子 (ko) meaning "child", as well as other kanji combinations. This name was borne by Japanese empress Nagako, the wife of Emperor Hirohito.
Means "goddess of snakes", derived from Sanskrit नाग (naga) meaning "snake, serpent" combined with the name of the Hindu goddess Lakshmi.
Means "king of snakes" from Sanskrit नाग (nāgá) meaning "snake" combined with राज (rāja) meaning "king, chief, sovereign".
From Sanskrit नागराज (nāgarāja) meaning "king of snakes", derived from नाग (nāga) meaning "snake" and राज (rāja) meaning "king".
From 流 (nagare, nagaru, ryuu) meaning "flow, stream, current".A notable bearer is the TV personality and actor Nagare Hagiwara (1953-2015) who used this as his stage name.
Nāgārjuna was an Indian monk and Mahāyāna Buddhist philosopher of the Madhyamaka (Centrism, Middle Way) school. He is widely considered one of the most important Buddhist philosophers.
From 流 (nagaru, nagare, ryuu) meaning "stream, current, flow".A notable bearer is Nagaru Tanigawa, the author of 'The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya' series.
Nagaswamy means lord of the snakes

column3: 長敏, 長才, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 長 (naga) meaning "chief, head, leader" combined with 俊 (toshi) meaning "talented, handsome" or 利 (toshi, ri) meaning "benefit, advantage". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: ながつき(Japanese Hiragana)|長月, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column12: The “rescuer” a person who saves, rescues, or delivers. Arabic spelling: ناجد
Alternate transcription of Hindi नगीना or Urdu نگینہ (see Nagina).
The name Nagemi written in Kanji means "throwing oneself". With "投" meaning "to throw; discard" and "身" meaning "self; body."
From Sanskrit नागेश (nāgeśa) meaning "lord of snakes", derived from नाग (nāga) meaning "snake" and ईश (īśa) meaning "ruler, lord".
Alternate transcription of Arabic نجاة (see Najat), chiefly used in Northern Africa.
Related to Naqvi, and the singer from the band AND ONE.
Means "song, melody" in Urdu and Pashto, ultimately from Arabic نغمة (naghma).
Alternate transcription of Persian نغمه (see Naghmeh).
Means "melody, tone, sound" in Persian, ultimately derived from Arabic نغمة (naghmah).

column3: 凪咲, 凪江, 凪恵, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 凪 (nagi) meaning "calm" combined with 咲 (e) meaning "blossom", 江 (e) meaning "creek, bay" or 恵 (e) meaning "favour". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 奈木葉, 渚葉, 凪羽, 凪波, 凪葉, 薙刃, 薙葉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree", 木 (gi) meaning "tree, shrub" or 渚 (nagi) meaning "strand, beach, shore", 凪 (nagi) meaning "calm" or 薙 (nagi) meaning "weed" combined with 葉 (ha) meaning "leaf", 羽 (ha) meaning "feathers", 波 (ha) meaning "wave" or 刃 (ha) meaning "an edge, a blade". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 渚帆, 凪帆, 渚歩, 凪歩, 渚穂, 凪穂, 凪布, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 渚 (nagi) meaning "strand, beach, shore" or 凪 (nagi) meaning "calm" combined with 帆 (ho) meaning "sail", 歩 (ho) meaning "walk", 穂 (ho) meaning "grain" or 布 (ho) meaning "cloth, textiles". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 凪佳, 凪香, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 凪 (nagi) meaning "calm" combined with 佳 (ka) meaning "beautiful, good" or 香 (ka) meaning "fragrance". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 凪子, 渚子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 凪 (nagi) meaning "calm" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Possibly derived from the Hebrew phrase hava nagila (נָגִילָה) meaning "let us rejoice". It has been used in Brazil since at least the 1980s.
Means "gemstone, jewel" in Hindi and Urdu, ultimately from Persian نگین (negīn).

In mythology, the Nagas and Naginis are the respectively masculine and feminine serpent people of various Asian cultures. Descriptions of the Nagas vary from culture to culture; in some, they are depicted as giant black snakes, and in others they are said to bear the lower half of a serpent and the upper half of a human. In most traditions, the Nagas are evil beings.A popular bearer is Lord Voldemort's snake Nagini in the Harry Potter books by J.K. Rowling.

column3: 渚乃, 凪乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 凪 (nagi) meaning "calm" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 凪男, 渚男, 凪生, 凪郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 凪 (nagi) meaning "calm" combined with 男 (o) meaning "male" or 郎 (o) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 渚 (nagisa) meaning "beach, shore" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: なぎと(Japanese Hiragana)|ナギト(Japanese Katakana)|和士, 梛斗, 凪冬, 椛人, 渚音, 薙杜, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 渚 (nagi) meaning "strand, beach, shore" or 成 (na) meaning "turn into, become, get, grow, elapse, reach", 銀 (gi) meaning "silver" combined with 人 (to) meaning "person", 冬 (to) meaning "winter", 叶 (to) meaning "grant, answer", 斗 (to), which refers to a Chinese constellation, 杜 (to) meaning "woods, grove", 翔 (to) meaning "soar, fly", 音 (to) meaning "sound", 十 (to) meaning "ten", 仁 (to) meaning "humanity, virtue, benevolence, charity, man, kernel" or 士 (to) meaning "samurai". Other kanji combinations are also possible.

Means "ship of the dead", derived from nagl ("dead person") and far ("ship; passage on a ship"). In Norse mythology this is the name of a ship helmed by Hymir (or Loki, depending on the text), which will put to sea at Ragnarǫk and take the inhabitants of Múpellsheimr to fight the gods. It is built from the nails of the dead.
Combination of nagl ("dead person") and fara ("to move, to travel"). In Norse mythology this is the name of Nótt's first husband, with whom she had two sons, both named Auðr.

From Lithuanian legends about Neringa and Naglis.In Lithuanian folklore, Neringa is a beautiful, gentle giantess who built a mound of sand to keep the stormy waves of the Baltic sea at bay and protect the village and the people who live in it. One day, she catches the eye of Naglis, a dragon (some legends call him a sea serpent) living nearby, who madly falls in love with her. When Naglis realizes that his love is unrequited, in his wrath and his grief, he starts eating the fishermen living in Neringa's village one by one. Neringa is greatly saddened by these occurences, and so she creates a strip of sand between the bay and the Baltic sea, which would seperate her and her subjects from the dragon forever.Its designated name day is August 13.
In the epic poem Padmavat, Nagmati is the identifed as the first wife and chief queen of King Ratan Sen. This is also the name of a river the state of Gujarat in India.
Means "tune, melody, singing voice" in Turkish.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نجم الدين‎ (see Najm Ad-Din). This spelling is chiefly used in Sudan.

column3: 和, 和美, 和実, 和心, 和水, 和海, 和笑, 菜香美, 奈心美, 菜瑚美, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|なご美(Kanji/Hiragana)|なごみ(Japanese Hiragana)|ナゴミ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 和み (nagomi), referring to a feeling of calmness and relaxation (compare Nagomu).It can also be suffixed with a kanji that can be (partially) read as mi, such as 美 meaning "beauty," 実 meaning "seed; fruit," 心 meaning "heart, mind," 水 meaning "water," 海 meaning "sea, ocean" or 笑 meaning "smile." For the first element, it can be split into kanji, a na kanji, like 奈 or 菜 meaning "greens," combined with a kanji that can be voiced to go, such as 心, 香 meaning "fragrance" or 瑚, part of Sango.

column3: 和, 和夢, 和武, 和歩, 和睦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|なごむ(Japanese Hiragana)|ナゴム(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From the verb 和む (nagomu) meaning "to be softened, calm down​" (compare Nagomi).It can also be suffixed with a kanji that can be (partially) read as mu, such as 夢 meaning "dream," 武 meaning "valour, bravery," 歩, from the verb 歩む (ayumu) meaning "to walk; to advance along, follow someone’s footsteps," or 睦 meaning "intimate, friendly, harmonious."
Alternate transcription of Kannada ನಾಗರಾಜ or Telugu నాగరాజ (see Nagaraja), as well as the Marathi form.

column3: 나경(Korean Hangul)|娜景, 娜敬, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 娜 (na) meaning "elegant, graceful, delicate" combined with 景 (gyeong) meaning "scenery, view" or 敬 (gyeong) meaning "respect, honour". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
This means "To be charmed, to be fascinated" in Tagalog. Related to Mahalina.

From the Hebrew verb נָחַם (nacham) meaning "to comfort". This name occurs in a biblical passage where it is unclear whether the bearer of the name is male or female, although most scholars agree that this person was likely male.
MEANING : binding, tying round, fetter, bolt, bondUsage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhalese, Kannada, Marathi, Gujarati, Malayalam, Hindi, Indian (Sikh ), Buddhist, Assamese
From Japanese 愛 (na) meaning "love, affection" and 花 (hana) meaning "flower". Other kanji combinations are possible. This name can be spelled as Young-Ae in Korean.

an Athabaskan word used to designate First Nations groups located in British Columbia, the Northwest Territories and Yukon between the upper Liard River and the 64th parallel north latitude. Nahane translates as "people of the west."

From naha, meaning "river of the land of the Naha people" in Na-Dene (Athabaskan) languages, spoken by indigenous cultures in British Columbia, the Northwest Territories, and the Yukon Territory. A prominent bearer of this name is Canadian politician Nahanni Fontaine. Additionally, the name's cultural significance is reflected in Canada through landmarks like Nahanni National Park Reserve and the South Nahanni River.
From Saka *Nahapāna meaning "protector of the clan". Name borne by a Western Satrap who reigned in either the first or second century CE.
From the Arabic نَهَار (nahār) meaning "day, daytime".
Variant transcription of Naharai.This transcription is used in the Revised Standard Version of the Bible.

The name comes from נחר (nhr), meaning "to snort vigorously". It comes from the root חרר (harar), meaning "heat source". It also comes from נחר (nahar), which describes a horse's snorting noise.In the Bible, Naharai the Berothite is one of David's warriors. He is also the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah. He is only mentioned once in the Bible, in 1 Chronicles 11:39.

Means "snake" in Hebrew, from the vocabulary noun נָחָשׁ (nachash or nāḥāš).This name also nearly coincides with - and, without niqqudot (diacritical vowel markings), is indeed identical to - the Hebrew vocabulary noun נַחַשׁ (nachash or náḥaš) "magic, spell, enchantment".

MEANING : putting on, crotchet, fetter, bond, girding roundUsage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhalese, Hindi, Sikh, Buddhist, , Mauritian, Fijian, Marathi, Malayalam, Assamese , Bengali, Kannada
Means "lake", deriving from the Classic Maya element nab ("lake, pool").
Nahbi, the son of Vophsi of the house of Naphtali, was a scout sent to Canaan prior to the crossing of the Jordan River according to Numbers 13:14.
From 나 (na) meaning "I, me" and 희 (hui) meaning "happiness".
Na means "elegant, graceful, delicate" and Hee means "joy,brightness and bliss"
Means "twin crowns"; a combination of Tahitian na denoting duplicates or twins and hei meaning "crown".
Means "rising, getting up" in Arabic, from the root ناهض (nahaḍa) meaning "to rise".
Means "the red-hot raging fires" from Hawaiian nā, "the (plural)", ahi, "fire", and 'ena'ena, "red-hot". This was the name of a 19th-century Hawaiian princess, the daughter of Kamehameha I.
Variant of Nahia derived from Basque nahikari "wish; desire; sympathy, affection; pleasure".
Variant transcription of Najla or Naila.
Derived from the Dakota Sioux word nahmana meaning "secret".
Variant of Naime, ultimately a form of Na'ima. It is also often used as a surname.

Possibly derived from Arabic نَيِّر (nayyir) meaning "luminous, bright" (related to نور (nūr) "light"), or perhaps from نَهْر (nahr) "river" or نهار (nahār) "day, daytime".A known (female) bearer of this name is Nahir Mariana Galarza (1998-), a first-year law student at the University of Concepción del Uruguay who was convicted of the murder of her partner, Fernando Pastorizzo, becoming the youngest woman to have been sentenced to life imprisonment in Argentina.
Means "Bear Trail, Bear Road" in Cheyenne.
Means "Little Bear, Bear Cub" in Cheyenne.
Means "One Bear, Lone Bear" in Cheyenne.
Means "Bear Stands Last, Last Bear Standing" in Cheyenne.
Means "Bear Stands in the Shade" in Cheyenne.

column3: 直帆, 南穂, 菜保, 奈歩, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "veggies, greens" combined with 帆 (ho) meaning "sailboat". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer is Naho Toda, a Japanese actress.

column3: なほこ(Japanese Hiragana)|ナホコ(Japanese Katakana)|菜穂子, 奈保子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens", 穂 (ho) meaning "grain" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible. Sometimes Naoko is transcribed this way.

column3: 菜穂美, 奈穂美, 南保実, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 菜 (na) meaning "veggies, green", 穂 (ho) meaning "grain", and 美 (mi) meaning "beauty, beautiful". Other kanji combinations can be used.
From the 15th-century Korean 날애(Nal-E), itself derived from the Traditional Korean 날개(Nal-Ge) meaning "Wing" from Korean 날(Nal) meaning 'fly' combined with suffix -개(Ge) meaning 'tool'.
Transferred use of the surname Nahri.
From Egyptian jr.t-ḥr-r-r.w meaning "the eye of Horus is against them".

From Ancient Hebrew נַחְשׁוֹן (naḥšôn) meaning "enchanter, diviner", itself from the word נָחַשׁ (nāḥaš) meaning "to whisper, to enchant".Nahshon appears in the Bible as the brother-in-law of Aaron, and the prince of the tribe of Judah, who was the first Jew to enter the Red Sea before the split of the waters (Exodus 6:23) which, according to a Jewish Midrash, he did by walking in head-deep until the sea split. He was the son of Amminadab; descendant in the fifth generation of Judah. Nahshon's grandson Boaz married Ruth of Moab, and their son Obed became the grandfather of David.In modern times it has seen some popularity among African Americans, likely influenced by the name Nashawn.
Means "four reed" in Nahuatl, from nahui "four" and acatl "reed, cane".

Probably means "to emerge from trickery" or "to be born from magic", derived from Nahuatl nahual "to transform, trick, disguise, conceal; to do magic" combined with quizqui "to divide, separate from, take out of".
Means "clear sound" in Nahuatl, also referring to the language.

column3: 나희(Korean Hangul)|娜姬, 娜熙, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 娜 (na) meaning "elegant, graceful, delicate" combined with 姬 (hui) meaning "beauty" or 熙 (hui) meaning "bright, splendid, glorious". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
Means "four rabbit" in Nahuatl, referring to the day of the Aztec calendar that the bearer was born.

In the Elamite pantheon, Nahundi was the god of the sun, but also the god of justice and law. His name - spelled Nahiti in earlier times - was apparently the same as the word for 'sun' in Elamite, although the literal meaning of that word is said to be "creator of the day". At least ten Elamite kings were named in his honour (which is consistent with the fact that nearly all rulers of Elam bore theophoric names).
From Sino-Vietnamese 奈 (nại) meaning "to endure, to bear".

column3: 菜衣, 奈衣, 那衣(Japanese Kanji)|ない(Japanese Hiragana)|ナイ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens", 奈 (na) a phonetic character that also has an obsolete meaning of "apple tree", and 那 (na) meaning "many", combined with 衣 (i) meaning "clothing". Other kanji combinations are possible.It can also come from ない (nai) meaning "absent".

column3: 菜以亜, 奈以亜, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens" or 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree", 以 (i) meaning "compared to" combined with 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Per the legend, an indigenous tribe believed that the moon was the goddess Jaci, who came at night and kissed and lit up the faces of the most beautiful virgins in the village. When the moon hid behind the mountain, she would take girls with her and turn them into stars.A beautiful virgin named Naiá dreamed of becoming a star, despite warnings that girls taken by Jaci lost their blood and flesh in becoming stars. Naiá roamed the mountains seeking out the moon each night, so obsessed she did not sleep or eat. While resting on the edge of the lake, she saw the moon's reflection on the water, and desperately seeking the goddess, dove into the water and drowned. To reward her for this sacrifice, Jaci turned her into a star different from all the others, the "star of the waters", which is the giant water lily (Victoria Amazonia) plant.A number of versions of the legend exist, based on a girl attempting to unite with the moon.

Possibly based on Naiara.This name was popularised in Spain and, to some extent, Latin America in 2006 and 2007 by Naiala Melo, a Brazilian-born contestant and winner of the 8th season of 'Gran Hermano', the Spanish version of the 'Big Brother' franchise.

From Chinese 耐 (nài) meaning "to be able to endure" combined with 庵 (ān) meaning "round thatched hut". Other hanzi combinations are possible. A notable bearer was writer Shi Nai'an (1296–1372), author of Shuihu zhuan (Water Margin).
From Arabic نائب (na'ib) meaning "representative, delegate, deputy".
From nai bili referring to a type of raft.

column3: 内部介, 内部輔(Japanese Kanji)|ないぶすけ(Japanese Hiragana)|ナイブスケ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 内部 (naibu) meaning "internal" and 輔 (suke) meaning "help, assist, support". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Possibly derived from Mongolian найдах (naidakh) meaning "to hope, trust, rely on".
Variant form of Najla or Naila.
Of unknown origin and meaning.The popularity of the name was boosted by the daughter of the actress Ornella Muti, Naike Rivelli born in 1974.

column3: 乃妃, 乃樹, 乃輝, 乃騎, 夢希, 奈息, 流暉, 那行, 夏生, 菜生, 成寿, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 乃 (nai), a possessive particle, 夢 (nai) meaning "dream", 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree", 流 (nai) meaning "current, a sink, flow, forfeit", 那 (na) meaning "what", 夏 (na) meaning "summer", 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens" or 成 (nai) meaning "turn into, become, get, grow, elapse, reach" combined with 妃 (ki) meaning "queen, princess", 樹 (ki) meaning "tree", 輝 (ki) meaning "radiance, shine, sparkle, gleam, twinkle", 騎 (ki) meaning "equestrian, riding on horses", 希 (ki) meaning "hope, beg, request, rare", 息 (iki) meaning "breath, respiration, son, interest (on money)", 暉 (ki) meaning "shine, light", 行 (iki) meaning "going, journey, carry out, conduct, act, line, row, bank", 生 (iki) meaning "life, genuine, birth" or 寿 (ki) meaning "longevity, congratulations, one's natural life". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Bashkir and Tatar form of Naila.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نائلة (see Naila), as well as an Indonesian and Malay variant.
Of uncertain meaning, this was the personal name of a consort of Digunai, the fourth emperor of the Jin dynasty.
Meaning unknown, perhaps an elaborated form of Naila. This name is borne by Mexican actress Nailea Norvind (1970-).

From Chinese 乃 (nǎi) meaning "to be" combined with 亮 (liàng) meaning "bright, radiant, light" or 良 (liáng) meaning "good, virtuous, respectable". Other combinations of hanzi can form this name as well.
Possibly a rhyming variant of Mailson or Ailson.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نعيمة (see Naima), as well as the usual Malay and Indonesian form.
Modern female name used among Pakistanis.
Derived from найм (naim) meaning "eight", зуун (zuun) meaning "hundred", нандин (nandin) meaning "precious, sacred" and цэцэг (tsetseg) meaning "flower(s)".

Means "eight hundred precious flowers" in Mongolian, from найм (naim) meaning "eight", зуун (zuun) meaning "hundred", нандин (nandin) meaning "precious, rare, sacred" and цэцэг (tsetseg) meaning "flower".
Chechen and Dagestani form of Na'ima

Probably a contraction of non aimé, meaning "unloved" in French. This is the name of a character in the French fairy tale "The Fortunate Punishment" by Henriette-Julie de Murat. Naimée is a princess cursed to be hated by all that see her, while her sister Aimée is blessed to be loved by all. The two sisters travel a river to reach the Prince of the Pleasant Island, whom both are in love with. As the prince falls in love with Aimée, Naimée drowns herself in the river.
Meaning unknown. It is borne by Irish singer Naimee Coleman (1976-).
From naim meaning "tranquil, happy, at ease" and jon meaning "soul, life"
From the dwarves of the same name from The Lord of the Rings, which in turn derive from the name of a dwarf in the Dvergatal (whose name means 'corpselike').
Means "pleasantness" or "beauty" in Hebrew, from the verb נעם (naem), meaning "to be pleasant".

This name is derived from Sanskrit and means "Lord of the Eyes" or "the one with beautiful eyes". It is primarily a masculine name used in Indian communities. In Hindu mythology, the name signifies beauty, grace, and is romantically linked to eyes, considered windows to the soul. Nainesh symbolizes the beauty of the eyes and is often connected to deities associated with beauty and grace. The name is popular among Hindus and is often considered auspicious due to its positive connotations related to vision and perception.
One with beautiful eyes Lord Krishna.
Comes from Sanskrit and means "the one with the beautiful eyes".
Derived from nā ("dead person"). This is the name of a dwarf in Norse mythology.

Originally given as the third name of a child who was named after two relatives or friends, meaning "the namesakes" from the Hawaiian plural definite article, nā, with inoa "name". It was popular in Hawaii from 2000-2005.
Meaning uncertain, perhaps an altered form of Nairoby. This name was used by Puerto Rican singer Ivy Queen (real name Martha Ivelisse Pesante Rodríguez) for her daughter born 2013.
Means "we will light up" in Hebrew, making it relative to Yair.
Derived from the Surselvan Romansh word nair (ner in other Romansh variants) "black; dark".
Means "she who has no self", an embodiment of the Buddhist philosophical concept of anātman.
Transferred use of the surname Nairn.
Feminine Scottish name that means "dwells at the alder tree river." It is closely related to the name Nairn, which comes from a geographical region and river in northern Scotland.
Derived from the Burgh of Nairn in Northern Scotland. The place name is taken from the name of a river.

column3: 奈彩, 七彩, 夏色, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree" combined with 彩 (iro) meaning "colour". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Variant of Nairobi. A known bearer of this name is Dominican badminton player Nairoby Abigail Jiménez (2000-).
French form of Nais. Naïs is the main character of Jean-Philippe Rameau's 1749 Naïs: Opéra pour La Paix, a play about the god Neptune falling in love with the titular nymph.
Nais was a naiad-nymph of the springs of the town of Pyrrhichus on the Malean peninsular of Lakedaimonia (southern Greece). She was the wife of the old rustic-god Silenus.

column3: 乃斗, 夏愛, 夜斗, 夜, 夜智, 夜月, 夢翔, 奈生人, 星斗, 那依十, 騎士, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column12: Naiton (Naiton in Bede) II.E. Pict mentioned in the Ulster annals -8th c.
Naïvane means: the one I gave in Kikongo
From Chinese 乃 (nǎi) meaning "to be, then, really, indeed" combined with 彦 (yàn) meaning "elegant, handsome, learned". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Means "eye" (a poetic word) in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit नयन (nayana).
From Chinese 乃 (nǎi) meaning "to be, then, really, indeed" combined with 正 (zhèng) meaning "right, proper, correct". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Nickname for Anastazija, Danaja and names starting with na, for example Naida, Natalija, etc.
Means "little Naja", derived from the popular Greenlandic name Naja combined with the diminutive suffix araq.
Dutch form of Naiad. Naiads were characters in Greek mythology, more commonly known as the nymphs of flowing water.
From the name of the city of Najaf in Iraq.
Means "a boy's new little sister" in Greenlandic.
Greenlandic name meaning "a brother's new sweet little sister", combined with Najagtâĸ and -nnguaq "sweet, dear".
Greenlandic name with the combination of Naja and affix -aaja is a Greenlandic affix used for and by children.
Greenlandic name meaning "a boy's sweet little sister". Combination of Naja and suffix -nnguaq "sweet, dear".
Combination of Naja, meaning "little sister (to a boy)" and nnguaq, a suffix meaning "sweet" or "dear."

Toponym of medieval origin, linked to repopulation of the lands of Segovia in the 11th century, that describes a gentle descent in a sector of the Guadarrama mountains in the area called the “Espaldar of the Najarra" (massif and peak) in Madrid province, Spain.
Alternate trancseiption of نجاة (see Najat) chiefly used in Northern Africa.
Means "bravery, courage in battle" in Arabic.
Variant of Naji. A known bearer is American jazz saxophonist and flautist Jerome Najee Rasheed (1957-), known professionally as Najee.
of noble birth, born into royalty, excellent

Urdu form of Najibullah as well as an Arabic variant transcription of the name.Known bearers of this name include the Pakistani actor Najeebullah Anjum (b. 1955) and the Pakistani politician Najeebullah Khan Niazi (1964-2014).
Means "brilliance of the faith, radiance of religion", derived from Arabic نَجْم (najm) "star, luminary" and دين (din) "religion, faith".
Alternate transcription of Arabic ناجح (see Najih).
Alternate transcription of Arabic نجاة (see Najat), chiefly used in Northern Africa
Alternate transcription of Arabic نجيبة (see Najiba), as well as a Malay and Indonesian variant.
Tajik and Uzbek form of Najibullah.
Means "successful, prosperous, fortunate" in Arabic, from the root نجح (najaḥa) meaning "to suceed".
Alternate transcription of Arabic ناجحة (see Najiha), as well as a Malay variant.
The name Najila is a girl's name of Arabic origin meaning "bright eyes". Pretty and feminine Arabic name.
When written as نجيم this name is a variant of Najm, and when written as نجم it is merely an alternate transcription of the name.
When written as نجيمة this name is a variant of Najma, and when written as نجمة it is merely an alternate transcription of the name.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نجلاء (see Najla).
Alternate transcription of Arabic نجلاء (see Najla) chiefly used in Morocco.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نجلاء (see Najla), as well as an Indonesian variant.
Arabic alternate transcription of Najma as well as the Indonesian and Maranao form.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نجم الدين‎ (see Najm Ad-Din).
Alternate transcription of Persian نجمه (see Najmeh).
Alternate transcription of Arabic نجم الدين‎ (see Najm Ad-Din), as well as the Persian form.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نجم الدين‎ (see Najm Ad-Din) chiefly used in North Africa.
Means "astral, celestial, star-like" in Arabic, from the word نجم (najm) meaning "star".
Uzbek and Tajik form of Najm Ad-Din.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نجم الدين‎ (see Najm Ad-Din), as well as the Dari Persian and Malay form.
Indonesian and Malay form of Najm Ad-Din.
First part of compound Arabic names beginning with نجم ال (Najm al) meaning "star of the" (such as نجم الدين (Najm al-Dīn) meaning "star of the faith").
Derived from najot meaning "salvation" and bibi meaning "learned woman".
Alternate transcription of Bengali নজরুল ইসলাম (see Nazrul Islam).

column3: 娜准(Japanese Kanji)|なじゅん(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From Chinese 娜 (nà) meaning "elegant, graceful, delicate" combined with 准 (jun) meaning "to allow; to grant; to permit". This name can also be formed from other character combinations.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نجوى (see Najwa), as well as the Indonesian and Malay form.
A creator-deity of the Sonjo people of Tanzania.

column3: 央, 半, 中(Japanese Kanji)|なかば(Japanese Hiragana)|ナカバ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 半ば (nakaba) meaning "middle, half."Other kanji that can be used for this name which have the same general meaning of "middle" include 央 and 中.This name is rarely used.
From the Hawaiian nā meaning "quieted, pacified" or "the (plural)" and kai meaning "sea(s)".
Elaboration of Nākai influenced by Nikaia.

column3: 菜花子, 菜華子, 菜香子, 菜日子, 七香子, 心子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens", 七 (na) meaning "seven" or 心 (naka) meaning "heart, mind, soul", 花 (ka) or 華 (ka) which both mean "flower", 香 (ka) meaning "fragrance" or 日 (ka) meaning "day, sun, Japan" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means "gift from God" in Mizo and Manipuri.
Nakani is an african name meaning take care
Combination of the phonetic elements na, kay and la or possibly based on Mikayla.
Variant of Nakeisha, It can be combined with some names ending in Tha
Means "cherries" in Hawaiian, from keli "cherry". Possibly Hawaiian form of Natalie.
Combination of the name prefix Na and the name Kendra.
Means "great city, governor, city lord". From Thai นคร (nakhon) meaning "city, town, municipality" and อินทร์ (in) referring to the Hindu god Indra.
Plural form of Nakhlah, means "date palm," but it also means "something that is purified."
Means "city, large town" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit नगर (nagara).
From Thai นคร (nakhon) meaning "city, town" and ชัย (chai) meaning "victory".

From Egyptian nḫt meaning "victorious, strong" or "champion". Nakht was an ancient Egyptian official who held the position of a scribe and astronomer of Amun, probably during the reign of Thutmose IV of the Eighteenth Dynasty.
Meaning “strength of Mut”, Mut being the mother goddess in Ancient Egyptian religion and mythology. Name of a daughter of Djehutyemheb and Bak-Khonsu, found in the Theban Tomb TT45.
The name of an early Ancient Egyptian Queen Consort, which means "strong is Neith".
A name with orgigins in Egypt, Nakhtre means "Strength of Ra". Ra was the god of the sun in Ancient Egyptian Mythology.
the first born girl in the family

Briefly charted on American popularity lists due to the short-lived television police drama series 'Nakia' (1974), which starred Robert Forster as a Navajo deputy sheriff. Since then, it has been used as an African-American name (both femenine and masculine), interpreted as a combination of the phonetic elements na, kee and ya
Etymology unknown. This was the name of the mother of Suleiman I of Persia.
From Japanese 那 (na) meaning "what", 木 (ki) meaning "tree" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.
Nakili is a character From Miskito mythology, who appears in a Miskito folktale. His/her name has no known meaning.
Means "denier" in Arabic, from أنكر (ʾankara) meaning "to deny". In Islamic belief this is the name of one of two angels (the other being Munkar) who test the faith of the dead.
Combination of the phonetic prefix na and the name Kira 2, possibly based on the sounds found in names such as Shakira and Nakia.
Short form of diminutives such as Antonakis and Stefanakis.

column3: 泣沢女, 啼沢女, 哭沢女(Japanese Kanji)
column12: The name of the Japanese goddess of spring water. Her name is derived from 泣 (naki) meaning "to weep", 啼 (naki) meaning "to wail, cry" or 哭 (naki) meaning "to cry, wail", 沢 (sawa) meaning "mountain stream, swamp, marsh" and 女 (me) meaning "woman".
Meaning “the beautifier; one who makes things beautiful”.
Possibly an English variant form of the Russian masculine name Nikita 1, which is commonly confused for a feminine name in English-speaking countries.

column3: ნაკო(Georgian)|菜子, 南子, 那子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Diminutive of feminine names that start with Na-, such as Naira and Nana 3.
Means "the warriors," from plural definite article nā and koa meaning "soldier, warrior, fighter."

Meaning unknown, likely from the Ioway language. A notable bearer was the Ioway woman Nakoma, the wife of 19th-century fur trader Peter Abadie Sarpy. Other usages in popular culture include a male character in the TV series 'The Life and Times of Grizzly Adams' and a supporting character in the animated film 'Pocahontas'.It has been claimed to mean "I do as I promise" or "we will stand together" in Ojibwe, but this is untrue.
Possibly an invented name inspired by Nakota and Nākoa, or from nā kona meaning "leeward winds" in Hawaiian. "Kaulana Nā Kona" is a Hawaiian folk song.
Alternate transcription of Thai นคร (see Nakhon).
From the name of the Indigenous Nakota peoples.

column3: 奈琴, 納言, 名琴, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree" combined with 琴 (koto), which refers to a type of musical instrument similar to a harp. Other kanji combinations are possible.
Of uncertain origin, perhaps a transferred use of the Bulgarian surname Nakova. This was used by American social media influencer Myka Stauffer for her daughter born 2011.
Nakri is the name of a flower.-Nakri has been used to name 5 tropical cyclones
Alternate transcription of Thai นักรบ (see Nakrop).

Means "star, heavenly body" in Sanskrit. In Hindu and Buddhist astronomy this is the name for a lunar mansion (a part of the ecliptic plane that the moon passes as it orbits the Earth). As a given name, this transcription represents both the masculine form नक्षत्रा and the feminine form नक्षत्रा.
From Ottoman Turkish نقش (nakş) meaning "painting, embroidery" (of Arabic origin) and دل (dil) meaning "heart" (of Persian origin).
From the Arabic نَقْشية (naqşîye(t)) meaning "pictorial, related to pictures, like a picture".

Means "mongoose" in Sanskrit, also referring to the particular colour of this animal. In the Hindu epic the Mahabharata Nakula is the fourth of the five Pandavas, the sons of Pandu. He is the twin brother is Sahadeva and is a renowned swordsman and horsekeeper. This is also an epithet of the Hindu god Shiva.
A Mi'kmaq goddess of the Sun, currently a famous bearer is the Mi'kmaq actress, Nakuset "Nikki" Gould.
Means "unwanted" in Marathi. This was traditionally given to girls whose parents wanted a boy.This name's usage has become controversial in recent years.
Combination of the phonetic element na with ka and ya o ky and a.
“Prosperity” , a Sesotho name used in the motto of Lesotho
Means "born on a Sunday" in Hausa.
A variant of Nalaya, which is likely a combination of phoenetic elements.

The name comes directly from the Arabic naal (shoe), nalain being the plural form. In predominately Muslim Southeast Asian countries, it is used on both males and females in honor of the mubarak nalain or nalain pak (blessed Sandals) of the prophet Muhammad. The symbol of the Prophet Muhammads sandals are commonly hung and walls or worn as a talisman as a good luck charm.
Derived from Sanskrit नाल (nāla) meaning "reed, lotus stalk". In Buddhist tradition this is the name of a disciple of the Buddha.
Derived from Persian نالان (nālān) meaning "lamenting, groaning, sighing".
From Persian نالان (nalan) meaning "complaining, groaning" and دل (dil) meaning "heart".
Of uncertain etymology, this was the personal name of Consort Yi, a consort of the Kangxi emperor.
Combination of the phonetic elements na, lay and ya, possibly based on names such as Alayah, Nala 2 and Anaya. Also compare Kalayah, Jalayah and Malayah.
Either means "happy ruler" or derived from Persian نعل (na'l) meaning "horseshoe" (of Arabic origin) combined with the Ottoman Turkish title بك (beg) meaning "chief, lord, master".
Borne by Lady Alexandra Naldera Curzon (1904-1995), daughter of the viceroy of India. It is derived from the name of Naldehra near Shimla, India, where she was conceived.

Combination of Nancy and Leigh. This name was used by actress Katherine Heigl and her husband Josh Kelley for their daughter, who was born in 2008. Her full name is Nancy Leigh Kelley, Naleigh is her nickname.
Possibly a male version of Nál, or derived from nagl ("dead person"). In Norse mythology this is the name of a dwarf, who may originally have been a demon of the dead.
A figure in 'The Dreaming' by Barbara Wood. The name is taken from an Australian Aboriginal language and means 'butterfly'.

column3: නලින්(Sinhala)|নলিন(Bengali)|नलिन(Hindi)|นลิน(Thai)|娜林, 娜琳, 娜凛, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Derived from Sanskrit नलिनी (nalini) meaning "lotus". It is a masculine name in Sri Lanka and India while it is unisex in Thailand.
An invented name, based on the sound of Aaliyah.
Of uncertain origin and meaning. This is the name of one of the characters in J. R. Ward's ongoing series of paranormal romance books Black Dagger Brotherhood.
Means "teddy bear" in Finnish and Swedish. Often used as a nickname for Björn. The fictional teddy bear Winnie-the-Pooh is called Nalle Puh in both Finland and Sweden.
Means "the fierce one" in Lozi, a Zambian language.
From the Chinese 娜 (nà) meaning "elegant, graceful" and 罗 (luó) meaning "gauze".
Name of a Catholic saint from Auvergne, France. According to Catholic tradition, she founded various abbeys along with her husband saint Calminius. After his death, she became a nun.
Sanskrit word which forms an element of sacred Vedic mantras. It means “to surrender with love”, and literally, “to bow (in a gesture of homage and respect)”.

Means "the eyes" in Hawaiian from nā "the (plural)" and maka "eye". In Hawaiian mythology, Nāmaka was a sea goddess, the daughter of Haumea, and the sister of Pele and Hiʻiaka. In 2005, a moon of the dwarf planet Haumea was discovered and later named Namaka (without the macron).
From nā mālie meaning "the peaceful" or "the tranquil" in plural form.
The meaning behind the name Namam is a small tree or a sapling;saplingˈsaplɪŋ/Submitnounplural noun: saplings1.a young tree, especially one with a slender trunk.2.a greyhound in its first year.
Meaning "God" in Tupí, this name is popular in North-Eastern Argentina, Paraguay and Brazil.
Combination of the sounds found in names such as Jamari, Amari and Kamari.
Combination of Ana and Maria, often used as a nickname.
Namatai means "Pray or praise and worship God".
Name of a King of Persis
Wife to the first man in Buganda Kingdom in Uganda, who is also believed to be the first living person
Means "to savour, to enjoy" in Xhosa, encouraging the child to savour life.
From Sino-Korean 南天 (nam-cheon) meaning "nandina", which consists of 南 (nam) meaning "south" and 天 (cheon) meaning "heaven, sky".
From the Garo word নম্ (nam) meaning "good" and চি (chi) meaning "water".
East Prussian German form of Naomi 1.
The name originates from a Semigallian chieftain in the 13th century of the same name.
Means "be of good cheer" in Setswana.

column3: น้ำฝน(Thai)|ນ້ໍາຝົນ(Lao)
column12: Means "rain water, precipitation" in Thai and Lao.
Alternate transcription of Tibetan རྣམ་རྒྱས (see Namgay).
From Tibetan རྣམ་རྒྱལ (rnam-rgyal) meaning "complete victory", derived from the intensifier རྣམ (rnam) and རྒྱལ (rgyal) meaning "conquest, victory".
Alternate transcription of Tibetan རྣམ་རྒྱས (see Namgay).
Alternate transcription of Tibetan རྣམ་རྒྱལ (see Namgyal).

column3: 남규(Korean Hangul)|南奎, 南圭, 南珪, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 南 (nam) meaning "south" combined with 奎 (gyu) meaning "star; sentence, writing; stride," 圭 (gyu) or 珪 (gyu), both meaning "auspicious jewel; hall,".

column3: 남혁(Korean Hangul)|南赫, 南奕, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 南 (nam) meaning "south" combined with 赫 (hyeok) meaning "bright" or 奕 (hyeok) meaning "in sequence, orderly". Other hanja combinations are possible.
Derived from the Georgian noun ნამი (nami) meaning "dew", which ultimately comes from Persian نم (nam) meaning "dew, moisture".
From Japanese 波 (nami) meaning "wave" combined with 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: なみえ(Japanese Hiragana)|波絵, 奈美恵, 汝美絵, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 波 (nami) meaning "wave" combined with 絵 (e) meaning "sketch, picture, etch, painting". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means "writer, printer, clerk" in Turkish, ultimately from Arabic نامق (nāmiq).
Namıka is a Turkish word meaning "printer, writer".
Non-Turkish spelling of Namıka.Namika is the stage name of the Moroccan-German singer Hanan Hamdi.

column3: なみこ(Japanese Hiragana)|七実子, 汝美子, 那実子, 波子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 波 (nami) meaning "wave", or 奈/那 (na) meaning "what" or 七 (na) meaning "seven" combined with 実 (mi) meaning "reality, truth, seed, fruit, nut", and 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Sino-Korean 南 (nam) meaning "south" combined with 一 (il) meaning "one". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From Japanese 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree" combined with 実 (mi) meaning "seed; fruit; nut" duplicated. Other kanji combinations are possible as well.
From the video game 'Kingdom Hearts'.The name contains the Japanese word なみ (Katakana ナミ, nami) "wave".

column3: 奈美乃, 奈稔, 波乃, 波望, 波野, 方乃, 凡乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree", 波 (nami) meaning "wave", 方 (nami) meaning "direction, way, side" or 凡 (nami) meaning "ordinary, common, mediocre", 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful" combined with 稔 (mino) meaning "ripe grain, harvest", 乃 (no), a possessive particle, 望 (no) meaning "hope" or 野 (no) meaning "area, field". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 南男, 南夫, 南雄, 波男, 波夫, 波雄, 浪男, 浪夫, 浪雄, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 南 (nami) meaning "south" or 波, 浪 (nami) meaning "wave" combined with 男 (o) meaning "male", 夫 (o) meaning "man, husband" or 雄 (o) meaning "hero, manly". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Namish is a masculine name of Indian (Hindu) origin, often associated with, or a variation of, the name Nimish. It primarily signifies "Lord of the mind," "charming," or "twinkling of an eye" (linked to, though distinct from, the Sanskrit-based meaning of Nimish or Maneesh). It is commonly used in various regions of India
Possibly means "little spouse", from Nahuatl namictli "wife, husband, spouse" and the diminutive suffix -ton, in which case it was likely a nickname for a child.

column3: 波世, 奈美代, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 波 (nami) meaning "wave" combined with 代 (yo) meaning "generation, era" or 世 (yo) meaning "world". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 波三, 浪三, 浪蔵, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 波, 浪 (name) meaning "wave" combined with 三 (zou) meaning "three" or 蔵 (zou) meaning "store, hide". Other kanji combinations are possible.
A famous bearier of this name is Nam-joo from the South Korean girl group Apink.
From Sino-Korean 南 "south" and 珠 "precious stone, gem, jewel, pearl".

From Sino-Korean 南 (nam) meaning "south" and 俊 (jun) meaning "talented, capable; handsome" or 準 (jun) meaning "follow, conform," as well as other hanja combinations.Bearers of this name include rapper and leader of the boy group BTS, RM, born Kim Nam-joon (1994-), and Korean-American artist Nam June Paik (1932-2006).

From Sino-Vietnamese 南柯 (nam kha) literally meaning "south-facing branch", figuratively "dreamland" or "dreaming of wealth", referencing a Tang dynasty short story, 南柯太守传 (Nam Kha Thái Thú Truyện) "The Governor of Nanke", which preaches caution of illusory dreams against an empty, materialistic life.
Namkhang is Latinized form of “น้ำค้าง” in Thai. Meaning “Dew”.
This name bases on the North Eastern Indian Tribal name Rongmei and it means a Brave Heart.
From the Garo word নম্ (nam) meaning "good" and মঁদে (mande) meaning "person".

In Sumerian mythology, she was a primeval goddess, corresponding to Tiamat in Babylonian mythology. She gave birth to An and Ki and the first gods, and with An she bore Enki. She was believed to be the one who came up with the idea to create mankind. She is an almost forgotten goddess, likely most popular in prehistoric times, though her name continued in the names of people, such as Ur-Nammu, the founder of the 3rd Dynasty of Ur.
This name appears to be most common in Tanzania.
From namoa meaning "chickens, fowls" or "toasted coconut" in Tongan.

Originally conceived by the writer-artist Bill Everett in 1939, Namor is the name of Marvel's earliest hero the Sub-Mariner. The name itself means "the Avenging Son" and is also a play on the word "Roman".
The name literally means "Noble" and can be given to boys and girls who come from one of the Mandailing clans.
Used in Ivory Coast. A famous bearer is Namori Meite (born 1988) a French-born Côte d'Ivoirean basketball player currently member of the Côte d'Ivoire national basketball team.
Greek form of Nemuel, as it first appeared in the Septuagint.
Derived from namoz meaning "prayer" and gul meaning "rose, flower".

column3: なんぱち(Japanese Hiragana)|南八, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 南 (nam) meaning "south" and 八 (pachi) meaning "eight".
Derived from the Tewa word Num-pa-yu meaning "snake that does not bite". This was borne by the Hopi-Tewa potter Nampeyo of Hano (1859-1942), the daughter of a Tewa woman and a Hopi man.
Alternate transcription of Thai น้ำผึ้ง (see Namphueng).

column3: 남라(Korean Hangul)|南路, 南羅(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 南 (nam) meaning "south" and 路 (ra) meaning "road, path, street; journey", or 羅 meaning "net for catching birds". Other hanja combinations are also possible.
MEANING - alive. Here न means not + मृत means deadOrigin - Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhala, Hindi, Marathi, Mauritian, Fijian
Name - Namrita नमृताMEANING - alive. It is feminine of नमृत. Here न means not + मृता means dead.It should not be confused with NamrataOrigin - Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, sikh, Buddhist, Nepali, Sinhala
variation of Namsun, means "city" and "first" other combinations can be made on the way of spelling the hanja.

column3: 남순(Korean Hangul)|南淳, 南順, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 남순 (see Nam-sun).
From the name of a Buddhist god of wealth and prosperity, derived from Tibetan rnam thos sras "prince all-hearing", ultimately from Sanskrit Vaiśravana.
Combination of Namsrai and Mongolian жав (jav) meaning "salvation, deliverance".
From Sino-Korean 南 (Nam) meaning "south" and 秀 (Su) meaning "excellent, outstanding, elegant, luxuriant" or 水 (Su) meaning "water". Other Hanja combinations are possible.

column3: 남순(Korean Hangul)|南淳, 南順, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 南 (nam) meaning "south" combined with 淳 (sun) meaning "honest, simple" or 順 (sun) meaning "obey, submit". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From Thai น้ำ (nam) meaning "water" and ทิพย์ (thip) meaning "divine".
Alternate transcription of Thai น้ำทิพย์ (see Namthip).
From native Korean 나무 (namu) meaning "tree; wood."
From Japanese 南 (namuchoru) meaning "south" or other kanji which are pronounced the same way.

Form of Nemuel used in the Douay-Rheims Bible (1582-1610), the Clementine Vulgate (1592) and the Nova Vulgata ("Neo-Vulgate", 1979). The latter two are respectively the former and current official Bible of the Roman Catholic Church.
Form of Nemuel used in the Latin Old Testament.
A Pocasset Wampanoag Native American Chief.
Means "calm, still, quiet, peaceful" or "modest, meek" in Mongolian.
Probably derived from either Mongolian намуу (namuu) meaning "poppy" or намуун (namuun) meaning "quiet, calm"
From Mongolian намуун (namuun) meaning "quiet, calm, peaceful, mild" and цэцэг (tsetseg) meaning "flower".
From Sino-Korean 南 (nam) meaning "south" and 允 (yun) "to grant, to allow, to consent".
Mongolian form of Tibetan Namgyal, meaning "victorious" or "complete victory". Coincides with a Mongolian word meaning "lull".

Dutch short form of Johannes or Johanna.This name can also be a short form of names that contain the Germanic element nand meaning "brave", such as Ferdinand and Nanthild. This particular etymology applies to both Dutch and Frisian.
Means "mint" in Azerbaijani, ultimately from Arabic نعناع (na'nā').

column3: 奈々安寿絵里, 奈々安寿恵里, 奈々杏寿恵里, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree" duplicated using 々, 安 (an) meaning "peace, quiet" or 杏 (an) meaning "apricot", 寿 (ju) meaning "long life", 恵 (e) meaning "favour, benefit" or 絵 (e) meaning "picture, painting, drawing, sketch" combined with 里 (ri) meaning "village". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ななえ(Japanese Hiragana)|七恵, 菜々絵, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 七 (nana) meaning "seven" combined with 恵 (e) meaning "favour, benefit". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 夏凪, 奈凪, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 夏 (na) meaning "summer" or 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree" combined with 凪 (nagi) meaning "calm". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 菜々巴, 菜々果, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens", 々, a phonetic character indicting a duplication of the beginning kanji combined with 果 (ha) meaning "fruit". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 夏 (na) meaning "summer", 南 (na) meaning "south" combined with 陽 (hi) meaning "light, sun, male". Other kanji combinations are possible.

The name Nanak is given to a boy when he is born at his mother's ancestoral village. The meaning comes from nanaka that is "the mother's village"Guru Nanak (1469-1539) born in Punjab was the founder of Sikhism and its first Guru.

column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens" or 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree", duplicated or 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens" combined with 那 (na) meaning "what" or 々, a phonetic character indicting a duplication of the beginning kanji. Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 凪 (na) meaning "calm" duplicated and combined with 音 (ne) meaning "sound". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Javanese and Sundanese lanang meaning "male, manly, brave".

column12: From 七 (nana) meaning "seven" and 緒 (o) meaning "thread". Other kanji combinations can be used.
From Japanese 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree", duplicated and combined with 留 (ru) meaning "to stay". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 七世, 奈々瀬, 那名星, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 七 (nana) meaning "seven" and 世 (se) meaning "world". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 七翔, 七都, 七音, 菜々都, 奈々人, 那奈人, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ななと(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From Japanese 七 (nana) meaning "seven" combined with 都 (to) meaning "capital (city)" or 翔 (to) meaning "soar, fly". Other kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: 七夏, 奈々津, 奈夏, 那夏, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 七 (na) meaning "seven" combined with 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Alternate transcription of 七海 (see Nanami).
Possibly means "Nanaya has gathered", deriving from the Akkadian element kanāšu ("to gather in (harvest, people)").
Means "Nanaya is the one who compensates", deriving from the goddess Nanaya, and the Akkadian element kašāru ("to compensate, to give its due").
Possibly means "Nanaya's joy", deriving from the Akkadian element rīšātu ("joy, happiness").

column3: なな代(Kanji/Hiragana)|奈々代, 菜採世, 七夜, 南奈世, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens", 採 (na) meaning "collect, gather" combined with 世 (yo) meaning "world". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 囡 (nān) meaning "daughter" and 冰 (bīng) meaning "ice".
Maybe a blend of Nancy and Frances.
From Korean 난초 (nan-cho) meaning "orchid", which comes from Sino-Korean 蘭草 (nan-cho).
Combination of Nanci and Lea. A famous bearer is American Olympic driver Nancilea Foster (1983-).
Variant of Nansine recorded in the 19th century.
from NAHUATL Nantzin, means my lovely mother, refference to Earth mother Tonantzin godess

From Sanskrit नन्दन (nandana) meaning "delighting, pleasing, rejoicing".
Derived from Sanskrit नन्दन (nandana) meaning "daughter", "son", or "rejoicing, gladdening". It is used as a feminine name in India, while it is masculine in Sri Lanka.
Walloon and Dutch short form of Ferdinande.
Derived from Gothic nand "bravery" (or from Gothic nanthjan "to venture, to risk, to dare") combined with Gothic hardus (hart in Old High German) "brave, hardy."
Means "sweet" in Zulu. This was the name of the mother of Shaka, famed warrior king of the Zulus in colonial South Africa (though her grave is marked Nindi).
Feminine diminutive of Nando.It coincides with the name of a flowering plant species, also known as "heavenly bamboo" or "sacred bamboo", which comes from Japanese 南天 (nanten).
Means "precious treasure", from Mongolian нандин (nandin) meaning "precious, rare, dear" combined with эрдэнэ (erdene) meaning "jewel, treasure".
Diminutive of Ferdinand, Fernando, or Sisenando.
Portuguese diminutive of Fernando. Also compare Fernandinho.A known bearer of this name is the Portuguese former soccer player Fernando "Nandinho" de Jesus Santos (b. 1973).
Means "daughter, she who delights" in Sanskrit, ultimately from नन्द (nanda) meaning "joy, delight". This is an epithet of the Hindu goddess Durga.
Derived from Gothic nand "bravery" (or from Gothic nanthjan "to venture, to risk, to dare") combined with Old High German rât "counsel."
Means "watched for, waited for, expected" in Malagasy.
The name of a 17th-century Native American woman of the Accawmacke tribe, daughter of Chief Debedeavon, who became an ally to the English colonists.
Derived from Gothic nand "bravery" (or from Gothic nanthjan "to venture, to risk, to dare") combined with Gothic vulfs "wolf."
Derived from Gothic nand "bravery" (or from Gothic nanthjan "to venture, to risk, to dare") combined with Old High German wini "friend."

Directly taken from Hawaiian nanea meaning "fascinating, interesting, enjoyable". It was one of the top 100 most popular names for girls born in Hawaii in 2005 and the name of a doll in the American Girl line, released in 2017.
A Shawnee character in the 1940 novel 'The Loon Feather' by Iola Fuller.
Diminutive of Agnesse and, to a lesser extent, Françwèse.
Czech, Slovak, Provençal and Louisiana Spanish form of Nanette.
Danish variant and Hungarian form of Nanette.
English variant and Hungarian and Romansh form of Nanette.
From the Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" and 芳 (fāng) meaning "fragrant, virtuous, beautiful".
From the Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" and 霏 (fēi) meaning "falling of snow and rain".
Variant of Nương, from a non-Sino-Vietnamese reading of Chinese 娘 (nàng)
From a noble honorific title meaning "lady, miss, princess" in Shan, typically used before the given name.

Means "future" or "even tomorrow" in Xhosa, figuratively "thank you". Often intended as being part of a phrase such as ungadinwa nangomso meaning "don’t be tired tomorrow". Meant to convey gratitude, and the hope for more of the same in the future.
From the Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" and 歌 (gē) meaning "song; sing, praise".
