column3: 南华, etc.(Chinese)|南華, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" combined with 华 (huá) meaning "splendid, illustrious, flowery, Chinese". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

Meaning uncertain. The earliest known attestation of this name occurs in a Svan source from the 13th century AD, so it might possibly be of Svan origin. Also compare the Georgian noun ნანა (nana) meaning "mother" as well as "darling child".Apart from that, there can also easily be cases where this name is a diminutive or variant of Nana 3, which is also of uncertain meaning and origin (though unlikely to be of Kartvelian origin). Also compare the feminine names Anana, Anano, Manana and Nanuli.A notable bearer of this name is the Georgian actress and singer Nani Bregvadze (b. 1936).
Venetian diminutive of Zuana and Swiss Italian cognate of Nannina.

A blend of the name Nanette with any feminine name ending in -ique, such as Angelique and Véronique. In France, Nanique is far more common as a surname, so there may be some cases where the inspiration was the surname itself, rather than a blend of existing names.
From the Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" and 晶 (jīng) meaning "crystal, clear, bright, radiant".
From Sino-Korean 蘭 (nan) meaning "orchid" combined with 朱 (ju) meaning "vermillion, scarlet, red". This name can be formed using other hanja combinations as well.
From the Chinese 囡 (nān) meaning "daughter" and 珏 (jué) meaning "two pieces of jade joined together".

This name is a diminutive, as is indicated by the Slavic diminutive suffix -ka.For Bulgarian, it is still uncertain of what name Nanka is a diminutive of. But in Georgian, Nanka is a Russian-style diminutive of Nana 3 and Nani.
From the Chinese 囡 (nān) meaning "daughter" and 鹂 (lí) meaning "chinese oriole".
From the Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" and 恋 (liàn) meaning "love, long for".
From the Chinese 囡 (nān) meaning "daughter" and 灵 (líng) meaning "spirit, soul".
From the Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" and 梅 (méi) meaning "plum" or 美 (měi) meaning "beauty, beautiful".
Nannaia was a Parthian moon goddess.

column3: 囡囡, 楠楠, 南南, 南楠, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 囡 (nān) meaning "daughter, child", 楠 (nán) meaning "Chinese cedar, Chinese giant redwood" or 南 (nán) meaning "south" combined with themselves. It can also be formed from 南 (nán) meaning "south" combined with 楠 (nán) meaning "Chinese cedar, Chinese giant redwood". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: นนภัทร, นันทภัทร(Thai)
column12: From นน (nanna) which is derived from the Sanskrit nanda, meaning joy or delight and ภัทร (phat / pat) from Sanskrit bhadra, meaning auspicious, excellent, or virtuous.
Variant of Nane, which in turn is a derivative of Nan.
Strictly feminine form of Nanne, where the diminutive suffix ke has been added to the name.
Diminutive of Anna, usually not used as a given name in its own right. This was the name of composer Mozart's older sister.
Scots diminutive of Agnes (as well as Ann).
Diminutive of Giovanna and, to a lesser degree, Anna.

Derived from a diminutive form of Ancient Greek νάννος (nannos) meaning "small child or animal, doll, dwarf; of excessive smallness". This was the name of a famous hetaera, named for her grandmother of the same name. She was possibly the same woman as the hetaera Nannarion.
Icelandic and Faroese form of Nanny.

column3: ნანო(Georgian)|なの(Japanese Hiragana)|ナーノ(Japanese Katakana)|菜乃, 奈乃, 七乃, 凪乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

In the case of male bearers, this name can be a corruption or variant of the biblical name Manoah. For female bearers, the meaning and origin is unknown at this point in time.

column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens", 乃 (no), a possessive particle combined with 羽 (ha) meaning "feather, plume", 葉 (ha) meaning "leaf", or 波 (ha) meaning "wave". Other kanji combinations can also form this name.

column3: なのか(Japanese Hiragana)|なの花(Kanji/Hiragana)|菜ノ花(Kanji/Katakana)|菜乃香, 菜乃華, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens", 乃 (no), a possessive particle combined with 花 (ka) meaning "flower". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: なのこ(Japanese Hiragana)|なの子(Kanji/Hiragana)|菜乃子, 菜野子, 凪乃胡, 菜子, 凪野子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 菜 (nano) meaning "vegetables, greens" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 奈音, 那音, 凪音, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: French, Gallo and Guernésiais diminutive of Anne 1, Franco-Provençal diminutive of Ana used in Savoy (compare Nana) and Walloon diminutive of Ane 1 and Ana.
A blend of the name Nanette with Anouk.
From the Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" and 倩 (qiàn) meaning "beautiful, lovely".

Deriving from the Sino-Korean elements 蘭 (nan), meaning "orchid", 雪 (seol) meaning "snow", and 軒 (heon) meaning "carriage, high, wide, balcony". This was the nomme de plume of a prominent female poet of the Joseon dynasty.
From the Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" and 纱 (shā) meaning "gauze, thin silk".
Etymology uncertain; derived in part from Sumerian še "grain". This was the name of a Sumerian goddess of prophecy, justice, fertility, and fishing.
From the Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" and 姝 (shū) meaning "beautiful girl".
Probably a variant spelling of Nancy.
Icelandic and Faroese form of Nancy.
Alternate transcription of Thai นันทวัน (see Nanthawan).
Alternate transcription of Thai นันทวัฒน์ (see Nanthawat).
East Frisian short form of Ferdinand.
Derived from Proto-Germanic nanþaz "brave, daring" and Old High German, Old Saxon helm "helmet".
Derived from Proto-Germanic *nanþ- "brave; daring" and Old High German helm "helmet".
From Japanese 南 (nantetsu) meaning "south" or from Japanese 南 (nan) meaning "south" combined with 哲 (tetsu) meaning "philosophy, clear". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Thai นันท (nantha) meaning "pleasure, joy, delight" and พร (phon) meaning "blessing".
From Thai นันท (nantha) meaning "pleasure, joy, delight" and วัน (wan) meaning "day".
From Thai นันท (nantha) meaning "pleasure, joy, delight" and วัฒน์ (wat) meaning "culture, development".
From Thai นันท (nantha) meaning "pleasure, joy, delight" and ยา (ya) meaning "drug, medicine, remedy".

From a Germanic name which meant "brave in battle", composed of the elements nanð "daring, brave, bold" (or Gothic nand "bravery", or Gothic nanthjan/nanþjan "to venture, to risk, to dare") and hild "battle". Nanthild was one of the five wives of the 7th-century Frankish king Dagobert I.
Variant of Nanthild. This name was borne by a 7th-century queen consort of the Franks.
From Thai นันทิ (nanthi) meaning "delighted, joyful, happy", ultimately from Sanskrit नन्द (nanda).
From Thai นันทิ (nanthi) meaning "delighted, joyful, happy", ultimately from Sanskrit नन्द (nanda).
Old French form of a Germanic name composed of the elements nand meaning "daring, brave" and heri "army".

In Celtic mythology, Nantosuelta is the goddess of nature, the earth, fire and fertility. Nantosuelta is often associated with water and depicted as being surrounded by water. The goddess's name literally translates as "of winding stream" or "sun-drenched valley", from the Proto-Indo-European root *swel- "swelter", found in Indo-European words denoting "sun".
Another name for Canonchet, a Narragansett sachem.
From Nuri prefixed with the first-person singular plain pronoun 나 (na).
Czech and Slovak diminutive of Naneta.
From the Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" and 蓰 (xǐ) meaning "increase fivefold".
From Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" combined with 仙 (xiān), used in Daoist philosophy, meaning "immortal, transcendent, celestial being, fairy". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" and 香 (xiāng) meaning "fragrant, sweet smelling, incense".
African American name possibly taken from the Igbo word n'anya meaning "love".
From Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" and 雁 (yàn) meaning "wild goose". Other hanzi combinations can form this name as well.
Means "one who goes about" in Cherokee. Notable bearer of this name is Nanyehi, who is known in English as Nancy Ward.
From the Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" and 怡 (yí) meaning "happy, joyful, joy, harmony".
From the Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" and 瑛 (yīng) meaning "luster of gem, crystal" or 影 (yǐng) meaning "shadow, image, reflection".
From the Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" and 瑜 (yú) meaning "fine jade, virtues".
From the Chinese 南 (nán) meaning "south" and 悦 (yuè) meaning "pleased, contended".
Probably a variant spelling of Nancy.

column3: 直晃, 直観, 尚明, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct" and 観 (aki) meaning "see, appear, observe, view". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: なおふみ(Japanese Hiragana)|直典, 尚史, 有典, 有史, 順文, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 尚 (nao) meaning "yet, esteem, still", 有 (nao) meaning "exist, happen, possess", 順 (nao) meaning "obedience, sequence, order, docility, obeying" with 文 (fumi) writing, sentence", 史 meaning (fumi) "history", or 典 (fumi) "ceremony, law, rule". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 直彦, 真彦, 尚彦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|なおひこ(Japanese Hiragana)|ナオヒコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct, honest", 真 (nao) meaning "real, genuine" or 尚 (nao) meaning "still, yet" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince". Other combinations of kanji can form this name as well.

column3: 直寛, 直裕, 尚大, 尚弘, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct" combined with 大 (hiro) meaning "big, large, great". Other kanji combinations are usable.

column3: 直久, 直寿, 尚久, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|なおひさ(Japanese Hiragana)|ナオヒサ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct, honest" or 尚 (nao) meaning "still, yet" combined with 久 (hisa) meaning "long time, long time ago" or 寿 (hisa) meaning "long life, lifespan". Other combinations of kanji can form this name as well.

column3: 直人, 直仁, 直史, 直飛人, 尚仁, 修人, 号男人, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|なおひと(Japanese Hiragana)|ナオヒト(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Nao combined with 人 (hito) meaning "person," also used as 仁 meaning "benevolence, compassion, humanity," 史 meaning "history" or using 2 kanji, combining a hi kanji like 飛 meaning "fly, soar" and a to kanji, e.g. 人.One bearer of this name is actor and singer Naohito Fujiki (藤木 直人) (1972-).

column3: 直一, 直市, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|なおいち(Japanese Hiragana)|ナオイチ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct, honest" combined with 一 (ichi) meaning "one" or 市 (ichi) meaning "market". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 直司, 直次, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct" and 司 (ji) meaning "officer, boss". This name can also be formed using other kanji combinations.
From the Chinese 婥 (nào) meaning "beautiful" and 晶 (jīng) meaning "crystal, clear, bright, radiant".

column3: 直次郎, 直二郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|なおじろう(Japanese Hiragana)|ナオジロウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct" combined with 二 (ji) meaning "two" or 次 (ji) meaning "order, sequence, next" and 郎 (rō) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: なおか(Japanese Hiragana)|ナオカ(Japanese Katakana)|奈丘, 順伽, 楠穂風, 七音歌, 奈織霞, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 直 (nao) meaning "direct, straight" combined with 風 (ka) meaning "wind, poetry, style, folk song". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 直勝, 尚勝, 直克, 尚克, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|なおかつ(Japanese Hiragana)|ナオカツ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct" or 尚 (nao) meaning "still, yet", combined with 勝 (katsu) meaning "victory" or 克 (katsu) meaning "overcome". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: なおかず(Japanese Hiragana)|ナオカズ(Japanese Katakana)|明量, 明員, 明計, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 明 (nao) meaning "bright, clarifying, enlightening" combined with 五 (kazu) meaning "five". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 直邦, 尚邦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|なおくに(Japanese Hiragana)|ナオクニ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct, honest" or 尚 (nao) meaning "still, yet" combined with 邦 (kuni) meaning "home country, Japan". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 直政, 直正, 直方, 尚政, 尚正, 尚将, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|なおまさ(Japanese Hiragana)|ナオマサ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct, honest" or 尚 (nao) meaning "still, yet" combined with 政 (masa) meaning "government", 正 (masa) meaning "right, proper, correct", 方 (masa) meaning "direction, way, side" or 将 (masa) meaning "commander, general, leader". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 婥 (nào) meaning "beautiful" and 妙 (miào) meaning "mysterious, subtle, exquisite".

column3: 直道, 直通, 直倫, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|なおみち(Japanese Hiragana)|ナオミチ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct, honest" combined with 道 (michi) meaning "path, road, way", 通 (michi) meaning "pass through" or 倫 (michi) meaning "ethics". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.
An epithet of the goddesses Durga and Lakshmi.

column12: Shift from Naohito.This name is rarely used.

column3: 直信, 直延, 直伸, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 直 (nao) meaning "common, straight, ordinary", 尚 (nao) meaning "esteem" or 正 (nao) meaning "right, proper, correct, justice" combined with 信 (nobu) meaning "trust" or 延 (nobu) meaning "prolong, stretch". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: なおのり(Japanese Hiragana)|直憲, 直矩, 尚典, 尚文, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct" combined with 文 (nori) meaning "writing, sentence" or 矩 (nori) meaning "Carpenter's square". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: なおお(Japanese Hiragana)|ナオオ(Japanese Katakana)|猶大, 尚翁, 奉生, 猶尾御, 己皇曖, 名諾峰, 汝牡男, 七雄緒, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 尚 (nao) meaning "still, as always" combined with 男 (o) meaning "male", 夫 (o) meaning "man, husband" or 雄 (o) meaning "hero, manly". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From 成 (nao) meaning "become" and 臣 (omi) meaning "one who serves a lord; a vassal, subject".
From the Chinese 婥 (nào) meaning "beautiful" and 然 (rán) meaning "yes, certainly; pledge, promise".

From Ancient Greek ναός (naos), the Doric Greek form of ναύς (naus) meaning "ship". It is a traditional name of the star Zeta Puppis. The star originally belonged to the former constellation Argo Navis, depicting the mythical ship of the Argonauts, but the ship has now been divided into three distinct constellations, with Puppis representing the stern of the ship.It coincides with the Ancient Greek word ναός (naos) meaning "temple, innermost part of a temple, sanctuary".

column3: なおし(Japanese Hiragana)|ナオシ(Japanese Katakana)|直, 道, 猶信, 巨志, 有司, 由士, 真氏, 順史, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 為 (na) meaning "the twelth string of a koto", 往 (o) meaning "past, previous, to head for, go towards", and 仕 (shi) meaning "civil service, official". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 直茂, 巨成, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 巨 (nao) meaning "enormous, giant" and 成 (shige) meaning "to become". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 直典, 直亮, 直輔, 直裕, 直介, 直助, 直佑, 直弼, 尚典, 尚亮, 尚輔, 尚裕, 尚介, 尚助, 尚佑, 尚弼(Japanese Kanji)|なおすけ(Japanese Hiragana)|ナオスケ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 直 (jika, jiki, choku, su.gu, tada.chini, nao.ki, nao.su, -nao.su, nao.ru, nao) meaning "fix, frankness, honesty, repair, straightaway" or 尚 (shou, nao) meaning "esteem, furthermore, still, yet" with 典 (ten, den, suke) meaning "ceremony, code, law, rule", 亮 (ryou, akiraka, suke) meaning "clear, help", 輔 (fu, ho, tasu.keru, suke) meaning "help", 裕 (yuu, suke) meaning "abundant, fertile, rich", 介 (kai, suke) meaning "concern oneself with, jammed in, mediate, shellfish", 助 (jo, suke, tasu.keru) meaning "assist, help, rescue", 佑 (u, yuu, tasu.keru, suke) meaning "assist, help" or 弼 (hitsu, tasu.keru, yudame, suke) meaning "help."One bearer of this name was Naosuke Ii (or Ii Naosuke if surname is used first) (井伊 直弼) (1815-1860) who was the Tairō (or, literally, great elder) of the Tokugawa shogunate from 1858-1860. His childhood name was Tetsunosuke (鉄之介), later Tetsusaburō (鉄三郎).

column3: 直多, 直太, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct" and 多 (ta) meaning "many". Other kanji combinations can be used to spell this name.

column3: 尚毅, 尚隆, 直毅, 直琢, 有孝, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 尚 (nao) meaning "esteem" combined with 貴 (taka) meaning "expensive". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer is Naotaka Amano, a Japanese model and Naotaka Takehara, a Japanese professional baseball outfielder for the Saitama Seibu Lions in Japan's Nippon Professional Baseball.

column3: なおたけ(Japanese Hiragana)|ナオタケ(Japanese Katakana)|順孟, 由威, 明丈, 成猛, 治丈, 巨赳, 有健, 眞雄, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 順 (nao) meaning "order, sequence, obedience" combined with 毅 (take) meaning "strong" or 剛 (take) meaning "sturdy". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer is Naotake Hanyu (1979-), a Japanese athlete.

column3: 直太朗, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|なおたろう(Japanese Hiragana)|ナオタロウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct" combined with 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big, great" and 郎 (rō) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 婥 (nào) meaning "beautiful" and 婷 (tíng) meaning "pretty, graceful".

column3: ナオト(Japanese Katakana)|直人, 尚人, 尚斗, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 直 (nao) meaning "direct, straight" combined with 人 (to) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations can also make up this name.

column3: 直与, 尚朝, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct" and 朝 (tomo) meaning "morning". Other kanji combinations can be used.
From 巨 (nao) meaning "enormous, giant" and 豊 (toyo) meaning "plentiful, abundant". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نوال‎‎ (see Nawal) chiefly used in North Africa.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نوال (see Nawal) chiefly used in North Africa.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نوفل (see Nawfal) chiefly used in North Africa.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نوفل (see Nawfal) chiefly used in North Africa.
Means "nine gems" from Thai เนาว (naowa) meaning "nine" (an archaic word) and รัตน์ (rat) meaning "jewel, gem".
From the Chinese 婥 (nào) meaning "beautiful" and 雯 (wén) meaning "cloud patterns".
From the Chinese 婥 (nào) meaning "beautiful" and 曦 (xī) meaning "sunlight, sunshine, early dawn".

column3: 直康, 直保, 直泰, 直養, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|なおやす(Japanese Hiragana)|ナオヤス(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct, honest" combined with 康 (yasu) meaning "peaceful, quiet", 保 (yasu) meaning "protect, maintain", 泰 (yasu) meaning "peaceful" or 養 (yasu) meaning "raise, rear, bring up". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 婥 (nào) meaning "beautiful" and 莹 (yíng) meaning "luster of gems, bright, lustrous" or 瑛 (yīng) meaning "luster of gems, crystal".

column3: 真明, 尚純, 真彬, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 真 (nao) meaning "truth, reality, sincere" or 尚 (nao) meaning "still, as always, in addition" and 明 (yoshi) meaning "bright, clarifying, enlightening", 純 (yoshi) meaning "pure, innocent" or 彬 (yoshi) meaning "refined". Other kanji combinations can be used, too.
From Japanese 尚 (nao) meaning "esteem" and 夕 (yu) meaning "evening". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 婥 (nào) meaning "beautiful" and 瑗 (yuàn) meaning "large jade ring".
From the Chinese 婥 (nào) meaning "beautiful" and 约 (yuē) meaning "treaty, agreement, covenant".

column3: 直行, 直之, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 直 (nao) meaning "straight" combined with 行 (yuki) meaning "row, line of text". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 婥 (nào) meaning "beautiful" and 珠 (zhū) meaning "bead, pearl, gem".

column3: 由清, 正純, 治泉, 成澄, 明栖⁠, 巨水, 有清, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 由 (nao) meaning "reason, cause, purpose, logic", 順 (nao) meaning "obedience, order, sequence", 正 (nao) meaning "correct, proper, justice" or 治 (nao) meaning "govern, administrate, rule, reign, cure, to treat", and 清 (sumi) meaning "refreshing, clear, pure, clean", 水 (zumi) meaning "water", or 泉 (zumi) meaning "spring (fountain)". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Diminutive of Napoleon. Most notably used by Hall of Fame baseball player Nap Lajoie.
Alternate transcription of Thai นภา (see Napha).
It's a name popular with royals of the Dagbani tribe of Northern Ghana. It means the queen's mother.
Alternate transcription of Thai นภาเพ็ญ (see Naphaphen).
it means someone born after twins
Greenlandic name meaning "standing upright" or "Greenland mountain ash".
Greenlandic name meaning "the risen one", "the erect one"
Means "sky" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit नभस् (nabhas).
From Thai นภา (napha) meaning "sky" and เพ็ญ (phen) meaning "full moon".
From Thai นภา (napha) meaning "sky" and รัตน์ (rat) meaning "gem, jewel".
Derived from Thai ภัสสร (pát-sŏn) meaning "light, halo, rays (of sunshine)".
From Thai นภา (napha) meaning "sky" and วรรณ (wan) meaning "colour, tint".

Meaning "Revival, Expansion, to breathe". According to the Syriac usage, “refreshment”, or "to be refreshed." It is derived from the root noun נפש (nepesh/naphash), breath or life.It is also traditionally translated as "soul."
Feminine form of Naphtali, influenced by Natalia.
Naphtuhim is a son of Mizraim and grandson of Ham first mentioned in Genesis 10:13.
Ancient name given to first born baby girls. Means Blessed by God, brave, loyal, sensitive and places others needs before hers.

In the Elamite pantheon, Napir was the god of the moon. Some sources state that the meaning of his name is "(the) shining one", but this is questionable - it is more likely that it is derived from Elamite nap or napir meaning "god" (see Napirisha).

Possibly derived from the name of the Elamite god of the moon Napir. Name borne by Napir-Asu, who was the queen of Elam during the Middle Elamite period. She is known from a bronze statue discovered in 1903.

This is the epithet of the god Humban and he was almost exclusively known by this name in later times. It means "Great God" in Elamite, derived from Elamite nap or napir "god" combined with Elamite risha or rišarra "great" (also compare Elamite rishair). At least three Elamite kings bore this name in the god's honour (which is consistent with the fact that nearly all rulers of Elam bore theophoric names), one of them being Untash-Napirisha, who lived in the 13th century BC.
Indonesian and Malay form of Nafisa.
A variant of Annaple, which is a Scottish (?) form of Annabel.
Likely a feminine form of Napoleon.
Feminine form of Napoleone. A known bearer of this name was Elisa Baciocchi Levoy (1806–1869), a niece of the French emperor Napoléon Bonaparte (1769-1821). She carried the name as a middle name.
French form of Napoleona. A known bearer of this name was Charlotte Bonaparte (1802-1839), a niece of the French emperor Napoléon Bonaparte (1769-1821). She carried the name as a middle name.
Feminine form of Napoléon influenced by Léonie.
Likely a feminine form of Napoleon.
Diminutive of Napoléon. In other words, you could say that this name is the French cognate of Napolino.
Diminutive of Napoléone. In other words, you could say that this name is the feminine form of Napolin.
Diminutive of Napoleone. It probably came into being independently, but it is also possible that it evolved (as a contracted form) from the diminutive Napoleoncino.
Possibly from Napoli, the Italian name for the city of Naples.

An Irish woman's name, current in the nineteenth and early twentieth century, particularly in the west of Ireland among Irish speakers. Described as a short form of Penelope, it seems to have served as a customary anglicisation of the Gaelic name Nuala/Fionnuala
Modern name from the vocabulary word napsugár "sunbeam, sunshine", itself a compound of the vocabulary words nap "sun, day" and sugár "beam, ray". Its name days are March 21 and July 3.
Means "the flowers," from plural definite article nā and pua meaning "flower, blossom."
Hawaiian feminine name meaning "the heavenly flowers".
From the Nivkh word for "animal" and puyd meaning "fly".
Corsican form of Napoleon, rarely given today.

Means "innocent." Compare Arabic Naqi. Features in Sanhedrin 43a in the Talmud, during an apocryphal description of the death of Yeshua the Nazarene, as one of his five disciples. Naqai uses a pun with his name alluding to Exodus 23:7, saying, "And the innocent {naki} and righteous you shall not slay," but the judges of the Sanhedrin respond with Psalm 10:8 - "In secret places he kills the innocent {naki}" - before giving him the death sentence.
Arabic of Nectanebo cheifly used by medieval Arab authors.
Urdu form of Naqibullah as well as an Arabic variant transcription of the name.

Of unknown meaning or origin.A noted bearer is Naqi’a (c. 680–627 BC, Assyria), a wife of King Sennacherib who held an advisory position to the throne under the title of queen mother during the reigns of Esarhaddon and Ashurbanipal, her son and grandson. Because Naqia sometimes adopted the Akkadian name Zakutu, a translation of Naqi'a, scholars have assumed that she was not native to Assyria. Some scholars suggest that Naqia was Hebrew while others contend that she was one of the women that Hezekiah sent to Sennacherib in 701 BC. Naqia was probably born in Babylonia, but her family may have originated in the Harran area.

Derived from the Arabic noun نقيب (naqib) meaning "chief, leader, captain". Known bearers of this name include the Afghan cricketer Naqib Nangarhari (b. 1998) and the Persian storyteller Naqib ol Mamalek, who is the author of the popular Persian epic Amir Arsalan (19th century AD).
Tajik and Uzbek form of Naqibullah.
Combination of the phonetic elements na and quan.
Derived from nā ("dead person"). This is the name of a dwarf in Norse mythology.

column3: 楢, 奈良, 那良, 名良(Japanese Kanji)|なら(Japanese Hiragana)|ナラ(Japanese Katakana)|나라(Korean Hangul)
column12: Short form of Gyulnara, the Armenian form of Gulnar.
Combination of Nara and the present determiner form of verb 차다 (chada) meaning "to fill."

Possibly means "one who gives (teachings) to men" or "one who gives water (offerings)", derived from Sanskrit नर (nara) meaning "man" or नार (nāra) meaning "water" combined with दा (dā) meaning "to give". According to the Puranas this is the name of a divine sage who serves as a messenger between humans and the gods. He is one of the mind-born sons of the god Brahma, said to have emerged from Brahma's thigh. In Buddhist tradition this is also the name of the 12th of the 27 buddhas preceding Siddhartha Gautama, known in Pali as Nārada.

column3: 나래(Korean Hangul)|娜萊, 羅來, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Variant of native Korean 날개 (nalgae) meaning "wing." It can also be written with hanja, combining a na hanja, like 娜 meaning "beauty" or 羅 meaning "net(ting)," with a rae hanja, such as 萊, referring to the goosefoot, or 來 meaning "coming."
Means "born on a Wednesday" in Sokoto Hausa.

From 奈 (na) meaning "Nara, what?" and 落 (raku) meaning "drop, come down, to fall, leave behind". Together, 奈落 means "hell, the underworld". This is the name of a demon from the manga and anime 'Inuyasha'.
Means "sun ornament" in Mongolian, from наран (naran) meaning "sun" and чимэг (chimeg) meaning "ornament".
Narancia Ghirga is a main character from manga 'JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 5: Vento Aureo'. His name is a mix of the words naranja and arancia both meaning "orange (fruit)" in Spanish and Italian.
Derived from the word narandža meaning ''orange'' (fruit, not the colour).
From the Spanish word naranja meaning "orange (fruit)", a cognate of Orange.
From Mongolian наран (naran) meaning "sun" and хүү (khüü) meaning "son, boy" or "dear, beloved".
From Mongolian наран (naran) meaning "sun" and мандах (mandakh) meaning "ascent, rising".
From Mongolian наран (naran) meaning "sun" and солонго (solongo) meaning "rainbow".
From Mongolian наран (naran) meaning "sun" and цацрал (tsatsral) meaning "light beam, rays, radiation".
From Mongolian наран (naran) meaning "sun" and цацралт (tsatsralt) meaning "emanation, bloom" (compare Narantsatsral).
Derived from Mongolian наран (naran) meaning "sun" and туяа (tuyaa) meaning "ray, beam (of light)".
Means "sun beam" in Mongolian, from наран (naran) meaning "sun" and туяа (tuyaa) meaning "ray, beam".
Derived from Mongolian наран (naran) meaning "sun" and зул (zul) meaning "lamp, torch".
Tamil and Malayalam form of Narasimha.
Means a Human body with lions face
Personal name of Naravas, a Berber Numidian king and Hannibal's brother in law.
Feminine form of Narayana. This is an epithet of the Hindu goddess Lakshmi.
Derived from Old Irish nár "modest" or "noble" and flaith "princess, lady".

Possibly derived from Ancient Greek νάρκη (narke) meaning "numbness, deadness, torpor" with the suffix αῖος (aios) "pertaining to, belonging to, of". In Greek mythology, Narcaeus was a son of Dionysus and the heroine Physcoa. He’s said to have founded a temple to Athena on Elis, giving her the local epithet of Athena Narcaea.

Allegedly a combination of Narcisa and Dalia 1 (i.e., the narcissus flower and the dahlia flower). It is also an anagram of Candelaria. A known bearer of the name is Mexican politician Narcedalia Ramírez (1971-).
Means "pomegranate flower" or "fire flower" in Azerbaijani.
Variant of Narciso, probably influenced by Francisco.
Italian form of Narcissus via Narkissos and variant of Narciso.
Originally the feminine form of Narcisszusz. Since this name also coincides with Hungarian nárcisz "daffodil", it is now considered a nature name.
Lithuanian form of Narkissos via its latinized form Narcissus.
Diminutive form of Narcissa and Narcisa.
Short form of Bernard and Leonard, which is primarily used in the south of the Netherlands.
Truncated form of Bernardine and Lèyonardine.
Alternate transcription of نرجس (see Narjis) chiefly used in Algeria

Ultimately from Greek νάρδος (nardos) meaning "nard plant, spikenard; fragrant oil or ointment of the nard plant", a word used in the New Testament to refer to the expensive perfume poured on Jesus at Bethany (an event known as the 'anointing of Jesus').
An Old Frankish creation from names deriving from Gothic narjan, Old German nerian "to rescue, protect, nourish", Old High German nara "nourishment" + Old High German wini "friend".
Alternate transcription of Thai นารีรัตน์ (see Narirat).
Alternate transcription of Thai นารีวรรณ (see Nariwan).
Perhaps an invented name blending Nayeli and Arely (and sharing a sound with other popular names such as Yareli and Karely).
Meaning unknown. It was borne by a Guanche man from La Palma who was christened in Seville.
From the Chinese 娜 (nà) meaning "elegant, graceful, delicate" and 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness".
Alternate transcription of Hindi नरेन्द्र or नरेंद्र (see Narendra).

Possibly derived from Proto-Norse *nǫrr "narrow", perhaps as in "close-minded, oppressive" or "thin, slender". In Norse mythology, this is the name of a son of Loki, and of a jötunn (the father of Nótt, the personification of night).
Means "sunrise" in Mongolian, from нар (nar) meaning "sun" and гарах (garakh) meaning "to appear, occur".
Alternate transcription of Persian نرگس (see Narges).
Means "pomegranate grain" in Azerbaijani, from nar meaning "pomegranate" and gilə meaning "grain, berry".
Derived from the Georgian noun ნარგიზი (nargizi) meaning "daffodil, narcissus flower". Also see the related name Nargiza, which is also commonly used in Georgia.

column3: ناری(Urdu)|นารี, นารี(Thai)|ណារី(Khmer)
column12: Nari is one of the sons of Loki and Sigyn. At the end of the epic poem "Lokasenna" Nari is said to be the brother of Narvi (also written as Narfi), while Sturlusson's Prose Edda uses Narvi as another name for Nari and names Váli as his brother.

Naria was a Gallo-Roman goddess worshiped in western Switzerland. While her functions have been lost to time, it can be deduced from the sole image of her that she may have been a goddess of good luck and blessings, as her image was done in the generic style of Fortuna, the Roman goddess of luck. The origin and meaning of her name are unknown.
Feminine variant of Neriah influenced via a rhyming variant of Mariah.

Coined for a short story called The Dice of God by South African romance novelist Cynthia Stockley (1863-1936). The short story was serialized in Cosmopolitan magazine starting in February of 1926, and appears to have been expanded and published as a stand-alone book the same year.

column3: 菜里花, 音香, 音夏, 愛果, 遂耶, 成香, 奈梨香, 南莉花, 也華, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens", 里 (ri) meaning "village" combined with 花 (ka) meaning "flower". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ナリコ(Japanese Katakana)|奈莉子, 奈里子, 奈理子, 成子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ნარიკო(Georgian)
column12: From 奈 (na) meaning "what", 里 (ri) meaning "village", and 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations can be used.

From the Avestan name Nairemanah which meant "manly mind" or "heroic minded", derived Avestan from nairiia meaning "heroic, manly" and manah meaning "mind, thought".In the medieval Persian epic Shahnameh written by Ferdowsi, Nariman is the father of the legendary hero Sam 2.
Derived from Lithuanian nerimti "to worry, be anxious" combined with mantus "intelligent" or manta "property, wealth".
Algerian Arabic feminine form of Nariman.

column3: なりみ(Japanese Hiragana)|也実, 也美(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 也 (nari) meaning "to be" combined with Japanese 実 (mi) meaning "reality, truth" or 美 (mi) meaning "beauty".
From Javanese nrima meaning "to accept". This name is traditionally given to boys born during a time of distress and is used by parents to express acceptance of their situation.
Uzbek and Tajik form of Nariman.

column3: 나린(Korean Hangul)|娜璘, 娜潾, 娜麟, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 娜 (na) meaning "elegant, graceful, delicate" and 潾 (rin) meaning "clear water" or 璘 (rin) meaning "luster of jade". Other Hanja combinations are possible. Could also be a variant of Nari.
Means "king, monarch" in Thai (a poetic word), ultimately from Sanskrit नरेन्द्र (narendra).
From Japanese na meaning "vegetables", ri meaning "white jasmine", and na meaning "why". Other kanji combinations are also possible.
Means "bitter orange" in Arabic and Persian.
Means "arranged in order, harmonious" in Malagasy.
Means "fine, small flower", ultimately from Azerbaijani narın meaning "fine, small" and Persian گل (gol) meaning "flower, rose".
From Thai นารี (nari) meaning "woman, lady" and รัตน์ (rat) meaning "gem, jewel".
From the Malagasy nary meaning "fire" and soa meaning "good".
Possibly a variant of Nerissa or Narcissa.
From Thai นารี (nari) meaning "woman, lady" and วรรณ (wan) meaning "colour, tint".
Most likely a variant of Neriah (Compare Sariah).
Alternate transcription of Arabic نرجس (see Narjis) chiefly used in North Africa.
Means "narcissus" in Arabic, ultimately derived from Greek (see Narcissus).
Alternate transcription of Arabic نرجس (see Narjis) chiefly used in North Africa.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نرجس (see Narjis) chiefly used in North Africa.

Derived from the Hebrew word for Narcissus taken from the mythological Greek name Narcissus. It belongs to the female Israeli singer Narkis Reuven-Nagar (1981-). As a given name it is relatively modern and extremely rare but as a surname it is a lot more common.
Most likely based off similar sounding names such as Marla, Carla and Darla.
Narmada is the 5th longest river in India. The name in Sanskrit also means "The Giver of Pleasure".
Means "sunrise" in Mongolian, derived from нар (nar) meaning "sun" and мандах (mandakh) meaning "ascent, rising".
Taken from the fictional land of Narnia from the Chronicles of Narnia by CS Lewis. Used six times for girls in 2005.
From Thai ณรงค์ (narong) meaning "war, campaign" and ชัย (chai) meaning "victory".
From Thai ณรงค์ (narong) meaning "fight, campaign" and เดช (det) meaning "power, might, authority".

column3: ณรงค์ฤทธิ์(Thai)
column12: From Thai ณรงค์ (narong) meaning "war, campaign" and ฤทธิ์ (rit) meaning "supernatural power, divine power".

column3: ณรงค์ศักดิ์(Thai)
column12: From Thai ณรงค์ (narong) meaning "war, campaign" and ศักดิ์ (sak) meaning "power".
From the name of the national tree of the Philippines, known for its strength and resilience.
Assyrian or Syriac form of Narseh. This name was borne by a notable Syriac poet-theologian from the 5th century AD.
French and Catalan form of Narses.
The hindu Mythology shows that the hindu god of vishnu took ten forms to destroy evil on earth. one of the form was narsimha which means part human-part lion
From нарăс (naras) meaning "February" and the female name ending пи (pi).
From the name of a race of superhuman giants in Caucasian mythology, derived from Proto-Iranian narθra- meaning "manhood" (from h₂nḗr meaning "man").

Of debated origin and meaning. Theories include a derivation from Albanian nartë "limpid, sparkling clean water" and derivation from Narta, the name of a town in southwest Albania known for its wines.
Combination of; nar and täç, which mean "fire" and "crown" consequently. Combined meaning is "crown of fire".
MEANING - "dancing, gesticulation, to perform on stage"ORIGIN - SANSKRIT, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhala, Sikh, Buddhist, Mauritian, Fijian

column3: なる(Japanese Hiragana)|成, 徳, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|나루(Korean Hangul)
column12: From Japanese 徳 (naru) meaning "virtue" or 成 (naru) meaning "to become". Other kanji or kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 徳栄, 成栄, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 洛⁠ (raku, tsura.naru, mato, miyako) meaning “capital city, Kyoto” combined with 栄 (ei, you, e, saka.eru, ha.e, ha.eru, -ba.e) meaning "flourish, glory, honour, prosperity, splendour". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Alternate transcription of Thai นฤมล (see Naruemon).
Means "pure, immaculate, unblemished" or "beautiful woman, goddess" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit निर्मल (nirmala).
Alternate transcription of Thai นฤพล (see Naruephon).
From Thai นฤ (narue) meaning "man, person" and พล (phon) meaning "force, strength, power".
Alternate transcription of Thai นฤพล (see Naruephon).
Alternate transcription of Thai นฤพล (see Naruephon).

column3: 成葉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|なるは(Japanese Hiragana)|ナルハ(Japanese Katakana)

column12: This name can be used to combine 成 (sei, jou, na.ru, (-)na.su) meaning "to be, to become," 也 (e, ya, ka, nari, mata, naru), related to 成, 育 (iku, soda.tsu/chi/teru, haguku.mu, naru) meaning "to bring up, to raise, to rear" or 鳴 (mei, na.ku, na.ru, na.rasu) meaning "to sound, to ring, to echo" with 美 (bi, mi, utsuku.shii) meaning "beauty," 実 (shitsu, jitsu, makotoni, mi, michi.ru, mino(.ru)), which means "reality, truth" or 海 (kai, umi, mi) meaning "sea, ocean."Examples of 3-kanji combinations include 奈瑠美, 奈留美, 那瑠美 and 菜瑠実 with 奈 (na, nai, dai, ikan, karanashi) or 那 (na, da, nani, nanzo, ikan), both used as phonetic kanji, 菜 (sai, na) meaning "greens, side dish, vegetable," 瑠 (ru, ryuu), part of 瑠璃 (ruri) meaning "lapis lazuli," and 留 (ryuu, ru, to.ma/eru, todo.ma/eru) meaning "fasten, halt."Bearers of this name include animator and animation director Narumi Kakinouchi (垣野内 成美) (1962-), pair skater Narumi Takahashi (高橋 成美) (1992-) and actress Narumi Yasuda (安田 成美) (1966-).

In the Elamite pantheon, Narundi was the goddess of victory and thus we can consider her to be a war goddess. It is uncertain what the meaning of her name was in the Elamite language. She, along with the goddesses Shiashum and Niarzina, was said to be a sister of the 'great goddess', namely Kiririsha. Some sources claim that she was also (or instead) the sister of the Sebittu or Sibitti (also Sebetti or Sibittu) "the Seven". These were seven benevolent demons - or gods - whose power could be harnessed against evil demons by means of magical incantations. They are not to be confused with the Babylonian Seven Sages.
