From Thai ณัฐ (nat) meaning "wise, intelligent, knowledgeable" and ณิชา (nicha) meaning "clean, pure".
Picard form and Walloon truncated form of Anatole.

From the name of a 1995 Avon perfume, itself from the surname of designer Josie Natori (1947-). It is occasionally spelled with a capitalized third letter as NaTori (or Na'Tori), apparently regarding it as a combination of the prefix na and the name Tori.

column3: 南十星, 七斗星, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|なとせ(Japanese Hiragana)|ナトセ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Taken from 南十字星 (minamijūjisei), referring to the Southern Cross.It can also be written with other kanji, e.g. 七斗星 with 七 (nana) meaning "seven" and 斗 (to), referring to the Chinese constellation known as the Dipper.This name is very rarely used.
Means "thank you" in Lamba, a Zambian language.

Possibly an invented name blending the popular phonetic prefix na and the name LaToya. It can be spelled Natoya or with a capitalized third letter as NaToya. This name is borne by Natoya Goule (1991-), a Jamaican middle-distance runner.
Short form of Natalie, Nathanael and other names that begin with nat-.
From Japanese 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" combined with 近 (chika) meaning "nearby, close". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: なつえ(Japanese Hiragana)|夏愛, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" combined with 愛 (e) meaning "love, affection". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: なつは(Japanese Hiragana)|夏羽, 那都波, 夏初, 夏巴, 夏波, 夏葉, 菜波, 捺波, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" combined with 羽 (ha) meaning "plumes, feathers", 初 (ha) meaning "beginning, start, first", 巴 (ha) meaning "comma design", 波 (ha) meaning "wave" or 葉 (ha) meaning "leaf". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ナツヒ(Japanese Katakana)|なつひ(Japanese Hiragana)|夏日, 夏陽, 夏妃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" combined with 日 (hi) meaning "day, sun, Japan" or 妃 (hi) meaning "princess". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: なつひこ(Japanese Hiragana)|夏彦, 己都彦, 成津彦, 奈鶴彦, 名通彦, 那豆彦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" and 彦 (hiko) meaning "prince, accomplished young man". Other kanji combinations can be used.
From Japanese 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" combined with 姫 (hime) meaning "princess". Other kanji combinations are also possible.
From Japanese 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" combined with 洋 (hiro) meaning "ocean". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" combined with 久 (hisa) meaning "long time ago". Other kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: 夏史, 夏人, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" and 史 (hito) meaning "history". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: なつほ(Japanese Hiragana)|ナツホ(Japanese Katakana)|夏歩, 夏帆, 菜津歩, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" and 歩 (ho) meaning "walk". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Means "Summer Color" or "Color of Summer".From Japanese 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" combined with 色 (iro) meaning "color, color of, complexion".Other Kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: 夏日, 夏風, 夏歌, 夏花, 菜束, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens" combined with 束 (tsuka) meaning "bundle". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.
This is a longest form of Natsuki or Tsukiko.

column3: 棗, 夏芽, 夏目, 夏眼(Japanese Kanji)|なつめ(Japanese Hiragana)|ナツメ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 棗 (natsume) meaning "jujube, date" or 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" combined with 芽 (me) meaning "bud, sprout" or 目, 眼 (me) meaning "eye". Other combinations of kanji can form this name as well. A feminine fictional bearer is Saffron City Gym Leader Sabrina (known as Natsume in Japanese) in the Japanese version of the 'Pokémon' franchise. A masculine fictional bearer is Natsume from the manga and anime 'Natsume's Book of Friends' (夏目友人帳, Hepburn: Natsume Yūjin-chō).

column3: 菜採子, 菜摘子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens", 採 (tsumi) meaning "to gather, to collect, to take" or 摘 (tsumi) meaning "to pluck; to pick" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: なつむ(Japanese Hiragana)|ナツム(Japanese Katakana)|菜紬, 夏武, 奈摘夢, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens" combined with 摘 (tsu.mu) meaning "to pluck, to pick" or 紬 (tsumu.gu) meaning "pongee". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" combined with 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 夏寧, 奈津音, 奈津祢, 奈都音, 菜愛, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" combined with 寧 (ne) meaning "peaceful; tranquil; serene; at peace". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: なつの(Japanese Hiragana)|ナツノ(Japanese Katakana)|夏野, 菜津野, 菜津乃, 菜都乃, 菜摘野, 奈津乃, 奈津野, 奈都乃, 奈都野, 那津乃, 那通乃, 那都乃, 捺乃, 南津乃, 南都乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" or 捺 (natsu) meaning "press, print, affix a seal, stamp" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Or, it could be spelled with 南 (na) meaning "south", 七 (na) meaning "seven" or 名 (na) meaning "name" combined with 津 (tsu) meaning "haven, port, harbor, ferry", 都 (tsu) meaning "metropolis, capital, all, everything" or 摘 (tsu) meaning "pinch, pick, pluck, trim, clip, summarize" that is then combined with 野 (no) meaning "area, field". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 夏男, 夏夫, 夏雄, 夏郎, 夏生, 夏央, 夏緒, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" combined with 男 (o) meaning "male", 夫 (o) meaning "man, husband", 雄 (o) meaning "hero, manly", 郎 (o) meaning "son", 生 (o) meaning "life, living", 央 (o) meaning "centre, middle", or 緒 (o) meaning "cord, string, thread". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" and 理 (ri) meaning "reason".

column3: ナツル(Japanese Katakana)|七絃, 七弦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 七 (na) meaning "seven" combined with 絃 (tsuru) meaning "crane". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer", 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 夏十, 夏人, 夏音, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" combined with 十 (to) meaning "ten", 人 (to) meaning "person" or 音 (to) meaning "sound". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous female bearer is Natsuto Wada (Natto Wada), Japanese script writer and film columnist.

column3: なつよ(Japanese Hiragana)|夏世, 夏代, 夏夜, 奈津代, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" combined with 世 (yo) meaning "world, society" or 代 (yo) meaning "generation". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 夏之, 夏雪, 夏行, 夏幸, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 夏 (natsu) meaning "summer" and 幸 (yuki) meaning "good fortune, happiness". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐชัย (see Natthachai).
Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐกานต์ (see Natthakan).
Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐกานต์ (see Natthakan).
Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐกิจ (see Natthakit).
Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐนันท์ (see Natthanan).
Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐนนท์ (see Natthanon).
Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐนันท์ (see Natthanan).

column3: ณัฐพงศ์, ณัฐพงษ์(Thai)
column12: Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐพงศ์ or ณัฐพงษ์ (see Natthaphong).

column3: ณัฐพงศ์, ณัฐพงษ์(Thai)
column12: Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐพงศ์ or ณัฐพงษ์ (see Natthaphong).
Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐรัตน์ (see Nattharat).
Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐวัฒน์ (see Natthawat).

column3: นาตยา, ณัฐญา, ณัฏยา(Thai)
column12: Derived from Sanskrit नाट्य (natya) meaning "dance". This can also be another way of transcribing the name ณัฐญา or ณัฏยา (see Natthaya).
Means "one who goes out at night", composed of Old Norse nátt "night" and -fari "farer" (from the verb fara "to go, to move, to travel"; compare Sæfari, a byname meaning "seafarer").
Derived from Thai ณัฐ (nat) meaning "wise, intelligent, knowledgeable".
From Thai ณัฐ (nattha) meaning "wise, intelligent, knowledgeable" and ชัย (chai) meaning "victory".
From Thai ณัฐ (nattha) meaning "wise, intelligent, knowledgeable" and กานต์ (kan) meaning "dear, beloved".
Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐกานต์ (see Natthakan).
From Thai ณัฐ (nattha) meaning "wise, intelligent, knowledgeable" and กิจ (kit) meaning "duty, work".
From Thai ณัฐ (nattha) meaning "wise, intelligent, knowledgeable" and นันท์ (nan) meaning "pleasure, joy".
From Thai ณัฐ (nattha) meaning "wise, intelligent, knowledgeable" and นนท์ (non) meaning "pleasure, joy".
Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐนันท์ (see Natthanan).

column3: ณัฐพล(Thai)|ณัฎฐพร(Thai)
column12: From Thai ณัฐ (nat) meaning "wise, intelligent, knowledgeable" and พล (phon) meaning "force, strength, power".

column3: ณัฐพงศ์, ณัฐพงษ์(Thai)
column12: From Thai ณัฐ (nattha) meaning "wise, intelligent, scholar" and พงศ์ (phong) or พงษ์ (phong) both meaning "lineage, family".

column3: ณัฐพงศ์, ณัฐพงษ์(Thai)
column12: Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐพงศ์ or ณัฐพงษ์ (see Natthaphong).
From Thai ณัฐ (nat) meaning "wise, intelligent" and รัตน์ (rat) meaning "gem, jewel".
From Thai ณัฐ (nattha) meaning "wise, intelligent, knowledgeable" and วัฒน์ (wat) meaning "prosperity, culture, development".
From Thai ณัฐ (nat) meaning "wise, intelligent, knowledgeable" and วุฒิ (wut) meaning "knowledge".

column3: ณัฐญา, ณัฏยา(Thai)
column12: Derived from Thai ณัฐ or ณัฏ (nath) both meaning "wise, intelligent, knowledgeable".
From Thai ณัฐ (nat) meaning "wise, intelligent, knowledgeable" and ธิดา (thida) meaning "daughter, girl".
From Thai ณัฐ (nath) meaning "wise, intelligent".
Variant of Nattie, used as a diminutive for Natalie or Natalia.
Alternate transcription of Thai ณัฐธิดา (see Natthida).
Diminutive of names beginning with Nat-, such as Natalie, as well as a Scots diminutive of Henrietta.
Derived from Icelandic nátt "night" and mǫrðr "marten".
Means "midnight sun", consisting of Old Norse nátt "night" and sól "sun". It was also an Old Norse byname, used in the Njáls saga.
Diminutive of Nathaniel, Natalie and other names containing the element nat.

This is believed to have originated as a nursery form of the Greenlandic word inequnartoq "sweet, cute", shortened and simplified to natuk through the common custom of babbling or cooing with a baby. Otherwise it may be a short form of the old name Arnatuk meaning "soul/name wandering" from arnattoq, which is ultimately derived from arnappoq "seeks a mother", referring to the mythological concept of a soul being born into different shapes and animals before crawling into the womb of a woman to be born again and reclaim his name.(Source: Oqaasileriffik.gl)
Diminutive of Natalia. It can also be a diminutive of Natela and Natia, especially when written as ნათუკა.
Meaning ‘He loves us’ in Nkore and Kiga.
From Thai ณัฐ (nat) meaning "wise, intelligent, knowledgeable" and วดี (wadi) meaning "possessing, having".
Diminutive of names like Netanel, Netanela, Anat 2, Yonatan / Yehonatan and Natan.
Short form of Natalia, Nataliya or Natalya.
A short form and nickname of Nadine.A notable bearer of this nickname is the German football player Nadine Angerer.

column3: 奈詩, 奈羽, 生雨, 菜生, 菜羽, 今, 夏海, 和生, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ナウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree" combined with 詩 (u) meaning "poetry, poem". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Derived from Ancient Greek ναῦς (naus) meaning "ship, boat" and βόλος (bólos) meaning "throw, cast of a net".
Portuguese form of Naukratios via it's Latinized form Naucratius.
Spanish form of Naukratios via it's Latinized form Naucratius.
An Orthodox saint in the 4th century. Son of Ss. Emmelia and Basil the Elder, and brother to St. Basil the Great, Ss. Theosebia and Gregory of Nyssa, and St. Macrina the younger.
Italian form of Naukratios via it's Latinized form Naucratius.

Ancient Persian form of the Avestan name Naotara or Nautara, which most likely means "younger, newer" and is derived from Avestan nauua or nava meaning "new, fresh". It is also possible that the name is ultimately derived from Proto-Indo-Iranian nutára "quick", thus giving the name the overall meaning of "the quick one".
A Proto-Norse name attested on the Hogganvik Runestone. Composed of ᚾᚨᚢᛞᛁᛉ (naudiz) "head" + ᚷᚨᛊᛏᛁᛉ (gastiz) "guest".
Indonesian and Malay form of Nawfal.
Means "fourth" in Nahuatl, literally "having the quality or likeness of four".
Greenlandic name meaning "Ross's Gull" with the combination of combination of Nauja and -nnguaq meaning "sweet, dear".
Possibly a combination of the phonetic element na and the French word jour meaning "day". This is the given name of rapper Toosii (2000-), as well as the title of his second album, 'Najour'.

Means "ruling the sea, master of the sea", derived from Ancient Greek ναῦς (naus) "ship" and κράτος (kratos) "power, strength". It coincides with the word ναυκράτης (naukrates), a kind of fish said to cling to the sides of boats.

Greek form of Naucratius, a Roman cognomen that means either "sea victory, ship victory, victorious ship" or possibly linked to the Egyptian port city of Naucratis. Used by two saints one of whom is the brother to Basil the great.
From na'u meaning "mine" or nāu meaning "your" and melia, Hawaiian name of the flower Plumeria; hence the meaning is "my flower" or "your flower".
Feminine form of Nu. Also compare Nut, which appears to be partially related.In Egyptian mythology, this is the name of one of the eight primordial deities of the Ogdoad.
Means "elder brother" or "next, future" in Burmese.

Transferred use of either the surname Naunton or the place name Naunton.A notable bearer of this name was the Welsh actor Naunton Wayne (1901-1970). However, it was not his birth name: it was his stage name, which he later (in 1933) made his legal name.
From nau ora meaning "some life; my life; your life".

Means "seafarer", from Ancient Greek ναῦς (naûs) meaning "ship" and‎ πλέω (pleo) meaning "to sail". It also refers to a kind of shellfish. In Greek mythology, this was the name of a son of Poseidon and the Daenid Amymone, the eponymous founder of Nauplia and the inventor of seafaring. It was also the name of his own son (who in some accounts is the same person), who fathered Palamedes, Oiax, and Nausimedon, and of an Argonaut who may have either been a descendant of the original Nauplius or also the same person.

Means "someone found" (literally "was found") in Comanche. This was the Comanche name given to American woman Cynthia Ann Parker, who was kidnapped in May 1836 at the age of 9 or 10 by a Comanche war band, who massacred her family's settlement. She was adopted by the Comanche and lived with them for 24 years. She married a Comanche chieftain, Peta Nocona, with whom she had three children, including the last free Comanche chief Quanah Parker.
Meaning: "grim, serious, strict". Derived from word "niūrus" (lit. grim).
Composed of nau meaning "mine, thine" and rea meaning "bright, joyful".
Means "the two young coconut shoots", referring to the southern archipelagos south of French Polynesia.
Means "March" in Kazakh, ultimately from Persian نوروز (nowruz). This is also the Kazakh name for Nowruz, an Iranian holiday commemorating the first day of spring.

Kazakh name that transliterates to "wealthy Nowruz" or "festive Nowruz". Combination of the Kazakh name Nauryz, meaning "March" (derived from Persian Nowruz) and the Kazakh word bay, meaning "wealthy" (derived from Tajik Persian boy).
From Kazakh наурыз (nauryz) meaning "March (the month)" and бай (bay) meaning "rich, wealthy".
From Kazakh наурыз (nauryz) meaning "March (month)" or referring to the Iranian New Year (Nowruz) combined with the Turkic military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".

column3: 今鹿(Japanese Kanji)|なうしか(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: This is the Japanese form of Nausicaä. It is possible that it was influenced by Nausicaä, the protagonist of Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind.
Catalan and Italian form of Nausicaa.
Portuguese and Spanish form of Nausicaa.
Latinized form of the Greek name Ναυσικύδης (Nausikydes).
Derived from Ancient Greek ναῦς (naus) meaning "ship" combined with γενής (genes) meaning "born". This was the name of an eponymous archon of Athens, who lived in the 4th century BC.
Greek variant and Albanian form of Nausikaa.
Derived from Greek ναῦς (naus) meaning "ship" (compare Nausicaa) and κράτος (kratos) meaning "power, strength". This name was borne by a Greek comic poet.
Derived from Ancient Greek ναῦς (naus) meaning "ship" and κῦδος (kydos) meaning "glory, renown".
Derived from Ancient Greek ναῦς (naus) meaning "ship" combined with μάχη (mache) meaning "battle".

Probably means "ship captain", derived from Ancient Greek ναῦς (naus) meaning "ship" and μέδων (medon) meaning "ruler" (compare medo, medomai). In Greek mythology, this was the name of a son of King Nauplius, along with his brothers Oiax and Palamedes.
Latinized form of Nausinikos. This name was borne by an eponymous archon of Athens, who lived in the 4th century BC.
Derived from Ancient Greek ναῦς (naus) meaning "ship" combined with νίκη (nike) meaning "victory".
Derived from Greek ναῦς (naûs) meaning "a boat" and φανής (phanes) meaning "appearing".
Derived from Ancient Greek ναῦς (naus) meaning "ship" and θοός (thoos) meaning "quick, swift".
Possibly from the word nautical, meaning “relating to ships”. Cameron Diaz named her son this in 2026.
In the Aeneid, Nautes is Aeneas's advisor.

Likely based on the English word nautical, which is derived from Latin nauticus meaning "pertaining to ships or sailors", ultimately from Greek ναῦς (naus) "ship". Use of the name may also be influenced by the American clothing company Nautica.
In early Mormon history, this was the name of a prominent Mormon settlement in Illinois. It means "beautiful" in Hebrew.
Derived from Arabic نَيِّر (nayyir) meaning "luminous, brilliant".

Derived from Guanche *(a)nuhazzeṭ meaning "the most elegant". According to Antonio de Viana's epic poem Antigüedades de las Islas Afortunadas de la Gran Canaria (1604), Nauzet or Nuhazet was a Guanche warrior who fought in the battle of Acentejo in the army of the mencey Bencomo.

West Greenlandic name meaning "the one who travelled from place to place", composed of nava- meaning "exchange, moving from place to place" and -giaq meaning "travel" or "is out". In Greenlandic mythology this is the name of a character who dies and travels from animal to animal as a spirit until he is finally reborn as a human.
From Sanskrit नवल (navala) meaning "new, novel, fresh".
Used by American author Brandon Sanderson for a character in his series of fantasy novels The Stormlight Archive (2010-), possibly inspired by the Sanskrit word नव (nava) meaning "new, fresh".

Greenlandic name meaning "one who alternates between different parties", derived from the Proto-Eskimo root *naverar "to trade, exchange" and the name suffix na. In legend Navarana was an Inuit woman who brought about disunity by alternating between her tribe of native Greenlanders and the Norse colonists. The name was assumed by the first wife of Danish polar explorer and author Peter Freuchen (1886-1957), a Greenlandic Inuit woman formerly known as Mekupaluk (died 1921). This was later used by Knud Rasmussen for the heroine of 'The Wedding of Palo' (1934), filmed in East Greenland in 1933.

Likely derived from Navarone, the name of a fictional Greek island from the novel The Guns of Navarone (1957) written by Alistair MacLean (1922-1987).A notable bearer of this name is the American musician Navarone Garibaldi (b. 1987), who is the only son of Priscilla Presley (b. 1945).
Transferred use of the surname Navarro.
Transferred use of the surname Navas.
Means "sort of spring" from Uzbek nav meaning "sort, kind" (borrowed from Arabic نَوَّعَ) combined with the given name Bakhor meaning "spring"
Possibly from the Kurdish nav meaning "name, reputation" and bihar meaning "spring".
Derived from Kurdish navdarbûn meaning "to become famous".
Name used in Sri Lanka, it probably means "wise leader".
This name has some meanings: The first is "beautiful" (from the name Nava). And the second is "oasis" (from the name Neveh).
Means "arrow-like", from Persian ناوك (nāvak) meaning "small arrow, dart" and Arabic مثال (mithāl) meaning "example, resemblance".
Means "new lord" from Sanskrit नव (nava) meaning "new, fresh" combined with the name of the Hindu god Indra, used here to mean "lord".
Coptic form of the Egyptian given name Neferhor.
Transferred use of the surname Navey.
Derived from Uzbek nav meaning "sort, kind" and gul meaning "rose, flower".
It means "prophet" in Hebrew ultimately from a word meaning "spokesperson".
Navia (also known as Nabia) was the goddess of rivers and water in Gallaecian and Lusitanian mythology. The name is still used in present-day Galicia.
From the Spanish word Navidad meaning "Christmas; Nativity". It could also function as a variant of Natividad.
Possibly derived from Latin nāvigō meaning "sail, navigate". This was the name of a brother of Saint Augustine of Hippo.
Uigvak(King Island) dialect Inupiatun name of writer and poet Joan Naviyuk Kane, etymology and meaning unknown, possibly related to the western Kalilit(Greenlandic) name Navagiaq
From Sanskrit नव (nava) meaning "new, fresh" combined with जिति (jiti) meaning "victory, conquering".
Alternate transcription of Punjabi Gurmukhi ਨਵਜੀਤ (see Navjeet).
From Sanskrit नव (nava) meaning "new, fresh" combined with ज्योतिस् (jyotis) meaning "light, brightness".
From Sanskrit नव (nava) meaning "new, fresh" and Hindi लीन (līn) meaning "engrossed, absorbed" (compare Lina 3).
Alternate transcription of Punjabi Gurmukhi ਨਵਨੀਤ (see Navneet).
From Sanskrit नव (nava) meaning "new, fresh" combined with प्रीति (prīti) meaning "pleasure, joy, love".
Navreet is a masculine name originated from indian subcontinent. It is a unique Boy name which means 'to start a new tradition, revolution'
I was born with it. It means beautiful, new flower and very unique.
From navro‘z, reffering to the festival of the New Year of the Zoroastrian calender, celebrated during the Sping equinox (see Nowruz).
Uzbek feminine name derived from nav'roz refering to a New Year's celebration widely celebrated in Central Asia, also meaning "springtime" or the name of a kind of apricot.
From navro‘z, reffering to the festival of the New Year of the Zoroastrian calender, celebrated during the Sping equinox (see Nowruz), combined with beg meaning "chieftan, master".
Derived from nav'roz refering to a New Year's celebration widely celebrated in Central Asia, also meaning "springtime" or the name of a kind of apricot, and gul meaning "rose, flower".
Derived from nav'roz refering to a New Year's celebration widely celebrated in Central Asia, also meaning "springtime" or the name of a kind of apricot, and oy meaning "moon".
Uzbek, Tajik and Turkish form of Nowruz. This name is masculine in Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, while in Turkey it is mostly found on females.
Greenlandic name meaning "sweet/dear find/discovery", combined with Navssâĸ and -nnguaq "sweet, dear".
Greenlandic name meaning "dear little find/discovery". Combination of Navssâĸ and -paluk "dear little".
Greenlandic name meaning "big/great find/discovery". Combination of Navssâĸ and suffix -rsuaq "big, great".
Means "to be praised, laudable" and "navigable" in Sanskrit. However, in Telugu, it allegedly means "blue".
Means "koa canoes" from Hawaiian na a plural article, and waʻa "canoe" combined with koa "koa tree". A known bearer is Nawaʻakoa Lisiate Foti Analeseanoa "Koa" Misi (1987-), an American footballer.
Likely from the royal title Nawab.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نواف (see Nawwaf).
Hawaiian unisex name meaning "the waters", derives from nā meaning "the" and wai meaning "waters".
Alternate transcription of Tibetan ངག་དབང (see Ngawang).
From Thai นว (nawa) meaning "nine" and ภัทร (phat) meaning "excellent, magnificent, pleasant".
Alternate transcription of Thai นวพล (see Nawaphon).

column3: นวพล, นวพร(Thai)
column12: From Thai นว (nawa) meaning "nine" or "new" and พล (phon) meaning "strength, power" or พร (phon) meaning "blessing". The spelling นวพล is masculine while นวพร is feminine.
Alternate transcription of Thai นวพล (see Nawaphon).

column3: นวพล, นวพร(Thai)
column12: Alternate transcription of Thai นวพล or นวพร (see Nawaphon).
Alternate transcription of Thai นวพร (see Nawaphon).
Alternate transcription of Arabic نوار (see Nawwar).

column3: ณวัชร์, ณวัฒน์(Thai)

column12: From the name of 13th-century Islamic scholar and jurist Yahya ibn Sharaf al-Nawawi, whose name was derived from the city of Nawa in present-day Syria.
Derived from Persian نواز (navaz) meaning "caress, cherish, soothe".
Alternate transcription of Thai นาวี (see Nawi).
Alternate transcription of Nawal chiefly used in Northern Africa.
The name means exalted, wise. It also means “Nova” in english.
Means "generous" in Arabic, also an archaic word meaning "sea, ocean".
Alternate transcription of Arabic نوفل (see Nawfal) chiefly used in North Africa.
Means "boat, ship" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit नावा (nāvā).

Meaning uncertain. Name borne by a ruling Kandake of Kush, who is known from a wall relief in her burial chamber at Meroe, which shows her wearing the royal coat, sash and tasselled cord; elements more commonly associated with male rulers of Kush.
Means "marine" or "seaman, mariner, sailor" in Thai.
Derived from Polish naj, a superlative particle, and Old Polish woj "warrior". This used to be an amuletic name, wishing the bearer to become "the (very) best warrior".

Feminine form of Nawoj. According to a legend, this was the name of a 15th-century Polish female student who dressed as a boy in order to study at the University of Kraków. A street in Kraków bears her name.

column3: 나운(Korean Hangul)|那芸, 娜雲(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 娜 (na) meaning "elegant, graceful, delicate" or 那 (na) meaning "that one" and 雲 (woon) "clouds" or 芸 (woon) meaning "rue, herb to keep insects away"
Nawraa' includes meanings of "beauty", "purity", and "radiancy". It is a derivative of Noor 1, which means "glowing light".
Alternate transcription of Bengali নওশীন (see Nowshin).
Alternate transcription of Bengali নওশীন (see Nowshin).
Derived from Kabardian Neχ daxe meaning "more beautiful".
From the Chinese 娜 (nà) meaning "elegant, graceful" and 纤 (xiān) meaning "fine, delicate, graceful".
Alternate transcription of Burmese နေ (see Ne).
Means "rare, unique" in Hindustani (Urdu and Hindi), ultimately from Persian نایاب (nâyâb).
From Japanese 夏 (na) meaning "summer", 悦 (ya) meaning "joy, pleased" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Feminine form of Nayan, from Sanskrit नयन (nayana) meaning "eye".
From the name of a type of plant that produces pink or white flowers (scientific name Catharanthus roseus).
Means "who has many desires" in Quechua.
From Sino-Korean 娜 "elegant, graceful, delicate" and 藝 "art; talent, ability".
stems from the root "na'im," meaning "blessing," "comfort," "bliss," or "contentment,"

column4: Spanish (Latin American, Modern, Rare)|Spanish (Mexican, Modern, Rare)

column12: From Sino-Korean 娜 "elegant, graceful, delicate" and 妍 "beautiful".

column3: 나영(Korean Hangul)|娜英, 娜榮, 娜永, 娜瑛, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 娜 (na) meaning "elegant, graceful, delicate" combined with 英 (yeong) meaning "flower, petal, brave, hero" or 榮 (yeong) meaning "glory, honour, flourish, prosper" or 永 (yeong), meaning "perpetual, eternal" or 瑛 (yeong) meaning "jade". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

From Egyptian nꜣy.f-ꜥꜣw-rwḏ meaning "his great ones (ancestors) are flourishing" or "his greatness is flourishing", derived from the possessive pronoun nꜣy combined with .f "his", the plural form of ꜥꜣ "great, big, important", and rwḏ "to be firm, to prosper".
From the Chinese 纳 (nà) meaning "take, receive, accept" or 娜 (nà) meaning "elegant, graceful" and 懿 (yì) meaning "virtuous, admirable" or 伊 (yī) meaning "he, she, this, that".
Hispanic variant of Arabic name Najib. A notable bearer is Nayib Bukele (1981-), the current president of El Salvador, who is of Palestinian heritage.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نايف (see Naif).
Name of a dragon in The Priory of the Orange Tree.Proto-Mongolic *na(y)imān ("eight") + Old Chinese *thun ("spring").
From the Chinese 娜 (nà) meaning "elegant, graceful" and 莹 (yíng) meaning "luster of gems, bright, lustrous".
Possibly an invented name blending the phonetic element nay with Kaylani, Jaylani or Laylani.
Possibly a variant to the name Nayla with suffix -lee. It is a similar to names such as Kaylee, Jaylee, ect.

column3: ナヨ(Japanese Katakana)|菜世, 名夜, 名容, 菜杨, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens" combined with 世 (yo) meaning "generations". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens", 余 (yo) meaning "over, more than" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 나영(Korean Hangul)|娜英, 娜榮, 娜永, 娜瑛, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangeul 나영 (see Na-yeong).
Supposedly means "love" or "wisdom" in ancient Hylian, a language in the 'Legend of Zelda' universe. In the games, Nayru is one of the goddesses responsible for the creation of Hyrule.
From the English vocabulary word nature (see Nature).

column3: なゆ(Japanese Hiragana)|ナユ(Japanese Katakana)|奈結, 菜佑, 七優, 奈由, 凪悠, 那遊, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|娜羽(Chinese)
column12: From Japanese 夏 (na) meaning "summer" or 南 (na) meaning "south" combined with 夕 (yu) meaning "evening". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens", 郁 (yu) meaning "fragrance" combined with 絵 (e) meaning "picture, painting, drawing, sketch". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 名雪, 那雪, 奈雪, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 名 (na) meaning "name, reputation" and 雪 (yuki) meaning "snow". Other kanji combinations can spell this name.

column3: なゆこ(Japanese Hiragana)|ナユコ(Japanese Katakana)|無夕子, 名由子, 七佑子, 鳴悠子, 那結子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 無 (na) meaning "nothing, not, nil, none" and 夕 (yu) meaning "evening" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: なゆみ(Japanese Hiragana)|菜弓, 七夕美, 奈有美, 南由美, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens" combined with 弓 (yumi) meaning "archery bow". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Sino-Korean "娜" (na) meaning " elegant, graceful, delicate" and "潤" (yun) meaning "soft, sleek". Other hanja can be used.

column3: 那由他, 那由多, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|なゆた(Japanese Hiragana)|ナユタ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 那由他/那由多 (nayuta), originally a Buddhist term referring to an extremely great number (often said to be 100 million), derived from Sanskrit नयुत (nayuta) meaning “myriad” or नियुत (niyuta), referring to a very high number.
This is the birth name of American rapper, singer, songwriter, and record producer, Future.
Means "gracefulness, elegance, civility" in Urdu, ultimately from Persian نزاکت (nazakat).
From Uygur نازاكەت meaning "kindness, politeness; elegance", cognate of Nəzakət.
Means "coy" in Turkish, ultimately from Persian نازان (nāzān).
Derived from Arabic نظر (nazar) meaning "attention, regard, look, gaze" combined with Kazakh and Kyrgyz бай (bay) meaning "rich, wealthy".
Derived from Arabic نظر (nazar) meaning "attention, regard, look, gaze" combined with begum the feminine form of the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master"
Portuguese and Asturian form of Nazareth.
Portuguese and Spanish form of Nazzareno.

From the biblical place name, now an Arabic city in northern Israel (see Nazareth). In the New Testament it is referred to as the home town of Jesus Christ, and is used as one of his titles: Jesus of Nazareth.It is also a Spanish variant of Nazaret, as well as an Armenian alternate transcription of the same name.
Derived from Uzbek nazar meaning "look, glance" and gul meaning "rose, flower".
Means "my sight, my vision" from Arabic نَظَر (naẓar) meaning "vision, gaze, sight".
Corsican and Sicilian form of Nazarius.
Russian and Ukrainian form of Nazaria and feminine form of Nazariy.
From the Turkish naz meaning "coy" and bahar meaning "spring".
From the Turkish naz meaning "coy" and can meaning "spirit, soul".
From Kurdish nazik meaning "delicate" and dar meaning "tree". Nazdar Ciziri is a Kurdish musician.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نظيف (see Nazif).
Alternate transcription of Arabic نزيه (see Nazih).
Alternate transcription of Arabic نزيهة (see Naziha).
Meaning organised or orderly. A famous bearer is Nazeem, a redguard from the game Skyrim.
Indian feminine first name, of which the meaning is currently unknown to me.
Means "graceful, charming" in Armenian, ultimately from Persian ناز (nāz) meaning "delight, coquetry".
Alternate transcription of Arabic ناظم (see Nazim), as well as the Persian form.
Means "lathyrus" in Turkish, a kind of flower.

Derivative of Persian ناز (nāz) meaning "airs and graces, coquetry". This name was mentioned by the 5th-century Armenian historian Movses Khorenatsi in the form Նազինիկ (Nazinik) as belonging to a beautiful dancer and performer of the 2nd century AD, who was a concubine of the ancient Armenian patriarch Bakur Syunetsi.
From Persian ناز (naz) meaning "delight, comfort, coquetry, affectation" combined with Arabic أمّ (umm) meaning "mother"
From the Turkish naz meaning "coy" and hanım meaning "lady".
Means "supporter, rescuer" or "brave" from Arabic نَاجَدَ (nājada) meaning "to help, aid, assist".
Traditional Austrian and Bavarian short form of Ignaz and Romansh short form of Ignazi.

Derived from the Georgian adjective ნაზი (nazi) meaning "gentle" as well as "delicate, soft, tender" (see Nazi) combined with the Georgian noun ბროლი (broli) meaning "crystal (glass)" (see Brola). As such, the meaning of this name is basically "as fragile as crystal glass".In Georgian literature, Nazibrola is the name of a character from the poem გამზრდელი (Gamzrdeli) written in 1898 by the Georgian poet Akaki Tsereteli (1840-1915).
Alternate transcription of Arabic نظيفة (see Nazifa), as well as the Malay form.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نزيهة (see Naziha), as well as the usual Malay form.
From Ottoman Turkish نازك (nazik) meaning "delicate, slender, clean, polite" and Persian ادا (ada) meaning "elegance, beauty, charm, coquetry, manners".
From Arabic نازل (nazil) meaning "descending, going down".
Arabic alternate transcription of Nazima as well as the Malay form.
A combination of Nazim and دين (dīn) meaning "religion, faith".
Means "prince, ruler, as consecrated, separate, an unpruned vine, undressed vine".
Arabic alternate transcription of Nazira as well as the Malay form.
Derived from nazira meaning "a literary work meant to represent or respond another work by another author" and oy meaning "moon".
Either from نذير (nadhīr) meaning "herald, warner" or نظير (naẓīr) meaning "similar, alike, counterpart" combined with дин (dīn) meaning "religion"
Means "pride, boasting" in Urdu, of Persian origin.
From the Turkish nazlı meaning "delicate, coy" and ay meaning "moon".
Possibly a combination of Nazlı, meaning "delicate", and Can meaning "soul".
From the Turkish nazlı meaning "delicate, coy" and Persian دل (del) meaning "heart".
From the Turkish nazlı meaning "delicate, coy" and fer meaning "lustre, brightness".
From the Turkish nazlı meaning "delicate, coy" and göz meaning "eye".
From the Turkish nazlı meaning "delicate, coy" and gül meaning "rose".
From the Turkish nazlı meaning "delicate, coy" and gülen meaning "smiling".
From the Turkish nazlı meaning "delicate, coy" and nur meaning "light".
From the Turkish nazlı meaning "delicate, coy" and sel meaning "flood".
From the Turkish nazlı meaning "delicate, coy" and su meaning "water".
From the Turkish nazlı meaning "delicate, coy" and tan meaning "dawn".
From the Turkish nazlı meaning "delicate, coy" and yar meaning "love, lover".
Derived from nazmiy meaning "poetic, in poetry".
It means "poem" in Arabic. This is the name of a protagonist in Susan Abulhawa's novel The Blue Between Sky and Water (2015).
Alternate transcription of Bengali নাজমুল (see Najmul).
From the first part of the Arabic phrase النجم الثاقب (an-najmu at-thaqibu) meaning "the piercingly bright star".
Parsi, Indian Muslim, and Bengali variant of Nazanin.
Either a diminutive or a variant form of Nazi.
From Uzbek nazokat meaning "refinement, grace", ultimately from Persian نزاکت (nazâkat) meaning "politeness, civility" combined with the title khan meaning "king, ruler".
From Ottoman Turkish or Persian ناز⁩ (naz) meaning "delight, comfort, coquetry, affectation" and Persian پرور⁩ (parvar), the present stem of پروردن⁩ (parvardan) meaning "to foster, nourish, cherish".
Means "to look, to see" in Arabic. In Islam, nazr is is a commitment to carry out an act. Notable bearer of this name is Nazr Mohammed (1977—), an American professional basketball player.
Possibly from Persian نظریه (nazariye), ultimately from Arabic نَظَرِيَّة (naẓariyya) "theory, theorem". A known bearer is Nazriya Nazim (1994–), a Muslim Indian actress from Kerala.
From the first part of the Arabic phrase نذر الإسلام (nazr al-Islam) meaning "vow of Islam" or "vow to Islam".
From the Arabic phrase نذر الإسلام (nadhr al-ʾIslām) meaning "vow of Islam" or "vow to Islam".

column3: なずな(Japanese Hiragana)|ナズナ(Japanese Katakana)|南沙, 那砂, 菜都奈, 奈津菜, 奈都菜, 名津菜, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 奈 (na) meaning "Nara, apple tree, what?", 那 (na) meaning "what", 名 (na) meaning "status, reputation, name" combined with 砂 or 沙 (suna) both meaning "sand". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.
Chechen and Ingush form of Nazir 1.
From the Kinyarwanda word incuti meaning "friend".
Means "What did I do?" This name is an expression of regret by a parent. Usually given by a single mother whose partner does not take responsibility of the child born.
Means "I have loved you" in Shona.
Means "I have been chosen" in Shona.
The younger oneListed in Asante's 'Book of African Names' (1991) as a Western African masculine name meaning "trick".
Means "beautiful", she said. The notable bearer of this name is N'Dambi (1970—), whose birth name is Chonita N. Gillespie.
Means "House of Spears" in the Ngema tribe of Cameroon. A famous bearer is Ndamukong Suh, the defensive tackle for the college football team Nebraska Cornhuskers.
It means "gold", this name serves as a given name and a surname.
Derives from the Albanian word nder, meaning "honour, respect".
Means "the thing", implying "the secret", in Xitsonga.
Means "I have eaten with them" in Chikaguru.
Derived from Njie, a Serer and Wolof patronym.
Means "patience is very good" in Igbo.
Means "I am alive thanks to God" in Kirundi.
Means "be joyful over me" in Xhosa.
Means "where do I go?" in Tshivenda.
A diminutive variant of the name Ndue, which a shortening of name Andon, the Albanian version of Anthony.
Means "young girl who pounds white maize into theke", which is used in ritualistic offerings to ancestors.
It is the name of a Congolese music genre and dance style derived from the Congolese Rumba and Kwassa Kwassa during 1990s.
Possibly means "I will guard" in Zulu.
Unknown meaning. This name shows up specifically in Kenya.
Ndubisi is an Igbo name derived from Ndu(Life) Bu isi(The first or of priority).This then means "Life is first or of Priority.
Means "let life not be lost" in Igbo.
Means "pray for long life" in Ijaw.
Means “life is precious, life is valuable” in Igbo.
Means "head (wo)man" in Luvale, languege spoken in Zambia and Angola.
Possibly from Sino-Vietnamese 你 (nễ) meaning "you". This was the birth name of Nguyễn Nễ (1761-1805), a poet and official of the Tây Sơn dynasty, and the elder brother of poet Nguyễn Du.
Means "to respect, show deference" in Vietnamese.
The name of the Irish god of water, cognate to Neptune.
Feminine form of Neacșu. This name was borne by the second wife of Alexandru cel Bun.

Neacșu's letter, written in 1521, is the oldest surviving document available in Old Romanian that can be reliably dated. Written using Cyrillic, it was sent by Neacșu Lupu, a merchant from Câmpulung, Wallachia (now Romania) to Johannes Benkner, the mayor of Brassó, Kingdom of Hungary (now Brașov, Romania), warning him about the imminent attack of the Ottoman Empire on Transylvania.
Neagoe Basarab (c.1459 – 15 September 1521) was the Voivode (Prince) of Wallachia between 1512 and 1521.

Possibly means "newer, younger", derived from Ancient Greek νεαρός (nearos) "young, youthful, new". In Greek mythology this was the name of several figures, including an Oceanid, one of the Niobids, and a nymph and minor goddess of Thrinakia, a mythical island, consort of the sun god Helios. Her name may be descriptive of the dawn sun, and she was probably the personification of the sun's risings. This name was also borne by a 4th-century BC Greek hetaira.
A character in the Protector of the Small series by Tamora Pierce.
From Ancient Greek νέος (neos) meaning "new, fresh, young" and ἀλκή (alke) meaning "strength, prowess". Nealces was an ancient Greek painter from Sicyon.
Transferred use of the surname Neale.
Transferred use of the surname Nealey.
Feminine form of Neal or Neil. Has also been used as a diminutive of Cornelius.
Either a feminine form of Neal or a diminutive of Cornelia.
Derived from the Irish word neamh meaning "heaven, sky".

Latinized form of Neandros. However, in modern times, this name is best known as a surname - the most prominent bearer of which is the German theologian and hymn writer Joachim Neander (1650-1680). His paternal grandfather had translated the family's surname of Neumann (which literally means "new man") to Greek and then romanized it.
French form of Neandros via Neander.

Italian and Spanish form of Neandros via Neander. A known bearer of this name was Neandro Schilling Campos (1875-1949), a prominent Chilean educator. A high school located in the Chilean city of San Fernando was named after him.
Means "young warrior" in Ancient Greek, derived from νέος (neos) meaning "young, youthful" as well as "new, fresh" and ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man".
Transferred use of the surname Néanne.

Derived from Νεάπολη (Neapoli), the name of several places in modern Greece. These places were originally called Νεάπολις (Neapolis), which means "new city" in ancient Greek, as it is derived from the Greek adjective νέος (neos) meaning "new, young" combined with the Greek noun πόλις (polis) meaning "city".
Possibly an Anglicized form of the surname Nerby.
Catalan form of Nearchos via Nearchus.
Italian feminine form of Greek Nearchos, predominantly found in the Emilia-Romagna region.
Russian form of Nearchos via Nearchus.
Derived from the elements the first being νέος (neos) "new" and the second is either derived from Greek ἀρχός (archos) "master" or from Greek ἀρχή (arche) "origin, source".
Latinized form of Nearchos. Used by a Christian saint.
Italian, Portuguese and Spanish form of Nearchos via Nearchus.
Croatian form of Nearchos via Nearchus.
"Neariah" was a descendant of David, and father of Elionenai. He was the son of Shemaiah.
Variant of Nesa, traditionally found in central Grisons.
This was the name of an Irish saint; variant of Nessa 3

From nb, "lord," and Amon, one of the chief gods of Ancient Egypt, whose name Jmn means "hidden one." Nebamun therefore means something like "my lord is Amun." Nebamun was a scribe and grain accountant known for the remarkable scenes painted on his tomb walls around 1350 BCE.
Nebat, meaning "Sprout," an Ephrathite of Zereda, was the father of Jeroboam.

From Egyptian nb-ḫꜣ-st-nb.t, possibly meaning "(he is) the ruler of all under his throne", from Egyptian nb "lord, master", ḫꜣ "herd", st "throne", nb "lord, master", and .t "you, your". This was the name of a prince of the Nineteenth Dynasty during the New Kingdom.

Latinized form of the Greek form of Hebrew נדבאי (Nadvay). Nebedeus was the father of Ananias, the Jewish high priest from about 47 to 59 AD. Ananias is mentioned in both Acts 23 and the writings of Josephus, but only Josephus mentions the name of his father, Nebedeus.
Ancient Egyptian masculine name meaning "Lord at the Horizon".

From Egyptian nbt meaning "lady, mistress". Name borne by several prominent ancient Egyptian women, including the first known female vizier in Egyptian history; she served under Pepi I. Her daughters Ankhesenpepi I and II later became consorts of Pepi I.

From Egyptian nbt-ꜥḥ meaning "lady of the palace", derived from nbt meaning "lady" combined with ꜥḥ meaning "palace". This was the name of a 14th-century BC Egyptian princess, a daughter of the pharaoh Amenhotep III.
Possibly derived from Egyptian nbt "lady, mistress" combined with an uncertain second element.
Means "lady of the offerings" or "satisfied lady" in Ancient Egyptian. This was the female counterpart of Atum and female principle of creation.
Possibly derived from Egyptian nbt "lady, mistress" combined with uncertain elements.
From Egyptian nbt-nht meaning "lady of the sycamore tree", derived from nbt "lady, mistress" combined with nht "sycamore tree".

From Egyptian nb.t-tꜢwj meaning "lady of the two lands", derived from nbt "lady, mistress" combined with tꜣ "land, realm, country" and .wj "the two of them", together referring to Upper and Lower Egypt as a single entity. This was used as a royal title as well as a given name.

From Egyptian nb-kꜣ meaning "lord of the soul", from Egyptian nb "lord, master, ruler" combined with kꜣ "soul". This was the throne name of an ancient Egyptian pharaoh of the Third Dynasty during the Old Kingdom period, in the 27th century BCE.
Means "the lord of the truth is Re" in Egyptian.
From Serbian не (ne) meaning "not" and бој (boj), from бојати се (bojati se), meaning "to fear". Therefore the name means "fearless".

From Egyptian nb-rꜥ, of highly attested etymology. It could highly mean "lord of the sun (of Horus)" since the sun had not yet become the object of divine adoration during his lifetime, derived from Egyptian nb "lord" and rꜥ "sun". This was the Horus name of the second early Egyptian king of the 2nd Dynasty

Nebraska is derived from transliteration of the archaic Otoe words Ñí Brásge (contemporary Otoe Ñí Bráhge), or the Omaha Ní Btháska meaning "flat water", after the Platte River that flows through the state.

From Egyptian nb-sn-rꜥ, meaning "their lord is Ra", from Egyptian nb "lord, master" combined with sn "they, them" combined with the Egyptian God Ra. This was the name of an Egyptian pharaoh of the 14th Dynasty of Egypt during the Second Intermediate Period.
Means "the lady of the fields" in Ancient Egyptian. This was the name of an Egyptian fertility goddess and wife of Khnum.
Probably means "the Two Ladies are satisfied".
Ancient Egyptian feminine name meaning "The two crowns on the head of her father".

Means "mist, fog, vapor" in Latin, ultimately from the Proto-Indo-European root *nebh- "cloud". In astronomy, a nebula is an interstellar cloud of gas and dust where stars are formed.Nebula is the name of a fictional character appearing in American comic books published by Marvel Comics. Created by Roger Stern and John Buscema, the character first appeared in 'The Avengers' 257 (July 1985). Originally depicted as a supervillain, Nebula was later depicted as an antihero and member of the Guardians of the Galaxy.
Means "left behind, survivor", derived from Nahuatl cahua, meaning "to leave, to abandon something; to be left, remain, survive".
Meaning uncertain, possibly related to Necahual.
Means "salvation, liberation" in Turkish, ultimately from Arabic نجاة (najāh).

From Latin necessitas meaning "unavoidableness, inevitableness, necessity, compulsion, force, exigency" as well as "fate, destiny, law of nature". In Roman mythology Necessitas was the personification of necessity, equivalent to the Greek goddess Ananke. She is depicted in works of art as being 'armed with a nail, wherewith to fix the decrees of Fate'.

Variant of Nehmetawy, the name of an Egyptian goddess from the New Kingdom period. Her name probably means “she who embraces the needy.” She was depicted in images as a woman breastfeeding a child, associated with motherhood. Sometimes, she was considered the wife of Neheb-Kau.
Meaning unknown, possibly a short form of Anésia.
Diminutive of Bernice, Denise and other names containing the sound nees.

Necile is the wood nymph in the the 1902 novel 'The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus' written by L. Frank Baum and illustrated by Mary Cowles Clark. In this story Necile is the adoptive mother of Santa Claus. From this book were made many adaptations.
Variant of Nicole. Necole was given to 60 girls in 1979 according to the SSA.
French form of Nektarios via Nectarius.

Of uncertain origin and meaning. One theory suggests, however, that this name might be derived from Proto-Celtic *nixto- "clean".This was the name of a sixth-century saint known as Saint Nectan who was said to be of Welsh birth and a son of the legendary Brychan Brycheiniog.
Greek form of Egyptian nḫt-nb.f meaning "the strong one of his lord", derived from Egyptian nḫt "strong, victorious" and nb "lord, master, ruler" combined with the suffix .f "he, him, his".
English form derived from either the Greek Nectanebos or Nectanebis. This was the name of the two last pharaohs of the Thirtieth Dynasty of Egypt.

Greek form of Egyptian nḫt-ḥr-ḥbt meaning "victorious is Horus of Hebyt", derived from the name of the Egyptian god Horus combined with nḫt "strong, victorious" and ḥbt "Hebyt", a village in Lower Egypt that contains the remains of an ancient Egyptian temple.
Derived from the English word nectar meaning "sweet". A known bearer of the name is the American actress Nectar Rose (1974-).
Portuguese form of Nektarios via Nectarius.
Spanish form of Nektarios via Nectarius.
Semi-latinized form of Nektarios. The proper and full latinization of the name is Nectarius.
Latinized form of Nektarios. This was the name of several saints.
Presumed to be a feminine name, found on a mediaeval Pictish cross slab.

From the name of a river, possibly related to Proto-Indo-European *ned- "thundering, roaring, rushing". This was the name of one of the nurses of infant Zeus in Greek mythology, a nymph said to have given her name to the river Neda as well as a nearby settlement (now called Eira).

Means "Yahweh is generous" in Hebrew, derived from the verb נָדַב (nadav) meaning "to give willingly" (by implication "to be noble"; also compare Nadab) and יָהּ (yah) referring to the Hebrew God. This name was borne by one of the sons of the Judean king Jeconiah.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نضال (see Nidal).
Nedaxe Seteney was a Circassian princess

Sicilian diminutive of Antonietta as well as a Sicilian form of Nella. The name was also adopted into Hungarian usage. Furthermore, this name is borne by the main female role in the opera 'Pagliacci'.

Latinized form of the Greek form of Hebrew נדבאי (Nadvay). Nebedeus was the father of Ananias, the Jewish high priest from about 47 to 58 AD. Ananias is mentioned in both Acts 23 and the writings of Josephus, but only Josephus mentions the name of his father, Nebedeus.
Directly taken from Breton nedeleg "Christmas", this name is considered a Breton cognate of Noël.
An elaboration and feminisation of Ned.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نضال (see Nidal).
Allegedly a truncated form of Enedina.

Meaning “sweet one” in Ancient Egyptian. This was the name of the first known named pet cat, who belonged to Puimre, Second Priest of Amun in the 15th century BCE. It was also borne by a son of Pharaoh Amenhotep II.
Transferred use of the surname Nedley.
Variant of Nedley. A notable bearer of this name is the Dutch jazz musician and composer Nedly Elstak (1931-1989).
It means child of God in Igbo.

Inspired by the name of a fictional place from the 1905 novel Nedra by George Barr McCutcheon. In the novel, Nedra is an island where some of the protagonists are stranded, but the cover illustration featuring a lady probably gave the impression that it was a personal name belonging to a female character. This name was then reused for several characters in early films.
Means "rarity" in Turkish, ultimately from Arabic ندرة (nudra).
Transferred use of the surname Nedrick.A notable bearer of this name is the American actor Nedrick Young (1914-1968).
Variant of Edward incorporating the diminutive Ned. It is the full name of Ned Flanders on 'The Simpsons'.
Derived from Persian نژاد (nežâd) meaning "descent, lineage".
Transferred use of the surname Needham.
derived from נאהבת meaning "beloved", which is a derivative of the root אהב meaning "love"
Norman and Anglo-Norman form of Njáll.
East and West Frisian variant of Neele and Finnish form of Nela.
This is the name of the wife of Ham according to the Book of Jubilees.
Variant of Nele.As an East Frisian name it was recorded from the 1500s onwards.
Diminutive of Cornelius or a transferred use of the surname Neeley.
Variant spelling of Nelie. A famous bearer of this name is Neelie Kroes (b. 1941), a Dutch politician and European Commissioner.
Neelix is a fictional character in the science fiction TV-series 'Star Trek: Voyager'. Neelix is also the stage name of a German DJ.
Diminutive of Cornelia via its short form Neele. As an East Frisian name it was recorded from the 1500s onwards.
In the Book of Jubilees, this name is used for the wife of Shem. It is likely from ancient Babylonian.
Variant of Neeltje. This was the name of possibly the mother of Rembrandt van Rijn, full name Neeltgen Willemsdochter van Zuytbrouck (1569-1640).

Coined by M. Morrisson for the protagonist of his novel 'Eesti-rahwa vabaduse võitluse üle' (1902). The origin and meaning of the name are uncertain, it is, however, likely that Morrison based the name on the old Livonian Meeme.
Italian and Corsican form of Nehemiah via Hellenized form Neemias.
Mostly the same as Neeraj. An feminization of Neeraj, in a sense.
One who is being led, as in being led to knowledge or "to a path".
Alternate transcription of Hindi नीति (see Niti).
Variant transcription of Devanagari निबा: (see: Nibah)
The Hungarian word for the forget-me-not flower.
Perhaps an Armenian variant of Nefeli.
From Egyptian nfr meaning "beautiful, good, perfect".
From Egyptian nfr meaning "perfect, complete". This is the name of a character from Monster High.

Derived from nefere (nfr) meaning beautiful, perfect, good and fre (fr) meaning Ra, (the Egyptian sun god, often symbolized as the primary deity). Neferefre was the name of an ancient Egyptian pharaoh of the 5th Dynasty, who reigned for a brief period around c. 2446–2440 BCE.
From Egyptian nfr-ḥtp.s meaning "her peace is beautiful", derived from nfr "beautiful, good, perfect" combined with ḥtp "peace, satisfaction; mercy" and the suffix .s "she, her, hers".
From Egyptian nfr-ḥr meaning "beautiful of face", derived from nfr "beautiful, good, perfect" combined with ḥr "face".
From Egyptian nfr-ḥtp meaning "the beautiful one is content", derived from nfr "beautiful, good, perfect" combined with ḥtp "peace, satisfaction".
From Egyptian nfr-jb-rꜥ meaning "beautiful is the heart of Ra", derived from nfr "beautiful, good, perfect" combined with jb "heart, mind, emotions" and the name of the god Ra.
Neferkare was an Ancient Egyptian Pharaon during the 25th century BCE. He was the third king of the Fifth Dynasty.

Possibly from Egyptian nfr-kꜣ-mnw meaning "the soul of Min is beautiful", from nfr "beautiful, good" combined with ka "soul" combined with the name of the Egyptian god Min. It could also mean "the soul of the established is beautiful" from the passive participle mn "to establish". This was possibly the name of an Eighth Dynasty pharaoh during the First Intermediate Period.
Ancient Egyptian masculine name meaning "The beautiful soul of Sokar".

From Egyptian nfr-mꜣꜥt meaning "Maat is beautiful" or "with perfect justice", derived from nfr "beautiful, good, perfect" combined with the name of the goddess Maat, literally "truth, virtue, justice".
From Egyptian nfr-nfrw-rꜥ meaning "beauty of the beauties of Ra". This name was borne by a daughter of the 14th-century BC Egyptian pharaoh Akhenaten.

Possible meanings include "beautiful one who closes" or "one who does not close".In Egyptian mythology, the word nefertem described a lotus flower that arose from the primordial waters when the world was created. This concept later evolved into a sun god worshiped in Lower Egypt. He was depicted as a man wearing a headdress made of a lotus flower and two plumes.
Variant of Nefertari famously held by African-American Playboy model and actress Neferteri Plessy (1980-).
From Egyptian nfrtj, derived from nfr "beautiful, good, perfect". This is the name of the titular character in ‘The Prophecy of Neferti’, an ancient Egyptian literary text.
From Egyptian nfrt-jꜣbt meaning "beautiful one of the east".
Ancient Egyptian feminine name meaning "the beautiful one of kas" (the plural of ka, meaning "soul").
Contains the Ancient Egyptian word nfr, meaning "beautiful, good, perfect".
Ancient Egyptian feminine name meaning "the beauty of the king of Lower Egypt".

Means "the beauty of Ra".An Egyptian princess of the 18th Dynasty (c.1472 BCE - c.1462/1457 BCE), she was the only known child of the Pharaoh Thutmose II and his wife Queen Hatshepsut, who would later go on to become a Pharaoh herself.
Variant of Hnefi or from Old Norse nefi meaning "nephew".
Crimean Tatar and Turkish form of Nafiza.
Female form of Næfr. This is the name of a sorceress in Norse mythology.

Nefretiri is an alternate English transcription of the Ancient Egyptian Nfrt-jrj, meaning "the most beautiful", the name of the favourite wife of the Pharaoh Ramses II, often transcribed as Nefertari in English. This transcription was used in the popular 1956 film The Ten Commandments.

Supposedly the name of one of the three virgins sacrificed to Elkenah, as mentioned in the Book of Abraham. The Book of Abraham does not mention their names. This comes from Missaticum Biblia, which has portions similar to the Book of Abraham, though its origin has not been proven legitimate. Herein, they are called Zeptah, Lilith, and Nefritiri. This same information is has in the sacred books of one Mormon Fundamentalist sect.
Old Norse combination of nef 'nostril, nose' and steinn 'stone'.
Spanish form of Naphtali. In modern times it is sometimes used as a feminine name.
Possibly related to Middle Welsh nef "heaven" (compare nefoedd "heavens"), or udd "lord, prince".
Dawn - One of Ethiopian General who fought and defeated Italian army in the 19th Century in in a place called Dogali, Ethiopia.
In Inuit mythology, Negafook is a god of weather systems, particularly wintry cold ones.

column3: 願, 希, 望, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 願 (negai) meaning "wish" or other kanji which are pronounced the same way.
The name of an antagonist on the Hit TV show, The Walking dead.
The meaning of Negasi is ‘he will wear a crown’.

The Negev is the southern region of the land of Israel, desert area with a lot of sand, during the day it is very hot, and at night it is very cold. Derived from Hebrew נֶּגְבָּה (negba) meaning "southward".
Uyghur form of Nimat. A bearer is Nëghmet Raxman (1983-), a Uyghur-Chinese television host.
Croatian and Serbian cognate of Niegosław.

Name of a Gaulish goddess of commerce worshipped in what is now the Netherlands, whose worship was prevalent when the Romans arrived to the area. She is believed to be a goddess of the sea, divination, and the Otherworld. The etymology is unknown, even though linguists agree that its origin is not Latin. Theories include a derivation from Indo-European *nāu- "boat" (in which case it may have meant "seafarer" or "steerswoman"), a derivation from Proto-Germanic *nehwa "close", a derivation from the Proto-Indo-European root *neiH- "to lead", a combination of Celtic *halen– "sea" and *ne- "on, at" and a combination of Indogermanic nebh "moisture, wetness" and either hel "to cover, to hide" or Gothic linnan "to disappear; to leave".

The exact meaning of Nehanda is debated, but it is often interpreted as meaning "she who listens" or "our beloved daughter has returned." This was the name of Zimbabwean spiritual medium Nehanda Nyakasikana (1840-1898). who led the fight against the British colonizers in what is now Zimbabwe in the 19th Century.
Means "he who belongs to the plow" in Egyptian.

Means "(one who) brings together".In Egyptian mythology he was originally the explanation of the cause of binding of Ka and Ba, two aspects of the soul, after death, hence the meaning of his name. Because of this, he was said to have guarded the entrance to Duat, the underworld. He was typically depicted as a snake with two head (and sometimes just one). As a snake god, he was also thought to have power over snake bites and, by extension, other poisonous bites. He was seen as the son of Renenutet and Geb.

Nehebu-Kau is a name that harks back to ancient Egypt. According to Egyptian mythology, this was the name of an ancient deity, a serpent god linked to death and funerary rites. In images, he was represented as a snake with human legs. Sometimes, he was considered the husband of the goddess Nehmetawy. There are many possible meanings for the name, such as “overturner of doubles”, “collector of souls” and “that which gives Ka.”

column5: ne-eh-MEE-a(Hawaiian, Biblical Hawaiian, Māori, Afrikaans, Biblical Finnish)|/ne.he.ˈmiː.a/(German)
column12: Afrikaans, Finnish, German, Hawaiian, and Māori form of Nehemiah.
French form of Nehemiah. While this is originally a masculine name, it has also been used as a feminine name in recent years.
Variant of Nehemiah used in the Swedish and Norwegian translation of the Bible.
From the nḥm.t-ˁw3ỉ; meaning "She who embraces those in need", the name of a minor Ancient Egyptian goddess, the wife of Nehebu-kau or, occasionally, Thoth.
From Egyptian nḥrj, of uncertain etymology. Possibly related to nḥr "to resemble, match up to", or to nḥ "prayer".

Possibly from Hebrew נחושת‎ (n'khóshet) "copper". Nehushta was the wife of King Jehoiakim and daughter of Elnathan ben Achbor of Jerusalem, according 2 Kings 24:8 in the Old Testament. She was also the mother of King Jehoiachin.
Variant of Néiser. A famous bearer is Ecuadorian soccer player Néicer Reasco (1977-).
Formed from the German name elements neid "necessity, need; envy, jealousy" and hart "hard".A notable namesake is the Medieval German poet and minnesinger Neidhart von Reuental.
From the given name Eneida and mar meaning "sea".
Form of Nephele used by the novelist Boccaccio in his work 'The Decameron' (1350).
Derived from French neige "snow". The name is ultimately derived from the title of the Virgin Mary Notre-Dame des Neiges "Our Lady of the Snows" (compare Nieves).
Alternate transcription of Arabic نائلة (see Naila) chiefly used in North Africa.
Possibly a feminine form of Neil. This name was born by Filipino actress Neile Adams (1932-)

Possibly a variant of Nelia (a short form of Cornelia) influenced by the spelling of Neil. A known bearer was Neilia Hunter Biden (1942-1972), the first wife of the 46th American president Joe Biden. She died in a car crash in 1972 with their one-year-old daughter, Naomi; their two sons, Beau and Hunter, were critically injured but survived.
Variant of Nelson, influenced by Neil.
Derived from נְעִימָה “melody, tone, musical arrangement" derived from the root נעם "gave a good feeling; to please"
Variant of Nena, traditionally found in the Surselva region.

column3: 音色, 寧色(Japanese Kanji)|ねいろ(Japanese Hiragana)|ネイロ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name is used as 音色 meaning "tone colour, timbre," a combination of 音 (in, on, -non, oto, ne) meaning "noise, sound" and 色 (shiki, shoku, iro) meaning "colour."It can also be written as 寧色 with 寧 (nei, mushi.ro) meaning "mild, gentle."
Variant of Nesa, traditionally found in the Engadine valley.

Transferred use of the German surname Neisser. Ulrich Neisser was a German bussinessman who migrated to Peru in 1936 and held the title of mayor of Arequipa from 1956 to 1966. It is likely that the name Néiser was popularised after him.
Possibly an invented name based on Deisy.
Catalan form of Neith. This name is extremely rare and has been used only once in Catalonia, in which case it was part of a hyphenated name.

Neit likely came from the Proto-Celtic *nei-t-, meaning “impassioned” or “fighting.”Neit was the Irish god of war. A pan-Celtic war deity known to the Romans, Neit was celebrated for his mastery of war and his ferocity.Neit was the Celtic god of war and husband to both Nemain and Badb, members of the fearsome Morrígan. He was the father of Fomorian Dot, grandfather of the fearsome Fomorian king, Balor of the Evil Eye, and the Dagda’s uncle. Although he fathered members of the Fomorian race that predated the Children of Danu, Neit joined the Tuatha dé Danann, including his wives and nephew, in their war for dominion of Ireland. At the Second Battle of Moytura in County Sligo, Neit fell, but the Tuatha dé Danann were ultimately victorious in their effort to take control of the Emerald Isle.
Lithuanian adoption of Nate, in use among Lithuanians since the middle of the 2000s.
From Egyptian nt-ḥtp meaning "Neith is merciful", derived from the name of the goddess Neith combined with ḥtp "peace, satisfaction; mercy". This was the name of a 31st century BC queen consort.

This is the name of a character in the popular manga and anime series Naruto. In his case, the name may come from the word (written as 捩子, 捻子, 螺子 or 螺旋) meaning "screw," which can be referred to his Eight Trigrams Palms Revolving Heaven.Though it's not given as a first name, Neji is being used as a surname.
Variant of Nejib influenced by French orthography.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نجيب (see Najib) chiefly used in Tunisia.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نجيبة (see Najiba) chiefly used in Tunisia.
Diminutive of Neja, occasionally used as a given name in its own right.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نجم الدين (see Najm Ad-Din) chiefly used in North Africa.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نجم الدين (see Najm Ad-Din), chiefly used in Tunisia.
From Japanese 音 (ne) meaning "sound" combined with 奏 (kana) meaning "play music, complete". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means “sorrows.” Form of the name Nekane.

Possibly from Egyptian n-kꜣw-bꜣ, perhaps meaning "(the one) belonging to the souls and power", from Egyptian n(j) "of, belonging to" combined with kꜣw, the plural form of kꜣ "soul" combined with bꜣ "working power, active power". This was the name listed by Manetho's Epitome. He was one of the early kings of the 26th Dynasty of Egypt. However, his status as king is not confirmed by any contemporary documents and he may well be an invention of later Saite rulers to legitimize their kingship.

The name of a princess of Abyssinia (present-day Ethiopia) in Samuel Johnson's novella 'The History of Rasselas, Prince of Abissinia' (1759). Its origins are uncertain, though it may be a derivative of Nicaula, the name for the queen of Sheba given by the antique Jewish author Flavius Josephus. Alternatively it may derive from Amharic naka "to wake" or kaye "scarlet".In the English-speaking world, it has been in occasional use from the early 1800s onwards.
From Egyptian nxbt meaning "of Nekheb", a city in Upper Egypt. Nekhbet was the tutelary deity of Upper Egypt, counterpart to Wadjet. She was often depicted as a vulture.

column3: ნეკო(Georgian)|寧子, 根子, 音子, 子子, 眠子(Japanese Kanji)|ねこ(Japanese Hiragana)|ネコ(Japanese Katakana)|Неко(Nenets)
猫葉, 猫波, 猫羽(Japanese Kanji)|ねこは(Japanese Hiragana)|ネコハ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 猫 (neko) meaning "cat" combined with 葉 (ha) meaning "leaf", 波 (ha) meaning "wave", or 羽 (ha) meaning "feather, plume, wing". Other kanji or combinations of kanji can form this name as well.
Means "auspicious, bringer of good luck (of a person)."
Derived from Albanian nektar "nectar" and, figuratively, "best part".
Macedonian form of Nektarios via Nectarius.
Croatian and Serbian form of Nektarios via Nectarius.
The name originates from the ancient Greek word nekyia (νέκυια), which describes a rite or ritual used to summon the spirits of the dead to question them about the future (a form of necromancy)
Polish diminutive of Aniela, Helena, Kornelia and Eleonora and Slovene diminutive of Eleonora, Kornelija and Anela.
Gift with purpose. Composition if Nia (meaning purpose) and Nala (meaning gift)
Combination of Nelly and Norwegian borg "castle, fortification".
Possibly a variant of Neleh, boosted in popularity by Neleh Dennis's appearance on Survivor in 2002. Neleah was given to 22 girls in 2002.
Helen spelled backwards.The name's usage was at its highest in 2002 when Neleh Davis (née Dennis) participated and became runner-up in the competitive reality television show 'Survivor: Marquesas'.

Possibly derived from the Mycenaean Greek name ne-e-ra-wo (Nehelawos) meaning "he who saves his people, leads his people home", composed of νέομαι (neomai) meaning "to return, come home" and λαός (laos) meaning "people, folk". Alternatively, it could derive from Ancient Greek νηλεής (neleés) meaning "merciless, pitiless; unpitied"; otherwise of pre-Greek origin. In Greek mythology, Neleus was a king of Pylos and twin brother to King Pelias of Iolcus, both sons of Poseidon and Tyro. This was also the name of a disciple of Aristotle and Theophrastus.
Short form of Cornelia or Kornelia.
A recent coinage gaining traction in 2020/21 in Germany, maybe derived from Cornelianus or created as a masculine form to Nele.
Dutch and English diminutive of Cornelia.
Diminutive of Neli and perhaps also of Nineli and Vineli.
Afrikaans and Norwegian short form of Cornelius.
Diminutive of names that end in -nela, such as Petronela.
Medieval Polish diminutive of Kornel and Korneliusz.
Latinized form of Niall. It was borne by Niall Ó Glacáin (1563-1653), an Irish physician who was known for working to treat victims of bubonic plague.

A character in the works of JRR Tolkien. The name is derived from the fictional Sindarin language, and is of uncertain etymology. The first element of the word is likely the Noldorin word nel meaning "three, tri-", the Sindarin word neldor meaning "beech" or the Sindarin root word nyel meaning "song, sweet sound". The second element may be the Sindarin word lass meaning "leaf" or the Sindarin word glas meaning "joy".
Perhaps a variant of Nelborg. It is mainly used in the county of Trøndelag in Norway.
Dutch diminutive of Cornelia and Petronella, formed using the diminutive suffix -ke. A literary bearer is Dutch novelist Nelleke Noordervliet (1945-), born Petronella.
Combination of the Dutch names Nel and Jan 1.
Perhaps an altered form of Lenora.
Short form of Anelma, Ihanelma and Sanelma.
Combination of Nela and the Slavic element slava.
Likely a variant spelling of Nelson. A notable bearer of this name was the American actor Nelsan Ellis (1977-2017).
Likely a variant of Nielsine (also Nilsine) often used by 19th century immigrants to the US.
Diminutive of Nela/Nella, itself a diminutive of names such as Kornelia, Helena, Aniela etc.
Welsh diminutive of Elin or Elinor.
Meaning unknown. It could possibly be an elaboration of Nell.
Means "third Finwë". In Tolkien's Legendarium this is the father-name of Maedhros.
Either a variation of Nemea or the word "amen" spelled backwards.
Nemamiah is considered the angel of just causes
Means "good, blessing, benefit" in Azerbaijani, ultimately from Arabic نعمة (ni'mah).
Alternate transcription of Arabic نعمات (see Nimat), as well as the Persian, Uzbek and Tajik form.
Derived from ne'mat meaning "blessings" and bibi meaning "learned woman".
Derived from ne'mat meaning "blessings" and oy meaning "moon".

Means "wooded district", derived from Ancient Greek νέμος (nemos) meaning "wooded pasture, glade". In Greek mythology, this was the name of a naiad of the springs of the town of Nemea in Argolis, a daughter of the river god Asopos. Alternatively, Nemea may have been another name for Pandeia, a daughter of Zeus and Selene.

Means "sanctuary, person with privilege" in Old Irish, derived from Proto-Celtic *nemetom "sacred place, sanctuary". In medieval Irish legend, this was the name of the leader of the Nemedians, the third group of people to settle in Ireland.
Means "to add, increase, enhance" in Mongolian.

Means "unerring, infallible; sure, truthful" in Ancient Greek. This was the name of one of the nereids in Greek mythology, known for her wise and "unerring" good counsel. Historical records show that this was otherwise used as a masculine name.
Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Nemesianus.
Extended form of Nemesius. This name was borne by a Roman poet from the 3rd century AD.

Meaning "sacred area", from the Celtic 'nemeto', itself from 'nemeton', a term designating Gaulish religious spaces.Nemetona is a Celtic goddess believed to be the eponymous god of the Germano-Celtic people known as the Nemetes. Artifacts worshiping her have overwhelming been found in and around their former territory. What inscriptions of her that survive correlate her to the Roman god of war, Mars, possibly meaning she was a goddess of war.

The name of one of the Morrígna/war goddesses in Irish mythology, Némhain appears in stories such as an Táin Bó Cuailgne. The etymology of the name is debated, but it is theorised to stem from neimneach, meaning "venom", and neimed, meaning "heaven" or "sanctuary".

column3: 音実, 子美, 音光, 子実, 音美, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ネーミ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Nemi is the title character of the comic strip Nemi (1997), written and drawn by Norwegian cartoonist Lisa Myhre. Its origin and meaning are unknown, there have, however, been speculations that Myhre might have based the name on the name of the Italian town and lake which is ultimately derived from from Latin nemus Aricinum "grove of Ariccia".

From Sanskrit नेमि (nemi) meaning "rim, felly (of a wheel)" and नाथ (nātha) meaning "master, lord". In Jain tradition this is the name of the 22nd of the 24 tirthankaras (enlightened spiritual teachers).
Of unknown origin and meaning. Current theories include a derivation from the masculine name Nils as well as an adoption of Latin nemine, the ablative form of Nemo.
Nemiza is the Slavic god of the wind.
Means "many stars" or "constellation of stars" in the Waorani language. This name is borne by a Waorani climate activist.
French form of Nemorino and French masculine form of Nemorina. This is the name of the main character's love interest in the play Estelle by Jean-Pierre Claris de Florian.
Spanish and Italian form of Nemorius.
Derived from Latin nemus, meaning "grove, pasture". This name was borne by a French 5th-century martyr who was beheaded by Attila the Hun.
Polish nie "not" + Polish mój "mine".This name is a so-called 'substitutional name', given to a child instead of a real name to deflect attention from evil powers.
From Egyptian nmtj meaning "one who travels" or "the strider", derived from nmj "to travel, traverse". This was the name of an ancient Egyptian falcon god, the god of ferrymen.
From Egyptian nmtj-nḫt meaning "Nemti is strong", derived from the name of the god Nemti combined with nḫt "strength, victory".
From Egyptian nmtj-m-zꜣ.f meaning "Nemty is his protection", derived from the name of the god Nemti combined with m "in, in the role of", zꜣ "protection", and the suffix .f "he, him, his".

Apparently means "Circumcised of God" in Hebrew. The name alternates with Jemuel for the same Biblical person.The biblical clan of the Nemuelites derive their name from an ancestor with this first name. Nemuel is also the name of two Israelities mentioned in the Bible.
From the name of the longest river in Lithuania.
Means "to change into" or "should" in Vietnamese.

column3: 音菜, 音奈, 寧那, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|Νένα(Greek)
column12: Short form of Nedeljka, Nevenka and other names beginning with Ne-.
Of uncertain meaning, likely linked to rain. Nenaunir is the villainous god of rain in Maasai mythology, being depicted as a rainbow snake or even a half-man half-lion.
Means either "to be idle, inactive, without profit" or "to have lived" in Nahuatl.
Possibly means "one who is in vain", derived from Nahuatl nencahui "to be in vain".

Muisca god of festivities, dance and drunkenness. Also the protector of artists and craftspeople. Assisted the Muisca people with building their homes, despite being drunk. When the Muisca celebrated with song, dance and chicha (a fermented maize drink), Nencatacoa danced and partied with them.
Means "negligent one" or "abandoned one" in Nahuatl.

It refers to abstinence from intoxicating wine (i.e. physical sobriety), so a more figurative meaning of the word would be "sober, clear-headed, temperate". The word is ultimately derived from the Greek verb νήφω (nepho) meaning "to drink no wine, to be sober". Also compare the Greek noun νεφέλιον (nephelion) meaning "small cloud", which is a diminutive of Greek νεφέλη (nephele) "cloud" - itself ultimately derived from Greek νέφος (nephos) meaning "cloud, mass of clouds". These may be etymologically related to the aforementioned nephalios and nepho. Finally, in Greek mythology, Nephalion was the name of one of the four sons of Minos.
