column12: Probably from Thai ปริญญา (bpà-rin-yaa) meaning "knowledge, understanding".
Either an elaboration of Prince with the suffix -ella or a blending of Prince and Priscilla. This name is chiefly used in Ghana and, in the United States, among Black Americans.
From the word princely, ultimately from prince and -ly.
Feminine form of Principius. This was the name of a 4th-century Roman virgin who was a follower of St. Marcella.

From Latin prī̆ncipium "beginning, origin, commencement", derived from Latin prī̆nceps "first, chief, distinguished". This was the name of a 5th-century Bishop of Soissons and a brother of St. Remigius.

A noun-name. The prinias are a genus of small birds belonging to the passerine bird family Cisticolidae. They are often also alternatively classed in the Old World warbler family, Sylviidae. The name of the genus is derived from the Javanese prinya, the local name for the bar-winged prinia. This word has only recently come into use as a name.
Alternate transcription of Thai ปริญญา (see Parinya).
Ecclesiastical title, derived from the Latin adjective for "earlier, first".
From priore 'prior', a nickname or occupational name, which probably most often originated as an occupational name for a servant of a prior or some important lay dignitary.
Combination of Priscilla or Prisca and the suffix -lyn.
Diminutive of Priscila, often used in Spanish.

Galician, Italian and Spanish form of Priscian.

A character in "Mother Bombie" an Elizabethan era stage play, by John Lyly.

Possibly popularized by the Mexican singer-songwriter Prisma (1948-), real name Silvia Tapia Alcázar. Active as a solo artist in the 1980s, she was known to give out prism necklaces at her concerts (that is, pieces of jewelry featuring a crystal or gemstone cut into a prism shape - which can be a simple triangular shape or a more complex geometric form - that is designed to refract light, creating a spectrum of colors and a dazzling effect).

From prit meaning "(nice) appearance" and gent "lineage, family".

Derived from Sanskrit प्रीति (prīti) meaning "pleasure, joy, love".
From Sanskrit प्रीति (prīti) meaning "pleasure, joy, love" combined with पाल (pāla) meaning "guard, protector".
Yiddish form of פְּרִי (peri) meaning "fruit" in Hebrew.
Catalan and Provençal form of Privatus.
Derived from Latin privatus "personal, individual, private, peculiar, separate". This was the name of a saint from Roman Gaul, who lived in the 3rd or 4th century AD.
From Javanese priya meaning "man, boy" combined with adi meaning "first" in Indonesian or "beautiful, good, valuable" in Javanese.
Derived from Sanskrit प्रिया (priyā) meaning "beloved, dear".
From Thai ปรียา (priya) meaning "darling, beloved" and นันท์ (nan) meaning "pleasure, joy, delight".
It is name used in Hindu religion and this name basically found in Indian Name. And it also know the brave warrior of the mughal king.
Means "pleasant, attractive" in Sinhala, derived from Sanskrit प्रियंकर (priyankara) meaning "agreeable, amiable".
From Sanskrit प्रिय (priya) meaning "beloved, dear" and अंशु (aṃśu) meaning "ray of light, beam, splendour".
From Sinhalese ප්‍රිය (priya) meaning "dear, beloved, pleasant, nice", ultimately from Sanskrit प्रिय (priya).

From Javanese priyatna meaning "to be careful, to remember".
From Javanese priya meaning "man, male", ultimately from Sanskrit प्रिय (priya).
From Javanese priya meaning "man, boy" combined with either the masculine suffix -na or the word ana meaning "being, having, holding".
Latinized form of Proandros. This was the name of a strategos of the Aetolian Confederacy, who lived in the 2nd century BC.
Derived from Ancient Greek πρό (pro) meaning "before, forth, forward" combined with ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man".

Short form of Prometheus. Derived from Greek προμηθεια (prometheia) meaning "foresight, forethought". In Greek myth he was the Titan who gave the knowledge of fire to mankind. For doing this he was punished by Zeus, who had him chained to a rock and caused an eagle to feast daily on his liver, which regenerated itself each night. He was eventually freed by Herakles.
Catalan form of Probus and variant of Probo.
Alternate transcription of Bengali প্রবীর (see Prabir).
Form of Probus in various languages. Catalan variant of Probe.

Roman family name (cognomen), derived from Latin probus, which means "good, virtuous, able, decent". One Roman emperor bore this name. There also were several saints of this name, the most famous of whom was martyred in 304 AD together with Andronicus and Tarachus.

Means "a going forward, advance, progress" in Latin. According to Christian legend Saint Processus was the name of a Roman soldier who guarded the apostles Peter and Paul when they were imprisoned at the Mamertine Prison in Rome, then converted to Christianity and was martyred.
Polish form of Prochoros via it's Latinized form Prochorus.
Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Proklos via Proclus.

Latinized form of Proklos. Proclus of Constantinople (c. 390 – 24 July 446) was the archbishop of Constantinople from 434 until his death. His contributions to the theology of the developing cult of the Virgin Mary place him among the early and foremost Marian theologians. He is venerated as a saint in the Catholic Church, the Eastern Catholic Churches, the Eastern Orthodox Church, and Oriental Orthodoxy.
Italian and Spanish form of Prokopios.
Latinized form of Prokopios. This name was borne by several Byzantines, Romans and saints.
Portuguese and Spanish form of Prochoros via it's Latinized form Prochorus.
Transferred use of the surname Proctor.
Latinized form of Prokyon. As a Roman name it's a cognomen.

Means "sold, sale" in Serbo-Croatian, from a passive adjective form of Serbo-Croatian pròdati "to sell", said to be used as an apotropaic name bestowed upon a child who has been handed over to a person who was safe from evil spirits. A famous bearer of the name was Bulgarian wrestler Prodan Gardzhev (1936-2003).

Feminine form of Prodan. Like its masculine counterpart, it is derived from the verb prodati, "to sell", literally meaning "sold". It was once given to divert evil spirits by telling them the child has already been " sold away ".
Latinized form of Prodikos. A notable bearer of this name was the Greek philosopher Prodicus of Ceos (5th century BC).

Means "prodigies" in Spanish, taken from the Mexican titles of the Virgin Mary, La Virgen de los Prodigios and Nuestra Señora de los Prodigios, meaning "The Virgin of the Prodigies" and "Our Lady of the Prodigies" respectively.She is the patroness of Tiripetío, located in the municipality of Morelia in the state of Michoacán.

Derived from the Greek adjective πρόδικος (prodikos) meaning "judged first", which consists of Greek πρό (pro) meaning "before, forth, forward" and the Greek noun δίκη (dike) meaning "justice, judgement" as well as "custom, usage".
Alternate transcription of Bengali প্রদীপ্ত (see Pradipta).
Modern Greek diminutive of Prodromos, as it contains the modern Greek diminutive suffix -άκης (-akis). This name is typically only used informally, meaning: it does not appear on birth certificates.
Diminutive of Profira, not generally used as a given name in its own right.
Transferred use of the surname Profit.
From Spanish progreso meaning "progress". In Spain, it was specially used during the Second Spanish Republic by republican parents who were eager to choose names related to republican values.
Latinized form of Prohairesios. This was the name of a 4th-century Armenian Christian teacher and rhetorician.

Probably from Greek προαίρεσις (proaíresis) meaning "choice, preference, resolution", ultimately derived from πρό (pro) "before, in front of" and αἵρεσις (hairesis) "taking, receiving, choice, purpose".

Means "pursuit of the foremost, pursuit in advance" in Ancient Greek, derived from (pro) "before" and ἰωκή (ioke) meaning "rout, pursuit, attack". In Greek mythology, Proioxis was the personification of onrush or persuit in battle, probably one of the Machai, daemons of the battlefield.
Derived from Ancient Greek πρό (pro) meaning "before, forth, forward" combined with κλέος (kleos) meaning "glory".

Probably derived from Greek περκνός (perknos) meaning "dusky, dappled, dark-spotted", a word also used to refer to a kind of eagle. In Greek mythology, Prokne was the wife of the Thracian king Tereus, and fed him their own son, Itys, in revenge for the rape of her sister Philomela. Tereus pursued Prokne and Philomela, and eventually all three were transformed into birds, Prokne into a nightingale (or in Latin sources, a swallow).
Pet form of the name Prokop (Prokóp,-i).
Variant of Prokofiy used in Anton Checkov's short story, "The Orator".
Georgian form of Prokopios. As for Russia, Prokopi is a variant transcription of Prokopiy there.
Feminine form of Prokopios. This name was most notably borne by the empress consort of the Byzantine emperor Michael I Rangabe (9th century AD).
Bosnian and Croatian form of Procopius.
Croatian and Polish form of Proculus.

Derived from Ancient Greek πρό (pro) meaning "before" and κύων (*kyon)‎ meaning "dog". This is the name of the brightest star in the constellation Canis Minor, rising before Sirius in most northerly latitudes, hence its name meaning "before the dog".

From name of Пролеткульт (Proletkult), Soviet art organisation. It's name is contraction of Пролетарские культурно-просветительные организации (Proletarskiye kulturno-prosvetitelniye organizatsii) "Proletarian Cultural-Educational Organisation".

Derived from Greek πρό (pro) meaning "before, forth, forward" combined with the Greek noun λόχος (lochos) meaning "ambush", a word that later came to signify a tactical sub unit of the ancient Greek army. The word is ultimately derived from the Greek verb λοχάω (lochao) meaning "to lie in wait for, to waylay" as well as "to snare".Also compare the Greek verb προλοχίζω (prolochizo) meaning "to lay an ambuscade beforehand".
Latinized form of Prolochos. In Greek mythology, this is the name of one of the Lapiths, a tribe from Thessaly.

Means "champion, defender, foremost fighter" in Ancient Greek, derived from πρό (pro) "before" and μάχη (mache) "battle". This was the name of several figures in Greek mythology, as well as being an epithet of Athena, Heracles, and Hermes.
Derived from Ancient Greek πρό (pro) meaning "before" and μέδων (medon) meaning "ruler" (see Medo).
Bosnian, Croatian and Serbian form of Prometheus.
Italian and Spanish form of Prometheus.
Catalan, Portuguese and Romanian form of Prometheus.
Bulgarian, Russian and Ukrainian form of Prometheus.
Derived from Ancient Greek πρόμος (promos) meaning "foremost man, chief". In Greek mythology, Promeus was a Dolionian who was killed by the Argonaut Idas.

Derived from Greek πρώ (pro meaning "early (in the day)", a variant of πρωΐ (proi) meaning "early in the day, during morning", and ἄναξ (anax) meaning "master, lord, chief".In Greek mythology, Pronax is the son of king Talaus of Argos and his wife Lysimache.

Derived from Ancient Greek πρόνοος (pronoos) meaning "careful, prudent", composed of πρό (pro) "before" and νόος (noos) "mind, thought" (compare Pronoia). This was the name of several figures in Greek mythology, including one of the fifty Nereids, and an Argive princess as the daughter of the soothsayer Melampus, considered to be a seer in her own right.

Means "foresight, forethought, foreknowledge" or "providence" in Ancient Greek, derived from πρό (pro) "before" and νόος (noos) "mind, thought". This was the name of an Oceanid nymph in Greek mythology, sometimes called the mother of Deucalion by Prometheus. It was also an epithet of the goddess Athena used in Delphi.

Roman family name which was probably derived from Latin propero "to make haste, to be quick". Sextus Aurelius Propertius, better known as Propertius, was a 1st-century BC Roman poet. He was a contemporary of Virgil and Ovid.
Italian feminine form of Propertius. Properzia de' Rossi was a female marble sculptor of the Italian Renaissance.
From the English word prophecy, ultimately from Ancient Greek πρό (pró, “before”) and φημί (phēmí, “I tell”)
From the English word prophet, ultimately from Greek προφήτης (prophetes) meaning "one who speaks for a god" (itself from πρό (pro) "before" and φημί (phemi) "to speak, to declare").

Contracted form of Proversa, which means "forwards looking, turned toward the front" from Latin pro- "forward direction" and the verb vertere "to turn". Postverta and Prorsa were surnames of Carmenta, a Roman goddess of prophecy and childbirth. She was 'the backwards and forwards looking goddess', described as turning backward and looking at the past (Postverta) as well as looking into the future (Prorsa, i.e. Proversa); 'poets, however, have personified these attributes of Carmenta, and thus describe them as the companions of the goddess.' Prorsa was considered a goddess who averts breech birth (when a baby is born bottom first instead of head first).
Transferred use of the surname Prose.

From Greek proselênos meaning "older than the moon" or "before the moon", which was "an epithet used of the people of Arcadia, who prided themselves on their antiquity" (Sheard, 2011). This was the name of an elderly witch in Petronius' 1st-century novel 'The Satyricon'.

The first element of this name is derived from Polish prosić "to ask (for/somebody), to request, to beg". Also compare Croatian prositi "to beg" and Czech prosit "to ask for, to beg". The second element is derived from Slavic mir "peace". As such, the meaning of this name is roughly "to ask for peace".
Spanish and Galician feminine form of Prosperus.
Feminine form of Prosper and Prospero and diminutive form of Prospera.
Meaning unknown. This was the name of the daughter of Salomon, King of Brittany.

Means "celebrate in song, praise in addition" or "sing besides", from Ancient Greek πρό (pro) meaning "before" and ὕμνος (hymnos) meaning "song, hymn". This was the name of one of the Asterionides in Greek mythology, Naiads who nursed the goddess Hera in her infancy.
Dutch and Flemish form of Protasius, which came into being via the medieval Dutch form Protaes.
Medieval Dutch form of Protasius. A more modern form of this name is Protaas, even though that name is (also) very archaic in this day and age.

Derived from Ancient Greek πρῶτος (protos) meaning "first" combined with either ἀγορεύω (agoreuo) "to orate, to speak publicly" or ἀγορά (agora), which can mean "assembly, market" as well as "speech".This name was borne by a pre-Socratic Greek philosopher from the 5th century BC.

French form of Protasius. This given name is no longer in use in France today, but it still survives in francophone countries in Africa, such as Rwanda.A known bearer of this name is the Rwandan businessman and politician Protais Zigiranyirazo (b. 1938).

Short form of compound names that contain the Ancient Greek element πρῶτος (protos) meaning "first", such as Protagoras and Protogenes.In Russia, Protas can also be a short form or variant of Протасий (Protasiy), which is the Russian form of Protasius.
Catalan form of Protasius and Russian variant transcription of Protasiy.

Portuguese form of Protasius. Known bearers of this name include the Brazilian physician and politician Protásio Antônio Alves (1859-1933) and Protásio Garcia Leal (1858-1943), who was one of the three founders of the Brazilian city of Três Lagoas.
Italian and Spanish form of Protasius. A known bearer of this name was the Mexican soldier and politician Protasio Tagle (1839-1903).

Derived from the Greek verb προτάσσω (protasso) meaning "to place (before), to put at the forefront" as well as "to appoint before" and "to define beforehand". Also compare the related Greek noun πρότασις (protasis) meaning "(the) putting forward, that which is put forward". You might also want to take a look at the name Protas, as there are a few sources in existence that appear to indicate that Protasios is an elaboration of this name.
Latinized form of Protasios. This name was borne by a Christian martyr from the 2nd century AD.
Polish form of Protasius. A known bearer of this name was the Polish noble Antoni Protazy Potocki (1761-1801).
Bosnian, Croatian and Serbian form of Proteus.
Italian and Spanish form of Proteus.

Latinized form of the Greek name Πρωτεσίλαος (Protesilaos), derived from πρῶτος (protos) meaning "first", ἕσις (hesis) meaning "sending forth; strive, desire" (itself from hiemi "to throw"),‎ and λαός (laos) meaning "people, folk".
Catalan, Portuguese and Romanian form of Proteus.
Bulgarian, Russian and Ukrainian form of Proteus.

This given name is best known for being the name of a 7th-century saint, who was bishop of the city of Besançon in eastern France and died in 624 AD. The meaning of the saint's name, which was often latinized to Prothadius in writing, is uncertain. One source states that it is derived from Latin protestatus meaning "testified, protested". Also compare the Roman cognomen Praetextatus, which is similar in appearance. An other source states that the name is of Greek origin and that it consists of Greek πρῶτος (protos) meaning "first" and Greek ἀϊδής (aides) or (haides) meaning "unseen, invisible" (see Hades).There is also a possibility that the name Prothade is of Gaulish origin, since during the saint's lifetime, there was a Gaulish aristocrat by the name of Protade (also known as Protades and Protadius), who was the lover of queen Brunhilda of Austrasia up until his death in 605 or 606 AD. In fact, saint Prothade could even have been related to this Gaulish aristocrat, since it is said that the saint's father was a member of the court of king Theuderic II, who was the grandson of the aforementioned Brunhilda of Austrasia.With that said, another known bearer of the given name Prothade was the French count and counter admiral Hippolyte of Astorg (1759-1828), whose full name was Jacques Pierre Prothade Hippolyte of Astorg.
Latinized form of Prothade. This name was borne by a 7th-century saint, who was bishop of the city of Besançon in eastern France and died in 624 AD.

Protheselaus is a verse romance composed in Anglo-Norman by Hugh of Rhuddlan at the end of the 12th century. Hugh lived at Credenhill near Hereford, according to his earlier poem Ipomedon.It is a sequel to Ipomedon in the same sense in which sequels were composed to the chansons de geste: Protheselaus is introduced as the son of Ipomedon, he has adventures that are similar to his father's, and faces similar problems. He is deprived of his inheritance. He is in love with Medea and believes (wrongly, it appears) that she hates him. With the help of Dardanus and Melander he attempts to conciliate her and travels through distant lands to prove his knightly prowess, then returns and enters her service in disguise. He travels to Burgundy, defends Ismeine, is made prisoner by the "Maiden of the Isle" (Pucele de l'Isle), finally escapes, recovers his inheritance and marries Medea.
Medieval French diminutive of Prothade (as -et is a French masculine diminutive suffix). This given name is no longer in use in France, but it still survives there as a patronymic surname.

A prince under Queen Belacane of Zazamanc (the first wife of Perceval’s father Gahmuret).He fought against Isenhart, one of Belacane’s suitors, and both warriors were killed in the duel. Gahmuret later gave Prothizilas’s duchy to Sir Lahfilirost (Lahifilirost).
Feminine variant of Prothous. This was the name of an Amazon warrior in Ancient Greek mythology.

Derived from Ancient Greek προθέω (protheo) meaning "to run before, run forward, outrun" (composed of πρό (pro) "before" and θοός (thoos) "quick, swift") and ἀνήρ (aner) meaning "man", functionally a combination of the names Πρόθοος (see Prothous) and Θοάνωρ (see Thowanor).In Greek mythology, Prothoenor was one of the Achaean leaders in the Trojan War.
Derived from Greek πρό (pro) meaning "before, forth, forward" and θοός (thoós) meaning "quick, swift".
Croatian and Russian form of Protogenes.

Derived from Greek πρωτογενής (prôtogenês) meaning "firstborn, primeval" (see Protogenes). This was the name of several figures in Greek mythology, as well as an epithet of the goddess Tyche (equivalent to Latin Primigenia, an epithet of Fortuna).
Portuguese and Spanish form of Protogenes.

Means "first-born" or "primeval" in Ancient Greek, derived from πρῶτος (protos) meaning "first" combined with γενής (genes) meaning "born" as well as "of a kind". This name was borne by an ancient Greek painter from the 4th century BC.
Latinized form of the name Bartatua, itself an Akkadian form of a Scythian name.
Central character in Paul Claudel's play The Satin Slipper (1929).
Romanian, Ukrainian and Russian form of Probus.

The name Prova is from the Indian origin. This name has various meanings. It means lights, radiance, sheen, brilliance, splendor and so on. It is used to indicate the glow of the sun. Again, this name is widely used in Indian literature. In poems Prova can mean a firefly (জোনাকিপোকা). It symbolizes freedom and success.
Prove is a god in the old Slavic religion. He is a fertility god and has relations with Perun.
Referring to the book of Proverbs in the Bible.
Derived from the English word denoting "a manifestation of divine care or direction; an instance of divine intervention".

Means "precaution, providence" in Latin. In ancient Roman religion, Providentia is a divine personification of the ability to foresee and make provision. She was among the embodiments of virtues that were part of the Imperial cult of ancient Rome.
Means "son of Proxenos" in Greek, derived from the name Proxenos combined with the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).This name was borne by an eponymous archon of Athens, who lived in the 3rd century BC.

Derived from Ancient Greek πρόξενος (proxenos) meaning "patron, protector" as well as "public foreigner, public friend", composed of πρό (pro) meaning "before" and (xenos) meaning "foreigner, guest, stranger".
Latinized form of Proxenos. A known bearer of this name was Proxenus of Atarneus (4th century BC), the guardian and brother-in-law of Aristotle.
Used by ape tyrant Proximus Caesar in Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes (2024).
Bosnian, Croatian, Lithuanian and Polish form of Proserpina.
Sicilian form of Procopius via Prokopios.

Derived from either Old French prude, the feminine form of the adjective pruz "brave; valiant" or from Old French preu "brave; valiant, chivalrous" (ultimately from Late Latin prōde "profitable, useful").

Roman cognomen which was derived from the Latin adjective prudens meaning "wise, prudent" as well as "foreseeing, foreknowing".In the Dutch-speaking world, this name is the Dutch form of Prudentius, whereas in the German-speaking world, it is a variant spelling of Prudenz.A notable bearer of this name is Prudens van Duyse (1804-1859), a Flemish writer and poet.

French form of Prudens and Prudentius.Notable bearers of this name include the French athlete Prudent Joye (1913-1980), the Belgian soccer player and coach Prudent Bettens (1943-2010) and Prudent Beaudry (1816-1893), an American politician of French Canadian descent who became the 13th mayor of Los Angeles in 1874.

Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Prudens. In Italy, this name is also encountered as a variant of Prudenzio, which is the main Italian form of Prudentius.A notable bearer of this name is Prudente de Morais (1841-1902), the third president of Brazil.
One of the Basque forms of Prudentia.
German form of Prudentius. A known bearer of this name was the Swiss poet Prudenz Meister (1875-1923).
Means "prudence" in Italian, directly from Latin prudentia.
Italian and Corsican form of Prudentia.
prudhvi means earth in hindhu religion in india
Transferred use of the surname Pruitt.
Used by C.S. Lewis in 'Prince Caspian' as the name of Caspian's aunt and Miraz's wife. He apparently based it on the phrase "prunes and prisms".

The French name for Sunny Baudelaire, a character from A Series of Unfortunate Events (Les Désastreuses Aventures des orphelins Baudelaire).It is claimed by some to be a variant of Pernille. It could also be taken from Prune.
From the name of the state Prussia.
From Serbian први (prvi) meaning "first". It is thus given to first born daughters.
Derived from Slavic elements prvi or prvo, meaning "first, firstly" and ljub, meaning "loved, beloved".
From Serbian први (prvi) meaning "first" and син (sin) meaning "son". The name is clearly given to first born sons.
From the word “Prydain” Meaning Britain, this was one of the mythological kings of Britannia, sometimes considered the founder of Britain

Means "dance in armour, armed dance" in Ancient Greek, referring to a kind of Cretan weapon-dance. This was the name of a prophet in Greek mythology, a demigod son of Hermes and the Lesbian nymph Issa.

Derived from Greek πρυμνεύς (prymneus) meaning "steersman", which is ultimately derived from Greek πρύμνα (prymna) meaning "stern, poop". Also compare Greek πρυμνός (prymnos) meaning "hindmost, undermost, end-most". In Greek mythology, Prymneus was one of the seven Corybantes, sons of Combe and Socus of Euboea. It was also the name of a Phaeacian who participated in the games organised by King Alcinous to honour Odysseus.

One of the 3,000 oceanids—the water-nymph daughters of the Titans Oceanus and Tethys. Her name translates to "root" or "undermost," and she's specifically recognized as the nymph of groundwater, deep wells, and cascading streams,
Probably onomatopoeic form. Pryntyl is a mermaid, the main character of Louis-Ferdinand Céline's Scandale aux abysses (1950), the name is also the title of a famous Italian song by Vinicio Capossela.
Transferred use of the surname Pryor.
Contracted form of ap Rhys "son of Rhys".

Derived from the Greek noun πρύτανις (prytanis) meaning "prince, ruler, lord, chief".This name was borne by a semi-mythological king of Sparta, who is thought to have lived in the 9th century BC.It was also the name of a Bosporan king from the 4th century BC.

The first element of this name is derived from the Polish adjective przed "in front of, before" (the latter can also be used to refer to an earlier point in time), which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic perdъ "in front of, against". Also compare modern Russian pered and Serbo-Croatian pred, both of which mean "before, in front of". The second element of this name is derived from Slavic bor "battle" or borit "to fight".

The first element of this name is derived from the Polish adjective przed "in front of, before" (the latter can also be used to refer to an earlier point in time), which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic perdъ "in front of, against". Also compare modern Russian pered and Serbo-Croatian pred, both of which mean "before, in front of". The second element of this name is either derived from Slavic mir "peace" or Slavic mer "great, famous". In other words, one could say that this name is the Polish cognate of Predimir.

The first element of this name is derived from the Polish adjective przed "in front of, before" (the latter can also be used to refer to an earlier point in time), which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic perdъ "in front of, against". Also compare modern Russian pered and Serbo-Croatian pred, both of which mean "before, in front of". The second element of this name is derived from archaic Polish pełk "regiment, group, people", which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic *pъlkъ "people, folk". Also compare modern Russian polk, Czech pluk and Serbo-Croatian puk, all of which mean "regiment".

The first element of this name is derived from the Polish adjective przed "in front of, before" (the latter can also be used to refer to an earlier point in time), which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic perdъ "in front of, against". Also compare modern Russian pered and Serbo-Croatian pred, both of which mean "before, in front of". The second element of this name is derived from Slavic slav "glory". In other words, one could say that this name is the Polish cognate of Predislav.
This name is either a more elaborate form of Przedmir, or an older form of the same name.
This name is either a more elaborate form of Przedsław, or an older form of the same name.
From Polish przed "before, in front" and sława "glory" roughly translating to "glory before me".
Shorter form (or variant form) of Przedmir.
Shorter form (or variant form) of Przedsław. This old Polish male name dates back to the 12th century AD.
Polish name from Slavic *pribyti "to arrive, to come" combined with čĭstĭ "honour, reverence; rank". In Old Polish, these elements became przybyć and cześć "reverence, honour; respect" respectively.

The first element of this name is derived from Polish przybyć "to arrive, to come" (also compare Polish przybywać and przyjść, which also mean "to arrive, to come"). The second element is derived from Slavic mir "peace". As such, this name's meaning is roughly "peace will come".
Composed of the elements of przyby ("to arrive") and rad ("to be happy, to enjoy"). Thus, it can mean "the one with whom joy comes".
Deriveds from przybyć meaning "to arrive" and rada meaning "counsel, advice".

The first element of this name is derived from Polish przybyć "to arrive, to come" (also compare Polish przybywać and przyjść, which also mean "to arrive, to come"). The second element is derived from Slavic slav "glory". As such, this name's meaning is roughly "glory will come".
From Polish przybyć meaning "to arrive, to come" and woj meaning "warrior".

From the English word psalm which refers to a sacred song or poem, especially one of the hymns by David and others which were collected into the Old Testament Book of Psalms. It is ultimately derived from Greek ψαλμός (psalmos) meaning "a song sung to the harp", from ψάλλω (psallo) "to pluck, to play a stringed instrument with the fingers". This name was used by the television personality Kim Kardashian and rapper Kanye West for their son born 2019.
Combination of the given name Samantha and the English word psalm.

From the title of the Book of Psalms in the Old Testament, the plural of Psalm. This was used for a character, a male former slave named Psalms Jackson, in the American Western drama television series Hell on Wheels (2011-2016).
Variant of Psamathe used in George Sandys's translation (1623) of Ovid's Metamorphoses, among other translations.
Latinized form of Psamtik, borrowed from Greek Psammetikhos.
Greek form of Egyptian pꜣ-smꜣ-tꜣwy meaning "he who unites the Two Lands". This is the name of an Egyptian pharoah.

From Egyptian psmṯk, possibly a short form of pꜣ-sꜣ-n-mṯk meaning "the man of Meṯek", Meṯek (or Metjek) being a hypothetical Libyan deity. Alternatively, it could derive from an Egyptian transcription of an Assyrian name. This was the name of three pharaohs of ancient Egypt.
Uncertain etymology. Psaumis of Camarina was a winning Olympic charioteer in 452 BCE.

Derived from Ancient Greek ψεκάς (psekas) meaning "raindrop, rain shower, drizzle". In Greek mythology, this was the name of one of the band of sixty young Oceanid Nymphs which formed the core retinue of the goddess Artemis.
The god of Life and Souls.
Pseudolus is the eponymous character in 'Pseudolus', a play by the ancient Roman playwright Titus Maccius Plautus.
From the English word pseudonymous, meaning “writing or written under a false name”. It is used as a pseudonym by American author Pseudonymous Bosch.

This name originates from Kashmir. It is an extremely rare name, and is not typical of the Kashmir region. The meaning of it is translated to "flower," "clearness or brightness," and "joy."This name is to not be mistaken with the British word "Posh," as the pronunciations are completely different.
Means "happy leader" in Adyghe, ultimately derived from pasha, an Ottoman Turkish military title.

'Psmith Rupert (in later incarnations Ronald Eustace) Psmith, dandyish Old Etonian (expelled) flaneur and social escapologist in the works of P.G. Wodehouse. Debuting in 'Lost Lambs' (1909; later (1935) renamed 'Enter Psmith'), he was the first of the major characters Wodehouse created. The P (silent) was his own addition.'(Source: Encyclopedia of Surnames (2007) by John Ayto)
The meaning of this name is still unknown to me at this time. This name was borne by a Coptic saint from the 3rd century AD.

A witty page in 'Campaspe', an Elizabethan era stage play, a prose comedy by John Lyly based on the story of the love triangle between Campaspe, a Theban captive, the artist Apelles, and Alexander the Great, who commissioned him to paint her portrait.
Medieval Polish vernacular form of Deborah, derived from the word for "bee".
Means "Peace of Ptah". This was the name of a 5th Dynasty vizier.
This is the name of the Mandaean demiurge (see Demiurgos), probably based on a Mandaic root pth meaning "to mold" (or related to Egyptian Ptah) and the divine suffix il, which is Hebrew 'el (El).
From Egyptian ptḥ-ms meaning "born of Ptah" or "Ptah is born", derived from the name of the god Ptah combined with msj "to be born".
Ancient Egyptian feminine name meaning "Beauty of Ptah".
From Egyptian ptḥ-špss meaning "Ptah is noble" or "Ptah is esteemed", derived from the name of the god Ptah combined with špss "to be noble, esteemed, splendid".
From Egyptian ptḥ-wr meaning "Ptah is great".

This name comes from a small genus of birds in the grouse subfamily, whose genus name is Lagopus. The name is derived from Scottish Gaelic tàrmachan, which is of unknown origin, and the Pt- spelling was adopted as early as the 1680s through a mistaken Greek construction, which may be based on the Greek word pteron meaning "wing."

Derived from Ancient Greek πτελέα (ptelea) meaning "wych elm", another name for the European elm tree. This was the name of one of the eight hamadryad daughters of Oxylos and Hamadryas, associated with the elm tree.

Means "people adorned with feathers", derived from the Greek verb πτερόω (pteroo) meaning "to feather, to furnish with feathers or wings" combined with the Greek noun λαός (laos) meaning "(the) people".
Ptocheia is, in Greek mythology, the personification of beggary. Her sisters are Amechania (helplessness) and Penia (poverty).
German form of Ptolemaios via Ptolemaeus.
French form of Ptolemaios via Ptolemaeus.
Variant of Ptolemy used in the Douay-Rheims Bible (1582-1610) and the King James Bible (both the original 1611 edition as well as the 1769 revised edition).
Croatian and Serbian form of Ptolemaios via Ptolemaeus.
Lithuanian form of Ptolemaios via Ptolemaeus.
Catalan, Portuguese and Romanian form of Ptolemaios via Ptolemaeus.
Polish form of Ptolemaios via Ptolemaeus.
Bulgarian, Russian and Ukrainian form of Ptolemaios.

Roman feminine given name derived from the Greek πολεμηιος (polemeios) meaning "aggressive" or "warlike" and κρατος (kratos) meaning "power". This was the name of a character in the play Rudens of Plautus.
Variant of Ptolemy used in the original 1611 edition of the King James Bible.

In the annals of history, there exists a fascinating tale surrounding the word "Pukalavan" and its linguistic origin, intimately intertwined with the Tamil language. According to the legends passed down through generations, Pukalavan was an ancient hero of Tamil origin, revered for his exceptional qualities and deeds that earned him the epithet of the "praised one."The story of Pukalavan dates back to a time when the ancient Tamil civilization flourished in the southern regions of the Indian subcontinent. Pukalavan was said to be a charismatic and noble warrior, hailing from a small village nestled amidst the lush landscapes of Tamil Nadu. He possessed unmatched courage, wisdom, and an unwavering sense of justice.As the legend goes, Pukalavan embarked on a series of remarkable exploits that endeared him to the hearts of the Tamil people. He fearlessly defended his village from marauding invaders and protected the innocent from harm. With his exceptional martial skills and strategic acumen, he led his people to numerous victories against formidable adversaries.Pukalavan's reputation spread far and wide, reaching the ears of the Tamil kings and scholars of the time. They were captivated by his remarkable qualities and began to sing his praises, extolling his heroism and noble character. The Tamil bards and poets composed epic verses and ballads that celebrated his deeds, spreading his name across the Tamil lands.In time, the name "Pukalavan" became synonymous with honor, valor, and reverence. The linguistic origin of the word "Pukalavan" can be traced back to the Tamil language itself. "Pukal" in Tamil means "praise" or "acclaim," while "avan" is a suffix denoting a person or individual. Thus, "Pukalavan" came to signify "the praised one" or "the one who is deserving of admiration and accolades."Through the passage of time, Pukalavan's legend and the etymology of his name became deeply intertwined with the Tamil language and culture. He became a symbol of heroism and the embodiment of the values cherished by the Tamil people. The name "Pukalavan" continues to be held in high regard, carrying the weight of centuries of adoration and respect for this mythical Tamil hero.

This was also the name of a signatory to the 1862 Moriori Crown Petition and Waitangi district leading elder named Pumipi Te Rangaranga.

From Chinese 普 (pǔ) meaning "universal, wide, vast" and 贤 (xián) meaning "virtuous, worthy", a calque of Sanskrit समन्तभद्र (samantabhadra). This is the Chinese name for the bodhisattva Samantabhadra.

Means "mountain, hill" in Auvergnat French. It is taken from the Spanish title of the Virgin Mary Nuestra Señora del Puy meaning "Our Lady of the Mountain". She is the patron saint of the town of Estella, located in the Spanish autonomous community of Navarre. According to folk legend, in 1085, some shepherds went to a mountain as they were attracted by some stars highlighting a cave, where an image of the Virgin was found.
Alternate transcription of Persian پویان (see Pouyan).

column3: 溥仪, etc.(Chinese)|溥儀, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 溥 (pǔ) meaning "big, great, vast, wide" combined with 仪 (yí) meaning "ceremony, rites". Other hanzi combinations are possible. A notable bearer was Aisin-Gioro Puyi (1906 – 1967), the last emperor of the Qing Dynasty who was forced to abdicate the throne in 1912.
Malay and Indonesian variant of Fawzi.
Means "to blossom, to bloom" in Burmese.
Meaning uncertain. It could be derived from Swedish pyre "small child, tot".
Derived from Norman pie "magpie" (via Old French pie, from Latin pica, the feminine of picus "woodpecker").

Derives from Priya. This is one of five virtues that is vigorously promoted by the Sikh Gurus. The other four qualities are Truth (Sat), Contentment (Santosh), Compassion (Daya) and Humility (Nimrata).
Loosely translated to "Cutie" or "Sweetie", a term of endearment occasionally used as a given name.
Means "to be full, to reach a specific point" in Burmese.

column3: ပြည့်ဖြိုး(Burmese)

column12: From name of river Pyana in Mordoviya, Russia. Similar sound to Russian пьяная (pyanaya) "drunk".
From the Hindi word प्यार (pyara) meaning "love"
It is one of Krishna's names.
Contraction of propaganda slogan Пятилетку — в четыре года! (Pyatiletku — v chetyre goda!) "Five year plan in four years!".
Alternate transcription of Burmese ပြေ (see Pye).
Old English name of unknown meaning, likely of Brittonic Celtic origin. A notable bearer was Pybba of Mercia, an early King of Mercia in the late 6th century.

Created by author George R. R. Martin for a character in his series 'A Song of Ice and Fire'. In the series, Pycelle is a Grand Maester who serves multiple monarchs of Westeros from the last years of the Targaryen dynasty onward.
Variant of Paaie, a Manx form of Peggy ("with loss of intervocalic consonant").
From 평 and 權 "power, right, authority" (gwon).
An imp in form of a dog reported by Mathew Hopkins in his 1647 pamphlet "The Discovery of Witches". Also the cat familiar of the witch in the 1958 movie Bell, Book and Candle.
From Egyptian pꜣ-jḥjꜣ, of uncertain etymology. The first element could be pꜣ "the aforementioned; the; he of, this of". This was the name a daughter of Thutmose IV.
Jèrriais and Cotentinais Norman form of Pierre.
Silesian and Vilamovian form of Piotr via German Peter.
Variant of Pike. A notable bearer of this name is the Dutch painter Pyke Koch (1901-1991).

Latinized form of Greek Πύλαιος (Pylaios), meaning "at the gate" or "of Pylae", the name of an Ancient Greek town in what is now Turkey, ultimately derived from πύλη (pyle) meaning "gate, entrance". In Greek mythology, Pylaeus was an ally of King Priam in the Trojan War, and fell in battle beside his brother Hippothous.

The first element of this name is derived from either the Greek noun πύλη (pyle) meaning "gate, entrance" or from the name of the Greek town of Pylos (see Pylos), which is etymologically related to the aforementioned word. The second element of this name is derived from the Greek noun ἀνήρ (aner) meaning "man". As such, the meaning of this name is either "man at the gate, gatekeeper" or "man from Pylos".In Greek mythology, Pylenor is the name of a centaur.

Derived from Greek πύλος (pylos) meaning "in the gateway", which is ultimately derived from the Greek noun πύλη (pyle) meaning "gate, entrance". Pylos is also the name of a town in modern Greece, which already existed in the time of Mycenaean Greece (under the same name) and was an important kingdom at the time.
Latinized form of Pylos. In Greek mythology, this is the name of a son of the god Ares, whom he had with Demonice.
Name given to the older sister of a mother.
Medieval diminutive of Euphemia, which was popular in England in the Middle Ages.

Derived from the Sino-Korean word 票 (pyo) meaning “slip of paper” or 表 (pyo) meaning “show”. It also coincides with the Hanja 표 meaning "ox (second earthly branch)". Other characters combinations are also possible.
Means "to smile" or "to grow, to proliferate" in Burmese.
"A recurring bird character in the WarioWare series"
Alternate transcription of Russian Пётр (see Pyotr)
Etymology uncertain. From Egyptian py-pwy or pj-pwj.
Meaning unknown. This was the name of a 6th century Welsh abbot.
English form of PyramusThe earliest known usage is from the mid-1800s. Rev Joseph Pyram King (1847 - 1948)
French form of Pyramus. A known bearer of this name was the Swiss botanist Augustin Pyrame de Candolle (1778-1841).

From the Greek Πύραμος (Pyramos), taken from the name of the river Pyramos and possibly derived from Greek πυρός (pyros) meaning "wheat", or perhaps πῦρ (pyr) meaning "fire". In classical mythology, he was the lover of Thisbe, who killed himself believing that she was dead.
Means "fire of a man", derived from Greek πῦρ (pyr) "fire" combined with Greek ἀνδρός (andros) "of a man".
Possibly based on Greek πῦρ (pyr) meaning "fire". This is the full name of American musician Rena Lovelis (1998-), a member of the band Hey Violet (along with her sister Szatania 'Nia' Lovelis).

Most likely of Celtic origin, though folk etymology links it to either Greek πυρήν (pyren) meaning "kernel, fruit stone" or to πῦρ (pyr) meaning "fire". In Greek mythology, Pyrene was an Iberian princess and lover of Hercules, for whom the mountain range the Pyrenees are named. Not to be confused with Pirene.
Masculine form of Pyrene. In Greek mythology, Pyreneus was a king of Thrace.
Pyrgo is the name of multiple women in Greek and Roman mythology, including the nurse of King Priam's children, who identifies the goddess Iris in the Aeneid.

Derived from Ancient Greek πύργος (pyrgos) meaning "tower, watchtower" and τέλος (telos) meaning "purpose, result, completion". This was the name of a famous Ancient Greek gem engraver, known mostly by the many forgeries of his works.

Means "bright with fire", from Ancient Greek πῦρ (pyr) meaning "fire" and λάμπω (lampo) meaning "to shine". This was the name of Plato's stepfather, an Ancient Greek politician.The modern Portuguese word pirilampo, "firefly", derives from this.

Derived from Greek πῦρ (pyr) meaning "fire". In literature, Pyro is the name of a fire-controlling mutant from the "X-Men" comics of Marvel. This character was also included in the film adaptations of the comics.

From the Greek elements πῦρ (pyr) meaning "fire" and κλέος (kleos) meaning "glory". In Edmund Spenser's poem The Faerie Queene (1590) this is the name of a reckless knight who, together with his brother Cymochles, represents emotional maladies that threaten temperance. Prince Arthur slays both brothers in Canto VIII.

Means "fiery, burning" in Ancient Greek, derived from πῦρ (pyr) meaning "fire". This was the name of the god of the wandering star Ἄρειος (Areios), the planet Mars) in Greek mythology. He is also known as Μεσονυξ (Mesonyx) "midnight".

Epithet of the goddess Artemis, probably derived from Ancient Greek πῦρ (pyr) meaning "fire". In some accounts, it’s the name of a nymph, the mother of Iasion by Minos. It is also the name of a genus of butterfly.
Latinized form of Pyrrhon. This was the name of the first Greek skeptic philosopher (3rd century BC), who founded the school of Pyrrhonism.
Derived from the Greek adjective πυρρός (pyrrhos) meaning "flame-coloured, yellowish-red" (see Pyrrhus).

Derived from Greek Πυθιος (Pythios), which is an epithet of the god Apollo. This epithet originated from his cult in the city of Πυθώ (Pytho), which is nowadays known as Delphi. The city's name is ultimately derived from the Greek verb πυθώ (putho) or (pytho) meaning "to rot, to decay". Also see Python and compare Pythias. It should also be noted that one source claims that this name is basically a short form of Pythagoras. Finally, a known bearer of this name was the Greek geographer and explorer Pytheas of Massalia, who lived in the 4th century BC.

From the name of Apollo's master priestess at Delphi, who was also known as the Oracle of Delphi. The name is derived from Πυθώ (Pytho), which is the old name of the city of Delphi. In turn, the city's old name is ultimately derived from the Greek verb πυθώ (putho) or (pytho) meaning "to rot, to decay". Also see Python.

Derived from Greek Πυθιος (Pythios), which is an epithet of the god Apollo. This epithet originated from his cult in the city of Πυθώ (Pytho), which is nowadays known as Delphi. The city's name is ultimately derived from the Greek verb πυθώ (putho) or (pytho) meaning "to rot, to decay". Also see Python.A known bearer of this name was the ancient Greek biologist and embryologist Pythias the Elder, who was the first wife of the philosopher and scientist Aristotle.In Greek mythology, the legend of Damon and Pythias (or Phintias) symbolizes trust and loyalty in a true friendship.
Latinized form of Pythokles. A known bearer of this name was Pythocles of Sicyon, an Olympic victor from the 3rd century BC.
Latinized form of Pythokritos. This name was borne by two eponymous archons of Athens, the earliest of which lived in the 5th century BC.

The first element of this name is derived from Pythios, which is an epithet of the god Apollo. Also compare the related name Python.The second element is derived from the Greek adjective δῆλος (delos) meaning "visible, conspicuous, manifest", which is ultimately derived from the Greek verb δηλόω (deloo) meaning "to make visible".This name was borne by an eponymous archon of Athens, who lived in the 4th century BC.

Feminine form of the Greek masculine name Πυθοδωρίδης (Pythodorides), which means "son of Pythodoros", as it consists of the name Pythodoros combined with the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).This name was borne by Pythodorida of Pontus (died in 38 AD), a Roman client ruler who was a granddaughter of the Roman politician and general Mark Antony. Her father's name was Pythodoros, so her name literally refers to the fact that she was his daughter. The name was later borne by her granddaughter, Pythodorida II (also known as Pythodoris), a Roman client ruler of Thrace.
Feminine form of Pythodoros. This was the name of a Roman client ruler of the Odrysian kingdom of Thrace, who reigned from 38 AD to 46 AD.
Means "gift of Pythios" or "gift of Python", from an epithet of the god Apollo derived from the name of the town in which the Oracle of Delphi resided, combined with δῶρον (doron) meaning "gift".
Latinized form of Pythodoros. This name was borne by two eponymous archons of Athens, the earliest of which lived in the 5th century BC.
Derived from Pythios, an epithet of the god Apollo, combined with δοτός (dotos) meaning "given, granted".
Latinized form of Pythodotos. This name was borne by an eponymous archon of Athens, who lived in the 4th century BC.
Derived from Pythios, an epithet of the god Apollo, combined with Greek κλέος (kleos) meaning "glory".
Derived from Pythios, an epithet of the god Apollo, combined with either κριτής (krites) meaning "judge, critic" or the related κριτός (kritos) meaning "chosen, picked out, separated; excellent".

The name of an enormous earth-dragon in Greek mythology (usually depicted as a serpent in ancient Greek art) who lived near the city of Πυθώ (Pytho), which is nowadays known as Delphi. The creature was named after the city, whose name was ultimately derived from the Greek verb πύθω (pytho) meaning "to rot, to decay" (also compare Pythios). Python was eventually slain by the god Apollo. This name occurs once in the New Testament, namely in Acts 16:16, where Paul and his companions happen upon a slave girl who is possessed by the spirit Python.In real life, this name was borne by the Greek philosopher Python of Aenus (4th century BC), the Greek statesman Python of Byzantium (4th century BC) and the Greek poet Python of Catana (4th century BC).

The first element of this name is derived from Pythios, which is an epithet of the god Apollo. Also compare the related name Python.The second element is derived from the Greek noun στρατός (stratos) meaning "army".This name was borne by an Olympic victor from the 4th century BC.
Latinized form of Pythostratos. A known bearer of this name was the Olympic victor Pythostratus of Ephesus, who won the stadion race at the 103rd Olympiad in 368 BC.

column3: 純, 純愛, 妃由亜, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ぴゅあ(Japanese Hiragana)|ピュア(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 純 (pyua) meaning "pure, innocent". Other kanji or kanji combinations can form this name as well.Usage of this name is influenced by the English word pure.
Derived from Kalmyk пүрвə (pürvä) meaning "Jupiter (the planet)", related to Tibetan Phurbu.

Pyxis is a small and faint constellation in the southern sky. Abbreviated from Pyxis Nautica, its name is Latin for a mariner's compass (contrasting with Circinus, which represents a draftsman's compasses). Pyxis was introduced by Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille in the 18th century, and is counted among the 88 modern constellations.
From Egyptian qꜣ-ꜥ, possibly meaning "the one whose arm is raised", derived from Egyptian qꜣ "raised" and ꜥ "arm". This was the name of the last king of the First Dynasty of Egypt.
Means "man in the moon". This is the name of a character in Greenlandic mythology.
In the context of the 99 Names of Allah, "Al-Qabid" (الْقَابِضُ) means "The Restrainer" or "The Withholder".
Means "occupier; tenant; seizer; possesser" in Urdu and Bengali, ultimately from the Arabic roots ق-ب-ض (q-b-ḍ).
Possibly derived from Mongolian хацар (khatsar) meaning "cheek, face; flank".
Either from къачхан (kaçhan) meaning "escaped, fugitive" or къач (kaç) meaning "cross" or "honour" and the Turkic title khan meaning "king, ruler".
Derived from Mongolian хад (khad) meaning "cliff, crag, rock, boulder".
Means "will of God, divine providence" in Azerbaijani.
Canaanite and Phoenician form of Qetesh.
Qadry is a masculine name meaning "capable", related to the Arabic name Qadir.

From Egyptian qꜣ-ḥḏt, meaning "he whose White Crown is high", from Egyptian qꜣj "high" and ḥḏt "White Crown", This was the name of a possibly Egyptian pharaoh who may have ruled during the 3rd Dynasty or could be a voluntarily archaistic representation of Thutmose III.
Means "hero" in Azerbaijani, of Persian origin.
Means "hero" in Uzbek, ultimately from Persian قهرمان‎‎ (qahramân) meaning "champion, hero".
Means "constant" in Mandaic, or otherwise from the Mandaic qaiamta meaning meeting "dedication, prayer of dedication, offering up, raising up".
Alternate transcription of Arabic قيس (see Qays).
Alternate transcription of Arabic قيصر‎ (see Qaysar), as well as the Urdu and Kazakh form.
Possibly a feminine variant of Qaisar.
Alternate transcription of Urdu قیصر (see Qaisar).
Derived from Uzbek qalam meaning "pen, pencil", "writing style", or "mascara" and gul meaning "rose, flower".
Derived from Uzbek qalam meaning "pen, pencil", "writing style", or "mascara" and oy meaning "month".
Means "straight, even eyebrows" in Uzbek. Straight eyebrows are considered a sign of beauty.

Derived from the Islamic religious title of qalandar, which is also known in English as calender (not to be confused with calendar). It is derived from Persian قلندر (qalandar) meaning "wandering dervish", which is ultimately derived from the older Persian word کلندر‎ (kalandar) meaning "uncouth man".
Combination of Qalandar with the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
Derived from Arabic قلبي (qalbī) meaning "my heart", from قلب (qalb) meaning "heart" and the suffix ي (ī) meaning "my".
Derived from the Arabic noun قلب (qalb) meaning "heart" combined with the Arabic noun نور (nur) meaning "light" (see Nur).This name appears to be strictly masculine in Indonesia.
Etymology uncertain, probably of Nubian origin.
Meaning uncertain, possibly a variant of Kalisha.

aloon is a Somali name with the following characteristics:Meaning: Qaloon generally means "strong" or "powerful."Origin: It is derived from the Somali language, where names often reflect qualities of strength and resilience. Qaloon conveys attributes of robustness and vigor.
Etymology unknown. This was the name of a Nuxalk warrior goddess associated with death, beginnings, creation, earthquakes, forest fires, and sickness.
Means "moon of the religion" from Arabic قمر (qamar) meaning "moon" and دين (dīn) meaning "religion, faith".
Means "moon of the era" from Arabic قمر (qamar) meaning "moon" and زمان (zaman) meaning "time, age, era".
From masculine قَمَرِيّ (qamariyy) or feminine قَمَرِيَّة (qamariyya), both meaning "lunar, related to the moon" in Arabic. It may therefore be seen as a strictly feminine variant of Qamar.

column3: قمر جہاں, قمرجهان, قمر جہاں(Persian, Arabic, Urdu)
column12: Means "moon of the world" from Arabic قمر (qamar) (see Qamar) meaning "moon" combined with Persian جهان (jahān) (see Jahan) meaning "world".
Derived from Uzbek qamar meaning "moon" and jamol meaning "beauty".
From qamar meaning "moon" and niso meaning "lady, women".
Alternate transcription of Arabic قمر الدين (see Qamar ad-Din).
Means "moon among women" from Arabic قمر (qamar) meaning "moon" (figuratively "something or someone beautiful, especially a face") and نساء (nisa) meaning "women". Also compare Badr-un-nissa.
From Arabic قنبر (qunbar, qunbur) meaning "lark". This was the name of a servant and companion of Ali.
Possibly from Arabic قَمَر (qamar) meaning "moon" (see Qamar).
Azerbaijani form of Qambar. It coincides with Azerbaijani qənbər meaning "cobblestone, boulder".
From the Azerbaijani qan meaning "blood" and dəmir meaning "iron".
Means "lamp, lantern" in Urdu, ultimately from Arabic قنديل (qindil).
Derived from Uzbek qand meaning "sugarcube" and gul meaning "rose, flower".
name of one of the mountain in kurdistan,symbol of defending
Derived from qandil which can mean "chandelier" or a kind of apple.
Derived from Arabic قانت (qānit) meaning "obedient, submissive, devout, pious".
Alternate transcription of Arabic قانتة (see Qanita), as well as an Indonesian variant.
Possibly from the Turkic title khan meaning "king, ruler" and the masculine name Timur.
Dena'ina Athabaskan meaning "One that sneaks around". English equivalent is "Fox".
Derived from Old Turkic kaplan meaning "tiger" (also see Kaplan).
From the Karachay-Balkar къара (qara) meaning "black" and батыр (batır) meaning "brave" or "hero".
From the Karachay-Balkar къара (qara) meaning "black" and бий (biy) meaning "bey, prince".
From the Azerbaijani qara meaning "black" and Turkish budun meaning "nation, tribe, people".
Possibly derived from Turkic *qarčïğa(y) meaning "hawk". Qarachaqay Khan was a 17th-century Iranian military commander of Armenian origin.
From the Karachay-Balkar къара (qara) meaning "black" and the diminutive suffix -чыкъ (çıq).
Means "carnation (flower)" in Azerbaijani, ultimately from Arabic قرنفل (qaranful).
Means "black-haired", from Azerbaijani qara meaning "black" and tel meaning "strand of hair".
Uzbek feminine name refering to a kind of sparrowhawk.

Meaning and origin unknown. He is a 4th saint venerated in Chaldean Catholic Church, Assyrian Church of the East, Syro-Malabar Church. Mar Qardagh (Mar means "lord" and it's like "holy"a honorific title) was a Sassanid prince who was martyred for converting to Christianity. There are Syriac manuscripts that tells his life: The History of the Heroic Deeds of Mar Qardagh the Victorious Martyr.
From the Azerbaijani qardaş meaning "brother" and ağa meaning "lord, master".
Means "the bald one" in a Semitic language, possibly Phoenician.
Means "reader, reciter of the Qur'an" in Pashto and Urdu.
Derived from the Arabic word qarib, meaning "close to" and the Arabic word Allah, meaning "God".
May come from the root qasaq meaning "to be soft, gentle".

Greenlandic name meaning "lightweight red wood". It was also a term for a piece of soft red wood shaped as human with a weapon and placed in the inner forefront of a qajaq to ward off witches, since it was believed that they were afraid of this piece of wood. This name is also related to K'asape.
Either from Arabic قاصِد (qāṣid), meaning "resolute, destined," or Arabic قَصيد (qaṣīd), meaning "poem."
Derived from قَسَمَ (qasama) meaning "to divide, to distribute". This was the name of a twelfth century Arabic-language Jewish poetess in Andalusia.

Arabized form of Kaci. In Arabic, Qassi (قاسي) means "hard", "tough", or "stern". For example, قاسي الملامح (qāsī al-malāmiḥ) is a phrase meaning "stern features" (used to describe someone with a tough or serious expression). When used as a name, it does not usually refer to its literal meaning. In Persian, the name Qassi is possibly borrowed from the Arabic word, though meaning more symbolic of strength and determination than a reference to emotional harshness.
Alternate transcription of Arabic قاسم (see Qasim).

Classical Syriac form of Castor, via the Greek form Κάστωρ (Kastor). It is also the ordinary vocabulary word for both "beaver" and "quaestor, secretary", although the latter sense can also be transliterated as qesṭōr.
Means "dew drop", ultimately derived from Arabic قطرة (qatra) meaning "drop" and أندى ('andaa) meaning "dew".
Dena'ina Athabaskan meaning "Head touches place". English equivalent is "Dream"
From Arabic قَوِيّ (qawiyy), meaning "strong, powerful, mighty." In Islamic tradition ٱلْقَوِيُّ (al-Qawi or al-Qawiyy), meaning The All-Strong, is one of the 99 names of Allah.
A knife used for clearing mountain land
Means "upholder of the faith" from Arabic قَوَّام (qawwām) meaning "upholder" combined with دِين (dīn) meaning "faith".
Variant of Kayla influenced by Qiana.
Qaynan was a god worshipped by the Sabaean people in pre-Islamic South Arabia. Based on etymology, Qaynan may have been the god of smiths.
Means "judge" in Persian, ultimately from Arabic قَاضِي‎ (qāḍī).

Means "he who refreshes his brothers".In Egyptian mythology he was one of the four sons of Horus, tasked with protecting his throne in the underworld. His image is depicted on the canopic jar that held the intestines of the deceased.
Albanian feminine form of Qemal, deriving from Arabic Kamal 1 and Turkish Kemal.
Derived from Albanian qëndresë "sojourn, stay; stamina, resistance; firm stance; perseverance, steadfastness".
Derived from Albanian qëndrim "stance, position; attitude; resistance".
Means "one who roams in the middle" in Greenlandic.
From the Aramaic word for rainbow, it is used as a female name among the Assyrian diaspora
The name of a goddess of fertility, sacred ecstasy and sexual pleasure, derived from the Semitic root Q-D-Š which means "holy".
Alternate transcription of Georgian ქეთევან (see Ketevan).
Alternate transcription of Georgian ქეთევანი (see Ketevani).
Variant of Keziah. A character in TV show The Vampire Diaries bears this name.
From Uygur قەيسەر meaning "indomitable", from Arabic قَیْصَر.
From the Aymara qhana meaning "clear; light, clarity" and aru meaning "word, language, voice".
From the Aymara qhana meaning "clear; light, clarity" and chuyma meaning "lung" in Aymara, conceptually seen as the 'heart' of a person or seat of sentiment and emotion in Aymara culture.
From the Aymara qhana meaning "clear; light, clarity" and qinaya meaning "cloud".
Means "one who watches, one who monitors" in Quechua.
Means "praise, marvel, admire" in Hmong Daw.
Means "one who ploughs the land" in Aymara.
Means "deposit of minerals, crystals or fossils" in Aymara.

The number 40 has many biblical references, including the 40 days Jesus fasted in the wilderness before beginning his ministry, and the 40 hours he lay in the tomb before the resurrection. Roman cognomen, meaning "quartered" and used as a feminine form of Quadratus.It was borne by Ummidia Quadratilla (1st century CE).

Quartz is also Steven's middle name.

Frank Baum's "The Wonderful Wizard of Oz" (1900), Quelala is a once mentioned character in the prior history of Oz, who saved a race of Winged Monkeys from being destroyed by putting them into servitude. He was from the north of Oz, also known as the Gillikin Country, where the colour of choice is purple.
