Possibly derived from Latin quercu meaning "oak tree".
From the Spanish word querida which is both a noun meaning "darling" and an adjective meaning "dear, beloved".
Variant of Cherubina used in Goa. A notable bearer was Indian comedian and actress Querobina Carvalho (1959-2025).
From Spanish querubín meaning "cherub", thus a cognate of Cherubino.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Cherubina.
From the English word quest meaning "a search", ultimately from from Medieval Latin questa meaning "search, inquiry".
Borne by Quetcy Alma Martínez De Jesús (1956-), a Puerto Rican child singer of the 1960s and 1970s who was based in New York City. Her name may be a derivative of Quetzalli.
From Nahuatl quetzalli, meaning "plumage of the quetzal bird, beautiful feather", figuratively meaning "something precious, something beautiful". Can also be a short form of Quetzalcoatl.

From Quetzala, the name of a river in Mexico. Quetzala is likely derived from Nahuatl quetzalli, "quetzal feather". The word quetzalli also denotes something precious. The quetzal held great cultural and religious significance to the Aztecs, and other indigenous peoples of Central America. It was a prominent, sacred image in artwork and legends.
Means "eagle plume" or "precious eagle" in Nahuatl, from quetzalli "quetzal feather, precious thing" and cuauhtli "eagle".
Means "owner of feathers", derived from Nahuatl quetzalli "quetzal feather, precious thing" and the possessive suffix -hua.
Means "quetzal feather arrow", from Nahuatl quetzalli "quetzal feather, precious thing" and mitl "arrow, dart".
The wife of Quetzalcoatl, whom he married before beginning his ministry.

Derived from Nahuatl quetzalli "quetzal feather, precious thing" and xihuitl "year" (or "turquoise"). Often given to boys born during the New Fire ceremony xiuhmolpilli, "the binding of the years", an event held every 52 years to align the Aztec’s ritual calendar with the annual calendar.
Means "feather flower" or "precious flower", from Nahuatl quetzalli "quetzal feather, precious thing" and xochitl "flower".
Guatemalan name referring to the Quetzal a native bird of Guatemala and Tecun Uman the last indigenious prince of Guatemala.
Was the last ruler of the Karenid dynasty (in modern Iran), ruling briefly in 839 until his assassination.
Meaning unknown, possibly means "his/her ancestor" in Nahuatl, derived from the singular suffix qui- and achtontli "great-grandfather, ancestor".
Unknown, possibly a variant of Keon or Cian.
Perhaps an elaboration of Qiana using the popular phonetic suffix tay.
Derived from Nahuatl quiyahui "to rain" or quiyahuitl "rainstorm".

Derived from Nahuatl quiyahuitl "rain, rainstorm" and tonalli "day, warmth of the sun". Possibly related to Quiauhtonatiuh, "sun of rain" or "rain of fire sun", the name of the sun of the third epoch of humanity according to Aztec tradition, which was destroyed by a rain of fire and lava.
Means "he speaks with determination" or "he resolved to do something" in Nahuatl.
Possibly derived from Nahuatl chihchihua "to make, fashion, craft" or "to adorn, dress, arrange".

Quicksilver is the 'mutant' name of a protagonist, and sometimes antagonist, of Marvel's line of X-Men and Avengers comics. His real name is Pietro Maximoff, and he is the son of Magneto. His mutant name is a reference to his ability of moving and thinking at superhuman speeds, and the fact he is typically depicted with silver hair. He is portrayed by actors Evan Peters in Fox's X-Men film series, and Aaron Taylor-Johnson in Disney's The Avengers film series.This is also the super-hero name of DC comics protagonist Max Mercury, who is also capable of super-human speed. He is sometimes known as Mercury.
Diminutive of Francisco, Francesc, Henrique, and Enrique.
Local vernacular form of Clémence found in the Poitou-Charentes region.
This name comes from the popular German folk song 'Tanz, tanz, Quieselchen'.It is not used as a given name in Germany.
Derived from Latin quietus, -a, -um "quiet". This was the name of a saint.
Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Quietus.
Of uncertain origin and meaning. Current theories, however, include a connection to Quentin.

Roman cognomen which was derived from Latin quietus meaning "quiet, at rest, peaceful, tranquil". This name was borne by Roman general Lusius Quietus (2nd century AD) and Roman usurper Titus Fulvius Iunius Quietus (3rd century AD).
Diminutive of Quigley. Reduced Anglicized form of Gaelic Ó Cuaig. In County Down it is Anglicized as Fivey, as if from cúig ‘five’.
Transferred use of the surname Quigley.
This is the name of Qui-Gon Jinn from Star Wars. He is a Jedi Master.
Derived from a Koryak word meaning "big raven". In Koryak mythology, Quikinna'qu (or Kutkinnaku) is a shapeshifting deity who taught humans to hunt, fish, and create fire.

Quilago (c. 1490–1515) was the queen regnant of Cochasquí, in modern-day Ecuador. She is known for leading native resistance to the expansion of the Inca Empire and was supposedly the mother of Atahualpa, the last Sapa Inca. Her story has become an origin myth in Ecuadorian national mythology, which has retroactively framed her as an Ecuadorian rebel against Peruvian invaders.

Means "she who creates plants, she who makes vegetables grow" in Nahuatl, from quilitl "edible herbs and vegetables" and the instrumental suffix -huaztli. This was the name of an Aztec creation deity, the patron of midwives, as well as a title or alternative name for the goddess Cihuacōātl. It was also the name of a kind of edible herb.

Most likely a combination of a name starting with Qui- (such as Quinn and Quirijn) with a name that ends in -lene, such as Helene and Marlene.However, it is also possible that this name is a short form of Aquilene, which is a variant form of Aquilina. Another possibility is that this name is a variant form of Queline, which is a rare short form of Jacqueline.
Spanish form of Cillian, referring to the saint.
Spanish form of Chilina or Kilina (finally going back to Aquilina).
In the case of Dutch soccer player Quilindschy Hartman (2001-), it is a combination of Quirine (the name of his sister) and Lindschy (possibly a Dutch form of Lindsay).
Diminutive of Aquilla.From the English word "quill" referring to a "pen made from a feather". From the Middle English quil 'fragment of reed' or 'shaft of feather'.
Transferred use of the surname Quillen.
Variant of Quill, or a diminutive of Aquila or Shaquille. It may also be transferred use of the surname Quille.
Metonymic occupational name for a spoon maker, from Old French cuiller 'spoon', 'ladle'.

Breton and French form of Killian, which is no longer in use as a given name today, but it still survives as a patronymic surname (which is most prevalent in Brittany and the rest of northwestern France).
Means "Crossed Swords" in French. Also the name of a town in Chile.
Quimburga is a latinisation of the Anglo-saxon name Cyneburga. Quimburga is the name of a notable cyclone in northern Germany in 1972.
Transferred use of the surname Quimby.
Means "mouse" in Nahuatl, a nickname for a child.
Diminutive of Joaquín, Xoaquín and Xaquín.
Possibly Italian diminutive of Quinzia. This name is also used as English feminine form of Quincy.
Spanish form of Quintia and (American) English feminization of Quincy.
A combination of the name ‘Quinn’ with the common suffix -ella.
Elaboration of Quin in the style of names such as Quanisha.
Catholic saint, hermit and bishop. He was originally a hermit in the region of Aix in Provence, France, becoming bishop of Vaison in that region.
Transferred use of the surname Quinley or a combination of Quin and lee.
From an Irish surname which was a variant of Quinlan.
Variant of Quincey, likely inspired by Quinn.
Feminine variant of Quinlan, influenced by Quinn and the popular name suffix lyn.

Catalan, Emilian-Romagnol and French form of Quintus as well as the Dutch, English and German short form of any given name starting with Quint-, such as Quinten and Quintijn (Dutch), Quintus and Quintinus (German) and Quintin (English).In popular culture, this name is best known for being the name of the shark hunter in the 1975 American film "Jaws", who was portrayed by the British actor Robert Shaw (1927-1978).

Perhaps from Latin quintanus "fifth-ranking", from quintus "fifth" (see Quintus) or a transferred use of the surname. In today's English-speaking world it is sometimes perceived as a feminine form of Quintin or Quentin.The American writer Joan Didion named her daughter Quintana Roo.
Meaning unknown, but a street in San Francisco bears the name.
Variant of Quantavia, maybe influenced by Quinn or Quintella.
Invented name, probably based on the element quan and Octavius.
Feminine diminutive of Quintus, using the suffix -elle.

Variant of Quintella inspired by the word quintessence, meaning "the fifth element", "aether". According to Medieval science, the quintessence was the material that filled the region of the universe beyond the terrestrial sphere. Later the word came to mean "a thing that is the most perfect example of its type".

This name comes from the word that can mean "a thing that is the most perfect example of its type" or, in its literal sense, "fifth essence." The word is derived from Middle French quinte essence, which is, ultimately originated from Medieval Latin quinta essentia, a combination of Latin quinta, the feminine equivalent of quintus meaning "five," and essentia meaning "essence."
English and German form of Quintianus.
Portuguese form of Quintianus and Spanish variant of Quinciano.

From the Roman cognomen Quintianus (originally written as Quinctianus), which was derived from the Roman nomen gentile Quintius. This was the name of the father and a nephew of the Roman general Tiberius Claudius Pompeianus (2nd century AD), as well as of several Roman Catholic saints.
French form of Quintianus. Not to be confused with Quentin.
French form of Quintiana. Also compare the masculine counterpart Quintien.
Catalan and Occitan form of Quintillus.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Quintilla. Also compare the masculine counterpart Quintilo.
Portuguese form of Quintilia. Also compare the masculine counterpart Quintílio.
Italian, Spanish, Galician and Portuguese form of Quintilianus (see Quintilian).
Italian and Spanish form of Quintilius.

Derived from Latin Quintilis, which was the name of the fifth month in the ancient Roman calendar. The month ultimately derived its name from the Latin ordinal number quintus meaning "fifth" (see Quintus). Also compare the Roman names Quintilius and Quintillus, which are etymologically related.This name was borne by an obscure saint martyred at Nicomedia. According to tradition, he died together with saint Capitolinus.
Latin diminutive of Quinta, which thus makes this name the feminine equivalent of Quintillus.
English variant spelling of Quintilia. Also compare Quintilla.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Quintillus.

French variant form of Quentine, of which the use has not solely been limited to France: it has been used in other francophone regions in the world (such as Québec in Canada and Wallonia in Belgium) and even in non-francophone countries, such as the Netherlands.In the English-speaking world, however, this name is usually simply the feminine form of Quintin, which is a variant form of Quentin.
Catalan form of Quintinianus (see also Quintinian).

Anglicized form of Quintinianus. This name was borne by a 3rd-century Roman consul or prefect of Sicily, who had the breasts of saint Agatha of Sicily amputated after she refused his romantic advances and held firm to her faith in Jesus Christ.
Feminine form of Quintinianus (see also Quintinian).
Italian and Spanish form of Quintinianus (see also Quintinian).

From the rare Roman agnomen Quintinianus (also found spelled as Quinctinianus), which was derived from the Roman cognomen Quintinus (which was originally spelled as Quinctinus).This was the name of a Roman consul ordinarius from the 3rd century AD.
French form of Quintinianus (see also Quintinian).
A blend of Quinton and Antonio.
Transferred use of the surname Quintrell.
Corsican and Sicilian form of Quintus.
Italian and Emilian form of Quintia.
A name appearing in Le Livre d’Artus, a work of Arthurian romance. He wass a Saxon king who, under King Hargadabran, fought Arthur’s forces at the battle of Clarence and was killed by Adragain.

Anna Quirentia Nilsson, better known as Anna Q. Nilsson, was a well-known Swedish-born silent movie actress. She was given her middle name because she was born on March 30, the feast day of Quirinus of Neuss.

Variant of Cyriacus. This was the name of several saints including the three-year-old son of Saint Julitta, a noble widow of Tarsus. According to the legend, which may be fictitious, his mother was forced to watch as he was beaten to death; she was then martyred herself.
Galician and Italian form of Quiricus.
Variant spelling of Quirijn or Quirine, depending on the sex of the bearer.
Perhaps a form of Cyrillus. It was borne by an obscure saint, one of a group of 35 martyrs executed in northwestern Africa.
Roman cognomen which was derived from Quirinus. A bearer of this name was Lucius Sestius Quirinalis Albanianus, a Roman proquaestor and suffect consul from the 1st century BC.
Variant of Quirin recorded in the 16th century in East Frisia.
Roman cognomen of unknown meaning (not to be confused with Quirinus). Publius Sulpicius Quirinius was a Roman governor of Syria when Jesus was born.
A king appearing in "Erec" by Chrétien de Troyes.
Most likely derived from Latin quiritis, the genitive form of quiris, a Sabine word meaning "spear". Quiritis was a Sabine goddess of motherhood, later equated with the goddess Juno.
Transferred use of the surname Quirt. In some cases of modern-day usage, it might also be considered a variant of Quiert, itself a variant of Quert.
Catalan form of Quiricus (probably a form of Cyriacus).

Origin uncertain. This was used for the title character in John Fletcher's play The Island Princess (written ca. 1619-1621): a princess of Tidore (an Islamic state in Indonesia) who vows to marry the man who frees her brother, the king, who has recently been captured by a local rival.

The name of an Akokisa woman, recorded in a mission record (the Akokisa being an extinct Native American tribe in what is now Texas). It has been suggested that the name could mean "full moon woman", in part from Atakapa ki.c "woman".

From a Taíno name for the Caribbean island of Hispaniola, which is made up of Haiti and the Dominican Republic. It has been applied poetically to the Dominican Republic since the Restoration War in the 1860s, and appears in its national anthem (sometimes known as 'Valiant Quisqueyans'). A known bearer was Quisqueya Henríquez (1966-2024), a Dominican conceptual artist.
Means "urinated on" in Greenlandic. Quissik was the name of a shaman, still remembered in local legends, who acquired that name when foxes in human figure urinated on him.
Feminine form of Quito or a short form of Laquita.

Possibly means "he suffers" or "he makes him suffer" in Nahuatl, derived from tlemati "to suffer something, with regret and anguish". Alternatively, it could derived from tlemaitl "hand-held brazier, clay censer", a device for carrying fire.
Transferred use of the suranem Quitman.
Variation of Kennocha, from its variation Kevoca.
Means "it has rained", derived from Nahuatl quiyahuitl "rain, rainstorm", the nineteenth day sign of the tonalpohualli.
From Chinese 渠 (qú) meaning "ditch, canal, drain" combined with 梁 (liáng) meaning "bridge, roof beam, ridge". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From the Aymara qulla meaning "medicine, remedy" and nayra meaning "eyes".
From the Aymara qulla meaning "medicine, remedy" and panqara meaning "flower".
From the Aymara qulla meaning "medicine, remedy" and uma meaning "water".
From the Aymara qullqi meaning "silver, money" and titi meaning "wildcat".
Possibly derived from Kwakiutl Indian quetutsa "sparrow". This is the name of a character in one of Greenland's best known myths.
Greenlandic name meaning "sweet little snow bunting", the snow bunting being a type of bird (see also Qulutaq).
Most likely an invented name. This name is borne by Qulyndreia Wallis, the mother of actress Quvenzhané Wallis.
Means "reddish-yellow, light brown, chestnut-coloured" in Azerbaijani.
Derived from Uzbek qumri meaning "turtledove" and qiz meaning "girl".
Means "turtle-dove" in Azerbaijani, ultimately from Arabic قمري (qumriyy).
From Karachay-Balkar къумлу (qumul) meaning "coastal, sandy" and the Turkic title khan meaning "king, ruler".
From Chinese 群 (qún) meaning "group, crowd, numerous, many", as well as other hanzi that are pronounced similarly.
From Bashkir ҡунаҡ (qunaq) meaning "guest" and feminine name element бикә (bikä).
Derived from qunduz meaning "otter" and oy meaning "moon".
Means "the very beautiful one" in Greenlandic.

column3: 群华, 群花, etc.(Chinese)|群華, 群花, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 群 (qún) meaning "group, crowd, flock" combined with 华 (huá) meaning "splendid, illustrious, flowery, Chinese" or 花 (huā) meaning "flower, blossom". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
Means "hemp-flower", deriving from the Akkadian qunnabu.

“It is meant in multiple meanings: such as obedience, humility, prayer, supplication, worship, standing, long standing, and silence. In Islam"It is stated that Qunoot in Witr is to recite supplications after Witr, taught by the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, Al-Hasan bin Ali. If he raises the bowing in the last rak’ah with which he prays Witr, he says after bowing, and after the prescribed prayer.
From Chinese 群 (qún) meaning "group, crowd, flock" combined with 英 (yīng) meaning "flower, petal, brave, hero". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
Most likely an invented name. This name is borne by Qunyquekya Wallis, the older sister of actress Quvenzhané Wallis.
From Sino-Vietnamese 國家 (quốc gia) meaning "nation, national".
From Sino-Vietnamese 國華 (quốc hoa) meaning "glory of the nation", composed of 國 (quốc) meaning "nation" and 華 (hoa) meaning "splendid, illustrious".
From Sino-Vietnamese 國際 (quốc tế) meaning "international", composed of 國 (quốc) meaning "country" and 際 (tế) meaning "between".
From Sino-Vietnamese 國體 (quốc thể) meaning "a nation's honor, national prestige", composed of 國 (quốc) meaning "nation, country" and 體 (thể) meaning "body, style, form".

Means "what God wants" in Latin. This was the name of a 5th-century saint from North Africa who was martyred in the Valerianus persecutions. He was a spiritual student and friend of Saint Augustine of Hippo.
Likely a variant of Corey and Corrie.
Possibly a variant of Cora. This is the name of several characters in popular culture, including a protagonist in the films 'TRON' and 'TRON: Legacy', and a figure in 'Star Trek'.
Name of the patron Saint of Cork (Ireland)
From the Latin phrase quo vadis meaning "where are you going?"
The name of the main character in E. Annie Proulx‘s The Shipping News (1993). The name apparently is based on the English word coil.
One of the many names in Greenlandic meaning "snow bunting". This is the name of Greenlandic influencer Qupanuk Olsen, better known as 'Q's Greenland'.
Possibly from the Azerbaijani qu quşu meaing "swan".

Possibly derived from the Quraysh tribe. The Quraysh were a powerful merchant tribe that controlled Mecca and its Ka'aba and that according to tradition descended from Ishmael. Muhammad was born into the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraysh tribe.

Variant of Karon 1 (which is simply a combination of the popular phonetic elements ka and ron), the spelling altered to correspond with the name of the central religious text of Islam. The word Quran literally means "book, reading, recitation" in Arabic, derived from the verb قرأ (qaraʾa) meaning "to read (aloud), to recite".
Derived from qurbon meaning "religious offering, oblation" and gul meaning "rose, flower".
Derived from qurbon meaning "religious offering, oblation" and jon meaning "spirit, soul".
Derived from qurbon meaning "religious offering, oblation" and oy meaning "moon".
Derived from qurbon meaning "religious offering, oblation" and poshsha , an endearing term for a girl or woman.
Derived from qurbon meaning "religious offering, oblation" and shakar meaning "sugar, candy, sweets".
Derived from qurbon meaning "religious offering, oblation" and sulu(v) meaning "beautiful".
Aramaic and Assyrian form of Quiricus.
Means "having a lot of gold" in Aymara.
Derived from Quechua quri "gold" and quyllur "star".
Derived from Quechua quri meaning "gold" and t'ika meaning "flower".

Means "consolation of the eye, delight, joy, pleasure" in Arabic, from قرة (qurra) meaning "comfort, pleasure, soothing" combined with عين (ʿayn) meaning "eye". This was a title of Fatimah Baraghani (also known as Táhirih), a 19th-century Persian poet, theologian and reformer.
First part of compound Arabic names beginning with قرة ال (Qurrat al) meaning "consolation of the, delight of the" (such as Qurrat al-Ayn).

Arabic and Assyrian form of Constantinus (see Constantine 1). A notable bearer of this name was the Syrian Arab intellectual Qustantin Zariq (1909-2000), who is better known in English as Constantin Zurayk or Zureiq.
From the Aymara quta meaning "lake" and wara wara meaning "star".
Means "base of the religion" from قطب (qutb) meaning "base, pole, axis" and دين (dīn) meaning "religion, faith".
Alternate transcription of قطب‌ الدین (see Qutb ad-Din).
Derived from qutli meaning "blessed, full of blessings" and bibi meaning "learned woman".
Derived from Uzbek qutli meaning "blessed, full of blessings" and jamol meaning "beauty".
Georgian form of Qutluğ. A notable bearer of this name was the medieval Georgian politician Qutlu Arslan (12th century), who was of Kipchak descent.
Possibly from the Ottoman Turkish قوتلو (kutlu, qutlu) meaning "fortunate, lucky" and ay meaning "moon".
Derived from the Old Turkic adjective qutluğ meaning "blessed, fortunate" as well as "happy".
Etymology uncertain. This was the Mongol personal name of Princess Supreme Jeguk, who was the wife of Chungnyeol of Goryeo.
From Uygur قۇتلۇق meaning "happy, joyous, lucky", cognate of Kutlu.

This name was first borne by American actress Quvenzhané Wallis (2003-). It is derived from the initial syllables of her parents' names, Qulyndreia and Venjie, combined with zhané, an altered form of the Swahili word jini meaning "fairy".
From Sino-Vietnamese 龜 (quy) meaning "turtle", referring to one of the Four Benevolent Animals in Chinese mythology.
From a non-Sino-Vietnamese reading of Chinese 跪 (quỳ) meaning "to kneel" or from Sino-Vietnamese 葵 (quỳ) meaning "sunflower".
From Sino-Vietnamese 樻 (quỹ) meaning "fund, treasury, cabinet".
Means "happy queen" in Quechua, from quya "queen" and kusi "happy, joyful".
Vietnamese form of Kaya, from Sanskrit काय (kāya). This is the Vietnamese name of Maha Kaya (?-1458), a king of Champa.
From Sino-Vietnamese 眷 (quyến) meaning "to have affection for, to take interest in, family members".
Means "to be determined to", from Sino-Vietnamese 決 (quyết) meaning "to determine, decide" and 心 (tâm) meaning "heart, mind, soul".
Vietnamese form of Kali 1, referring to Maha Kali, the king of Champa from 1441 to 1442 and 1446 to 1449.
Derived from Quechua quyllur meaning "star" and rit'i meaning "snow". This is a famous Peruvian religious festival.
From Sino-Vietnamese 炯 (quýnh) meaning "bright, brilliant, intelligent".
Derived from Uzbek quyosh meaning "sun, sunlight" and oy meaning "moon".
From a non-Sino-Vietnamese reading of Chinese 橘 (quýt) meaning "tangerine, mandarin orange".

The general consensus is that this name is ultimately derived from the Georgian verb უყვარს (uqvars) meaning "to love", which basically gives the name the meaning of "beloved". Also compare Saqvarela.This name was borne by four medieval rulers of Samtskhe (each from the Jaqeli dynasty), the last of whom lived in the 16th century.In Georgian literature, Qvarqvare is the name of the eponymous character of the popular Georgian Soviet comic play Qvarqvare Tutaberi (1928) written by the Georgian playwright Polikarpe Kakabadze (1893-1972).
Variant of Queen. Qween Amor (1988-) is a performance artist who predominantly utilizes public space for her performances.
Perhaps a blend of Quintarius and Ontario.

Created by author George R. R. Martin for a character in his series 'A Song of Ice and Fire'. In the series, Qyburn is a former maester who was expelled from the Citadel for unethical experiments and necromancy.
Means "to go out, to become" in Vietnamese.
This name is based off a god
Means "he who delayed at birth" in Somali.
From Japanese 羅 (ra) meaning "gauze, thin silk" combined with 天 (ama) meaning "heavens, sky". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means "exalted" or "thunder". In the Bible, this is a son of Cush.
Means "thunder of Yahweh" in Hebrew. This is a minor character in the Bible, a prince who returns from exile in the book of Nehemiah.
In the case of American television writer Raamla Mohamed she was named after a little girl who had the same name her mom later added an extra a so her name could be pronounced correctly
Alternate transcription of Hewbrew רַעֲנָן (see Raanan).
Raanu was the Agori leader of the Fire Tribe.
Means "liberal; bestowing" in many Indian languages.

Name: Raavi / Raawi रावीMEANING - sounding, roaring ,praise. It is derived from Sanskrit word Raav / राव. It is the name of a river in IndiaIt shouldn't be confused with Sanskrit boy name Ravi / रवि which means SunUsage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhala, Hindi, Sikh, Buddhist
MEANING - King, royalOrigin - Nepali, Indian, Tamil Usage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhala, Hindi, Sikh, Buddhist, Hindi, Mauritian, Fijian Nepali, Hindu - राय
Possibly a feminine version of Rabe.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رباب (see Rabab), chifely used in Morocco.
Dargin form of Ramadan. Another source suggests that it is derived from Arabic رب (rabb) meaning "master, lord, king" and Persian دانا (dana) meaning "wise, learned".
The ambitious crown prince of Calormen in 'The Horse and His Boy' by C.S. Lewis.
Galician and Portuguese form of Raban via it's Latinized form Rabanus.
Italian, Spanish, Sardinian, and Esperanto form of Raban via it's Latinized form Rabanus.
Invented variant of Rastaban. This is the name of Rabastan Lestrange, a character in the "Harry Potter" series written by J.K. Rowling.
Either a German diminutive of Raban or a Swedish diminutive of Rafael.Name day in the Finland Swedish calendar: June 1st
A short form of Radbod. It coincides in spelling and pronunciation with modern German word Rabe "raven".
Alternate transcription of Arabic ربيعة (see Rabi'a), chifely used in Morocco and Algeria.
Probably a feminine form of Rabe. This name became popular in Germany in the early 1970s, due to Rabea Hartmann (born in 1947), a German TV personality.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رباب (see Rubab) chiefly used in North Africa.
A corrupted vernacular Middle English form of Rebecca. This was used in the south of England in the latter half of the 16th century.
A spelling of Rebecca which seems to have been used in the 1600s and 1700s, and was apparently revived in the late 1990s.
From Tibetan རབ་རྒྱས (rab-rgyas) meaning "very broad, very wide", derived from རབ (rab) meaning "very, extremely" and རྒྱས (rgyas) meaning "extensive, broad, wide".
Alternate transcription of Tibetan རབ་རྒྱས (see Rabgay).
Alternate transcription of Thai ระเบียบ (see Rabiap).
Alternate transcription of Arabic رابعة (see Raabi'a), as well as the Indonesian, Malay and Urdu form.
Chechen and Ingush form of Rabi'a.

Means "white tail", derived from Spanish rabo "tail" and Spanish cano "white". The original word described a horse with white hairs in its tail, though nowadays rabicano refers to a certain coat color for horses, specifically in roans. In literature, Rabicano is a magical horse featured in the epic romantic poem "Orlando Furioso" written by Ludovico Ariosto.
Alternate transcription of Arabic ربيع (see Rabi 1).
Alternate transcription of Arabic ربيع (see Rabi 1) chiefly used in Northern Africa.
Variant of Ravindra used by Sikhs.
Combination of the name Rabindra and Sanskrit नाथ (nātha) meaning "master, lord". A notable bearer was Bengali writer and composer Rabindranath Tagore (1861-1941).
From Arabic ربيع العالم (rabi' al-'alam), meaning "spring of the world".
Rabmag is the name of two figures in the Bible.
Meaning as of yet unknown. It is either a short form of a longer name, or an independent name in its own right.

Radagaisus (died 23 August 406) was a Gothic king who led an invasion of Roman Italy in late 405 and the first half of 406. A committed Pagan, Radagaisus evidently planned to sacrifice the Senators of the Christian Roman Empire to the gods and to burn Rome to the ground. Radagaisus was executed after being defeated by the half-Vandal general Stilicho. 12,000 of his higher-status fighters were drafted into the Roman army and some of the remaining followers were dispersed, while so many of the others were sold into slavery that the slave market briefly collapsed. These Goths later joined Alaric I in his conquest of Rome in 410.

She is typically depicted as a woman with cow horns holding a sun disc on her head, similar to Hathor. She appears during the Fifth Dynasty (c.2494 BCE - c.2345 BCE), considered a companion of Ra, though never reaching the importance of Hathor. She is also known as a wife of the war-god Montu, forming a trinity with him and Harpocrates in Karnak and Medamud.

In the medieval poem "The Wedding of Sir Gawain and Dame Ragnelle", Arthur had fallen into the power of the Grim Baron, Gromer Somer Joure, who made him swear to return in a year and a day and either bring the correct answer to the riddle. or meet his death. While searching for the answer, Arthur met in Inglewood Forest a lady carrying a lute and riding a beautiful, richly caparisoned palfrey - but the woman herself was incredibly ugly and hideous. The Foul Lady was Dame Ragnell, Gromer's sister (though she did not tell Arthur that), and she gave Arthur the answer to the riddle in return for his and Gawaine's promise that Gawaine would wed her.The answer to the riddle is generally given as "Women most desire to have power over men", or "To have their own will in all things"Once she was married, she explained to Gawaine that he could choose whether to have her beautiful at night for himself alone and ugly by day in the sight of the world, or beautiful by day and ugly by night. Stymied, or at least pretending to be, he gave the choice back to her. His generosity broke the enchantment completely - her stepmother had transformed her into an ugly hag until the best man in England married her and gave her control over his body and goods.There is inconclusive evidence that her name was taken from a pagan god known to Middle English writers. Both Arthur and Gawaine refer to her repeatedly as a fiend or devil.

From Japanese 楽 (raku) meaning "enjoyment, ease, simplicity, comfort, music" combined with 人 (to) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer is Rakuto Tochihara, a Japanese actor from Tokyo, and a graduate of Horikoshi High School.
From Japanese 楽 (raku) meaning "music" combined with 雲 (un) meaning "cloud". Other kanji combinations are possible.
English short form of the Spanish name Esmeralda.
Possibly a variation of the English name Alden.
Gascon corruption of Eulalia (via the truncated form Lalia).
a combination of the suffix Ra and the name Linda.
Feminine form of Ράλλης (Rallis), a Greek form of the Norman name Raoul.
Medieval Greek form of Radulf (see Ralph), reportedly via its French form Raoul.A known bearer of this name was the Greek painter and writer Rallis Kopsidis (1929-2010).
Perhaps a combination of Ramona and Alana.
Extremely rare feminine form of Ralph.

Variant form of Ralphina, of which the spelling and pronunciation was inspired or influenced by French feminine names.A known bearer of this name was Ralphine North McDonald (1842-1918), the wife of the American colonel and businessman Mark Lindsey McDonald (1833-1917). Her husband had built a reservoir in California in the late 19th century, which he went on to name Lake Ralphine, in honour of her.
Means "fifteenth day of a lunar month, day of a full moon" in Vietnamese.
Ramaa is one of the names of Goddess Lakshmi
Malayalam and Tamil form of Ramachandra.
Combination of the name Ramadan and Persian شاه (shah) meaning "king".
Alternate transcription of Arabic رمضان (see Ramadan), as well as the Indonesian and Swahili form.
Serbian name for an angel of joy, possibly referring to Judeo-Christian angel Ramiel.

Ramah in Benjamin was a city of ancient Israel. It was located near Gibeon and Mizpah to the West, Gibeah to the South, and Geba to the East. It is identified with modern Er-Ram, about 8 km north of Jerusalem.
Malayalam and Tamil form of Ramakrishna.
From Sanskrit रामलिङ्ग (rāmaliṅga) meaning "mark of Rama", derived from the name of the Hindu god Rama 1 combined with लिङ्ग (liṅga) meaning "mark, sign, form".
Tamil and Malayalam form of Ramana.
Means "lord Rama" from the name of the Hindu god Rama 1 combined with Sanskrit नाथ (nātha) meaning "master, lord". This is another name of Rama.
Tamil and Malayalam form of Ramanatha.
From Sanskrit रमण (ramaṇa) meaning "pleasing, delightful" and दीप (dīpa) meaning "lamp, light".
Alternate transcription of Punjabi Gurmukhi ਰਮਨਦੀਪ (see Ramandeep).
An old man who is a retired star in 'The Voyage of the Dawn Treader' by C.S. Lewis.
From Sanskrit रमण (ramaṇa) meaning "pleasing, delightful" and प्रीति (prīti) meaning "pleasure, joy, love".

The first element of this name is derived from the Lithuanian adjective ramus meaning "calm, quiet, peaceful" (see Ramūnas). The second element is either derived from Lithuanian mantus meaning "intelligent" (see Daumantas) or from Lithuanian manta meaning "property, estate" as well as "wealth, riches, fortune".
Alternate transcription of Hindi and Marathi रामप्रसाद or Bengali রামপ্রসাদ (see Ramprasad).
Possibly an abbreviation of rangimārie meaning "peace"; or interpreted as "lucky day" from Rā "day, sun" and Waimarie meaning "luck".
Means "lord Rama", from the name of the Hindu god Rama 1 combined with Sanskrit स्वामिन् (svāmin) meaning "master, chief, lord".
Variant of Rahmat, chiefly used in Senegal.
Derived from the Sesotho tjato meaning "agility".
Variant of Rahmat. It is chiefly used in Niger and Ivory Coast.
Relating to Ramadon,to commemorate the first revelation of the Quran to Muhammad according to Islamic belief.Meaning "Revolution".
Tajik and Uzbek form of رمضان (Ramazan), which is the Persian and Ottoman Turkish form of Ramadan.

It’s actual meaning is “the one who calms the heart” And it’s a name given to someone born during or after a difficult period…..Or a child that brings relief, rest, or stability to the family…… Rambai is a traditional personal name from the Sayawa (also called Zaar) people of Bogoro and Tafawa Balewa in Bauchi State, Nigeria.The Sayawa are an indigenous ethnic group whose language, Zaar, belongs to the West Chadic branch of the Afro-Asiatic language family — the same large linguistic family that includes Hausa, Arabic, Hebrew, and Amharic.
Derived from the Germanic element hraban or hramn "raven" combined with Old High German bald "bold, brave."
From the Ancient Germanic Ragimbald, comprised of ragin "advice" and bald "bold".
Medieval Italian diminutive of Rambaldo, as -uccio is an Italian masculine diminutive suffix.
A Hebrew acronym R-M-B-N (/ˌrɑːmˈbɑːn/; רמב״ן‎) from Rabbeinu Mōšeh bēn-Nāḥmān, "Our Rabbi Moses son of Nahman"). It is the Hebrew name of Nachmanides.

Diminutive of Ramberto.A well known bearer waa Rambertino di Guido Buvalelli (died 1221) who was a Bolognese judge, statesman, diplomat, and poet. He was the earliest of the podestà-troubadours of thirteenth-century Lombardy. His reputation has secured a street named in his honour in his birthplace: the Via Buvalelli Rambertino in Bologna.
Italian form of Rambert. A known bearer of this name was the Italian military leader Ramberto Malatesta (died in January 1330).
Medieval Italian diminutive of Ramberto, as -uccio is an Italian masculine diminutive suffix.
Means "plantain" in Sanskrit. In Hindu mythology this is the name of an apsara (female celestial spirit) known for her talent in dance and music.
Medieval German short form of masculine Ram- names of which the second element starts with b-, such as Rambald and Rambert.
Swedish dialectal variant of Ramborg used until the 19th century.
Indonesian and Malay variant of Ramadan.
Alternate transcription of Ramadan chiefly used in Northern Africa.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رمضان (see Ramadan) chiefly used in North Africa.
Shortening of Ramadan, the ninth month of the Islamic calendar.
Derived from French dimanche des Rameaux "Palm Sunday". This name used to be given to children born on this day.
Variant of Rami most used in Syria.
The name Rameel means 'Mercy Of God' or in The Ancient Assyrian it means 'God is in a high place'. This name tends to be used by Assyrians and is a Christian Catholic name.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رامز (see Ramiz), as well as the usual Urdu and Dhivehi form.
Invented name combining the popular prefix ra with the given name Jamel.
Possibly an invented name inspired by Jamelle.
Combination of the names of the Hindu deities Rama 1 and Indra.
From Japanese 星 (ra) meaning "star", 姫 (me) meaning "princess" combined with 海 (ru) meaning "sea, ocean". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Malayalam and Tamil form of Ramesha.
Medieval English borrowing of Old French Ramette.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رامز (see Ramiz).

The name of the Egyptian high priest in Giuseppe Verdi's 1871 opera 'Aida'. This name has also been used as a given name in the Dominican Republic and Haiti. In these cases, usage is most likely related to Rafael 'Ramfis' Trujillo and his son Ramfis Trujillo, who were both briefly dictators of the Dominican Republic.
Derived from the Germanic element hraban or hramn "raven" combined with Old High German fridu "peace."
In the case of Ramgen 'Ram' Revilla (1988-2011), a Filipino actor who was murdered at age 23 years, it is a combination of Ramon and Genelyn, the names of his parents.

column3: 来未, 羅海, 蘭美, 良実, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|रामी(Sanskrit, Hindi, Marathi, Nepali)|רמי(Hebrew)
column12: Finnish pet form of Reimund and Abram 1.

column3: 羅美亜, 裸魅亜, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|راميا(Arabic)|ראמיה(Hebrew)
column12: From Japanese 羅 (ra) meaning "lightweight fabric", 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful" combined with 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 良 (ra) meaning "good", 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
this name Ramila originate from eastern part of nepal with its meaning "Good looking" " beauty" "loving"
Elaboration of Rama, ultimately derived from Lithuanian adjective ramus meaning "calm" (compare Jorinta).
Occitan and Catalan form of Ramirus (see Ramiro).
Possibly intended as a feminine form of Ramses.
Combination of the phonetic element ra and the given name Amiyah.
Derived from Indonesian and Malay ramalan meaning "prediction, prophecy".
Form of Ramnarayan primarily used in Trinidad and Tobago and Guyana by people of Indian descent.

Anglicized form of Ramón. Possibly transferred use of the surname Ramone in homage to the American punk rock band the Ramones, which was inspired by Paul McCartney's use of the pseudonym Paul Ramon during his Silver Beatles days.
A feminine variant of Ramon by combining it with Etta
Form of Ramon/Ramone and Ramona. More often used as a feminine name.
Combination of the phonetic element ra with the name Lamonte.
Short form of Ramona.This name is extremely rare as an official name on birth certificates; it is almost always used informally.
From Spanish and Portuguese ramos meaning "branches", in reference to the Christian festivity Domingo de Ramos ("Palm Sunday").
From Egyptian rꜥ-ms meaning "Ra is born", derived from the name of the god Ra combined with the root msj "to be born". Compare Ramesses.

Meaning "heights of Gilead," it was a Levitical city and city of refuge east of the Jordan river in the Hebrew Bible, also called "Ramoth in Gilead" (Deuteronomy 4:43; Joshua 20:8; 21:38) or "Ramoth Galaad" in the Douay-Rheims Bible. It was located in the tribal territorial allotment of the tribe of Gad.
Variant of Ramazon, which is the main Uzbek form of Ramazan (see Ramadan).
Name : Rampa रम्पाmeaning: the implement of a worker in leatherUsage - Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhala, Hindi
Form of Ramprasad primarily used in Trinidad and Tobago and Mauritius by people of Indian descent.
In some versions of Rapunzel, Rapunzel's name is Rampion, after the lettuce her father stole.
Transferred use of the surname Ramsamy.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Rameses.
Meaning uncertain. This was the name of a prominent Sasanian musician.
Derived from the Germanic element hraban or hramn "raven" combined with þruþ "strength."

column3: ラム(Japanese Katakana)|らむ(Japanese Hiragana)|麗夢, 羅夢, 良夢, 来夢, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 麗 (ra) meaning "beautiful, lovely, resplendent" combined with 夢 (mu) meaning "dream". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 良 (ra) meaning "good", 夢 (mu) meaning "dream" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Romansh form of Raimund, traditionally found in the Surselva region and in central Grisons.
Derived from the Germanic element hraban or hramn "raven" combined with Old High German mund "protection."
A skilled knight slain by Karyet (Gareth) in Ulrich von Zatzikhoven's Lanzelet.He could be identified with Wace's Romarec or Wolfram's Gahmuret.
Transferred use of the surname Ramus.

Derived from the Lithuanian adjective ramus meaning "calm, quiet, peaceful" (see Ramūnas) combined with Baltic vyd meaning "to see" (see Vytautas). Also compare other names that end in -vydas, such as Alvydas and Tautvydas.
Derived from the Germanic element hraban or hramn "raven" combined with Old High German wart "guard."
Derived from Sanskrit ramya (रम्य) "lovely; pleasing; delightful; beautiful; charming".Ramya is the stage name of Indian actress Divya Spandana (born 1982).
From Sino-Korean 羅 "net for catching birds" combined with 勉 "endeavor, make effort; urge". Other hanja combinations can also form this name.
The name Ramza is rarely given in the south slavic languages (Mostly in Dalmatia). The name is very likely a corruption of the name "Erasmus", the patron saint of sailors.
Tatar and Russified Bashkir feminine form of Ramzi.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رمزي (see Ramzi).
Dialectal variant of Rầm or Dần.

column3: רַן, רָן, רן(Hebrew)|冉, 然, 染, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Means "singing" or "(he) sang" in Hebrew (being the past tense masculine singular form of the verb לָרֹן laron "to sing, utter joyful sounds").

column3: ラナ(Japanese Katakana)|らな(Japanese Hiragana)|楽夏, 羅南, 来奈, 羅菜, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|رڼا(Pashto)
column12: Derived from Norman ranne "queen" (via Old French royne, reine, from Latin rēgīna). This name was used as a translation of Malka (see also Reine).
comes from fiction, name means strong and courageous and somewhat reckless.
From Sanskrit रण (raṇa) meaning "battle, war, combat" and जित (jita) meaning "conquered, defeated, won".
Anglicized form of Raghnailt. A 12th-century bearer was Ranalt O'Farrell, wife of Hugh O'Connor, the last king of Connacht.
Derived from the classical Hebrew רְנָנָה meaning "happiness, singing, rejoicing"
Derived from rana meaning "green, green fields" and niejta meaning "girl, daughter". This is the Sami goddess of spring and fertility.
Means "folded, kept aside" or "calm, smooth" in Malagasy. This was the name of three queens of Madagascar.
Derived from Sanskrit रण (raṇa) meaning "delight, pleasure, gladness" combined with वीर (vīrá) meaning "man, hero, husband".
Transferred use of the surname Rance.
Derived from the English name Francis or Frances.
Masculine kurdish name from southern Kurdistan (Iraqi Kurdistan)
Alternate transcription of Arabic رندة (see Randa).

In the Saga of Ragnar Lothbrók, his second wife Áslaug changes her name to Randalín when she goes to avenge the lives of her stepsons.Her name is of uncertain origin and meaning. One theory tries to connect her name to Old Norse rǫnd "shield" and hlín which is both the Old Norse word for "protection" and a poetic term for "woman".
Likely a combination of Randall and Darius. Can be spelled with a capital on the "D", RanDarius.
Combination of the Old Norse name elements rǫnd "shield; rim, edge (of a shield)" and sól "sun".
Not sure, possibly a form of Ander or Randel
Modern form of Randgríðr. This name is not used as a personal name in Norway, but a valkyrie bears this name.
Derived from the Germanic name elements rǫnd "shield" and gríð "peace, protection, mercy, truce". This is the name of a Valkyrie in Norse mythology.
From Sanskrit रण (raṇa) meaning "battle, war, combat" and धीर (dhīra) meaning "wise".
Possibly an elaboration of Randi 1 using the phonetic element sha.

Short form of various compound names formed with rand "(shield) rim" as the first or second element, such as Bertrando or Randolf. Estonian folk etymology likes to associate this name with Estonian rand "shore".The name was borne by an Alemannic leader who sacked Mainz in the 4th century.
From the Old German elements rant meaning "rim (of a shield)" and walt meaning "power, authority" meaning "powerful rim".
Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish form of Randoald.
Portuguese, Italian, and Spanish form of Randolf.
Derived from the Germanic name elements rǫnd "shield" and ulfr "wolf".

From the English word "random".Random was the name of a male character in The Chronicles of Amber series by Roger Zelazny. In 'Mostly Harmless', the fifth book in the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy series by Douglas Adams, Random is Arthur Dent's and Trillian's daughter.
Transferred use of the surname Randon.

Extremely rare variant of Ransom, which was originally an East Anglian patronym derived from the personal name Rand (or Rande), a medieval short form of Germanic names containing the element rand meaning "rim (of a shield)".
Old Swedish and younger form of Randví.
Old Norse combination of rǫnd "shield" (with a rim) and vé "home", "temple", "sanctuary".
Variant reading of Nebra, now meaning "Ra is my lord". This is a highly questionable reading as this would assume that the Sun was already being worshiped as an independent deity.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رنيم (see Ranim).
Ancient Egyptian masculine name meaning "Ra is beautiful".

column4: English (American, Modern)|English (Australian, Modern, Rare)|English (New Zealand, Modern, Rare)
column5: rah-nee(American English, Australian English, New Zealand English)
column12: Variant of Rani 1, Ronnie, or Renee influenced by the spelling of Raleigh.
Combination of the name Ran, means "singing" or "(he) sang", and El, reference to God.
An invented name likely inspired by Vanessa.

Meaning and origin unknown. This name is borne by the Dutch (protestant) preacher Ranfar Kouwijzer (b. 1973), who occasionally has interviews with the media and also writes columns and articles for Dutch newspapers (such as Trouw). His name is extremely unusual in the Netherlands, to the point that it looks foreign. Yet, he was born in the Netherlands and appears to be of ethnic Dutch descent as well. It looks like his parents might have invented his name. The fact that he is the only bearer of the name on all of Facebook points to this, as does the fact that there is next to no concrete information about the name on the Internet.
Means "to try hard" or "evening glow" in Vietnamese.
A feminine marker in Bahnar, used before the given name.

From Sanskrit रङ्ग (raṅga) meaning "place of assembly, arena" combined with नाथ (nātha) meaning "master, lord". This is the name of a Hindu deity particularly revered in southern India. He is considered a form of Vishnu.
Tamil and Malayalam form of Ranganatha.
It means "recollection; remembrance", from the verb kurangarira.

Means "widow" in Balinese. In Balinese mythology this is the name of a demon who embodies the forces of evil, considered the nemesis of Barong. Her eternal battle with Barong is depicted in Balinese dance, in which she is portrayed as an old woman with long hair and nails and a terrifying face with fangs, protruding eyes and a long tongue.
Alternate transcription of Tibetan རང་གྲོལ (see Rangdol).
Alternate transcription of Pashto رنګين (see Rangin).
Younger form of Ragnhilda traditionally found in the western parts of Sweden.
Transferred use of the surname Ranger.
From a Javanese title for a village chief or low-ranking court official.
Means "heaven of the gods" in Maori. A place in Hawaiki, the ancestral land.

The japanese "Ran" means "Chrysanthemum".While "Giku" means "Riot/War".-------------------------------------"Ran" is the Japanese name for "orchid", "giku" is the Japanese word "apprehension" or "uneasiness".
Means "ocean sky" from rangi "sky" and moana "ocean".
Means "colourful" in Pashto, from Persian رنگین (rangin).
Derived from Rangi and nui meaning "large, big, vast, great." This is another name for the Maori god of the sky.
This is the name of the god who divided Heaven and earth and shaped man. This is also the name of a Maori Chief named Te Rangi Tokona.
Means "to create, to establish, to build" in Thai.
Derived from Pali raṃsima meaning "radiant, having rays".

column3: รังสิมันต์(Thai)
column12: Derived from Pali raṁsimant meaning "sun, radiant, having rays".

column3: รังสิมันต์(Thai)
column12: Alternate transcription of Thai รังสิมันต์ (see Rangsiman).
Faroese and Old Danish form of Hrani.
Greek short form of Ourania and Romani short form of Urania.
Means "God is Joy" in Hebrew-------------------------------------Combination of the name Rani 2 means "my joy" or "my song" and El, reference to God.
Variant of Raniero. This name is is borne by Ranieri III di Monaco. It is also the Italian name of Rainier III, Prince of Monaco.
Origin - Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhala, Hindi, Sikh, Buddhist MEANING - "a bridle"Indian pronunciation - raNikA
Portuguese form of Ragnhild (compare Raginhild) and variant of Renilda.
Means "musical ringing sound, sweet singing voice" in Arabic, from the root رنم (ranima) meaning "to sing a song, to chant, to recite in a singsong voice".
Alternate transcription of رنيم (see Ranim), chiefly used in Northern Africa.

The first element of this name is derived from Serbo-Croatian rani or rano "early, forward", which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic ranъ. Also compare Polish rano "morning" and Czech/Slovak ráno "morning", which also derive from the same Proto-Slavic root. The second element is derived from Slavic mir "peace". As such, the meaning of this name is roughly "early peace".

From Russian ранний (rannyy) "early", given to first born or child born early in morning. This was likely based on Medieval Slavic naming trends in names such as Odynets and Tretyak or inspired by popular Russian fairy tale Zorka, Vechorka, and Polunochka about princesses named after time of day they were born.

The first element of this name is derived from Serbo-Croatian rani or rano "early, forward", which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic ranъ. Also compare Polish rano "morning" and Czech/Slovak ráno "morning", which also derive from the same Proto-Slavic root. The second element is derived from Slavic slav "glory". As such, the meaning of this name is roughly "early glory".
Derived from Sanskrit रणित (raṇita) meaning "sounding, rattling, ringing, tinkling".
Form of Rania, using German phonetics.
Southern Indian and Sinhalese form of Ranjit.

column3: 蘭夏, 蘭花, 蘭華, 蘭香, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Short form of Ragneiðr (variant of Ragnheiðr) or Ragnhildr.
Transferred use of the surname Rankin.

column3: ラン子(Kanji/Katakana)|らん子(Kanji/Hiragana)|融, 蘭子, 爐子, 乱子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 蘭 (ran) meaning "orchid" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child" and the kanji used among both genders is 融 (ranko) meaning "hot air; steam (during cooking)". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 燃 (rán) meaning "light fire, ignite" and 玲 (líng) meaning "tinkling of jade".
Ranma Saotome is a fictional character and the titular protagonist of the manga series Ranma ½.

column3: 蘭丸, 藍丸, 嵐丸, 欄丸, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|らんまる(Japanese Hiragana)|ランマル(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Ran combined with the suffix 丸 (maru) meaning "circle, round," used before the Meiji Period (1868-1912) as a suffix denoting affection (along with -maro (麿/麻呂)) and was given to boys of upper class until they came of age, usually at ages 13 to 17.One bearer of this name was Sengoku period military commander Mori Ranmaru (森 蘭丸), also known as Mori Naritoshi (森 成利) (1565–1582). From an early age, he was an attendant to powerful daimyō Oda Nobunaga (織田 信長) (1534–1582) and Ranmaru was well-known for his devotion, loyalty, and bravery, culminating in his seppuku upon Nobunaga's death.This name is rarely used.
From Japanese 蘭 (ran) meaning "orchid" combined with 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: らんな(Japanese Hiragana)|蘭菜, 蘭奈, 蘭那, 蘭和, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 蘭 (ran) meaning "orchid" combined with 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Possibly Frisian in origin, in which case the name is probably derived from a feminine Germanic given name that contains one of the following three Germanic elements: ragin meaning "advice" (see Rayner), rand meaning "rim (of a shield)" (see Randolf) or hraban meaning "raven" (see Ronne). Otherwise, this name may be a short form of (combined) given names that end in -ranne, such as Floranne and Loranne.
Diminutive of names like Miranda, Randall and Randolf.
The first element of this name is either derived from Old Norse regin or rögn "advice", or from Old Norse rann "house." The second element is derived from Old Norse veig "strength".
Combination of the Old Norse name elements rann "house" and vár "spring (the season); woman (in a poetic context); truth".
From the given name Ra'no and xon meaning "king, ruler".
Means "beautiful year". This was the name of a minor goddess associated with the Ancient Egyptian New Year.

column3: 藍々, 蘭々, 爛々, 乱々(Japanese Kanji)|らんらん(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: Derived from the Japanese kanji 藍 (ran) meaning "indigo" or 蘭 (ran) meaning "orchid" or 爛 (ran) meaning "be sore, inflamed, bleary, fester" or 乱 (ran) meaning "chaos, disorder, revolt, rebellion" combined with 々 an iteration mark denoting the repetition of the previous kanji.Other kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: 蘭梨, 蘭莉, 蘭里, 蘭林, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 蘭 (ran) meaning "orchid" combined with 梨 (ri) meaning "pear". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Ransley is a name and it’s used for a boy of Old English origin. It may derive from the Old English words hraefn (Raven) and leah (meadow), which combine to mean “Raven meadow”. Another possible meaning is “reed marsh fam”. And if you want to pay a tribute to Ransley you know, or to honor the intelligent and mysterious raven, this could be a perfect name!

Possibly used in reference to the word ransom, meaning money paid or delivered in exchange for the release of something or someone.Used most often in the 19th-century it has since fallen out of use. Notable bearers include L.A. city council member Ransom M. Callicott, writer Ransom Riggs, automobile businessman Ransom E. Olds (for whom Oldsmobile was named), and University of Wisconsin-Madison professor Ransom Asa Moore.The name has also been used for numerous fictional characters, from books such as C.S. Lewis' 'Out of the Silent Planet' and films such as 'Knives Out'.
Norwegian combination of rann "house" and steinn "stone".
蘭 (ran): 蘭 is an orchid.太郎 (taro): It actually means the taro plant, but another meaning is "man" (basically).

column3: 嵐人, 嵐斗, 嵐星, 嵐翔, 嵐都, 嵐音, 蘭斗, 蘭都, 蘭飛, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 嵐 (ran) meaning "storm, tempest" or 蘭 (ran) meaning "orchid" combined with 人 (to) meaning "person", 斗 (to), which refers to a Chinese constellation, 星 (to) meaning "star", 翔 (to) meaning "soar, fly", 都 (to) meaning "metropolis, capital, all, everything", 音 (to) meaning "sound" or 飛 (to) meaning "fly". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means "lake, pond, body of water" in Javanese.

Medieval Italian diminutive of Raniero, as -uccio is an Italian masculine diminutive suffix.Ranuccio can also be a contracted form of Ranalduccio in some cases, which is a variant form of Rinalduccio.This name was borne by the paternal grandfather of Pope Paul III (1468-1549), who went on to name his son after him.
Derived from the Germanic element hraban or hramn "raven" combined with Gothic vulfs "wolf."

Raoden's storyline centers on his efforts to retain his sanity and improve the Elantrian way of life beyond the anarchy to which it succumbed when Elantris fell. He also manages to calm and disperse or incorporate the gangs which were terrorizing new Elantrians upon their arrival.

The lucky number of Rawal is 9, and lucky days are Wednesday, Friday. The Rawal lucky metal is Bronze, and lucky stone is Sapphire. Rawal (also spelled Raval) or Raol originally is a (regional) variation -like Rawat- of the Hindi princely ruler title Ra(d)ja(h) (literally "king") used in some princely states in Rajputana and Western India (notably Gujarat), and is now also used as a caste designation or surname by several communities in Southern Asia. Rawal caste is mentioned at 50th number in the scheduled caste list of Rajasthan.

Rawen is a Tunisian unisex given name of Kurdish and Persian origin (see Raouane and Ravan). It is derived from the Kurdish and Persian root (rew / raw) meaning to move or to flow. Symbolically interpreted as “soul”, “spirit”, or “the one who moves” which evokes a sense of motion, vitality , and inner life.

Derived from Hebrew rekhah "soft; tender; velvety; silky".Recha Freier (1892-1984) was a German-born Jewish teacher and poet who founded the Youth Aliyah organization in 1933. The organization saved the lives of 22,000 Jewish children by helping them to leave Nazi Germany for Palestine.Recha is also a prominent character in Gotthold Ephraim Lessing's play Nathan the Wise, a fervent plea for religious tolerance published in 1779.

It is possible that the name is derived from Old English *Rædburh, composed of the elements ræd meaning "advice, counsel, wisdom" and burg meaning "fortress".

The first element of this archaic name is derived from Proto-Slavic rědъkъ "rare, sparse". Compare modern Russian redkij or redkiy, Croatian rijedak and Polish rzadki, all of which mean "rare, scarce, uncommon". The second element is derived from Slavic mir "peace", which gives the name the meaning of "peace is rare". Croatian and Serbian form of Redimir.

The name Redon appears in ancient inscriptions found in Santa Maria di Leuca (present-day Lecce), and on coins minted by the Illyrian city of Lissos, suggesting that he was worshipped as the guardian deity of the city, and probably as a sea god. The fact that Redon was always depicted on coins wearing a petasos demonstrates a connection with travelling and sailing, which led historians to the conclusion that Redon was the deity protector of travellers and sailors.

Of uncertain origin. This was the name of the last known survivor of the Transatlantic slave trade, a woman from present-day Benin in West Africa who was kidnapped at about age 12, sold to American slavers and taken to Alabama in 1860. She died in 1937.

P. C. Regalianus, known in English as Regalian, was a Roman usurper for a few months in 260 and/or 261, during the Crisis of the Third Century, a period of intense political instability in the Roman Empire. Regalian was acclaimed emperor by the troops along the Danube river, a region of the empire that frequently experienced barbarian raids, probably in the hope that he might be able to secure the frontier. Regalianus was married to Sulpicia Dryantilla, a woman from a prestigious senatorial family. ,How exactly he met his end is not entirely clear, but the most commonly accepted theory is that he died during a raid of Carnuntum by the Roxolani, possibly aided by a contingent of his men who had grown to oppose him.
In addition to the puritan usage, it has also seen usage as a diminutive of Beauregard.

Rehabiah is a name of Biblical origin mentioned three times in the Hebrew scriptures as the ancestor of a group of Levites. In 1 Chronicles 23:17 he is identified as as the son of Eliezer who is the son of Moses. According to 1 Chronicles 24:21 he is the father of Isshiah yet in 1 Chronicles 26:25 he is the father of Jeshaiah. In Hebrew Rehabiah means ‘Breadth; or extent; of the Lord’.

column12: This name is best known for being the name of the 7th-century Frankish saint Remaclus, who was born in Aquitaine (located in what is nowadays the southwest of France). His name is a corruption of Remagilus or Rimagilus, which are both latinizations of his original Germanic name, which must have been either Ramigil, Remigil or Rimigil.The second element of these names is either derived from Gothic gild meaning "sacrifice" or from the Germanic element gisil meaning "hostage" or "pledge". The first element is much more uncertain. In the case of Ram-, it might have been derived from the Germanic element hraban or hramn meaning "raven" or from Gothic ragin meaning "advice". Even Old Norse rammr meaning "strong" is a possibility. In the case of Rim-, it might have been derived from Old Norse hrim meaning "rime, hoarfrost" or from Gothic rimis meaning "peace, quietness, calmness". And finally, in the case of Rem-, all of the former possibilities are possible.

From Spanish remolino meaning "whirlwind". This is the name of an obscure title of the Virgin Mary, Nuestra Señora del Remolino (Our Lady of the Whirlwind), venerated in El Molar (Madrid, Spain).

column3: れもん(Japanese Hiragana)|レモン(Japanese Katakana)|怜門, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: It means "lemon" in Japanese, derived from the English word lemon.
Franco-Provençal and Gallo form of Raymond.
Gallo form of Raymond and French and Dutch variant of Remon.
Possibly a Latvian adoption of Rem.
Means "noisy/boisterous celebration" and/or "clamor" in Finnish.A famous bearer is Remu Aaltonen (born Henry Olavi Aaltonen), a Finnish drummer, singer and the lead musician of the band Hurriganes.
Invented name, likely combining the sounds of names likel Remigio and Samuel.
Albanian and Crimean Tatar feminine form of Remzi.
Means "knower of signs", from Arabic رمز (ramz) meaning "symbol, emblem" and Persian شناس (shenas), the present stem of شناختن (shenakhtan) meaning "to know".

column3: Ρένα(Greek)|レナ(Japanese Katakana)|れな(Japanese Hiragana)|玲奈, 礼菜, 玲七, 伶那, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|رەنا(Uyghur Arabic)
column12: Greek short form of Irini and Irene, Estonian short form of both Irena and Renate, and Scandinavian and German short form of Renate and Renata as well as a short form of names beginning with the Germanic element regin or ending in -rena. This name is borne by German artist Rena Tangens.
Dutch form of Renatus. Known bearers of this name include the Flemish politician Renaat Landuyt (b. 1959) and the Flemish architect Renaat Braem (1910-2001).
The meaning of this name is shared: some say that the meaning is "a flower/ perfume/ sand from heaven" or "a good smell long tree". Even this name is unisex more girls got that name.

column3: 恋愛, 蓮藍, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Combination of the names Ren and Ai 1.
An alternate Polish form of Reynold. It is used to render the name of Count Reginald I of Guelders in Polish as Renald I, Hrabiia Geldrii.
Possibly a combination of Rena and the popular suffix -lyn.

column3: 怜和未, 玲奈美, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 怜 (re) meaning "pity, sympathize" or 玲 (re) meaning "tinkling of jade", 和 (na) meaning "peace, harmony" or 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree" combined with 未 (mi) referring to the Sheep, the eighth of the twelve Earthly Branches or 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful". Other kanji combinations are also possible.
Corsican variant of Rinatu and Sicilian form of Renato.
Medieval Italian diminutive of Renata, as -uccia is an Italian feminine diminutive suffix.
Medieval Italian diminutive of Renato, as -uccio is an Italian masculine diminutive suffix.
Diminutive of Renée and cognate of Renette.
Transferred use of the French surname Renault.
From Chinese 仁 (rén) meaning "compassionate" combined with 博 (bó) meaning "wide, extensive, gamble" or 波 (bō) meaning "wave". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Transferred use of the surname Rendall.
MEANS: PRAISELIGUISTIC: VENDAORIGINATE FROM "RENDANI MUDZIMU" WHICH MEANS PARAISE GOD
Dutchization of the English name Randall.
Used in the role-playing game Dragon Age: Origins (2009). Possibly derived from the Spanish rendón meaning "bold, daring".
Means "firm belief" or "straightforward, sharp" in Indonesian.
This name is from the fictional book The Dragon Wall. It is a welsh name but can be used in North America.
From Chinese 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness" combined with 娥 (é) meaning "be beautiful, good". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 麗音, 礼音, 玲音, 伶音, 澪音, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 麗 (re) meaning "lovely, beautiful" combined with 音 (ne) meaning "sound". Other kanji combinations are possible.Usage of this name is, most likely, influenced by the name Rene or Renee.
Brazilian Portuguese and Franco-Provençal form of René.
Spelling of Renée that puts the accent on the second e. This is how American actress Reneé Rapp spells her name.
Dutch and Flemish diminutive of Renee.
From the English word renegade meaning "rebel, traitor".
Variant of Reinhilde used in the Philippines.
This is borne by the retired South African soccer player Reneilwe 'Yeye' Letsholonyane (1982-).
Variant of Renelde. It coincides with a place name, which belonged to a former tributary of the Seine.
Renen (and / or Ranen) means "to chant", "to sing" or "to praise" in Hebrew.Also Ranen is a settlement in the Negev region. The name of the settlement is based on Isaiah 35: 2.

In Egyptian mythology she was the goddess of nourishment and the harvest, and as such was worshiped mainly during harvest. She was often depicted as a cobra or as a woman with the head of a cobra. She was sometimes portrayed as the consort of Sobek, Shai, or Geb, with whom she had the snake god Nehebkau. Over time she became increasingly associated with Wadjet (the cobra on the crown of pharaohs), until she eventually became an aspect of Wadjet.
From Egyptian rn.s-rs meaning "her name is awake", derived from rn "name, identity, reputation" combined with the suffix .s "she, her, hers" and rs "to wake, awaken".
Possibly a blend of Renee and Vanessa
Gallo cognate of Renette and Reinette.
Referring to being "born again." See also Renata, the Latinized form originally used by Puritans before switching to the Anglicized variant.

Taken from the surname Renfrew.In the book series The Witcher, as well as the television adaptation, Renfri is an exiled princess who was born during a solar eclipse, and thus allegedly filled a prophecy along with many other girls who would bring about the end of the world. Because of this she was pursued by the obsessed sorcerer Stregobor and vilified by her stepmother, who sent thugs to kill her in the forest. Eventually she became the leader of a band of thieves and vowed vengeance on Stregobor, and Geralt of Rivia attempted to persuade her to abandon this quest.
Rengarenga means "New Zealand lily" in Māori, a native plant known as Arthropodium cirratum.

column3: 蓮華, 蓮花(Japanese Kanji)|れんげ(Japanese Hiragana)|レンゲ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 蓮華/蓮花 (renge), referring to the lotus flower that is sacred to Buddhists, as well as Hindus.Examples of fictional (female) characters include Renge Serizawa (芹沢 蓮華) from Battle Girl High School, Renge Hōshakuji (宝積寺 れんげ) from Ouran High School Host Club and Renge Miyauchi (宮内 れんげ) from Non Non Biyori.
Maybe a blend of Renger and Rainier.

West Frisian and medieval Dutch form of a Germanic name that was composed of the elements ragin meaning "advice, counsel" and ger meaning "spear".A notable bearer of this name is the Dutch racing driver Renger van der Zande (b. 1986).
Means "colourful", derived from Kurdish rengê meaning "colour".

From Chinese 仁和 (rénhé) meaning "benevolent, kindhearted"; or from 人 (rén) meaning "man, person, mankind, people" combined with 禾 (hé), a general term for "cereals". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 蓮舫(Japanese Kanji)|れんほう(Japanese Hiragana)|レンホウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Japanese transcription of Chinese 蓮舫, 莲舫 (see Lianfang).
From the Chinese 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness" and 虹 (hóng) meaning "rainbow".
From the Chinese 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness" and 花 (huā) meaning "flower".
Means "baobab tree" in Malagasy, ultimately from reny meaning "mother" and ala meaning "forest".

column3: 蓮一, 練一, 錬一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 蓮 (ren) meaning "lotus" combined with 一 (ichi) meaning "one". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Variant of Rainier, as well as a shorter form of Régnier.
Portuguese and Spanish form of Reinhild.

column3: レンジ(Japanese Katakana)|れんじ(Japanese Hiragana)|蓮司, 恋二, 漣道, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 蓮 (ren) meaning "lotus" and 司 (ji) meaning "boss, officer". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column12: From 廉 (ren) meaning "expensive, honest, clean", 士 (ji) meaning "warrior, samurai", and 朗 (ro) meaning "bright, clear". Other kanji combinations can be used.
From the Chinese 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness" and 菊 (jú) meaning "chrysanthemum".
From the Chinese 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness" and 娟 (juān) meaning "beautiful, graceful".

column3: れんか(Japanese Hiragana)|レンカ(Japanese Katakana)|廉加, 恋夏, 蓮佳, 怜歌, 廉花, 恋華, 蓮香, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 怜 (ren) meaning "wise", 廉 (ren) meaning "cheap, rested, contented, peaceful", or 恋 (ren) meaning "romance, love" combined with 佳 (ka) meaning "excellent, beautiful, good, pleasing", 香 (ka) meaning "fragrance" or 歌 (ka) meaning "song, sing". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 蓮吉, 廉吉, 廉麒, 連吉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 蓮 (ren) meaning "lotus" combined with 吉 (ki) meaning "good luck". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: れんこ(Japanese Hiragana)|レンコ(Japanese Katakana)|れん子(Kanji/Hiragana)|レン子(Kanji/Katakana)|漣子, 恋子, 廉子, 蓮子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 恋 (ren) meaning "romantic love" or 漣 (ren) meaning "continuously flowing, ripple" and 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness" and 兰 (lán) meaning "orchid".
Transferred use of the surname Renley.
From the Chinese 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness" and 玲 (líng) meaning "tinkling of jade".

Variant of Renley.A protagonist in American author Geogre R.R. Martin's 'A Song of Ice and Fire' novel series is named Renly Baratheon. He was portrayed by Gethin Anthony in the HBO television adaptation of the novels, 'Game of Thrones'.

column3: れんま(Japanese Hiragana)|蓮真, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 蓮 (ren) meaning "lotus" combined with 真 (ma) meaning "true, reality". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness" and 美 (měi) meaning "beauty, beautiful" or 妹 (mèi) meaning "younger sister".
Early Ancient Egyptian epithet given to queens which means "She who caries Seth 2".
From the surname Renn, or the similar-sounding names Ren or Wren.
Transferred use of the surname Rennard.
From the Chinese 任 (rèn) meaning "allow, appoint, trust, rely on" and 念 (niàn) meaning "say, idea, think of".
Transferred use of the surname Rennick.
Diminutive of names containing the element ren, such as Rene, Irene, Rennard or Warren.
Short form of names having the first name element ragin "advice, council".
From Japanese 廉 (ren) meaning "peaceful, honest", 之 (no), a possessive marker combined with 助 (suke) meaning "assistance". Other kanji combinations are also possible.
Pet form of various names that contain the -ren- sound.
Possibly an extremely rare variant transcription of Ranya.

column3: れの(Japanese Hiragana)|レノ(Japanese Katakana)|令乃, 令之, 冷希, 廉乃, 怜乃, 恋乃, 玲乃, 玲奏, 玲埜, 玲希, 玲音, 玲野, 礼乃, 礼野, 羚乃, 蓮乃, 蓮之, 蓮希, 鈴乃, 鈴埜, 零乃, 麗乃, 麗野, 黎乃, 澪乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Short form of Moreno and other names ending in -reno.
