column12: From Japanese 礼 (re) meaning "a bow, the gesture of bending at the waist", 乃 (no), a possessive particle combined with 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: れのん(Japanese Hiragana)|レノン(Japanese Katakana)|蓮音, 恋音, 澪音, 鈴暖, 礼暖, 怜暖, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 蓮 (ren) meaning "lotus" combined with 音 (on) meaning "echo, sound". Other kanji combinations are possible as well.This name is influenced by Lenon and/or Lennon.
From Japanese 令 (re) meaning "order, command", 乃 (no), a possessive particle combined with 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.
Diminutive of Reyna via the form Reynota.
Derived from Latin renovata meaning "renewed, restored, revived". Its use as a given name during the Reformation was possibly inspired by the renovation of the Church.

column3: 廉兵, 連平, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 廉 (ren) meaning "clean, honest, inexpensive" and 兵 (pei) meaning "soldier, battle, war". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Means "year" in Ancient Egyptian. This was the name of the goddess of fertility, youth and spring.
From Egyptian rnpt-nfr meaning "good year" or "beautiful in years", derived from rnpt "year" (or the name of Renpet, goddess of youth) combined with nfr "beautiful, perfect, good".

From Egyptian rnpt-nfrt, a variant form of Renpetnefer. This was the name of a sister and/or wife of Imhotep, regarded as a minor goddess associated with the new year. It was also a common name for Egyptian women during the Old Kingdom and later.
From the Chinese 任 (rèn) meaning "allow, appoint, trust, rely on" and 巧 (qiǎo) meaning "artful, clever, skillful".
From Japanese 恋 (ren) meaning "love" combined with 櫺 (ren) meaning "carved or patterned window sills". Other kanji with the same pronunciations can also be used to form this name.

column3: 蓮里, 恋莉, 連理, 栞妃, 恋璃, 怜凛, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 蓮 (ren) meaning "lotus" combined with 里 (ri) meaning "village". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 漣 (ren) meaning "ripples" combined with 麟 (rin) meaning "scale". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness" and 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle".
Given name of the American social psychologist Rensis Likert who developed the Likert scale questionnaires.
Diminutive and feminine form of Rens.

column3: 廉介, 練介, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 廉 (ren) meaning "grounds, suspicion" or 練 (ren) meaning "white silk" combined with 介 (suke) meaning "shell, shellfish". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: レンタ(Japanese Katakana)|れんた(Japanese Hiragana)|廉太, 蓮太, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 蓮 (ren) meaning "lotus" combined with 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big". Other combinations of kanji are possible.

column3: 蓮太, 恋太, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column12: Means "tremor, shake, collapse" in Iban. This was the name of a 19th-century Iban hero.

column3: レンタロ(Japanese Katakana)|れんたろ(Japanese Hiragana)|連太郎, 廉太郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
レンタロウ(Japanese Katakana)|れんたろう(Japanese Hiragana)|錬太郎, 練太郎, 廉太郎, 漣太郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 練 or 錬 (ren) meaning "to train, to temper, to polish", 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness" and 恬 (tián) meaning "quiet, calm, peaceful".

column3: レント(Japanese Katakana)|れんと(Japanese Hiragana)|蓮斗, 恋人, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 蓮 (ren) meaning "lotus" combined with 人 (to) meaning "person" or 斗 (to), which refers to a Chinese constellation. Other kanji combinations are possible.

This name appears to be a shortened version of the old English personal name, Raegenweald. Renton is thus the 'tun' or small village, of Raegen. According to George Black the Rentons of Renton were hereditary foresters of Coldingham during the reign of King William the Lion.
Czech and Slovak diminutive of Renáta. Also compare Renuška.
Czech and Slovak diminutive of Renáta. Also compare Renuša.
Transferred use of the surname Renwick.
From the Chinese 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness" and 娴 (xián) meaning "elegant, refined".
From the Chinese 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness" and 香 (xiāng) meaning "fragrant, sweet smelling, incense".

column3: 蓮也, 蓮夜, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 蓮 (ren) meaning "lotus" combined with 也 (ya) meaning "also" or 夜 (ya) meaning "night, evening". Other kanji combinations can also make up this name.
From the Chinese 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness" and 瑶 (yáo) meaning "precious jade".
From the Chinese 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness" and 怡 (yí) meaning "happy, joyful, harmony".

column3: 廉与, 廉代, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 廉 (ren) meaning "bargain, reason, charge, suspicion, point, account, purity, honest, low price, cheap, rested, contented, peaceful" combined with 与 (yo) meaning "bestow, participate in, give, award, impart, provide, cause, gift, godsend" or 代 (yo) meaning "world, society, age, generation, era of rule". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 仁宇, 仁裕, 仁玉, 人语, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 仁 (rén) meaning "compassionate" combined with 宇 (yǔ) meaning "house, eaves, universe". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 錬三郎, 連三郎, 廉三郎, 練三郎, 蓮三郎(Japanese Kanji)|れんざぶろう(Japanese Hiragana)|レンザブロウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Combination of Ren and Saburō.This name is very rarely used.
From the Chinese 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness" and 芷 (zhǐ) meaning "angelica, iris".
From Japanese 蓮 (ren) meaning "lotus" combined with 三 (zou) meaning "three". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 獅, 獅子, 獅央, 怜央, 玲央, 蓮央, 礼央, 怜生, 怜旺, 麗桜, 怜大, 零王, 嶺臣, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|れお(Japanese Hiragana)|レオ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Borrowed from Leo, as seen in the occasional usage of 獅 (or 獅子), on its own or as a first element kanji.More often though, a re(i/n) kanji, like 怜/伶 meaning "clever, smart," 玲 meaning "tinkling," 蓮 meaning "lotus," 礼 meaning "thanks, gratitude; gift," 麗 meaning "lovely, beautiful," 零 meaning "zero" or 嶺 meaning "peak, summit," combines with a kanji can be (partially) read as o, such as 央 meaning "middle, centre," 生 meaning "grow," 旺 meaning "vigorous, prosperous," 桜 meaning "cherry (tree, blossom)," 大 meaning "large, big," 王 meaning "king, ruler," or 臣 meaning "retainer, attendant."Male bearers of this name include professional shōgi player Reo Kurosawa (黒沢 怜生) (1992-) and footballer Reo Mochizuki (望月 嶺臣) (1995-).
"With fire, to fire, with determinaation." Name came from someone unique, who also died in a fire, iconic.
Likely an invented name modeled after similar names such as Leola.

column3: 獅, 獅王, 玲音, 伶音, 澪音, 蓮恩, 廉穏, 怜遠, 怜央, 令桜, 礼央夢, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|れおん(Japanese Hiragana)|レオン(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Transferred use of the surname Reon (only in English).In Dutch (and sometimes also in English), this name is likely a combination of Leon with any masculine given name that starts with R-, such as Robert.

column3: 怜央奈, 怜於奈, 玲央奈, 玲於奈, 伶於奈, 伶央奈, 礼央奈, 玲緒菜, 玲央名, 怜緒菜(Japanese Kanji)|れおな(Japanese Hiragana)|レオナ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: As a unisex name, this name can be used as 怜央奈, 怜於奈, 玲央奈, 玲於奈 or 伶於奈 with 怜 (ryou, rei, ren, awa.remu, sato.i) meaning "wise", 玲 (rei, re) meaning "sound of jewels", 伶 (ryou, rei, wazaogi, re) meaning "actor", 央 (ou, o) meaning "centre, middle", 桜 (ou, you, sakura) meaning "cherry", 於 (o, yo, aa, oi.te, o.keru, yori) meaning "as for, at, in, on" and 奈 (dai, na, nai, ikan, karanashi) meaning "Nara, what?"As a feminine name, it can be used as 伶央奈, 礼央奈, 玲緒菜, 玲央名, 怜緒菜 with 礼 (rai, rei, re) meaning "bow, ceremony, remuneration, salute, thanks", 緒 (sho, cho, itoguchi, o) meaning "beginning, cord, end, inception, strap, thong", 菜 (sai, na) meaning "greens, side dish, vegetable" and 名 (myou, mei, na, -na) meaning "distinguished, name, noted, reputation."One female bearer is actress Reona Hirota (広田 レオナ), born Kumi Fukikoshi (吹越 久美) (1963-).One male bearer is physicist and winner of Nobel Prize in Physics, Reona Esaki (江崎 玲於奈), better known as Leo Esaki (1925-).Usage of this name for girls is, most likely, influenced by the name Leona. For boys, it's, most likely, influenced by the name Leon.
From Japanese 怜 (reo) meaning "pity, sympathize" combined with 音 (ne) meaning "sound". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.
From Japanese 玲 (re) meaning "tinkling of jade", 央 (o) meaning "centre, middle" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

Latinization of an unknown name, possibly Reor (see Reidar). Reorus Torkillus (b. 1608, d.1643) was a Swedish priest who was the first Lutheran clergyman in what is now the United States. It was very common for Swedish priests to latinize their names after being ordinated.

column3: レオト(Japanese Katakana)|れおと(Japanese Hiragana)|澪遠, 玲弟, 恋音, 鈴己, 莉勇柊, 彼央人, 麗曖斗, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 澪 (re) meaning "water route, shipping channel" combined with 音 (oto) meaning "sound". Other kanji combinations are possible.

As a maiden, Repanse had charge of the Grail and carried it in the Grail Procession. After Perceval became the Grail King, Repanse fell in love with Feirefiz, Perceval’s pie-bald half brother, at Arthur’s court. Repanse and Feirefiz married and moved to India, where they became the parents of Prester John.
Feminine form of Reparatus. Used by a 3rd century virgin martyr.
Derived from Latin reparatus meaning "recovered, retrieved; renewed, restored", as it is the perfect passive participle of the verb reparo "to recover, to retrieve; to restore, to repair, to renew".
Meaning, "feel or express sincere regret or remorse about one's wrongdoing or sin." Name given to 'bastard' children.

Middle English: from Old French repentir, from re- (expressing intensive force) + pentir (based on Latin paenitere ‘cause to repent’). Meaning, " the activity of reviewing one's actions and feeling contrition or regret for past wrongs." Referring to being sorry for one's sins. Name often given to children borne out of wedlock.
Roman cognomen derided from Latin repens "sudden, unexpected".
In I Chronicles 26:7–8, Rephael, "healed of God," was one of Shemaiah's sons. He and his brethren, on account of their "strength for service," formed one of the divisions of the temple porters.
Rephaiah, "the Lord has healed," a descendant of David was the father of Arnan and the son of Jeshaiah.

Used in the 'House of Night' series of fantasy novels (written by American author P. C. Cast and her daughter Kristin Cast), where it belongs to the favorite son of the fallen angel Kalona. It is probably taken a biblical term which "can refer either to a mythical race of giants, or to dead ancestors who are residents of the Netherworld."

From late Middle English (in the sense ‘supply abundantly’) from Old French repleniss-, lengthened stem of replenir, from re- ‘again’ (also expressing intensive force) + plenir ‘fill’ (from Latin plenus ‘full’). Meaning, "restore (a stock or supply of something) to the former level or condition." Referring to replenishing of the soul or to the Biblical command to multiply and replenish the earth.

Either from Serbian реп (rep) meaning “tail” or Serbian репа (repa) meaning “turnip, beet” combined with a diminutive suffix. Originally used as a surname in the 14th century, some would later use it as a first name in the 15th century.

Means "rest" in Spanish. It is taken from the titles of the Virgin Mary La Virgen del Reposo and Nuestra Señora del Reposo, meaning "The Virgin of the Rest" and "Our Lady of the Rest", respectively. She is the patron saint of Valverde del Camino in the Andalusian province of Huelva, hence the name's particularly high concentration there.

column3: レプン カムイ(Ainu Katakana, Japanese Katakana)
column12: Ainu god (Kamuy) of the sea, depicted as either an orca or a harpoon-wielding young man.
Galician and Spanish form of Rechiar.
Portuguese form of Rechila, the name of a 5th-century Suevic king of Gallaecia.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Richimund.
Means "water flowing to the sea" in Maori, from rere "flow" and moana "sea".

column3: れりあ(Japanese Hiragana)|麗理亜, 麗, 玲梨亜, 玲梨愛, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 麗 (re) meaning "lovely, beautiful", 理 (ri) meaning "reason, logic" combined with 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 礼留飛(Japanese Kanji)|れるひ(Japanese Hiragana)|レルヒ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: In the case of Japanese ski jumper Reruhi Shimizu (1993-), he was named after Austrian military officer Theodor Edler von Lerch, who introduced ski into Japan in the 1910s.The kanji used for Shimizu's first name are 礼 (rai, rei, re) meaning "bow, ceremony, remuneration, salute, thanks," 留 (ryuu, ru, to.meru, to.maru, todo.meru, todo.maru, ruuburu) meaning "detain, fasten, halt, stop" and 飛 (hi, to.basu, -to.basu, to.bu) meaning "fly, scatter, skip (pages)."
In Peanuts, Rerun is the younger brother of Lucy and Linus.
Short form of Theresa or Teresa.One of the main characters in Cornelia Funke's 'Inkheart' Trilogy, Meggie's mother, bears this name.
From the English word rescued, ultimately from Latin ex 'out' and quatiō 'I shake'. Possibly referring to being "rescued by God".
Spanish form of a German name comprised of the element reths, a variant of rad or ragin "advice, counsel" and sinþs "path"
Austrian and Bavarian German diminutive of Theresa, Therese and Theresia.It is rarely used as an official given name. One known namesake is the German politician Reserl Sem née Fürstberger (b. 1953).
From the English word. In the case of Reservoir Smith, a gypsy girl, daughter of Shadrack Smith, she had reputedly received her name from the site, close to a reservoir, where she was born.
Dari Persian and Pashto variant of Rashad.
Means "silk" in Hindi and Punjabi, ultimately from Persian ابریشم (abrīsham).
Probably a combination of a name starting with Re- and ending in -o (such as Renato) with Shane.

Derived from Semitic ršf meaning "to absorb, to consume" or "to burn" (descended into Hebrew as רשף (reshef) "burning heat" or "plague"). This was the name of a Canaanite and Semitic deity of plague, the underworld, and war.
Variant of Rezia appearing in the Latin Vulgate Bible.
Derived from Latin resignatus meaning "unsealed, opened" as well as "resigned".A notable bearer of this name was saint Resignatus of Maastricht (died in 465 AD).
Etymology uncertain. Possibly from the Arabic رَسْم (rasm) meaning "drawing, painting; trace" and Turkish nur meaning "light".

The name ‘Resna’ started to gain its popularity in the 1990’s and originated in Bangldesh which means ‘Admired'. Although not in the Bengali dictionary, the meaning of the name is well known internationally.
From the English word resolute meaning "determined, unwavering".
Means "Thursday" in Javanese, ultimately from Sanskrit बृहस्पति (bṛhaspati).
Respendial was a Western Alanian King in the Iberian Peninsula. He led one of two groups of Alans, an Iranian people, across the Rhine and into the region.
Feminine form of Restitutus. This was the name of a 4th-century Christian martyr from Roman Africa.
French form of Restituta. This name has not enjoyed as much use as its variant Restitude has, which is why this name is nearly extinct while that name is not.

Italian, Spanish, Galician and Portuguese form of Restitutus. Known bearers of this name include the Argentine soccer player Restituto Brito (born c. 1929) and Restituto del Valle (1865-1930), a Spanish poet and Augustinian cleric.

Roman cognomen which was derived from Latin restitutus meaning "replaced, restored" as well as "revived", itself ultimately derived from the Latin verb restituo meaning "to replace, to restore" and "to revive".This name was in use throughout the Roman Empire, but it was especially common in North Africa, where it may have been a rough Latin translation of the Phoenician name B'LŠLM or Baalshillem meaning "Ba'al has given in exchange (for a deceased child)".
Meaning, "return (someone or something) to a former condition, place, or position." Referring to a restoration of faith.
Meaning, "unemotional, dispassionate, or moderate behavior; self-control."
Means "blessing, benediction, prayer" in Indonesian, from Sanskrit सिद्धिर् अस्तु (siddhir astu).
Roman cognomen which first started out as a contraction of the cognomen Restitutus.
Common diminutive of Restituto. This is also occasionally used as a diminutive of Restituta.
Polish form of Restitutus. A known bearer of this name was the Polish historian and political activist Restytut Staniewicz (1929-2011).
This name has no meaning since it is written only in hiragana.
Means "skilled at child rearing" in Ainu.
Unaccented form of Resurrección primarily used in the Philippines.
From the English word resurrection. Cognate of Resurrección.
Originally a short form of Margaréta, now occasionally used as a given name in its own right.
Transferred use of the surname Retief.
Transferred from the surname Rétif.Rétif de la Bretonne was a pen name of the French writer Nicolas-Edmé Rétif.
Maybe a feminine form of Rétif.
From Javanese rêtna meaning "diamond, jewel", ultimately from Sanskrit रत्न (ratna).
Directly taken from Latvian rets "rare; sparse, scarce; uncommon".

column3: 烈, 洌, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|れつ(Japanese Hiragana)|レツ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Sino-Japanese reading of kanji like 烈 meaning "violent, furious; extreme, intense" and 洌 meaning "pure."One fictional bearer of this name is Retsu Unohana (卯ノ花 烈), a Soul Reaper from the manga and anime series 'Bleach'.This name is rarely used.
From Japanese 烈 (retsu) meaning "fury, rage, violent, vehement" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child." This is the name of the protagonist of the 2016 Sanrio anime 'Aggressive Retsuko'.
Diminutive of Loretta, Margaretta and other names ending in retta. In the case of comedian Retta, it's a diminutive for Marietta.
Diminutive of Margaret, Loretta, and other names containing -ret-.

From the English word meaning "to come back" (itself from Old French re- "back" and torner "to turn"), which was given to a boy born in 1708 in Guilford, Connecticut, supposedly in memory of an incident from his parents' courtship; it is popularly claimed that his mother, Hannah Willard (1674-1749) - after repeatedly rejecting his father, Janna Meigs (1672-1739) - finally relented, crying to him as he rode away "Return, Janna, return!" The name has since been borne by more than a dozen of Return Meigs' descendants, including his son, Return Jonathan Meigs (1740-1823), and grandson, Return Jonathan Meigs, Jr. (1764-1825; the fourth Governor of Ohio and fifth U.S. Postmaster General).
Referring to our bodies returning to the earth.
Feminine form of Retyk and Retycjusz.
Variant of Ronan. The name may also be derived from Breton reunig "seal" and thus have arisen as a direct translation of Rónán.

Georgian form of the Middle Iranian given name Rēw, which is ultimately derived from the Avestan adjective raēva meaning "rich, splendid, opulent".This name was borne by two kings of Iberia (now Georgia), the earliest of which lived in the 3rd century AD.
Hungarian. Allegedly the name of one of Attila the Hun's brothers, although not all sources agree.
Meaning, "firmament", "flow, move", "inexhaustible" and "the abyss" in Tahitian. Cognate of Rewa.
Means "Talk or gossip about". This is a name given to address neighbours that continue to gossip about your family
Revali is one the four champions in the video game The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild.

Revan is the name of a fictional character in the 'Star Wars' universe, known as both a Jedi and a Sith (as Darth Revan). Revan is the main character in the RPG 'Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic' (2003) and appears in numerous other 'Star Wars' media. In the game the player may chose Revan's gender and much of the dialog is gender neutral. However, canonically, Revan is male.The origin of his name is unknown, but it is probably not his birth name. An out-of-universe explanation is that the name is derived from revanchism, ultimately from French revanche "revenge".
REVANNA IS A ONE OF THE NAME OF GOD SHIVA

MEANING : wealthy, opulent, splendid, brilliant, handsome. It is the name of a son of lord Surya Usage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhalese, Hindi, Sikh, Buddhist, Kannada, Marathi, Gujarati, Assamese, Malayalam, Bengali, Oriya
Malayalam and Tamil form of Revati.
Alternate transcription of Malayalam രേവതി or Tamil ரேவதி (see Revathi).

Feminine form of Sanskrit रेवन्त् (revant) meaning "wealthy, rich, brilliant, splendid, beautiful". In various Hindu texts Revati is the consort of Balarama, the elder brother of Krishna. This is also the name of the 27th lunar mansion (nakshatra) in Hindu astrology, corresponding to a star in the constellation Pisces.
Means "overflowing, saturated" in Hebrew, from the element רָוָה (ravah) "to be saturated, drink one's fill". A modern Hebrew word name.
From the English word reveille (the traditional tune played to wake up the troops), ultimately from French réveillez meaning "wake up!".
Variant of Revekka, the Modern Greek form of Rebecca (via Biblical Greek Rhebekka).
Modern Greek and Russian form of Rebecca.
Meaning, "enjoy oneself in a lively and noisy way, especially with drinking and dancing."

From the name of the final book of the New Testament or directly the English word revelation "act of revealing or disclosing", both ultimately from Latin revelatio "disclosure". A famous bearer of the name is former South African cricketer Revelation Plaatjie (1982-).
Anglicized form of Raibhilín, which is a variant form of Roibhilín.
Possibly a female form of Revel.
Perhaps a feminization of Revelin. Otherwise, the name is probably a combination of a name starting with R- with Evelynne. It could even have been inspired by the English verb to revel in some cases.
This is the name of Brazilian footballer Réver Humberto Alves Araújo. He is simply known as Réver.
Possibly a feminine form of Rewerd or, in an American context, more likely an attempt at feminizing Revere or Reverdy.
Probably transferred from the surname Reverdy.
Transferred use of the surname Revere.
From the English word reverence meaning "deep respect".
Derived from Reverend, an English honorific title for certain Christian clergy and ministers.A known bearer of this name was the American inventor Reverend "Revra" DePuy (1860-1921).
Spanish and Galician form of Reverianus. A known bearer was the Spanish componist Reveriano Soutullo Otero (1880-1932).
Extended form of Reverius. This was the name of a saint from the 3rd century, who had left his native Italy for missionary work in Roman Gaul, but was eventually martyred.
Derived from Latin revereor "to respect, to honour, to fear".
Often used as a diminutive of Reverie.

Oliver spelled backwards.Notable people with the name include Revilo P. Oliver (1908–1994), American professor and polemicist and Oliver Christianson, American cartoonist known by the pen name Revilo.
Meaning, "return to consciousness; restore to health," from Middle French revivre, from Latin revivere "to live again," from re- "again" + vivere "to live."
Form of Rebecca used in the Jewish diaspora.
From the American multinational cosmetics, skin care, fragrance, and personal care company.

Feminine form of Revmir, which is a variant form of Revomir.In some cases, this name can also be a contraction of Russian революций мировой армия (revolyutsiy mirovoy armiya) meaning "army of the world revolution".This name was created by Communist parents who were eager to reject traditional names.

Feminine form of Revocatus.This name was borne by an obscure saint. Other notable bearers of this name include the Brazilian journalist and writer Revocata Heloísa de Melo (1853-1944) and her mother Revocata dos Passos Figueiroa de Melo, who was also a writer.
Italian and Spanish form of Revocatus.

Derived from Latin revocatus meaning "recalled, called back", which in turn is derived from the Latin verb revoco meaning "to recall, to call back" as well as "to revive". Also compare the English word revocable, which is etymologically related.This name was borne by a few obscure saints, the best known of which is the one that was martyred together with Perpetua and Felicitas (also known as Felicity) in Carthage around 203 AD.
Bulgarian and Russian form of Revocatus.

Derived from the English noun revolt, which is a term used to refer to an act of rebellion. This word was used as a given name by Puritans who had arrived in what is nowadays the United States of America.
Derived from the Russian noun революция (revolyutsiya) meaning "revolution". Like names such as Melor and Vilen, this name was created by Communist parents who were eager to reject traditional names.

Contraction of Russian революция мировая (revolyutsiya mirovaya) meaning "world revolution" as well as of революционный мир (revolyutsionnyy mir) meaning "revolutionary world". This name was created by Communist parents who were eager to reject traditional names.
Short form of Reverend. This is at least the case for the American inventor Revra DePuy (1860-1921).
Name of the main female protagonist of the anime Black Lagoon. In the anime, Revy is short for Rebecca.

A dithematic name formed of the Frisian name element RÊD "advice, council" (ultimately from Germanic rat) and walt "power, leader, ruler".However, given the extreme rarity of the surname in the Netherlands (especially in this day and age), the given name Rewalt is more likely to be a combination of two existing names the second of which is probably Walter.

Rewani was an Ottoman poet. Rewani wrote a Diwan dedicated to Selim I known for its ghazels, which sing in a gentle flowing manner of human and mystic love, most of which were later set to music. Also Rewani's Ishret-name was the first Ottoman Turkish poem with a bacchic theme, which inspired the saki-names genre that became popular a century later.
Taken from the English word Reward
Derived from Sanskrit रेवत् (revat) meaning "wealthy, prosperous, abundant".
"Rewen of Cornwall", also known as Richard of Cornwall (c. 1209 - 1272).
Formed from the Frisian name elements RÊD "advice, council" and WARD "to guard".
Maori form of Dave, Louis and Levi.
Transferred use of the surname Rexford.
Aragonese and Galician form of Regina.
Feminine form of Rex. It may have been modeled on Maxine and influenced by Rexanne.
Possibly from the surname, or a combination of Rex with the popular suffix ley.
Feminization of Rex using the trendy -lynn suffix.
Combination of the name Rex with the suffix -ton.
Allegedly derived from Sanskrit riya "singer; graceful".
Goddess Lakshmi, First Ray Of Sunlight, flowing stream of water, influential personality,Graceful Singer,earth goddess in Greek
Modern name coined from the English word ray combined with Sanskrit अंश (aṃśa) meaning "share, portion, part".
Russian transcription of Rachel (after the English pronunciation).
The name Reydan means "Gift of God, Handsome King". The most time this name was used was in 2017 when only 5 boys were named Reydan
Combination of the given name Rey 1 with the suffix -ella or a feminine form of Rey 1.

Medieval Dutch form of Reier, which is nowadays a bit more common than Reier itself, but not as common as the modern (variant) spelling Reijer, which is the most prevalent out of the three of them.Known bearers of this name include the Dutch Golden Age painter Reyer van Blommendael (1628-1675) and the Dutch poet and playwright Reyer Anslo (1622-1669).
Alternate transcription of Arabic ريحان (see Rayhan).
Alternate transcription of Persian ریحانه (see Reyhaneh).
There is a River by the name of REYHER! It's location is close to the city of Prague. Once belonged to Orissa. River is still there!
South African diminutive of Marijke, or feminine form of Rijk/Reik, or from Old Norse reykr meaning "smoke"
Probably derived from the place name Reykjadalur, composed of Old Norse reykr meaning "smoke" and dalr meaning "dale, valley".
Combination of Rey 1 and the suffix la.
Combination of Rey 1 and the popular suffix -lyn.
Combination of Rey-, from names beginning with this pattern, e.g. Reynaldo, and -mar, from names beginning in that pattern such as María or Maribel.
Combination of Reynaldo or Rey 1 and Mark.
Conbination of Reynaldo or Rey 1 and Martin.
Variant of Rain 1 or a shortening of any names with the name Reyn in there. (Example Reynold for males and Reyna for females.)

Medieval English variant of Regina (influenced by Old French reine, meaning "queen"), Judeo-Anglo-Norman variant of Reine and Judeo-Spanish variant of Reina 2. As a Jewish name, Reyna was used as a translation of Malka.

Medieval Dutch form of Reinhard.This is one of the names by which Reynard the Fox is known in medieval Dutch literature. The most influential Dutch version of the story is Van den vos Reynaerde (13th century) written by Willem die Madoc(ke) maecte. Although the central character is named Reynaerde in the title, he is not consistently referred to by that name in the original text: the forms Reynaerd and Reynaert are also used by the author.
Icelandic form of Ragndis as well as a combination of the Old Norse name elements reynir "rowan (tree)" and dís "goddess; woman, lady; seeress".

Derived from the Old Norse elements reynir meaning "rowan tree" (compare Reynir) and hildr meaning "battle". Alternatively it may be an Icelandic form of Reinhild (in which the first element is derived from Germanic regin "advice, counsel, decision").
Maybe a blend of Reynaldo and Daniel. It is very common in Cuba.
Taken directly from Icelandic and Old Norse reynir meaning "rowan, mountain ash".
Name of one of Reynard's cubs in Reynard the Fox, a literary cycle of medieval allegorical Dutch, English, French and German fables.
Transferred use of the surname Reynolds.
Means "reed, cane" in Icelandic. It is primarily used as a second name.
Croatian short form of Tereza and Slovene short form of Terezija.
Derived from reza meaning "small, tiny" and gul meaning "rose, flower".
Derived from the Uzbek reza meaning "a small piece, trifling, small" and or which can mean "honour" or, on the other hand, "shame".
Derived from Albanian rreze "ray (of light)" and ar "golden; gold" or artë "golden".
From Arabic رضا الرحمن (rida al-rahman), meaning "satisfaction of the merciful".
Derived from Tatar рәсидә (räsidä) meaning "mature, ripe"; ultimately from Arabic رَشَدَ (rašada) "to be well guided, to be of age".
Means "livelihood, sustenance, nourishment" in Indonesian, ultimately from Arabic رزق (rizq).

column5: REE-zee-ə(Biblical English, Biblical Hebrew)|REE-zyə(Biblical English, Biblical Hebrew)|RU-ZIE-ə(Biblical English, Biblical Hebrew)
column12: From the Hebrew name רִצְיָא (Ritzya) meaning "delight". Possibly from the root רָצוֹן (ratzon) meaning "desire, wish, favor, goodwill". In the Book of 1 Chronicles, Rezia was one of the sons of Ulla, an Asherite.
Diminutive of Terezija via Reza, used as a given name in its own right.
From Kurdish rêz meaning "line, row" or "respect, honour".
Diminutive of Reza, used as a given name in its own right.
Medieval Hungarian form of Erazmus via German Rasmus.
Derived from the Czech word "řezník" meaning "butcher". It is also the name of a character from the novel "The 5th Wave" by Rick Yancey.

Transferred use of the surname Reznor. American musician Trent Reznor (1965-) is the lead singer of the rock band Nine Inch Nails. The name Reznor was given to 17 boys born in the United States in 2017, according to the U.S. Social Security Administration.
Regent of Damascus in the time of Solomon.
Malay, Bengali and Kabardian form of Ridwan.
Indonesian and Malay variant of Rida.
Of unknown origin and meaning.A known bearer of the name is the German politician Rezzo Schlauch (Green Party).
Was used in George R. R. Martin's series "A Song of Ice and Fire"
Created by author George R.R. Martin for use in the series "A Song of Ice and Fire." Queen Rhaella Targaryen is the mother of the character Daenerys.

Created by author George R. R. Martin for a character his series of fantasy novels A Song of Ice and Fire and the television adaptation House of the Dragon (2022-). In the series, Rhaenyra Targaryen is a claimant to the throne of Westeros.
Was used in Goerge R. R. Martin's series "A Song of Ice and Fire
Rhaffi Hadizadeh Kharazi was the top candidate in 2017 of the political micro-party 'bergpartei, die überpartei' in Berlin.
Possibly a Welsh form of Ragnailt. This is the name of Blodeuwedd's maid in the play Blodeuwedd (The Woman Made of Flowers) (1923-25, revised 1948) by the Welsh dramatist Saunders Lewis.

From Welsh rhain meaning "stiff" or "stretched out", sometimes interpreted as "spear". This was borne by a son of the legendary 5th-century king Brychan Brycheiniog, and by a 9th-century king of Dyfed.
Alternate transcription of غالية (see Ghalia), chiefly used in Morocco.
An epithet of the Greek Goddess of retribution, Nemesis, meaning "the Goddess of Rhamnous". Rhamnous was an ancient Greek city and the site of Nemesis' most prominent sanctuary.
Meaning unknown.Rhamondre Stevenson (1998-), the New Engand Patriots running back, is a famous bearer.
Possibly from the Xitsonga word rhanga meaning "to begin".

Derived from Ancient Greek ῥανίς (rhanis) meaning "a drop, raindrop". In Greek mythology, this was name of one of the band of sixty young Oceanid Nymphs which formed the core retinue of the goddess Artemis.
Combination of Rhea and the popular element lyn.
Recent coinage of uncertain origin and meaning. Theories include an elaboration of Rhéa.

Latinized form of Old English Hrêðe or Hrêða. Rheda is a goddess attested solely by Bede in his 8th-century work De temporum ratione, where she is connected with the month "Rhedmonth" (which is the equivalent of modern day March).
Anglicized form of Rhys, this form is usually seen as a masculine spelling, although like all forms of the name it can be masculine or feminine.
Possibly a variant of Rena or Rina 1.
Derived from Greek ῥῆμα (rhēma) meaning "a saying, utterance, word", literally "that which is spoken", a term used in Christianity to refer to the concept of rhematos Christou "the word of Christ".
Rheme was used in African Mythology and means 'The Life'
This name is given to the prince of Emberfall in Brigid Kemmerer's novel 'A Curse So Dark And Lonely,' a modern retelling of Beauty and the Beast.
The name of two different nymphs in Greek mythology, one an oread of Mount Cyllene and lover of Hermes, the other the mother of Medon by Oïleus.
Possibly an invented name based on the sounds found in names such as Renee and Denise.
Variant spelling or Wren or Ren given to 5 girls in 2018.
Meaning unknown. Rhenzy Feliz is an American actor.
Hellenized form of Old Persian Raivamithra.
Variant of Rhion, from Welsh ri meaning "lord, king".
Means "will, course". In the Bible, Rhesa is the son of Zorobabel, father of Joanan, in the genealogy of Jesus.
Variant of Rhett. According to the SSA, 8 boys were named Rhet in 2018.

Possibly a variant of Rita, the spelling perhaps influenced by that of Rhea or Greek ῥήτωρ (rhetor) "public speaker, orator". This name was borne by American journalist and suffragist Rheta Dorr (1868-1948). It was brought to public attention by the 1933 murder of a 23-year-old Chicago woman named Rheta Wynekoop.
Derived from Greek ῥήτωρ (rhetor) meaning "orator, public speaker". This was the name of the last major classical astrologer with surviving excerpts.
Latinized form of Rhetorios. A bearer of this name was the classical astrologer Rhetorius of Egypt, who lived in the 6th and early 7th century AD.
Combination of the name Rhett and the popular suffix -ley.
Female form of Rhett. Combination of Rhett and Lyn.
Spenser famously includes Irish waterways in his list of guests at the fantastic marriage of the rivers Thames and Medway, in Book IV of The Faerie Queene, including the river nymph Rheusa.

Derived from Ancient Greek ῥηξήνωρ (rhexenor) meaning "bursting through ranks of armed men (of the enemy)", which consists of ῥῆξις (rhexis) meaning "breaking, bursting, breaking forth" combined with ἀνήρ (aner) meaning "man".This is the name of several characters from Greek mythology, one of which is a son of king Nausithous of the Phaeacians. Rhexenor was also an epithet of Achilles, a Greek warrior who was one of the heroes of the Trojan War.
Short form of Rhiannon or Rhianna. Also sometimes used as a variant of Ry.
Variant of Rhea, Ria, Rhiannon, or Rhian.
From the welsh word meaning maiden (see Rhian)

Derived from Welsh rhiain "maiden" (originally "queen" from Celtic *r-gan-) and mellt "lightning". Rhiainfellt or Rhieinfellt was the name of a great-granddaughter of Urien Rheged who became the wife of the 7th-century Anglo-Saxon king Oswy of Northumbria.
Extremely rare spelling variant of Rhianon, which might simply be a misspelling of this name given how few bearers there are.
Although Rhiann is first and foremost a short form of the name Rhiannon, it is sometimes associated with Welsh rhiain "maiden".
Variant of Rhiann or a variant of Rhianna.
Combination of Welsh rhiain "maiden" (compare Rhian) and gwen "white; fair; blessed".
Possibly a derivative of Old Welsh rudd "red", in which case it is a cognate of Ruadhán. This was the name of an early Welsh saint, remembered in the parish and village of Llanrhidian on Gower.

From the Old Germanic name Reginwis, itself from the roots regin "advice, counsel, decision" and wīs "wise". Its spelling was influenced by the Dutch word for the river Rhine (Rhijn in the old spelling). A famous bearer was Dutch poet Rhijnvis Feith (1753-1824).
From Sanskrit ऋजुता (ṛjutā) meaning "straightness, honesty, sincerity".
Etymology uncertain, perhaps from the Mandaic rhimat meaning "mercy".
Used by British author C.S. Lewis in his 1950s fantasy series The Chronicles of Narnia. Given to the sword of Peter Pevensie.

Apparently from the name of the River Rhine in western Germany, which is ultimately from Gaulish Renos meaning "that which flows". It was used by American author Lauren DeStefano in her 'Chemical Garden Trilogy'.
Uncertain etymology. Rhinthon was a Hellenistic dramatic poet.

As a masculine name, this is a modern Welsh form of Ryan, or a masculine form of Rhian, coined from Welsh ri "leader".As a feminine name, this is a variant of Rhian (which is essentially a short form of Rhiannon, though it is often associated with Welsh rhiain "maiden").This name has been used since the mid-20th century.
Derived from the Greek noun ῥῖψις (rhipsis) meaning "a throwing, a hurling" combined with the Greek noun λαός (laos) meaning "(the) people".
Latinized form of Rhipsolaos. A known bearer of this name was the Olympic victor Rhipsolaus of Laconia, who won the stadion race at the 39th Olympiad in 624 BC.

Welsh form of the old Celtic name *Rigovellaunos, perhaps meaning "most kingly" or "lord-ruler" (from ri and gwallon). This name belongs to several characters in the Welsh 'Triads' (11th- to 14th-c.), including a son of Urien "who fought against the Saxons and enjoyed a number of victories". It was also borne by a half-brother of the 11th-century ruler Gruffudd (or Gruffydd) ap Llywelyn.
Possibly derived from Greek ῥόδον (rhodon) meaning "rose". This was used in Libistros and Rhodamne, a 13th-century Byzantine romance written at the imperial court of Nicaea.

Means "rose flower" from Greek ‘ροδον (rhodon) "rose" combined with ανθος (anthos) "flower, blossom". According to the 6th-century Byzantine poet and historian Agathias Scholasticus, this name was borne by a contemporary actress, who may have been his lover; in her case it was likely a stage name. It was later used by the 12th-century Byzantine writer Theodore Prodromos for the heroine of his romance 'Rhodanthe and Dosikles'.
Elaboration of Rhoda with the popular suffix -della or -ella.
Variant spelling of Roderick. A known bearer of this name was Sir Rhoderick McGrigor (1893-1959), a senior officer of the British Royal Navy.
From the name of the African country of Rhodesia, now called Zimbabwe.
Possibly derived from Greek ῥόδον (rhodon) meaning "rose".
Means "made of roses, pink" in Greek, a word derived from ῥόδον (rhodon) "rose" and an adjectival suffix.
Possibly from Greek ῥόδον (rhodon) meaning "rose", or Ῥόδος (Rhodos) meaning "Rhodes", and ἵππος (hippos) meaning "horse".
The personified god of a river in the Troad region of Anatolia (modern-day Turkey). Like all river gods, he was considered an immortal son of the Titans Oceanus and Tethys.

From Ῥοδογούνη (Rhodogoune), a hellenization of the Old Persian name *Vṛda-gaunā meaning "rose-coloured, rosy-complexioned" (compare Sogdian warδγōn "rosy" and Persian gulgūn "rose-coloured", both thought to be cognates), apparently altered through association with Greek ῥόδον (rhodon) "rose". This name was borne by several Achaemenid princesses. It was also borne by a 2nd-century BC Parthian princess who married the Seleucid king Demetrius II Nicator - the basis for the title heroine of Pierre Corneille's 1645 tragedy Rodogune.
From Greek ροδον (rhodon) "rose" combined with νίκη (nike) meaning "victory"

Derived from Ancient Greek ῥοδωπός (rhodopos) meaning "rosy-faced, rosy", which consists of ῥόδον (rhodon) meaning "rose" combined with ὤψ (ops) meaning "eye, face, countenance". This was the name of several figures in Greek mythology, including an Oceanid and playmate of Persephone, a naiad daughter of Strymon, and a queen of Thrace who was turned into a mountain range by the gods along with her husband, Haemus.

From the Roman cognomen Rhodopianus meaning "from Rhodope". Rhodope was the name of a late Roman and early Byzantine province as well as of a mountain range. In both cases, the name is ultimately of Thracian origin. Also compare Rhodope, of which the first element is ultimately etymologically related.This name was borne by saint Rhodopianus the Deacon, who was martyred during the reign of the Roman emperor Diocletian (244-311). His original name was most likely Rhodopianos, since he lived and died in the eastern part of the Roman Empire, where Greek was the dominant language.
From the name of the flower.

Uncertain etymology; possibilities include Phoenician 𐤄𐤓𐤏𐤃 (hrʿd) meaning "snake", referring to the island apparently once being home to many serpents, Ancient Greek ῥόδον (rhodon) meaning "rose", or ῥόα (rhoa) meaning "pomegranate". This was the name of the goddess and personification of the island Rhodes in Greek mythology, wife of the sun god Helios. In some accounts she is called a daughter of Poseidon and either Aphrodite, Amphitrite, or the telekhine Halia; in others she is a daughter of Oceanus, or of the river god Asopos, which would make her a naiad.
Derived from Greek ῥόδον (rhodon) meaning "rose" and θέα (thea) meaning "sight, view". Alternatively, the second element could derive from θεά (thea) meaning "goddess".
Diminutive of Rhoda used in the Victorian era.

Probably derived from Greek ῥοικός (rhoikos) meaning "crooked, bent" or "bow-legged". This was the name of a Samian sculptor of the 6th century BCE, as well as the name of a centaur who was killed by Atalanta after he attempted to assault her in Greek mythology.
Derived from Greek ροή (rhoe) meaning "flow, stream". In Greek mythology, this was the name of a woman loved by Apollo. It was also the name of a naiad daughter of the river Scamander.

A variant of Rowena, the daughter of the Saxon leader Hengist, given in marriage to King Vortigern of Britain by Hengist in exchange for the country of Kent. She is first found in Nennius.Vortigern’s marriage to Rowena horrified many of Vortigern’s subjects – as well as the British clergy – because Rowena was a heathen and Vortigern was a Christian, and also because the union cemented an uncomfortable alliance between the British and the Saxons.When Vortigern’s son, Vortimer, took the throne from his father and defeated the Saxons, Rowena pretended that she wished to convert to Christianity. She was able to get close to Vortimer, and she then poisoned and killed him, allowing Vortigern to reclaim the throne and the Saxons to return. Her character is found in Godfrey of Viterbo’s Pantheon as Angria and in Baudin Butor’s romance as Sardoine.Rowena appears as the main character in Thelwall’s The Fairy of the Lake. A heathen sorceress, she falls in love with Arthur (here presented as the contemporary of Vortigern and Ambrosius) and embarks on an elaborate scheme to seduce him by magic, calling upon her supernatural allies such as Queen Hela of the Infernal Regions and the demon Incubus. Thwarted by the Lady of the Lake, Arthur’s guardian, she murders her husband Vortigern and offers Arthur the crown along with herself. Arthur, horrified at her crime, burns Rowena and her castle to the ground.

column3: 里歌子, 里花子, 麗歌子, 麗花子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: りかな(Japanese Hiragana)|李叶, 莉叶, 里愛, 璃哉, 梨奏, 璃奏, 里奏, 涼奏, 莉奏, 里佳菜, 里香菜, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: 凛花乃, 李叶, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 凛 (ri) meaning "dignified, severe, cold", 花 (ka) meaning "flower" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 理吉, 利吉, 理喜智(Japanese Kanji)|りきち(Japanese Hiragana)

Transferred use of the surname Rikihana, which is the Maori form of Dickson.

column3: 吏基積, 吏生和, 吏行五, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: 力丸(Japanese Kanji)|りきまる(Japanese Hiragana)|リキマル(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name is used as 力丸 with 力 (rii, riki, ryoku, chikara) meaning "bear up, exert, power, strain, strength, strong" and 丸 (gan, maru, maru.i, maru.meru) meaning "curl up, explain away, full, make round, month, perfection, pills, roll up, round, seduce."Before the Meiji Period (1868-1912), -maru (丸) was used as a suffix denoting affection (along with -maro {麿/麻呂}) and was given to boys of upper class until they reached 14.Two fictional bearers of this name include Rikimaru, one of the main characters in the Tenchu video game series, and Rikimaru Nangō (南郷 力丸), one of the characters in the kabuki play, Aotozōshi Hana no Nishikie (青砥稿花紅彩画/あおとぞうしはなのにしきえ), which is also known as Shiranami Gonin Otoko (白波五人男) or Benten Kozō (弁天小僧).Rikimaru is also used as a surname.

column3: 力之助, 力之介, 力之輔, 力之典, 理紀之助, 理喜之助, 利喜之助(Japanese Kanji)|りきのすけ(Japanese Hiragana)|リキノスケ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 力 (rii, riki, ryoku, chikara) meaning "bear up, exert, power, strain, strength, strong" and 之 (shi, oite, kono, kore, no, yuku) meaning "of, this" with 助 (jo, suke, tasu.keru) meaning "assist, help, rescue," 介 (kai, suke) meaning "concern oneself with, jammed in, mediate, shellfish", 輔 (fu, ho, tasu.keru, suke) meaning "help" or 典 (ten, den, suke) meaning "ceremony, code, law, rule."Examples of Rikinosuke with 4 kanji include 理紀之助, 理喜之助 and 利喜之助 with 理 (ri, kotowari) meaning "arrangement, justice, logic, reason, truth", 利 (ri, ki.ku) meaning "advantage, benefit, profit", 紀 (ki) meaning "account, chronicle, history, narrative" and 喜 (ki, yoroko.basu, yoroko.bu) meaning "rejoice, take pleasure in."In modern times, it is very rarely given to boys, if given at all.

column3: 力男, 力雄, 力夫, 力生, 利喜男, 利喜雄, 利喜夫, 利喜生(Japanese Kanji)|りきお, りきを(Japanese Hiragana)|リキオ, リキヲ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can be used to combine 力 (rii, riki, ryoku, chikara) meaning "bear up, exert, power, strain, strength, strong" with 男 (dan, nan, o, otoko) meaning "man, male," 雄 (yuu, o-, osu, on) meaning "male, masculine," 夫 (fu, fuu, bu, otto, sore, o) meaning "husband, man" or 生 (shou, sei, i.kiru, i.keru, -u, u.mare, o.u, ki, na.ru, ha.eru) meaning "birth, genuine, life."Alternatively, the first kanji can be substituted for two, for example, 利喜 with 利 (ri, ki.ku) meaning "advantage, benefit, profit, gain" and 喜 (ki, yoroko.bu) meaning "rejoice, pleasure."Although Rikio is largely a masculine name, it was occasionally used on females (particularly those born from the mid-19th century to the early 20th century), whose names were mainly written phonetically.

Has origins in Sanskrit and Hindu. Can mean "one who is like a rose" or "blossoming beauty", suggesting both grace and delicate femininity. It is also associated with the rose, a flower often symbolizing beauty and blossoming.

column3: 力士, 力志, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|りきし(Japanese Hiragana)|リキシ(Japanese Katakana)

column3: 力貴翔, 吏貴翔, 力貴斗, 吏貴斗, 黎生人, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

Other kanji are possible.

The first element of this name is derived from the Lithuanian verb rimti meaning "to calm down, to quieten". It is related to the Lithuanian adjective ramus meaning "calm, quiet, peaceful" (see Ramūnas) and the Lithuanian noun ramybė meaning "tranquility, peace, quiet". The second element of this name is derived from Lithuanian daug meaning "much" (see Daumantas). As such, the meaning of this name is basically "a lot of calmness" and thus likely refers to a person who is very calm and quiet.
Often associated with tradition or heritage, it is considered unisex in some contexts.

The first element of this name is derived from the Lithuanian verb rimti meaning "to calm down, to quieten". It is related to the Lithuanian adjective ramus meaning "calm, quiet, peaceful" (see Ramūnas) and the Lithuanian noun ramybė meaning "tranquility, peace, quiet". The second element of this name is derived from old Lithuanian gailas, which usually means "strong, potent" but has also been found to mean "sharp, jagged" as well as "angry, fierce, violent" and "miserable, sorrowful, remorseful". Also compare the modern Lithuanian noun galia meaning "power, might, force".In short, the meaning of this name is basically "quietly strong".

Other cultures view them as a symbol of life and fertility.In Modern Israeli Hebrew, the word 'rimon' is also used to mean hand-grenade.

The first element of this name is derived from the Lithuanian verb rimti meaning "to calm down, to quieten". Rintrah is a character in William Blake's mythology, representing the just wrath of the prophet. Rintrah first appears in 'The Marriage of Heaven and Hell': "Rintrah roars and shakes his fires in the burdened air" shows him personifying revolutionary wrath. He is later grouped together with other spirits of rebellion in 'The Vision of the Daughters of Albion'.Rintrah is also a character in the Marvel Universe, the figure is obviously inspired by Blake's mythology.

Medieval Italian diminutive of Rino, as -uccio is an Italian masculine diminutive suffix.In addition to that, this name was also often used as a short form of Marinuccio and other pet forms that end in -rinuccio.It is also possible that in some cases, the name was used as a contracted (short) form of Rinalduccio.

column3: りんや(Japanese Hiragana)|リイナ(Japanese Katakana)|倫哉, 凛耶, 林也, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 林 (rin) meaning "grove" and 夜 (ya) meaning "night". Other kanji combinations can be used.
From Japanese 鈴 (rin) meaning "bell, chime" combined with 世 (ze) meaning "generations". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means "holder of wealth" from Tibetan རིན (rin) meaning "worth, value, riches" and འཛིན (dzin) meaning "to hold, to bear".
Alternate transcription of Tibetan རིན་འཛིན (see Rinzin).

column3: 燐蔵, 晋三, 伸三, 新三, 臨蔵, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 燐 (rin) meaning "ignus fatuus, phosphorous, will-o-the-wisp" or 臨 (rin) "to look at, to confront", and 蔵 (zō) meaning "to hide, possession, ownership". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Riobaldo is the main character in João Guimarães Rosa's 1956 novel Grande Sertão: Veredas (The Devil to Pay in the Backlands in English), an adaptation of the faustian motif to the sertão.
From Japanese リオ (Rio), meaning "village center" and 私 (i), meaning joy. Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means "kingly" from the Old Breton element ri "king, ruler".

column3: 莉央子, 莉緒子, 理央子, 里桜子, 凜音子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|りおこ(Japanese Hiragana)|リオコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Rio 2 combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child."This name is rarely used.
Combination of the Portuguese words rio ("river") and mar ("sea"), influenced by other names ending in mar, like Leomar and Gladimar.

column3: リオン(Japanese Katakana)|りおん(Japanese Hiragana)|理苑, 理温, 理音, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
りおな(Japanese Hiragana)|リオナ(Japanese Katakana)|李桜奈, 里央菜, 莉绪奈, 里緒奈, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 李 (ri) meaning "plum", 桜 (o) meaning "cherry blossom" combined with 奈 (na) meaning "Nara, what?, apple tree". Other kanji combinations are possible.

In Irish mythology, Riondal was a legendary High King of Ireland from the ancient Fir Bolg race. According to foundational texts like the Lebor Gabála Érenn (Book of Conquests of Ireland) and Geoffrey Keating’s History of Ireland, Rionnal ruled for approximately six years.
From Javanese ria or riya meaning "happy, joyful" or "arrogant, proud" combined with either the masculine suffix -na or the word ana meaning "being, having, holding".

From the English word riot which refers to an uproar, tumult or unrestrained behaviour. The word derives from Old French riote meaning "dispute, quarrel, chattering, argument". This name was used by Barbadian singer Rihanna for her son born 2023.

column3: 凜音, 理央斗, 理雄斗, 璃音斗, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 凜 (ri) meaning "dignified, severe, cold" combined with 音 (oto) meaning "sound". Other kanji combinations are possible.
It means "hight bank" from the archaic word ripa "bank" (nowadays riva) and alta "high". This name is given to honour Madonna di Ripalta a miraculous image of the Virgin in Foggia.
Maori form of Rebecca. It coincides with a Maori verb meaning "to crucify".

column5: ree-fath(Biblical English, Irish Mythology, Irish, Scottish)
column12: Name of Gomer second-born son in Genesis ch. 10. Irish/Scottish oral tradition (Leber Gabala Eirinn) lists him as the ancestor of the Scots (including the Irish). They too call him the second son of Gomer. Places named for him: Rhiphean Mountains.

Uncertain etymology, possibly derived from Ancient Greek ῥιπή (rhipé) meaning "rapid movement; throw, cast, hurl; sweep, rush (of wind, fire)". This was the name of a Trojan hero and figure from Virgil’s Aeneid, stated to be the most just and righteous of the Trojans.
Jaredite king and son of Shez in The Book of Mormon.
From the surname Ripp, influenced by the popularity of similar names like Ripley.

Ripred is an abnormally large rat and capable fighter who appears in Suzanne Collins' The Underland Chronicles. He is an important character in all five of the series' books. Ripred is what many people and animals in the Underland refer to as a "rager", or a natural born killer.
Short form of Hripsime in the case of Hripsime 'Ripsi' Terzian, a participant in the first season of the American reality television series Bad Girls Club (2006).

Variant form of Richelle. Alternatively, in some cases, usage of this name can be inspired by the French surname Riquelle (also Riquel), which was derived from the male personal name Rickel, a short form of Germanic names containing the element ric "power, rule".
Transferred use of the surname Riquelme.
The middle name of American influencer Quenlin Quen Blackwell.

column3: りら(Japanese Hiragana)|梨楽, 吏良, 季良, 吏羅, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|리라(Korean Hangul)
column12: From Japanese 梨 (ri) meaning "pear", 季 (ri) meaning "plum", or 吏 (ri) meaning "officer, official" combined with 楽 (ra) meaning "comfort, music", 羅 (ra) meaning "silk gauze, thin silk, lightweight fabric or clothing, Latin" or 浦 (ra) meaning "bay, inlet". Other kanji combinations are possible.Usage of this name is most likely influenced by the name Lila 2.
Provençal form of Henriette via Rirette.
Probably derived from the French word rire "laughter".It can also be seen as a nickname of Henriette.The name was borne as a pseudonym by the French individual anarchist Rirette Maîterejean.

column3: りり(Japanese Hiragana)|音, 利々, 梨里, 李梨, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Japanese form of Lily. It could be spelled with 音 (riri) meaning "sound, timbre" or a combination of 利 (ri) meaning "profit, benefit" with 々, a phonetic character indicting a duplication of the beginning kanji. Other kanji combinations are possible.
Influenced by the Name Lily. Combination of Kanji Characters "利" meaning "Interest", or "Advantage", and "理" meaning "Reason".

column3: リリア(Japanese Katakana)|りりあ(Japanese Hiragana)|梨々叶, 俐々海, 理々娃, 凛々朱, 莉々杏, 凜々空, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

Māori form of Liliana. The word riri means "defence" and "lily" in Māori.

column3: りりえ(Japanese Hiragana)|リリエ(Japanese Katakana)|凛々衣, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 凛 (ri) meaning "dignified, severe, cold" duplicated and combined with 衣 (e) meaning "clothes". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column12: From Japanese 凛 (ri) meaning "dignified, severe, cold" duplicated and combined with 葉 (ha) meaning "leaf, needle, blade (of a plant)". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 莉里帆, 里莉歩, 莉里穂, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 莉 (ri) meaning "white jasmine", 里 (ri) meaning "village" combined with 帆 (ho) meaning "sail". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: リリカ(Japanese Katakana)|りりか(Japanese Hiragana)|璃理香, 梨里佳, 麗里加, 梨里果, 莉々果, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.Possibly inspired by Lilica.

column3: リリコ(Japanese Katakana)|りりこ(Japanese Hiragana)|りり子(Kanji/Hiragana)|リリ子(Kanji/Katakana)|李々子, 凛々子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 凛 (ri) meaning "cold, dignified", 々 meaning that the previous sound is repeated, and 子 (ko) meaning "child, sign of the rat, first sign of the Chinese zodiac". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 里 (ri) meaning "village" duplicated and combined with 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Sundanese diminutive of feminine names containing the sound rin (or other similar sounds), such as Rinawati.

column3: リリナ(Japanese Katakana)|李梨奈, 莉里那, 莉々奈, 梨々菜, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 李 (ri) meaning "plum", 梨 (ri) meaning "pear" combined with 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column12: From Japanese 李 (ri) meaning "plum" and 織 (ri) meaning "to weave" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

From Japanese 里 (ri) meaning "village", 利 (ri) meaning "profit, benefit" combined with 林 (rin) meaning "woods; grove; forest; copse". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means "tidy, neat, orderly" in Toba Batak.

column12: This is the Japanese form of Lilith.

column12: From Japanese 利 (ri) meaning "profit, advantage, benefit", 梨 (ri) meaning "pear" or 凛 (ri) meaning "dignified, severe, cold", 李 (ri) meaning "plum" or 々 used to duplicate 梨 combined with 翔 (to) meaning "soar, fly", 都 (to) meaning "metropolis, capital, all, everything" or 斗 (to), which refers to a Chinese constellation. Other kanji combinations are possible.

Means "depart, inherit" in Proto-Polynesian. This was a name of an araki "king" of Rapa Nui named Riro Kāinga before his name was changed to Simeon Riro after his baptism. His full name Timeone Riro 'a Kāinga Rokoroko He Tau translates to "Simeon departs the village recite the song". Simeon was his baptismal name before he changed it to Riroroko "inherit peace". Rokoroko is a variant of rongorongo "chant, recite" and Roko a variant of Rongo.
From Japanese 理 (ri) meaning "reason, logic" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column12: Popularised by pop singer Kaela Kimura with the release of her third single 'RIRURA RIRUHA', which is also known as 'Real Life Real Heart', in 2005 (there are a few instances of this name being used before the single's release).This name can also be written with a variety of kanji, combining a ri kanji like 里 meaning "village," 梨 meaning "pear," 莉, part of 茉莉 (matsuri) which refers to the Arabian jasmine, 凛 meaning "cold; dignified" or 璃, part of 琉璃/瑠璃 (ruri) meaning "lapis lazuli," with a ru kanji, such as 瑠, 琉 or 流 meaning "current, flow," and a ha kanji like 葉 meaning "leaf," 花 meaning "flower," 芭, part of 芭蕉 (bashō), referring to the Japanese (fibre) banana, or 心, taken from English heart.This name is rarely used.

column3: りさ子(Kanji/Hiragana)|麗佐子, 利佐子, 利咲子, 利瑳子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 麗 (ri) meaning "resplendent, graceful, beautiful, lovely", 咲 (sa) meaning "blossom" or 瑳 (sa) meaning "polish, luster" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child, sign of the rat, first sign of the Chinese zodiac.". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: りさな(Japanese Hiragana)|梨沙菜, 綾彩奈, 李早奈, 梨真, 理彩奈, 莉更, 莉早奈, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: 莉紗乃, 里紗乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|りさの(Japanese Hiragana)|リサノ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 莉 (ri) meaning "white jasmine" or 里 (ri) meaning "village" combined with 紗 (sa) meaning "thread, silk" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.
From Japanese 理 (ri) meaning "reason, logic", 紗 (sa) meaning "gauze, thin silk" combined with 男 (o) meaning "male". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 梨郷, 理聖, 莉智, 璃里, 吏聡, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 璃 (ri) meaning "lapis lazuli, glassy" or 莉 (ri) meaning "white jasmine" and 郷 (sato) meaning "village", 聖 (sato) meaning "holy, sacred" or 里 (sato) meaning "country, hometown, village, hamlet". Other kanji combinations are possible.

From Sino-Korean 俐 (ri) meaning "smooth, clever, sharp" combined with 世 (se) meaning "world, era, generation". Other Hanja combinations are possible.

Diminutive of Rise, using the Danish word lille "little" (compare Lill).
From Arabic ريشة (risha) meaning "feather, plume, quill".

Rishaan is a name of Hindi origin and holds diverse meanings. Widely interpreted as ‘good’ or ‘strong,’ it also signifies ‘Lord Shiva,’ ‘saint,’ and ‘seeker of enlightenment.’ Additionally, Rishaan could mean ‘one who meditates on the Lord’s name,’ encapsulating spiritual significance. Rishaan, synonymous with Lord Shiva, is rooted in Hinduism
Alternate transcription of Hindi ऋषभ (see Rishabh).
From Sanskrit ऋषभ (ṛṣabha) meaning "bull" or "best, most excellent".

Means "lord of bulls" from Sanskrit ऋषभ (ṛṣabha) meaning "bull" and नाथ (nātha) meaning "master, lord". In Jain tradition this is the name of the first of the 24 tirthankaras (enlightened spiritual teachers).
Yeshua's (God) Strong/ powerful Warrior, Yeshua's (God) Justice and Liberty.
Tatar, Bashkir and Kazakh form of Rashad or Rashid.

Combination of the name Risna and the feminine suffix -wati.
Possibly derived from Persian رسالت (resâlat), meaning "prophetic mission".

column3: 立秋(Japanese Kanji)|りっしゅう(Japanese Hiragana)|リッシュウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 立秋 (risshū), a traditional East Asian solar calendar term denoting the start of autumn (usually August 7-23).This name is very rarely used.
Variant of Risto. Rista Cvetković-Božinče (1845 - 1878) was one of the earliest freedom-fighters for the Macedonian struggle and Old Serbia during the time of the Kumanovo Uprising.
Feminine form of Rista and Risto.
Finnish dialectal form of Kristiina. Ristiina is also the name of a former municipality in Eastern Finland.
English name meaning "from the brushwood farm"

column12: From Japanese 梨 (ri) meaning "pear" combined with 寿 (su) meaning "longevity, long life". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Feminine form of Riszôrd and cognate of Ryszarda.
Diminutive of Harriet. A bearer of this nickname was Harriet Green Ross, the mother of Harriet Tubman.
Either derived from Sanskrit ऋत (ṛtá) meaning "true, enlightened, luminous, righteousness" or रीत (rīt) meaning "custom, rite, rule".
Walloon form of Richard. The name coincides with Walloon ritchåd "Eurasian jay (bird)".
Variant of Richelle. The spellings Richelle, Richel, and Ritchel are more common.
Alternate transcription of رتاج (see Ritaj), chiefly used in Northern Africa.
Means "lord of seasons" from Sanskrit ऋतु (ṛtu) meaning "season, period" and ईश (īśa) meaning "ruler, lord".
Origin - Sanskrit, Indian, Marathi, Sikh, buddhistMEANING - follower of sacred law, praising

Short form of Agoritsa and diminutive of Glykeria and Eleftheria.

column3: りつは(Japanese Hiragana)|リツハ(Japanese Katakana)|葎葉, 律芭, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 葎 (ritsu) meaning "ratio" combined with 葉 (ha) meaning "leaf, needle, blade (of a plant)". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 率陽, 律春, 律晴, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 率 (ritsu) meaning "rate, ratio, percentage" or 律 (ritsu) meaning "law" combined with 陽 (haru) meaning "light, sun, male", 春 (haru) meaning "spring" or 晴 (haru) meaning "clear weather". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 率平, 律平, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 率 (ritsu) meaning "rate, ratio, percentage" or 律 (ritsu) meaning "law", and 平 (hei) meaning "peace, peaceful, pacifist". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: りつひこ(Japanese Hiragana)|リツヒコ(Japanese Katakana)|律彦, 立彦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 律 (ritsu) meaning "law" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "prince". Other kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: 率裕, 律寛, 浩, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 率 (ritsu) meaning "rate, ratio, percentage" or 律 (ritsu) meaning "law" combined with 裕 (hiro) meaning "abundant", 寛 (hiro) meaning "generous, tolerant", or 浩 (hiro) meaning "prosperous." Other kanji combinations are possoble.

column3: 律人, 栗人, 栗史, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 律 (ritsu) meaning "law, ratio" or 栗 (ritsu) meaning "chestnut", and 人 (hito) meaning "person" or 史 (hito) meaning "history, chronicle".

column3: 率二, 律司, 律二, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 率 (ritsu) meaning "rate, ratio, percentage" or 律 (ritsu) meaning "law" combined with 二 (ji) meaning "two" or 司 (ji) meaning "officer, boss". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: リツカ(Japanese Katakana)|立加, 栗佳, 律香, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 立 (ritsu) meaning "erect, rise, set up, stand", 栗 (ritsu) meaning "chestnut", or 律 (ritsu) meaning "law, ratio" combined with 加 (ka) meaning "add, include, join", 佳 (ka) meaning "beautiful, excellent, good", or 香 (ka) meaning "incense, smell, perfume". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 率和, 律和, 率一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 率 (ritsu) meaning "rate, ratio, percentage" or 律 (ritsu) meaning "law" combined with 和 (kazu) meaning "harmony, peace" or 一 (kazu) meaning "one". Other kanji are possible.

column3: りつき(Japanese Hiragana)|リツキ(Japanese Katakana)|立樹, 律輝, 律来, 率紀, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 里 (ri) meaning "village" combined with 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon, month". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 律子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|りつ子(Kanji/Hiragana)|リツ子(Kanji/Katakana)|りつこ(Japanese Hiragana)|リツコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 律 (ritsu) meaning "law" (which is also commonly written in hiragana りつ or katakana リツ) combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". This name can be formed from other combinations of kanji as well.

column3: りつみ(Japanese Hiragana)|リツミ(Japanese Katakana)|莉摘, 律味, 梨都美, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 梨 (ri) meaning "pear", 都 (tsu) meaning "capital (city)" combined with 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 栗奈, 律奈, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 栗 (ritsu) meaning "a chestnut tree" combined with 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From 律 (ritsu) meaning "law" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 律信, 律 延, 立信, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 律 (ritsu) meaning "law, ratio", 栗 (ritsu) meaning "chestnut", or 立 (ritsu) meaning "erect, rise, set up, stand" combined with 信 (nobu) meaning "trust", 延 (nobu) meaning "prolong, stretch". Other kanji are possible.

column3: りつお(Japanese Hiragana)|リツオ(Japanese Katakana)|律男, 律夫, 律雄, 律生, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 律 (ritsu) meaning "law" combined with 夫 (o) meaning "man, husband". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: りつと(Japanese Hiragana)|リツト(Japanese Katakana)|律翔, 律門, 立人, 立斗, 理都冬, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 律 (ritsu) meaning "law" combined with 人 (to) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 律允, 律哉, 律也, 律弥, 立也, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 律 (ritsu) meaning "law" combined with 允 (ya) meaning "to grant, to allow, to consent". Other kanji combinations are possible.

From 立 (ritsu) meaning "erect, rise, set up, stand", 栗 (ritsu) meaning "chestnut", or 律 (ritsu) meaning "law, ratio" combined with 代 (yo) meaning "generation" or 世 (yo) meaning "world". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Transferred use of the surname Ritter.

Rittersporn is a German word meaning "delphinum".The name is used for the original Jaskier (denoting a different kind of plant in Polish) in the German translation of 'The witcher' by Andrzej Sapkowski.
From Thai ฤทธิ์ (rit) meaning "power" and ชัย (chai) meaning "victory".
From Thai ฤทธิ์ (rit) meaning "power" and รงค์ (rong) meaning "colour".

column3: ฤทธิศักดิ์(Thai)
column12: From Thai ฤทธิ์ (rit) meaning "power" and ศักดิ์ (sak) meaning "power, honour".

column3: ឫទ្ធី, រិទ្ធី(Khmer)
column12: Alternate transcription of Khmer ឫទ្ធី or រិទ្ធី (see Rithy).
Possibly a diminutive of Charity or Rita.
Directly taken from Latvian ritums "flow, passage".

Means "deciduous tree, tree with seasonal leaves" from Sanskrit ऋतु (ṛtu) meaning "season, period" and पर्ण (parṇa) meaning "leaf". In the Hindu epic the Mahabharata this is the name of a king of Ayodhya. As a given name, however, it is feminine.
From Sanskrit ऋतु (ṛtu) meaning "season, period" and and राज (rāja) meaning "king".
Derived from Latvian ritēt “to flow” and vara ‎“power, force; reign".

column3: ริฏวาน, ริฏวัน, ริดวัน(Thai)
column12: Indonesian and Thai form of Ridwan.
Alternate transcription of Bengali ঋত্বিক (see Ritwik).

From Sanskrit ऋत्विक् (ṛtvik), the nominative case of ऋत्विज् (ṛtvij) referring to a person (usually a priest) who performs a seasonal sacrifice or ritual. The term is ultimately from ऋतु (ṛtu) meaning "season, period" and यज् (yaj) meaning "to sacrifice, to worship".

column3: 凛初, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|莉羽, 莉雨, 李羽, 李雨, 梨羽, 梨雨, 理羽, 理雨, 里羽, 里雨(Japanese Kanji)|りう(Japanese Hiragana)|リウ(Japanese Katakana)
龍子, 竜子, 流子, 柳子, 隆子, 瑠子, 理生子, 理宇子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|りう子(Kanji/Hiragana)|りうこ(Japanese Hiragana)|リウコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Archaic transcription of Ryūko. The first element can also be written with ri and u kanji, such as 理 (ri) meaning "reason, logic," 生 (u) meaning "birth" or 宇 (u) meaning "eaves, roof."Disregarding the first sentence, this name is extremely rare.
Diminutive of names containing riv such as River, Rivera, and Rivka, or a variant spelling of Riff, a diminutive of Riffert and Rifke.

Diminutive of Rivaldo. A famous bearer is the Brazilian soccer player Rivaldo Vítor Mosca Ferreira Júnior (1995-), who is usually called simply Rivaldinho; he is the son of the soccer star Rivaldo Vítor Borba Ferreira (who is commonly known only by his first name).
Medieval form of Rhiwallon used in the early German versions of the Tristan legend, where it belongs to Tristan's father, the king of Parmenie.
Means "jealous rivalry" in Latin. She was the Roman equivalent of Nemesis.
Variant of Riwanon. This was the name of the mother of Saint Hervé.
Possibly a variant of Riva or Rivia.
Derived from Breton ri "king" and belin "brilliant".
Possibly a blend of River with the popular name suffix en. It coincides with an English adjective meaning "split, torn apart", related to Old Norse rífa "to scratch, to rive".
Transferred use of the surname Rivera or an elaboration of River.
Feminine elaboration of River using the popular name suffix lee. Also compare Riverlynn.
Elaboration of River using the popular suffix lyn, possibly inspired by Brooklyn and Lakelynn.
Combination of River and Rose. It existed in the US popularity chart beyond 1000 since 2018 where it was given to six babies, then it charted again in 2021 where it was given to seven babies.
Transferred use of the surname Rivers.
Transferred use of the surname Rivet.
From the rivia (רְבִיעַ‎), which is a cantillation mark found in religious texts, including the Torah.
Likely an invented name inspired by Vivian.
Means "coast" in Italian, also used in the English speaking world, ultimately derived from Latin riparius.

Rivina is the name of a plant in the pokeweed family.The plant was named to honour the German botanist August Quirinus Rivinus. His surname is a humanist latinisation of the original German surname Bachmann.
Transcription variant of Rivka and English spelling of Rivka.
Variant of Riwal. This was the name of a legendary ancient Celtic prince of Cornouaille (472-544).

Maori form of Levi. This word in the Maori tongue is a general term for potato. This is not just a first name but a last name. This was the name of farmhand and son Wairua elder of Te Rōpiha, Rīwai Te Rōpiha. This is a middle name of Ngāi Tahu rugby player Manuera Benjamin Rīwai Couch (1925-1996).
Derived from Old Breton ri "king" and uuallon "valorous".
Breton cognate of Rhiannon. Saint Riwanon was the mother of Saint Hervé.
Derived from Old Breton ri "king" and uuaroe "game". Saint Riware was the brother of Saint Riwanon and the uncle of Saint Hervé.
Probably a male form of Rivina.
Low German and Frisian short form of names beginning with the element ric.
From Chinese 日 (rì) meaning "sun, day" combined with 夏 (xià) meaning "summer, great, grand" or 霞 (xiá) meaning "rosy clouds, mist".Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 日祥, 日香, 日翔, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 日 (rì) meaning "sun, day" combined with 祥 (xiáng) meaning "good luck, good omen", 香 (xiāng) meaning "fragrant" or 翔 (xiáng) meaning "soar, glide". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
Variant spelling of Rikst. Known bearers of this name include the Dutch actress Rixt Leddy (b. 1976) and the Dutch speed skater Rixt Meijer (b. 1982).
Alternate transcription of Arabic رياض (see Riad).
Alternate transcription of Arabic رياض (see Riad).

column3: りやこ(Japanese Hiragana)|リヤコ(Japanese Katakana)|里弥子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 里 (ri) meaning "ri, unit of measurement, village" combined with 弥 (ya) meaning "universally" and 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

From Sino-Korean 李 (ri) meaning "plum tree" and 靈 (yeong) meaning "spirit, soul, deity".

column12: From 理 (ri) meaning "logic, reason" combined with 世 (yo) meaning "world" or 好 (yo) meaning "fondness". Other kanji combinations can be used.
