Feminine form of Szilárd. This name was traditionally also used as a vernacular form as well as a Hungarian translation of Konstancia.
Derived from Hungarian szín "color; complexion", which would have been understood as "beautiful face; being beautiful". The name coincides with Modern Hungarian színes "colorful".
Derived from Hungarian szín "color; complexion" (compare Színes).
Old Hungarian name, probably derived from the ancient Hungarian word for "grey". Another possible meaning is "Syrian woman".
Derived from Latin syringa "lilac (shrub or flower)" (ultimately from Ancient Greek σῦριγξ (sûrinx) which also meant “shepherd's pipe”).
Etymology uncertain, perhaps from an older form of szürke meaning "grey".
Derived from the Old Hungarian name Sziron which is of uncertain origin and meaning.
Short form of Szixtina, meaning "scraped, polished".
Polish form of Solomon, used by Polish Jews.
Hungarian variant of Smillaaraq, a name created by Peter Hoeg.
Polish form of Shmuel, used by Polish Jews.
From Polish szukać "to search" and sława "glory", roughly translating to "in search of glory".
East Prussian German short form of Sulamith, the German form of Shulamith, as well as a short form of Ursula. Common name in the 1800s.
Vilamovian form of Simon 1 and Polish diminutive of Szymon.
Jewish-Polish form of Samson, also used as diminutive for Szymon.
Shortening of African American names starting with ta- (example Talisha for females and Tashaun for males).
From Sino-Vietnamese 佐 (tá) meaning "to help" or 借 (tá) meaning "to borrow".
From Sino-Vietnamese 寫 (tả) meaning "to write, describe, depict".
Variant transcription of Tamil தாழை (see Tazhai).
Means "thank you so much" in Dagbani.
Variant transcription of Tamil தாளினி (see Talini).
Means "lord of wonder". Taamash-Yerdi was the god of fate in Vainakh mythology who could grow in size when angered.
MEANING - night Usage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhala, Hindi, Sikh, Buddhist
Means "the rather huge one" in Greenlandic.
Short form of Taaniel, used as a given name in its own right.
Means "she who frees" in Odia. It is one of Durga's names.
MEANING : to cause to jingle or rattle
Variant of Taatsiaq with the endearing suffix -nnguaq.
Variant transcription of Tamil தாழை (see Tazhai).
Short for Tabitha. For males, it is used as a nickname such as is the case with Tab Hunter.
Tabarak is an Arabic name for boys and girls that means “he/she is blessed”, “he/she is raised in status”.

Chiefly Uruguayan name, allegedly of Guarani or Tupi origin and meaning "village man" or "one who lives far from town". The Uruguayan poet Juan Zorrilla de San Martín used it for the title hero of his epic poem Tabaré (1888), which depicts the tragic love between Tabaré, an indigenous Charrúa man, and Blanca, the sister of a Spanish conquistador.
Derived from Arabic تَبْرِيك (tabrīk), itself a form of بَرَّكَ (barraka) meaning "to kneel, to invoke a blessing".

column3: 束沙, 束紗, 束彩, 多葉沙, 多葉紗, 多葉彩, 多羽紗, 多羽彩, 多波砂, 多巴沙(Japanese Kanji)|たばさ(Japanese Hiragana)|タバサ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Japanese transliteration of Tabitha.Apart from being written phonetically, it can also be written with kanji. For 2 kanji, the first kanji is 束 (soku, taba, taba.neru, tsuka, tsuka.neru) meaning "bundle, sheaf." For 3 kanji, the first 2 kanji are 多 (ta, oo.i, masa.ni, masa.ru) meaning "frequent, many, much" and 葉 (you, ha) meaning "blade, leaf, needle," 羽 (u, ha, hane, wa) meaning "feather," 波 (ha, nami) meaning "billow, wave, ripple" or 巴 (ha, uzumaki, tomoe) meaning "comma-design." They are combined with 沙/砂 (sa, sha, suna) meaning "sand," 紗 (sa, sha, usuginu) meaning "gauze, gossamer" or 彩 (sai, irodo.ru, sa) meaning "colouring, paint."This name is rarely given to girls in Japan, if at all.
Possibly derives from the Egyptian name Beketamun, which means "The Handmaid of Amun". Name borne by a Nubian queen who lived during the Twenty-fifth Dynasty of Egypt.
My Uncle Johnny named my son this: Tabemohats meaning "Bright Sun"
Transferred use of the surname Taber.
It is from the King James Bible. It means “the fire of God”Numbers 11:3 King James Version (KJV)3 And he called the name of the place Taberah: because the fire of the Lord burnt among them.

Latinised name of the Scythian goddess of fire and kingship *Tāpayantī, meaning "the Burning One" or "the Flaming One", deriving from an element likely related to similar elements from other Indo-European languages, such as the Avestan tāpaiieⁱti ("to be warm").
From Japanese 旅 (tabi) "trip, travel" and 人 (to) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations can also make up this name.

A name invented by the late Greek poet and epigrammatist Palladas, drawing from the Ancient Greek word τάβλα (tabla) meaning "tabula, dice table" and the name of the muse Calliope, joking that this is the muse that an avid backgammon player worships instead. Some modern sources refer to Tabliope as the goddess of gambling.
Means "she lives", possibly deriving from the Akkadian element bašû ("to be, exist").

Of uncertain etymology. Name borne by a king of Sidon (fl. 549-539 BCE), known for his elaborate sarcophagus which was unearthed in 1887. A later king of Sidon also bore this name, but is more commonly known by the Hellenized variant Tennes.

Frisian short form of names that have Gothic thiuda or Middle High German diet (both of which mean "people") for a first element, and of which the second element starts with a "b." The names Dietbald and Theudebert are good examples of that.
Famous bearer is Taborah Johnson (born March 21, 1953), also known as Tabby Johnson, a Canadian singer and actress.
From Tabrett Bethell, an Australian actress and former model
Derived from the name of a type of grape and raisin.
Alternate transcription of Thai ทับทิม (see Thapthim).
Meaning uncertain. Name borne by a queen of the Qedar tribes, who ruled circa 675 BCE.
Derived from Chinese 塔 (ta) meaning "tower, pagoda, spire", 不 (bu) meaning "not" and 煙 (yan) meaning "smoke, mist". It was the name of the name of an Empress of Qara Khitai.
From Sino-Vietnamese 作 (tác) meaning "to do, perform, carry out".
Means "country, state", from Sino-Vietnamese 社稷 (xã tắc), composed of 社 (xã) meaning "god of earth" and 稷 (tắc) meaning "god of millet". It can also come from Sino-Vietnamese 崱 (tắc) meaning "lofty".
Means "red tomahawk" in Lakota. From the Lakota čhaŋȟpí 'tomahawk' and lúta (lu'-tah) 'scarlet, to be red'.
From Arabic تاج (tāj) meaning "crown" and bermek meaning "given".
Belarusian form of Tatiana, more often transliterated as Tatsiana.
Derived directly from Latin tace meaning "be silent". Also compare Tacey and Silence.
Spanish. A diminutive of Natacha or Anastacia. As a word by itself, not a name, Tacha could mean "stain," "chip" or "mark."
Primarily historical Armenian masculine name derived from the ancient Iranian name element *tačata- meaning "swift, strong", or from *Tačat-aspa, meaning "possessing swift horses".
Feminine form of the Old Armenian name Tachat, formed by added the feminine suffix ուհի (uhi).
Combination of the phonetic element ta and the given name China.
Portuguese and Hungarian form of Tatia.
Unaccented version of Tácia and a variant of Tatia/Tasia.

Derived from Latin tace "to be silent". In Roman mythology, (Dea) Tacita was a goddess of the dead. According to Ovid, she was originally a water nymph called Lara or Lala, a daughter of the god Almo who was raped by Mercurius and eventually became a goddess of the underworld. She has been occasionally identified with Larunda.
From the Turkish taçlı meaning "crowned" and yıldız meaning "star".
Derived from the word täç, meaning "crown", and the given name Myrat.
Dutch or Frisian short form of names containing the name element DIET resp. THIAD (from Germanic *þeudō) "people".
After the city of Tacoma in the American state of Washington, meaning "snow-covered mountain".
Allegedly means "here is the one related to a Christian" in Guanche (compare Arume). It was found in a baptismal register from Seville in the 15th century.
Variant of Tacey. In the Betsy-Tacy series of children's books by American writer Maud Hart Lovelace (1892-1980), it is a diminutive of Anastacia.

column3: 祥亮, 唯旦, 隆諒, 只誠, 正丙, 資聡, 理暁, 直顕, 禎輝, 迪哲, 真彰, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 真 (tada) meaning "true, reality, sincerity", 惟 (tada) meaning "but, however, nevertheless", 維 (tada) meaning "maintain, keep, hold together", 董 (tada) meaning "director, dong, head of department or organization", or 祥 (tada) meaning "happiness, good omen, auspiciousness" combined with 照 (aki) meaning "illumination, shining", 章 (aki) meaning "chapter; section", 顕 (aki) meaning "appear, existing, visible, apparent", 誠 (aki) meaning "sincerity", 旦 (aki) meaning "morning, dawn", or 諒 (aki) meaning "excuse, forgive". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ただあつ(Japanese Hiragana)|タダアツ(Japanese Katakana)|忠温, 忠篤, 忠敦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 忠 (tada) meaning "loyalty" combined with 温 (atsu) meaning "warm", 篤 (atsu) meaning "deep, true, sincere" or 敦 (atsu) meaning "honest". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 迪房, 忠房, 資総, 周総, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 迪 (tada) "edify, way, path, reason, lead, pursue" and 房 (fusa) meaning "chamber; room; house". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 唯春, 唯治, 直温, 忠美, 忠陽, 忠晴, 忠温, 公敏, 規明, 惟晴, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 唯 (tada) meaning "just, only, simply" combined with 春 (haru) meaning "spring" or 治 (haru) meaning "govern, regulate, administer". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 忠秀, 忠英, 忠栄, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 忠 (tada) meaning "loyalty" combined with 栄 (hide) meaning "glory, honor", 秀 (hide) meaning "to excel, surpass" or 英 (hide) meaning "wisdom, brilliance".

column3: 理彦, 直彦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 隆 (tada) meaning "noble, prosperous", 只 (tada) meaning "only, simply, just", 理 (tada) meaning "reason, logic", 資 (tada) meaning "property, resources, material", or 直 (tada) meaning "straight" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ただひろ(Japanese Hiragana)|タダヒロ(Japanese Katakana)|徒仁, 只寛, 但弘, 唯広, 忠宏, 惟洋, 徒優, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 徒 (tada) meaning "disciple, only" combined with 浩 (hiro) meaning "prosperous". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 唯寿, 只尚, 隆悠, 正常, 忠永, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 正 (tada) meaning "correct, proper, justice, right" combined with 永 (hisa) meaning "longevity, long, lengthy", 常 (hisa) meaning "eternal, unchanging, ordinary, usual" or 悠 (hisa) meaning "permanence". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 只仁, 理仁, 隆人, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 隆 (tada) meaning "noble, prosperous", 只 (tada) meaning "only, simply, just", 理 (tada) meaning "reason, logic", 資 (tada) meaning "property, resources, material", or 直 (tada) meaning "straight" combined with 仁 (hito) meaning "compassionate, benevolence". Other kanji combinations can be used.A notable bearer is Tadahito Iguchi (1974-), a baseball player.

column3: タダイチ(Japanese Katakana)|唯一, 忠一, 只一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 忠 (tada) meaning "loyalty" and 一 (ichi) meaning "one". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Those who answered God's call/agreed or believed in God's word

column3: 忠勝, 忠毅(Japanese Kanji)|ただかつ(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From the Japanese kanji 忠 (tada) meaning "loyalty" combined with 勝 (katsu) meaning "win; victory" or 毅 (katsu) meaning "strong".Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 忠精, 正清, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Fromm 正 (tada) meaning "proper, correct, right, justice" and 清 (kiyo) meaning "pure, clean". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 直子, 資子, 理子, 只子, 隆子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 隆 (tada) meaning "noble, prosperous", 只 (tada) meaning "only, simply, just", 理 (tada) meaning "reason, logic", 資 (tada) meaning "property, resources, material", or 直 (tada) meaning "straight" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: タダクニ(Japanese Katakana)|忠邦, 忠国, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 忠 (tada) meaning "loyalty" and 国 (kuni) meaning "country, large place". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Means "person who possesses a lot of good luck" in Somali.

column3: 侃真, 格真, 格正, 糾克, 匡克, 宰正, 只正, 忠順, 忠正, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 侃 (tada) meaning "upright and strong" combined with 真 (masa) meaning "true, reality". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer was Tadamasa Hayashi, a Japanese art dealer who introduced traditional Japanese art such as ukiyo-e to Europe.

column3: 唯道, 唯通, 忠宝, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 唯 (tada) meaning "just, only, simply" or 忠 (tada) meaning "loyalty" combined with 宝 (michi, takara) meaning "treasure, jewel", 道 (michi) meaning "path" or 通 (michi, tsu) meaning "pass through". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 忠需, 忠光, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 禎 (tada) meaning "divine grace, auspicious, straightforward" combined with 需 (mitsu) meaning "demand, request, need". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 忠信, 忠宣, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ただのぶ(Japanese Hiragana)|タダノブ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 忠 (tada) meaning "loyalty, devotion" combined with 信 (nobu) meaning "trust, believe" or 宣 (nobu) meaning "declare, announce". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 忠法, 忠憲, 忠紀, 忠則, 忠徳, 忠教, 忠度, 忠礼, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ただのり(Japanese Hiragana)|タダノリ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 忠 (tada) meaning "loyalty, devotion" combined with 法 (nori) meaning "law, rule", 憲 (nori) meaning "law", 紀 (nori) meaning "record, chronicle", 則 (nori) meaning "rule, law, measure, norm", 徳 (nori) meaning "virtue, benevolence", 教 (nori) meaning "teachings, doctrine", 度 (nori) meaning "degrees, occurrence, time" or 礼 (nori) meaning "manners, etiquette". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 忠雄, 忠男, 忠夫, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ただお(Japanese Hiragana)|タダオ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 忠 (tada) meaning "loyalty, devotion" combined with 雄 (o) meaning "hero, male, manly", 男 (o) meaning "male, man, son" or 夫 (o) meaning "man, husband". This name can be formed from other combinations of kanji as well.

From Japanese 忠 (tada) meaning "loyalty" combined with 臣 (omi) meaning "one who serves a lord; a vassal, subject". Other kanji combinations are also possible.This is the name of Tadaomi Karasuma, a character from the Japanese comic science fiction manga series Ansatsu Kyōshitsu (known as Assassination Classroom in English) written and illustrated by Yūsei Matsui.

column3: ただせ(Japanese Hiragana)|タダセ(Japanese Katakana)|唯世, 正聖, 多々星, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 正 (tada) meaning "proper, correct, justice, right" combined with 聖 (se) meaning "holy, sacred". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Possibly a form of Dasha combined with the prefix ta.

column3: 正, 訂, 糺, 糾, 質, 匡, 董, 格, 貞, 理, 忠, 規, 政, 督, 義, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ただす(Japanese Hiragana)|タダス(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From the verb 正す/訂す (tadasu) meaning "to correct, rectify, reform, amend," cognate with the verbs 糺す/糾す (tadasu) meaning "to ascertain, confirm, verify" and 質す (tadasu) meaning "to inquire, question" (compare Tadashi which, in that case, is derived from a classical adjective). It can also be written as 匡 or 董.Other kanji with connotations to these verbs include 格 meaning "method; rule, law," 貞 meaning "chastity," 理 meaning "reason, logic," 忠 meaning "loyalty, devotion, faithfulness," 規 meaning "standard," 政 meaning "rule, government," 督 meaning "command, supervise" and 義 meaning "morality, justice, honour."One bearer of this name was career diplomat and cabinet minister Hayashi Tadasu (林 董) (1850-1913).

column3: 忠相, 忠佐, 忠輔, 忠介, 忠助, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 忠 (tada) meaning "loyalty" combined with 相 (suke) meaning "nature, personality", 佐 (suke) meaning "aid, help", 輔 (suke) meaning "help", 介 (suke) meaning "shell, shellfish" or 助 (suke) meaning "assistance". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 雅崇, 忠敬, 雅威, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 忠 (tada) meaning "loyalty" combined with 崇 (taka) meaning "lofty, to adore, revere, worship", 敬 (taka) meaning "respect, honor, reverence, awe" or 隆 (taka) meaning "high, hump, noble, prosperity". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 忠友, 忠朝, 忠知, 唯知, 直智, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 忠 (tada) meaning "loyalty" combined with 友 (tomo) meaning "friend". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 直俊, 唯俊, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 直 (tada) meaning "straight, direct" and 俊 (toshi) meaning "talented, handsome". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Tada means "Merely, Only, Simply" and Yasu means "Cheap, Inexpensive, Relax".

column3: 忠偉, 理偉, 忠順, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 理 (tada) meaning "reason, logic" and 偉 (yori) meaning "admirable". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 忠義, 忠吉, 忠良, 忠善, 直美, 直由, 直義, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 直 (tada) meaning "real, sincere, true" combined with 美 (yoshi) meaning "beauty". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 禎幸, 迪幸, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 禎 (tada) meaning "divine grace, auspicious, straightforward" or 迪 (tada) "edify, way, path, reason, lead, pursue" and 幸 (yuki) "happiness". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Diminutive of names beginning in tadd- or tad-.A famous bearer is Tadd Fujikawa, a Japanese American professional golfer.

Feminine form of Taddeo.A famous bearer was Italian noblewoman Taddea Visconti (1351-1381), Duchess of Bavaria. She was the first wife of Stephen III, Duke of Bavaria, and the mother of Isabeau of Bavaria, the Queen consort of King Charles VI of France. Through Isabeau's daughter Catherine of Valois, Taddea is an ancestress of the Tudor dynasty which ruled England from 1485 to 1603.
Swedish and Finnish form of Thaddeus.
Variant of Teddy and diminutive of Thaddeus and Thaddea

Spanish feminine form of Tadeo, Catalan and Romanian feminine form of Tadeu and Polish feminine form of Tadeusz. A famous bearer of this name was Sor Tadea de San Joaquín (1755-1827), born Tadea García de la Huerta, a Chilean Carmelite nun and poet. Her poem Relación de la inundación que hizo el río Mapocho de la ciudad de Santiago de Chile, en el Monasterio de Carmelitas, Titular de San Rafael was published in Lima in late 1783 or early 1784, and is one of the first published poems by a Chilean woman on record.
Form of Tadeoz with the Georgian nominative suffix -ი (-i). It is only used in Georgian when the name is written stand-alone.
Ukrainian form of Thaddeus. Used mostly in Western Ukraine.

Possibly from Egyptian tꜣ-dj-bꜣstt, perhaps meaning "(she) is there for Bastet", from Egyptian tꜣ (ta) "she of, this of, that of" combined with dj (di) "here, there" combined with the Egyptian goddess Bastet. This was the name of two Ancient Egyptian queen consorts during the Third Intermediate Period.
It means "we have loved profusely/a great deal", from the verb 'kudisa' meaning "to love a lot/profusely". A longer form of the name may be Tadisisa.
It means "we have loved profusely/a great deal and with much abundance", from the verb 'kudisisa' meaning "to love a lot/profusely and with great abundance". A shorter form of the name may be Tadisa.
Means "We've been loved by God" in Shona.
Zimbabwean name....it mean God is proud of us
Alternate transcription of Arabic تاج الدين (see Taj ad-Din) chiefly used in Algeria.

Name borne by a Mesopotamian goddess associated with the underworld, often thought of as the daughter of Nergal. The etymology is uncertain, although possible elements have been identified in both Akkadian (dāmasu meaning "to humble" or dāmašu meaning the interrogative form of "cover up") and Ge'ez (damasu meaning "to abolish, destroy, hide").
Romanian form of Zadok, not generally used as a given name.
Alternate transcription of Thai ทัศนัย (see Thatsanai).
Alternate transcription of Thai ทัศนีย์ (see Thatsani).

From Hurrian Tadu-Hepa, in which the second element is the name of the sun goddess Hepa (also transcribed Hebat, Heba, Kheba, Khepat or Hepatu). This was the name of a princess of the Mitanni kingdom in northern Mesopotamia, who married the Egyptian pharaoh Amenhotep III at the very end of his reign and later became one of the wives of Akhenaten (when he took over his father's royal harem). Thus some Egyptologists have proposed that Tadukhipa and Kiya were the same person (in which case Kiya would have been a diminutive of Tadukhipa).
Diminutive of Tadeoz and its short forms Tade and Tado, as it contains the Georgian diminutive suffix -უნა (-una).
Diminutive of Tadeusz. This name was borne by a character in Thomas Mann's novella Death in Venice (1912).
From the name of the Taj Mahal, a mausoleum located in the Indian city of Agra. Its name comes from Persian تاج محل (taj mahal) meaning "crown of the palace".

column3: たえ(Japanese Hiragana)|タエ(Japanese Katakana)|妙, 田恵, 多永, 多栄, 多映, 太重, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Sino-Korean 太 (tae) meaning "great", 泰 (tae) meaning "exalted", 怠 (tae) meaning "idle", or other hanja characters with the same pronunciation

Means "able" in Māori. From Māori phrase "iti rearea teitei kahikatea ka taea" meaning "the small bellbird overcomes the tall kahikatea tree" interpreted as "although small you can ascend great heights". In Cook Islands Māori taea means "club, weapon".
From Sino-Koren 太 (tae) meaning "large, great, big" and 滼 (beom) meaning "float, fly". Other Hanja combinations are possible.
Alternate romanization of korean hangul "댁연" (Taek-yeon) Famous bearer of this name is Ok Taecyeon from korean boy group 2PM

column3: 태은(Korean Hangul)|太恩, 態恩, 太銀, 態銀, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 太 (tae) meaning "largem great, big" or 態 (tae) meaning "manner, bearing, attitude" combined with 恩 (eun) meaning "saviour, mercy" or 銀 (eun) meaning "money". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From Sino-Korean 泰 "great, exalted, superior; big" and 根 "root; foundation"

column3: 태기(Korean Hangul)|泰起, 泰基, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 泰 (tae) meaning "big, large, great; easy, calm," combined with 起 (gi) meaning "rise, stand up, begin" or 基 (gi) meaning "foundation, base". Other Hanja combinations are possible.
Derived from Korean Hanja 泰(tae) meaning "big" and 坤(gon) meaning "land, earth".
From Sino-Korean 泰 (tae) meaning "peaceful" and 景 (gyeong) meaning "scenery, view".
From Sino-Korean 泰 (tae) "great, exalted, superior; big" and 夏 (ha) meaning "summer, great, grand".
Combination of a tae hanja, e.g. 泰 meaning "big, large, great; easy, calm," and a heon hanja, e.g. 憲 meaning "lesson, guidance; enlightenment."

column3: 태훈(Korean Hangul)|泰勛, 泰勳, 泰熏, 太勳, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 태훈 (see Tae-hun).

Korean unisex name which can have several different meanings depending on the hanja chosen; 太 (tae) meaning "big, great" or 泰 (tae) meaning "great, superior, exhalted, big" and 熙 meaning "bright, glorious", or 泰 (tae) as before and 希 meaning "hope".

column3: 태훈(Korean Hangul)|泰勛, 泰勳, 泰熏, 太勳, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 泰 (tae) meaning "peaceful" or 太 (tae) meaning "very, extreme" combined with 勛/勳 (hun) meaning "meritorious deed, rank" or 熏 (hun) meaning "smoke, fog, vapour". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 태현(Korean Hangul)|太鉉, 太炫, 泰現, 泰賢, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 太 (tae) meaning "very, extreme" or 泰 (tae) meaning "peaceful" combined with 鉉 (hyeon) referring to a device used to lift a ritual tripod cauldron, 炫 (hyeon) meaning "shine, glitter", 現 (hyeon) meaning "appear, manifest" or 賢 (hyeon) meaning "virtuous, worthy, wise". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From Sino-Korean 泰 "great, exalted, superior; big" and 亨 "smoothly, progressing, no trouble".

column3: 태현(Korean Hangul)|太鉉, 太炫, 泰現, 泰賢, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 태현 (see Tae-hyeon).

From the Korean Hangul character 태 (tae) based on the Hanja character 泰 (tài) meaning "big; great; good" combined with 형 (hyung; hyeong) derived from 亨 (hēng) meaning "bright; brilliant; smooth; progressing".Other characters combinations are also possible.A famous bearer is Kim Tae-hyung (김태형; b. 1995), also known by his stage name V, a South Korean singer and songwriter. He is a vocalist of the South Korean boy group BTS.
Meaning uncertain. Possibly begins with the feminine prefixes ⲧⲁ- (ta) or ⲧ- (ⲧ-).

The name Tae-il(태일) can be written in "泰壹" , "泰肷" or many other ways in Hanja. Meaning various on how written in Hanja. People famous have the name such as: Jeon Tae-il(전태일) was a South Korean activist in protest of poor working conditions in South Korea later burning himself(1948-1970). Yoon Tae-il(윤태일) is a South Korean Handball player(1964). Lee Tae-il(이태일) is an artist under popular Korean singing group B-block(블락비)(1990). Moon Tae-il(문태일) is an artist under new Korean singing group NCT(엔시티)(1994). Fictional character Han Tae-il(한태일) was acted by Hwang Jung-min(황정민) in South Korean movie Man in Love(남자가 사랑할 때). Fictional character Park Tae-il(박태일) was acted by Ahn Jae-hyun(안재현) in South Korean drama You're All Surrounded(너희들은 포위됐다).

column3: 태진(Korean Hangul)|泰鎭, 泰珍, 泰振, 泰進, 泰辰, 兌鎭, 太珍, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Combination of a tae hanja, like 泰 meaning "big, large, great; easy, calm," 兌 meaning "change, switch; happiness" or 太 meaning "big, large; heavy," and a jin hanja, such as 鎭 meaning "quellable," 珍 meaning "treasure," 振 meaning "shake," 進 meaning "advance, progress" or 辰, referring to the Dragon as the fifth of twelve earthly branches in the Chinese zodiac.
From Sino-Korean 泰 (tae) meaning "peaceful" and 俊 (jun) meaning "beautiful, handsome".

A “responsible” and “matured” person, this name is the original version said often to be Tae-yung.This name was more known after some youtubers were called that and someone else popular who almost got the name as well.

column3: 妙子, 多恵子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|たえこ(Japanese Hiragana)|タエコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 妙 (tae) meaning "mysterious, strange, excellent" or 多 (ta) meaning "many" and 恵 (e) meaning "favour, benefit" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". This name can be formed from other combinations of kanji as well.
From Sino-Korean 澤 "marsh, swamp; grace, brilliance; damp, moist; fertile" and 運 "luck, fortune; ship, transport".
From Sino-Korean 澤 "grace, brilliance; fertile" and 演 "perform, put on; exercise".
From the fairy character from the video game The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask. He is the brother of Tatl, the game's main fairy companion.
From Sino-Korean 泰 "great, exalted, superior" and 民 "people, subjects, citizens". A famous bearer is South Korean singer Lee Tae-min (1993-).

column3: ແຕງໂມ(Lao)|แตงโม(Thai)
태오(Korean Hangul)|太五, 態五, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 太 (tae) meaning "large, great, big" or 態 (tae) meaning "manner, bearing, attitude" combined with 五 (o) meaning "five". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 태오(Korean Hangul)|太五, 態五, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangeul 태오 (see Tae-o).

column3: 태리(Korean Hangul)|泰梨, 泰利, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 泰 (tae) meaning "big, large, great; easy, calm" and 梨 (ri) meaning "pear (tree)" or 利 (ri) meaning "benefit, advantage," along with other hanja combinations.Bearers of this name include actor Lee Tae-ri, born Lee Min-ho (1993-), and actress Kim Tae-ri (1990-), the latter of which caused the name to jump in popularity for girls since 2016, when she made her feature film debut in the film 'The Handmaiden'.
From Egyptian tꜣ-Ꜣs.t meaning "she of Isis" or "belonging to Isis", derived from tꜣ "the aforementioned; the; she of" combined with the name of the goddess Isis.

column3: 태석(Korean Hangul)|兌錫, 泰錫, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 兌 (tae) meaning "to exchange" or 泰 (tae) meaning "peaceful, safe" combined with 錫 (seok) meaning "tin". This name can be formed by other hanja character combinations as well.
From Sino-Korean 泰 (tae) "great, exalted" and 順 (sun) "obey, submit to, go along with". Other hanja can be used.
Meaning unknown. This is the name of a character in Ossetian Mythology and the Caucasian Nart sagas. He is a close friend and favorite of God.
From Sino-Korean 泰 "great, exalted, superior; big" and 愚 "stupid, doltish, foolish".

column3: 태완(Korean Hangul)|太完, 態完, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 太 (tae) meaning "large, great, big" or 態 (tae) meaning "manner, bearing, attitude" combined with 完 (wan) meaning “complete, finish, settle, whole”. Other hanja combinations can form this name as well

column3: 태원(Korean Hangul)|泰元, 泰源, 泰遠, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 泰 (tae) meaning "peaceful" combined with 元 (won) meaning "first, origin", 源 (won) meaning "spring, source" or 遠 (won) meaning "distant, far". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From Sino-Korean 泰 "great, exalted" (tae), and 連 "join, connect; continuous; even" or 姸 "beautiful" (yeon). A famous bearer is South Korean singer Kim Tae-yeon (1989-).
Means "calm". Taeyeon is also a popular singer in South Korea under groups Girls' Generation and TTS and has her own solo career.
From Sino-Korean 泰 "great, exalted, superior" (tae) and 榮 "glory, honor; flourish, prosper", 映 "project; reflect light" or 英 "petal, flower, leaf; brave, a hero" (yeong).

column3: 태윤(Korean Hangul)|太允, 太胤, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 太 (tae) meaning "large, great, big" combined with 允 (yun) meaning "allow, consent" 胤 (yun) meaning "heir, successor”. Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

Means "belonging to the white oracle" in Yoruba, derived from ti meaning "belonging to", àlà meaning "white cloth; banner" and ifá meaning "divination; oracle". It is possibly used as diminutive of a longer name as well.
Means "one who is respected" in Amharic.
From the English word for the woven fabric, the name of which is derived from Persian تافته (tafteh).
From the character Taffy Tucker introduced in 1942 in the comic strip 'Terry and the pirates'.The name is motivated by the candy coloured hair of the comic character.
Tafia is a type of rum made in Haiti from molasses, refuse sugar, or the like. It is (rarely) used as a given name both in Haiti & the Hawaiian islands.
Possibly derived from the name of a river in northwestern Algeria.
Alternate transcription of Arabic تفسير (see Tafsir), as well as the usual Urdu form.
Means "interpretation, explanation" in Arabic, a derivative of فسر (fassara) meaning "to interpret, to explain". In Islam the term denotes an exegesis or commentary of the Quran.
Transferred use of the surname Taft in honor of famous bearer President William Taft.
We are now rich, we are enriched
Diminutive of Taggart or variant of Tagg. Also used as a nickname by people with initials T.A.G.

column3: 田上, 田神(Japanese Kanji)|タガミ(Japanese Katakana)

column12: From the given name Tagan and Arabic تاج (tāj) meaning "crown".
From Guanche *tagayakt, meaning "farmer". This was recorded as the name of a 22-year-old Guanche woman who was sold at the slave market in Valencia in 1494.

column3: 耕(Japanese Kanji)|たがやす(Japanese Hiragana)|タガヤス(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From verb 耕す (tagayasu) meaning "to till, plough, cultivate," derived via a sound shift from a combination of 田 (ta) meaning "rice field" and verb 返す (kaesu) meaning "to restore; to turn over."This name is very rarely used.
Short form of Taggart and variant of Tadg.
Transferred use of the surname Taggart.
Alternate transcription of Arabic تغريد (see Taghrid).
Means "(she) will rejoice", making it relative to Yagil.
Russian form of Tahir, used particularly in Dagestan, Bashkortostan and Tatarstan.
Alternate transcription of Arabic تغريد (see Taghrid).
Borne by an indigene who was christened in Seville, Spain.
Allegedly means "two lodges meet" in Ojibwe.
Tahan was a son of Ephraim according to Numbers 26:35 and 1 Chronicles 7:25.
First part of compound Arabic names or phrases, that in itself derived from طہارت ال meaning "cleanliness of the".
Perhaps means "porpoise" in Hebrew, indicating a kind of leather or skin. In the Bible, Tahash was the third son of Nahor by his concubine Reumah (Gen. 22:24).
Means "hawk, falcon" in Lakota. From čhetáŋ 'hawk, falcon'.
From the genitive form of Estonian täht, cognate with Finnish Tähti.
Alternate transcription of Persian طاهره (see Tahereh).
Means "greeting, salutation" in Arabic, a derivative of حيا (ḥayyā) meaning "to greet".
Variant of Taiel. The name is found mainly in Argentina.It is also the name of a character in the computer game "The Elder Scrolls—Skyrim".
Means "someone who is well balanced" in Somali.
This name is of Polynesian origins with emphasis placed on "Ta" meaning One and "hilia" meaning 'to choose' thus the name Tahilia can mean Chosen One.
Alternate transcription of Arabic طاهرة (see Tahira).
Tahiri Veila appears in the Star Wars books as a Jedi Knight/Sith Apprentice after 22 ABY.
"Queen" The beautiful One who overcomes obstacles and reigns with grace. A luminary soft as the as the moon and as bright as the sun. Signified by the color purple indicating her royalty.
Derived from the word Tahiti, itself from Proto-Polynesian tafiti, meaning “distant, remote.”
Alternate transcription of Arabic تحية (see Tahia).
Alternate transcription of Arabic تحية (see Tahia).

Variant of Taj (which in turn was used by American musician Tito Jackson, a member of the Jackson 5, for his first son born 1973 - Toriano Adaryll 'Taj' Jackson Jr. - in whose case Taj is a nickname formed from his initials). A known bearer is Tahj Mowry (1986-), an American television actor.
Possibly an elaboration of Tahj using the phonetic element jay. Also compare Ajee, Tyjae.
From Finnish tähkä meaning "ear of grain", and pää meaning "head". It is the Finnish name for Rapunzel and not used as a given name in Finland.
Origin uncertain; may be a variant of Tahlia.
Perhaps a variant of Tahlia influenced by Zali. This is borne by Tahli Gill (1999-), an Australian curler who competed at 2022 Winter Olympics.
Meaning: " Woman/girl who recites the Quran often"
A portmanteau of Tammy, meaning "perfection" and Kahlil, meaning "friend". The resulting meaning is "perfect friend."
Alternate transcription of Arabic تحميد or Bengali তাহমিদ (see Tahmid).
Alternate transcription of Persian تهمینه (see Tahmineh).
A noted bearer is actor Tahmoh Penikett whose mother is a White River First Nations member. According to Tahmoh, his grandmother chose the name and that it is Upper Tanana, or Nebesna, in origin.
A fictional character from the show "The Legend of Korra".
From the name of the river on the California/Nevada border. Means "the lake" in Washo language.
Allegedly means "here is the one from the abode" in Guanche. It was borne by a 5-year-old Guanche girl sold at the slave market in Valencia in 1497.
Means "Wrapped in Blanket Woman" in Cheyenne.

Means "prohibition, sanctity" in Arabic, from the root حَرَّمَ (ḥarrama). This is the name of the 66th chapter of the Quran (surah at-Tahrim), which discusses prohibitions within the context of the Prophet Muhammad's wives.
From the Arabic تَحْرِيم (taḥrîm) meaning “made inviolable”, the name of one of the chapters of the Quran.
Means "liberation, release" in Arabic, from the root حَرَّرَ (ḥarrara) meaning "to free, to liberate, to emancipate".
Alternate transcription of Arabic تحسين (see Tahsin).
Means "improvement, beautification, perfection" in Arabic, from the root حَسَّنَ (ḥassana) meaning "to improve, to perfect".
Means "killdeer", a type of bird, in Cheyenne.
From Estonian täht, cognate with Finnish Tähti.
Means "to cook" and "sweetheart" in Māori. Tahu is the god of food and feasts, and the embodiment of the dining hall in Māori mythology.

column3: 大, 泰, 太, 耐, 諦, 泰衣, 泰維, 泰依, 多衣, 多以(Japanese Kanji)|たい(Japanese Hiragana)|タイ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can be used as 大 (tai, dai, oo-, -oo.ini, oo.kii) meaning "big, large", 泰 (tai) meaning "calm, easy, peace, peaceful, Thailand," 太 (ta, tai, futo.i, futo.ru) meaning "big around, plump, thick", 耐 (tai, ta.eru) meaning "enduring" or 諦 (tai, tei, akira.meru, tsumabiraka, makoto) meaning "abandon, give up."Rare examples of Tai with 2 kanji for females include 泰衣, 泰維, 泰依, 多衣 and 多以 with 衣 (i, e, kinu, -gi, koromo) meaning "clothes, dressing, garment", 維 (i) meaning "fibre, rope, tie", 依 (i, e, yo.ru) meaning "consequently, depend on, due to, reliant, therefore" and 以 (i, mo'.te) meaning "because, by means of, compared with, in view of."Tai, when used as either 大 or 泰, can be used for both genders.In the Edo Period (1603-1868), it was used as an uncommon to very uncommon feminine name.One bearer of this name was film director and screenwriter Tai Katō (加藤 泰) (1916-1985).
Means "to paint, to tattoo" in Māori.
Means "long wooden weapon" in Māori. A taiaha is a carved Māori battle spear.
Combination of the names Tai and An 1
Means "great respect", a combination of Tahitian taia "to respect, to fear" and nui "great, immense".
Alternate transcription of Arabic طيب (see Tayyib), as well as the usual Malay form.

column3: たいちろ(Japanese Hiragana)|タイチロ(Japanese Katakana)|太一郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
たいちろう(Japanese Hiragana)|タイチロウ(Japanese Katakana)|太一郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big", 一 (ichi) meaning "one" and 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.
Varient of Daichuan, Daijuan, Daiquan, Daizhuan, Taichuan, Taijuan, Taiquan, or Taizhuan (using Wade-Giles transcription).
From Chinese 泰 (tài) meaning "peaceful" combined with 川 (chuān) meaning "river, stream". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Form of Thaïs - also compare its Italian form Taide. In Slavic countries, this name can also be a variant of Taisiya, which is ultimately of Coptic origin.
Meaning uncertain. This name might possibly be a masculinization of Taida.
Meaning unknown. Compare this name with the similar-looking names Taida and Taidas, both of which are in use in Estonia's fellow Baltic country Lithuania.
Variant of Taieb influenced by French orthography.
Alternate transcription of Arabic طيب (see Tayyib) chiefly used in North Africa.
From Mapuche tayül denoting a song by a shaman.Used as a given name in Argentina and Uruguay.
Manx cognate of Tadg. This name was traditionally Anglicized as the etymologically unrelated Timothy.
Of uncertain origin and meaning, this name has been in use from the late 19th century onwards. A derivation from Latvian taiga has been suggested.

column3: 耐吾, 泰梧, 大五, 諦湖, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 太 (tai) meaning "large, big, great" combined with 吾 (go) meaning "I, me, myself, ego". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 大平, 泰平, 太平, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 大 (tai) meaning "big, great" and 平 (hei) meaning "peace, flat, even". Other kanji combinations can be used.
From Japanese 耐 (tai) meaning "withstand" combined with 一 (ichi) meaning "one". Other kanji combinations are possible.Famous bearer of this name Japanese businessman Taiichi Ohno.

column3: 太一郎, 泰一郎, 壹一郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 太 (tai) meaning "thick, big", 一 (ichi) meaning "one" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Finnish variant of Taina as well as a Finnish diminutive of Tarja and Taimi.

column3: 太極, 太极(Chinese)|泰司, 泰士, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|たいじ(Japanese Hiragana)|タイジ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: A Mandarin Chinese name sounding similar to and which is a cognate of Tae-ji. Probably means “Supreme Ultimate” in Mandarin Chinese.

column3: 諦道郎, 大司郎, 太治郎, 泰次郎, 耐二郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 耐 (tai) meaning "enduring" combined with 二 (ji) meaning "two" and 郎 (ro) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Variant of Tywan, the spelling influenced by Juan 1 and possibly Taiwan.
Means "tiger" in Māori. A notable bearer of this name is New Zealand actor and film director Taika Waititi (born 1975).

From Japanese 大 (tai) meaning "big, great" combined with 海 (kai) meaning "sea, ocean" or it can also come from Japanese 大海 (taikai) meaning "sea; ocean". Other kanji combinations are also possible.Famous bearer of this name is Japanese football player Taikai Uemoto. He is currently playing for V-Varen Nagasaki.
In Japanese, the term 太鼓 (taiko) refers to any kind of drum, but outside Japan, it is used to refer to any of the various Japanese drums. Taiko have a mythological origin in Japanese folklore.
From Japanese 大 (tai) meaning "big, large" combined with 空 (kuu) meaning "sky". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Derived from a Brythonic loan word represented by Welsh telediw "well formed, beautiful".

From the English word tails. This is the nickname of Miles Prower, a character in the Sonic the Hedgehog series and main tag-along partner of Sonic. Miles Prower is a two-tailed fox, hence the nickname.
Tailtiu is the name of a presumed goddess in Irish Mythology.
Taimani is of Tongan origin, meaning 'diamond'. It's now used by the entire Pacific community, especially in Fiji, Sāmoa and other Polynesian nations.
Means "wet plain" in Māori from tai meaning "water, sea" and mania meaning "plain, plateau, slip", or a variant spelling of Taimani/Taimana meaning "diamond" in Tongan and Māori.
Variant transcription of Taymas, which is a variant form of Taymaz.

column3: 大美, 泰美, 鯛実, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|たいみ(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From Japanese 大 (tai) meaning "large, big", 泰 (tai) meaning "peaceful, calm" or 鯛 (tai) meaning "sea bream, red snapper" combined with 美 (mi) meaning "beauty, beautiful" or 実 (mi) meaning "truth, reality". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Alternate transcription of Urdu تیمور (see Taimur).
Probably derived from the Mongolian name Tömörkhaan.
Means "great star" in Tupi-Guaraní.Karajá god related with Venus ("Morning Star") who came to the Earth in the form of man and teach humanity the agriculture.
Of uncertain origin, this was the name of a consort of Nurhaci. Due to the similarity of her name with that of Daiyinzha, the two have often been confused.
From taininihi meaning "neap tide". Also a loan word from English meaning "tiny". This is the name of Taini Morrison who was a Maori arts performer in New Zealand.
Means "big tidal wave" in Maori. Tainui is a historic canoe from Hawaiki.
Means "nourishing" and "coastal health" from tai meaning "coast, tide, sea" and ora meaning "life" in Māori and Tahitian.
Derived from Miwok tapa "to spread wings, to flap", with the implied meaning "valley quail spreading wings as it alights".

column3: 泰权, etc.(Chinese)|泰權, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 泰 (tài) meaning "peaceful" or "most" combined with 权 (quán) meaning "counterpoise" or "power, right". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Means "(she) will light up" in Hebrew, making it relative to Yair.

column3: 平良, 太良, 泰良, 大楽, 坦, 平, 和, 萍, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 太 (tai, ta) meaning "thick, big", 泰 (tai) meaning "peaceful, calm", 大 (tai) meaning "big, great", 坦 (taira) meaning "flat, smooth", 田 (ta) meaning "rice paddy", 平 (taira) meaning "level; even; flat", 和 (taira) meaning "peace, harmony" or 萍 (taira) meaning "duckweed" combined with 良 (ra) meaning "good", 洋 (ra) meaning "ocean", 楽 (ra) meaning "comfort, music" or 等 (ra) meaning "rank, class, order". Other kanji or kanji combinations can form this name as well.A famous bearer is Taira Imata (1975-), a Japanese actor who is represented by the talent agencies, Shōnen Shachu and Ace Agent.

column3: 泰莉(Japanese Kanji)|たいり(Japanese Hiragana)|タイリ(Japanese Katakana)

column12: From tai meaning "sea, tide" or "cry" and ria meaning "phantom, vision" in Tahitian.
Arabic meaning little bird from the word "Ta'ir" meaning bird
Bulgarian, Russian and Spanish and Galician form of Thaïs.
Irish Gaelic.Direct translation = TreasureTreasury bord in Ireland = An TaiscePet name in west Cork = mo dTaiscín (my little treasure)

column3: 太清, 苔世, 苔政, 泰晴, 泰正, 泰聖, 泰誠, 大征, 大晴, 大生, 大聖, 大誓, 大晟, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 苔 (tai) meaning "moss", 泰 (tai) meaning "Thailand, calm, peaceful" or 大 (tai) meaning "big, great" combined with 成 (sei) meaning "to become", 青 (sei) meaning "blue, green", 生 (sei) meaning "grow, birth, life, genuine" or 星 (sei) meaning "star, dot". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Variant of Tyesha that takes influence from Aisha.

column3: 帝釈天(Japanese Kanji)|たいしゃくてん(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From Japanese 帝 (tai) meaning "god, emperor", 釈 (shaku) taken from Sanskrit शक्र (śakra) and 天 (ten) meaning "sky, heaven". This is the Japanese name for the deity Shakra.

column3: 大志, 大司, 泰士, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 太 (tai) meaning "big, great" combined with 史 (shi) meaning "history". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer is Taishi Nakagawa, a Japanese actor, host, and model. He is best known in his role as Kakeru Asuda in the 2011 drama 'Kaseifu no Mita' and Noboru Yoshikawa in the 2012 live action drama remake of 'Great Teacher Onizuka'.
Georgian form of Taisiya and Romanian form of Thais. According to Orthodox Christian ecclesiastical traditions, Taisia (Thais in English) is venerated as a Virgin-Martyr alongside Saint Drosis.
Belarusian, Latvian and Lithuanian form of Taisiya as well as a Russian and Ukrainian variant transcription of the name.
An invented name made to sound like the names Paisley or Haisley.
Most likely a combination of Tais with Mary. This name is best known for being the name of the Cuban-born Italian volleyball player Taismary Agüero (b. 1977).
Variant spelling of Tyson, which is more phonetical in nature.A notable bearer of this name is the Brazilian professional soccer player Taison Barcellos Freda (b. 1988).
Dutch and French form of Taissa.

Extremely rare Russian variant of Taisa as well as an anglicized form (or variant transcription) of the name.A well-known bearer of this name is the Ukrainian-American actress Taissa Farmiga (b. 1994).
Variant transcription of Taissiya, which is a rare variant form of Taisiya.
Estonian transcription of Russian Таисия (see Taisiya).

column3: たいすけ(Japanese Hiragana)|タイスケ(Japanese Katakana)|泰輔, 退助, 大翼, 夷⁠佑, 碓⁠侑, 敦⁠亮, 苔介, 黛佐, 殆資, 耐右, 諦丞, 太祐, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: This name is used as 退 (tai) meaning "drive out, withdraw, retreat" or 泰 (tai) meaning "calm, peaceful, Thailand" combined with 侑 (suke) meaning "help, assist, urge to eat" or 匡 (suk) meaning "straighten, correct, rectify". Other kanji combinations are also possible.
Diminutive of Taís, Taísa and Taíssa. Also see Taisy.
Variant form of Daisy. See also Taísy.
Possibly a short form of Teitur and/or derived from Old Norse teitr “cheerful, merry”.
Means "king of the sea", a combination of Tahitian tai meaning "sea" and te ari'i meaning "the king".

column3: 帯人, 戴斗, 泰人, 泰斗, 泰登, 大翔, 民愛, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Fijian and Samoan form of Titus.
Means "spring tide, tidal wave" in Māori.

From Greenlandic taatsiisaq or taatsiigaq meaning "the one whom one has held back to mention (name)", from a Greenlandic endearment term: "the fancied mention", carefully not mentioning the name, but expressing endearment nevertheless, because the child was named after a deceased relative, from Greenlandic atsiaq meaning "the one named after a deceased person" and from a hypocoristic word taa(nna)tsiaq meaning "the dear, sweet one".
Combination of Taitsiaĸ and the suffix -nnguaq "sweet, dear".
Name of a 19th century Ethiopian empress known for founding the now-capital city of Addis Ababa and fending off Italian invasion of Ethiopia
Means "peaceful hero" in Mongolian, from тайван (taivan) meaning "peaceful, quiet, still" and баатар (baatar) meaning "hero".
Means "peaceful celebration" in Mongolian, from тайван (taivan) meaning "peaceful, quiet, still" and баяр (bayar) meaning "joy, celebration".
From Mongolian тайван (taivan) meaning "peaceful, quiet, still" and мэнд (mend) meaning "health, well-being", often used as a greeting.
From Mongolian тайван (taivan) meaning "peaceful, quiet, still" or "peace, tranquility" and сайхан (saikhan) meaning "nice, beautiful, handsome".
Means "peaceful happiness" in Mongolian, from тайван (taivan) meaning "peaceful, quiet, still" and жаргал (jargal) meaning "happiness, blessing".
Derived from Old Estonian taivas (taevas in Modern Estonian) "heaven".
Variant of Tywan, the spelling influenced by that of the country of Taiwan in East Asia.
Combination of the names Tai and Ya
Combination of the names Tai and Yan 2
From Chinese 太阳 (tàiyáng) meaning "the sun" or "extreme Yang". Other homophonic character combinations can be used to infuse the name with extra meaning.
From the Chinese 泰 (tài) meaning "great, superior, exalted" and 瑶 (yáo) meaning "precious jade".
A name traditionally given to a first-born twin.
From the Chinese 泰 (tài) meaning "great, superior, exalted" and 意 (yì) meaning "thought, idea".

column3: たいよう(Japanese Hiragana)|タイヨウ(Japanese Katakana)|太陽, 大洋, 大耀, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From the vocabulary words 太陽 (taiyo) meaning "the sun" or 大洋 (taiyo) meaning "the ocean", spelled with 太 (tai) meaning "big, large, great" and 陽 (yo) meaning "sun, light, male" and 洋 (yo) meaning "ocean" respectively. Other kanji combinations can be used.
The name of a legendary queen regnant of Yamatai, successor of queen Himiko. Her name is derived from 臺 (tai) meaning "tower, lookout, platform" and 與 (yo) meaning "to give, award, provide".

column3: 太陽, 泰洋, 泰陽, 大耀, 大陽, 太洋, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 太 (tai) meaning "big, thick", 泰 (tai) meaning "peaceful, calm" or 大 (tai) meaning "big, large" combined with 陽 (you) meaning "light, sun, male", 洋 (you) meaning "ocean" or 耀 (you) meaning "shine, sparkle, dazzle". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 太专, etc.(Chinese)|太專, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 太 (tài) meaning "very, extreme" combined with 专 (zhuān) meaning "only, unique, focused on one thing". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 大三, 大蔵, 大造, 太三, 太蔵, 太造, 泰三, 泰蔵, 泰造, 退三, 退蔵, 退造(Japanese Kanji)|たいぞう(Japanese Hiragana)|タイゾウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 大 (tai, dai, oo-, -oo.ini, oo.kii) meaning "big, large", 太 (ta, tai, futo.i, futo.ru) meaning "big around, plump, thick", 泰 (tai) meaning "calm, easy, peace, peaceful, Thailand" or 退 (tai, shirizo.ku, shirizo.keru, hi.ku, no.ku, no.keru, do.ku) meaning "retreat, withdraw, retire, resign, repel, expel, reject" with 三 (san, zou, mi, mi'.tsu, mi.tsu) meaning "three", 蔵 (sou, zou, osa.meru, kaku.reru, kura) meaning "have, hide, own, possess, storehouse" or 造 (zou, tsuku.ru, tsuku.ri, -dzuku.ri) meaning "create, make, structure, physique."As a word, Taizō (退蔵) means "hoarding." Taizō (胎蔵) is also used to refer to the 'Garbhadhatu' or the 'Womb Realm,' though that is not used as a name.One bearer of this name was film director Taizō Fuyushima (冬島 泰三), born Koshirō Maede (前出 小四郎) (1901-1981).This name was most commonly used from the Edo Period (1603-1868) to the second half of the 20th century but nowadays, it's rarely given to boys, if given at all.
From Chinese 太祖 (tàizǔ) meaning "great progenitor", used as a temple (posthumous) name for the founding emperors of dynasties.
Kazakh name that translates to "crown", ultimately derived from Arabic al-tāj, meaning "crown".
Means "crown of the religion" from Arabic تاج (tāj) meaning "crown" combined with دين (dīn) meaning "religion, faith".
Possibly a variant of Taja 1, occasionally used as a masculine name. Also compare Tahj.
Alternate transcription of Arabic تاج الدين (see Taj ad-Din).
Means "crown of Allah", derived from Arabic تاج (taj) meaning "crown" combined with Allah.
Possibly from the Uzbek tajalli meaning "brightness, luster".
Means "magnificence, beauty, splendor, adornment, dignity" in Arabic, related to the root جمل (jamala) meaning "to be beautiful".
Alternate transcription of Arabic تجامال or Urdu تجمل (see Tajamal).
Elaboration of Taja 1 using the popular phonetic suffix nay, influenced by Janae and Dejanae.
The name comes directly from the Georgian word for a temple. In Georgian legend, this is the name of Noah's wife.
East Frisian short form of names that contain the element thiad- "people".
Alternate transcription of Arabic تاج الدين (see Taj ad-Din) chiefly used in Morocco.

Combination of the Kazakh word taj, meaning "crown" (ultimately derived from Arabic al-tāj, meaning "the crown") and the Kazakh word bay, meaning "wealthy, rich, flamboyant". Variant spelling of Tazhibai.
Combination of the Kazakh word taj, meaning "crown" (ultimately derived from Arabic al-tāj, meaning "the crown") and the Turkic title beg, meaning "chieftain" or "ruler".
Possibly a variant of Taja or a feminine form of Taj. A notable bearer is Canadian actress Tajja Isen (1991-), who is of Trinidadian descent.
Medieval Polish diminutive of Tatiana and Slovene diminutive of Taja.
From a Turkic word meaning "crowned", ultimately from Persian تاج (tāj) meaning "crown". This was the name of a wife of Safavid shah Ismail I and mother of Tahmasp I.
Derived from Serbo-Croatian тајна, tajna, meaning "a secret".
Combination of the prefix ta with the name Juan 1, making it a masculine form of Tajuana.
Alternate transcription of Arabic تاج الدين (see Taj ad-Din), as well as the Dari Persian, Malay and Indonesian form.
Indonesian and Malay variant of Taj ad-Din.
First part of compound Arabic names beginning with تاج ال (tāj al) meaning "crown of the" (such as Taj ad-Din).
The Guaraní name for the lapacho flower.

column3: さしば(Japanese Hiragana)|鷹, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 鷹 (taka) meaning "hawk, falcon, eagle". Other kanji or kanji combinations are possible.Taka was most commonly used in the feudal era.

column3: 貴明, 孝明, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 貴 (taka) meaning "valuable" and 明 (aki) meaning "bright". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Derived from the Uzbek taka meaning "male goat" and boy meaning "rich, wealthy".

column3: 孝江, 高恵, 孝絵, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 孝 (taka) meaning "filial piety, obedience" and 江 (e) meaning "inlet, bay". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 貴文, 隆文, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|たかふみ(Japanese Hiragana)|タカフミ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 貴 (taka) meaning "precious, valuable" or 隆 (taka) meaning "noble, prosperous" combined with 文 (fumi) meaning "writing". Other combinations of kanji can form this name as well.

column3: 孝晴, 高晴, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 孝 (taka) meaning "filial piety" and 晴 (haru) meaning "fine, clear weather". Other kanji combinations can be used.
From 昂 (taka) meaning "high spirited, to raise the head" and 秀 (hide) meaning "excellent, outstanding." Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 位彦, 栄彦, 王彦, 岳彦, 貴彦, 恭比古, 敬彦, 顕彦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 位 (taka) meaning "rank, place" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince". Other kanji combinations are also possible.A famous bearer is Takahiko Nomaguchi, a Nippon Professional Baseball player for the Yomiuri Giants in Japan's Central League.

column3: 威央, 郁久, 郁尚, 貴久, 義久, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 威 (taka) meaning "intimidate" combined with 央 (hisa) meaning "centre, middle". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer is Takahisa Masuda, a Japanese idol from Johnny's Entertainment.

column3: 貴人, 孝一, 高仁, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 貴 (taka) meaning "valuable, worthful, superior, aristocratic" and 人 (hito) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 高一, 孝市, 幸一, 尭一, 貴一, 尚一, 崇壱, 鷹一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 高 (taka) meaning "tall, high" combined with 一 (ichi) meaning "one". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 鷹一郎, 隆一郎, 高一郎, 貴一郎, 孝一郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 鷹 (taka) meaning "eagle, falcon, hawk", 一 (ichi) meaning "one" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other combinations of kanji characters are also possible.

Name that was given during the Hēan Period, to a Regional Governor of Dazaifu, "藤原 隆家" FUJIWARANOTAKAIE, married to "源重信の娘" Daughter of MINAMOTONOSHIGENOBU and "藤原景斉の娘" Daughter of FUJIWARANOHITOSHI and "源兼資の娘" Daughter of MINAMOTONOKANESUKE and "藤原為光の娘" Daughter of FUJIWARANOTAMEMITSU and "加賀守正光の娘" Daughter of KAGANOKAMIMASAMITSU. The Kanji Character "隆" meaning "Grand", with the Kanji Character "家" meaning "House". See also Korechika, Tēshi.
Possibly an invented name using the phonetic elements ta, kay and sha. Also compare Takisha.
Possibly a combination of the popular name prefix ta and Kaya 2.

column3: 孝司, 敬得, 尭治, 喬次, 貴爾, 毅爾, 孝治, 孝爾, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 孝 (taka) meaning "filial piety" combined with 司 (ji) meaning "take charge of, control, manage". Other kanji combinations can also form this name.

column3: 孝和, 高数, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 高 (taka) meaning "tall, high" and 数 (kazu) meaning "number". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: タカキ(Japanese Katakana)|貴己, 喬規, 尭紀, 孝樹, 昂生, 高城, 崇記, 天貴, 隆規, 隆樹, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 昂 (taka) meaning "to raise the head, high spirited" combined with 喜 (ki) meaning "rejoice". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means "something that has been bartered/exchanged for" in Malagasy.

column3: 隆丸, 孝丸, 高丸, 尭丸, 鷹丸(Japanese Kanji)|たかまる(Japanese Hiragana)|タカマル(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 隆 (ryuu, taka) meaning "high, hump, noble, prosperity," 孝 (kyou, kou, taka) meaning "child's respect, filial piety," 高 (kou, taka.i, taka, -daka, taka.maru, taka.meru) meaning "expensive, high, tall," 尭 (gyou, taka.i) meaning "far, high" or 鷹 (ou, you, taka) meaning "hawk" with 丸 (gan, maru, maru.i, maru.meru) meaning "curl up, explain away, full, make round, month, perfection, pills, roll up, round, seduce".Before the Meiji Period (1868-1912), -maru (丸) was used as a suffix denoting affection (along with -maro {麿/麻呂}) and was given to boys of upper class until they reached 14.This name is rarely given to boys, if given at all.A fictional bearer of this name is Takamaru (鷹丸), a character from the Famicom game 'The Mysterious Murasame Castle'.Takamaru (高丸) is also used as a surname.

column3: 貴正, 孝正, 貴雅, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 貴 (taka, ki) meaning "valuable" or 孝 (taka) meaning "filial piety" combined with 正 (masa) meaning "right, proper" or 雅 (masa) meaning "elegant, graceful". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: たかみ(Japanese Hiragana)|タカミ(Japanese Katakana)|たか実, たか美(Kanji/Hiragana)|岳実, 岳美, 貴己, 貴三, 貴実, 貴臣, 貴水, 貴美, 貴巳, 空弓, 空見, 空実, 孝海, 孝己, 孝実, 孝美, 孝巳, 孝弥, 孝已, 鷹実, 鷹身, 鷹美, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 貴 (taka) meaning "expensive", 岳 (taka) meaning "mountain peak", 空 (taka) meaning "sky", 孝 (taka) meaning "filial piety" or 鷹 (taka) meaning "eagle, falcon, hawk" combined with 己 (mi) meaning "self", 三 (mi) meaning "three", 実 (mi) meaning "fruit", 臣 (mi) meaning "minister; statesman; official", 水 (mi) meaning "water", 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful", 巳 (mi) meaning "sign of the snake", 弓 (mi) meaning "archery bow", 見 (mi) meaning "to see", 海 (mi) meaning "sea, ocean", 弥 (mi) meaning "extensive, full" or 身 (mi) meaning "body, identity". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous female bearer Takami Ominami, is a long-distance runner from Japan, whose main event is the marathon and a famous male bearer is Takami Itō, a Japanese author who won an Akutagawa Prize in 2006.

column3: たかみち(Japanese Hiragana)|タカミチ(Japanese Katakana)|嵩通, 宇道, 尊路, 鳳倫, 崇理, 隆実, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 貴 (taka) meaning "valuable" or 孝 (taka) meaning "filial piety" combined with 道 (michi) meaning "path". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: たかみつ(Japanese Hiragana)|タカミツ(Japanese Katakana)|貴充, 峻光, 高満, 崇光, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 貴 (taka, ki) meaning "valuable" and 光 (mitsu) meaning "light, radiance". Other kanji combinations are usable.
From Taka meaning “High” (高) and Mizu meaning “Water” (水) and Ko meaning “Child” (子), can be read as “High water child”.

column3: 京森, 京森, 鷹森, 隆盛, 貴盛, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 京 (taka) meaning "capital city, ten quadrillion, ten thousand billion, Tokyo, Kyoto" combined with 森 (mori) meaning "forest". Other kanji combinations can be used.
A notable bearer is rally driver Takamoto Katsuta.

column3: 孝宗, 貴宗, 隆宗, 隆意, 孝旨(Japanese Kanji)|たかむね(Japanese Hiragana)|タカムネ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 孝 (taka) meaning "filial piety" combined with 宗 (mune) meaning "religion, sect, clan, ancestry". Other kanji combinations can also form this name.

column3: たか奈(Kanji/Hiragana)|貴菜, 貴奈, 貴鈴, 尭己, 孝名, 梢菜, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 貴 (taka) meaning "expensive" combined with 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens" (mostly feminine) or 己 (na) meaning "male" (mostly masculine). Other combinations of kanji are also possible.
Etymology unknown. This is the Igloolik name of Sedna.

column3: たかなお(Japanese Hiragana)|タカナオ(Japanese Katakana)|敬尚, 隆直, 孝尚, 高直, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 貴 (taka) meaning "expensive, valuable" combined with 尚 (nao) meaning "still, as always". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: たかね(Japanese Hiragana)|タカネ(Japanese Katakana)|高嶺, 貴音, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: This name can be written with 高 (taka) meaning "tall, high" or 貴 (taka) meaning "valuable, expensive, worthful" and 嶺 (ne) meaning "peak, summit" or 音 (ne) meaning "sound". Other kanji combinations can be used.The word 高嶺 (takane) is used to mean "amazing, peerless", and does not usually refer to a literal mountain peak.

column3: たかのぶ(Japanese Hiragana)|貴誠, 高信, 貴延, 貴信, 高宣, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 貴 (taka) meaning "worthful, expensive, valuable" and 誠 (nobu) meaning "sincerity". Meaning varies depending on the kanji used.

column3: たかのり(Japanese Hiragana)|宇礼, 学基, 喬教, 尭仙, 高統, 孝登, 啓雅, 隆経, 鷹敬, 貴矩, 天乗, 崇度, 尊式, 太加成, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 宇 (taka) meaning "roof, eaves, the universe, the whole world", 学 (taka) meaning "education, learn, school, study, science", or 喬 (taka) meaning "boasting, tall, high" combined with 仙 (nori) meaning "enlightened person, sage, hermit, mage, wizard", 基 (nori) meaning "to be based on, foundation" or 智 (nori) meaning "intellect, knowledge, wisdom". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: たかおみ(Japanese Hiragana)|タカオミ(Japanese Katakana)|隆臣, 孝臣, 鷹臣, 貴臣, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 貴 (taka) meaning "valuable" or 孝 (taka) meaning "filial piety" combined with 臣 (omi) meaning "one who serves a lord; a vassal, subject".
From Japanese 宝 (takara) meaning "treasure, jewel" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Of Australian Aboriginal origin (Pintupi, to be precise), the meaning of this name is not yet known to me at the moment. A known bearer of this name is Takariya Napaltjarri (b. circa 1960), an Australian Aboriginal painter.

column3: 孝郎, 喬郎, 崇郎, 隆郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 孝 (taka) meaning "filial piety" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 隆繁, 隆重, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 貴 (taka, ki) meaning "valuable" or 孝 (taka) meaning "filial piety", 隆 (taka) meaning "prosperous", combined with 繁 (shige) meaning "flourishing, luxuriant", 成 (shige) meaning "become", or 重 (shige, ju, cho) meaning "main, principal, heavy, severe".
Meaning "we are resilient"; it derives from the verb kushinga.

column3: 敬輔, 孝輔, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 敬 (taka) meaning "respect, honor, reverence" combined with 輔 (suke) meaning "help". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 貴栖⁠, 孝栖, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 貴 (taka, ki) meaning "valuable" and 栖⁠ (sai, sei. su.mu, sumika, sumi, su) meaning “nest”. Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 高忠, 隆忠, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 崇 (taka) meaning "lofty, to adore, revere, worship", 敬 (taka) meaning "respect, honor, reverence, awe" or 隆 (taka) meaning "high, hump, noble, prosperity" combined with 忠 (tada) meaning "loyalty". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 貴晃, 孝晃, 貴照, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 貴 (taka) meaning "expensive, precious, aristocratic, superior, to esteem" combined with 晃 (teru) meaning "clear". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 高人, 隆斗, 崇人, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 高 (taka) meaning "tall, high" or 考 (taka) meaning "consideration, thoughts" and 人 (to) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations can be used.
A notable bearer is Takatomi Nobunaga, a music composer.

column3: 貴智, 貴友, 威知, 喬具, 喬朝, 賢知, 孝朋, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 貴 (taka) meaning "expensive" combined with 智 (tomo) meaning "knowledge, wisdom". Other kanji combinations can also form this name.

column3: 孝才, 貴慧, 高歳, 高淑, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 孝 (taka) meaning "filial piety" combined with 利 (toshi) meaning "benefit". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 天次, 高禎, 崇継, 貴嗣, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Japanese masculine name derived from 天 (taka) meaning "heaven, sky" and 次 (tsugu) meaning "next, second". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 尊氏(Japanese Kanji)|たかうじ(Japanese Hiragana)|タカウジ(Japanese Katakana)

column12: Means "single moon, unique moon" in Azerbaijani.

column3: たかや(Japanese Hiragana)|タカヤ(Japanese Katakana)|鷹, 崇弥, 鷹矢, 高哉, 尊也, 昂耶, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 貴 (taka) meaning "expensive, valuable" or 孝 (taka) meaning "filial piety" combined with 也 (ya) meaning "also". Other kanji combinations are used.

column3: たかよ(Japanese Hiragana)|タカヨ(Japanese Katakana)|たか代(Kanji/Hiragana)|宮世, 貴与, 岳代, 宇容, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 宮 (taka) meaning "palace, shrine" combined with 代 (yo) meaning "generation". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer is Takayo Mimura (1985-), a Japanese actress.

column3: 鎬偉(Japanese Kanji)|タカヨリ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 鎬 (taka) meaning "grind line, bevel on a blade" and 偉 (yori) meaning "admirable". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 喬美, 將貴, 賢貴, 喬貴, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 喬 (taka) meaning "tall, high" combined with 貴 (yoshi) meaning "expensive, worthful, precious, superior, aristocratic, to esteem" or 美 (yoshi) meaning "beauty, beautiful". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Takbir - "magnification (of God)" is the Arabic phrase Allāhu akbar meaning "Allah is greater (than everything)".It is a common Islamic Arabic expression, used in various contexts by Muslims; in formal prayer), in the Adhan (Islamic call to prayer), as an informal expression of faith, in times of distress or joy, or to express resolute determination or defiance.It was not used as a name until 21st century.
Means "destiny, fate" in Indonesian, ultimately from Arabic تقدير (taqdīr).

column3: たけ(Japanese Hiragana)|タケ(Japanese Katakana)|威, 岳, 巌, 毅, 丈, 竹, 武, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 威 (take) meaning "intimidate", 岳 (take) meaning "mountain peak", 巌 (take) meaning "rock", 丈 (take) meaning "height", 竹 (take) meaning "bamboo" or 武 (take) meaning "military, martial". Other kanji or kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: たけあき(Japanese Hiragana)|偉哲, 偉暁, 岳亮, 岳昌, 竹昭, 竹彰, 建暁, 建顕, 建昭, 勇爽, 勇顕, 雄顕, 雄昭, 雄章, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 偉 (take) meaning "admirable", 岳 (take) meaning "mountain peak", 健 (take) meaning "robust, healthy, strength, strong", 勇 (take) meaning "brave" or 雄 (take) meaning "hero, manly" combined with 哲 (aki) meaning "philosophy, clear", 亮 (aki) meaning "clear, help", 彰 (aki) meaning "obvious, clear", 陽 (aki) meaning "light, sun, male", 朗 (aki) meaning "bright, clear", 暁 (aki) meaning "dawn, daybreak", 顕 (aki) meaning "manifest, display", 爽 (aki) meaning "clear, sweet, refreshing, resonant" or 揚 (aki) meaning "scatter, spread". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 武文, 健史, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|たけふみ(Japanese Hiragana)|タケフミ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 武 (take) meaning "military, martial" or 健 (take) meaning "strong, healthy" combined with 文 (fumi) meaning "writing" or 史 (fumi) meaning "history". Other combinations of kanji can form this name as well.
From 敬 (take) meaning "respect, honor, reverence" and 房 (fusa) meaning "bunch, fringe, house, lock (of hair), room, tassel, tuft". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 武治, 竹治, 丈春, 丈晴, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 武 (take) meaning "military, martial" or 竹 (take) meaning "bamboo", combined with 治 (haru) meaning "administer, govern, rule". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 豪栄, 建栄, 建豪, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 丈 (take) meaning "length", 建 (take, ken) meaning "build, construction", 雄 (take, o) meaning "man", 全 (zen, take) meaning "whole, all" combined with 統 (to, take) meaning "sediments", or 伯 (take, haku, hyaku, osa, hatagashira) meaning "count, earl, chief official, Brazil" combined with 秀 (hide) meaning "excellent, outstanding", 英 (ei, hide) meaning "excellent, fine", 豪 (hide, go, take, ko, tsuyoi) meaning "magnificent, bold, Australia", or 栄 (ei, hide, shige) meaning "lush, luxuriant, honor, glory". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 岳弘, 竹洋, 偉浩, 武寛, 健裕, 丈博, 毅比呂, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 岳 (take) meaning "tall mountain, peak" combined with 弘 (hiro) meaning "to spread, enlarge, expand". Other kanji combinations are possible.
